title: Drive native lowerer to differential fixture parity with the CIR frontend
description: Using the same fixture-family-by-family approach that proved out in slate-ozsg.4, run tests/fixtures/*.c under --frontend native (lowering + rewrites profiles) and fix bugs until 100% parity with the CIR-frontend pass rate. File individual fixture regressions as child bugs under this issue as they're found rather than batching them into one issue.
acceptance_criteria: 100% of tests/fixtures/*.c differential tests (lowering + rewrites profiles) pass under --frontend native, matching current CIR-frontend pass rate.
notes:
Continued from the previous note (compound-assign Decl fix). Found and fixed 3 more Decl-emission-class bugs, same pattern (address-temp Objs created via new_lvar but never StmtKind::Decl-marked, so the lowerer references them before declaring them) plus one unrelated variadic-FFI bug:

1. VLA size temp Decl scoping (compute_vla_size in parser.rs): size_var temps DID get a Decl (via my earlier fix) but it was nested inside a StmtExpr embedded in the expression tree -- fine for compound-assign's self-contained use, but VLA size temps get referenced by a LATER, separate statement (the alloca() call), so nesting the `let` inside a Rust block scoped it out of existence by the time it was needed. Fixed by refactoring compute_vla_size to take `decls: &mut Vec<Stmt>` and have callers hoist those Decls into their own enclosing statement list (parse_declaration's local-decl path) or, when there's no enclosing stmt list (the sizeof(vla_type) expression-context call site), wrap the whole self-contained result in one StmtExpr instead of nesting per-dimension.

2. VLA pointer local itself (parse_declaration's VLA branch, ~line 1823): `let idx = self.new_lvar(name, ty.clone())` for the VLA's own pointer-typed local never got a Decl at all -- pushed the assign-from-alloca statement but no declare-first statement. Added `stmts.push(Decl(idx))` before the alloca assignment.

3. decay_to_ptr bug in exprs.rs (unrelated to Decl-emission, found while chasing the above): CType::Vla was grouped with CType::Array in the "needs .as_ptr().cast_mut() to decay" branch, but types.rs already lowers Type::Vla straight to a raw pointer RType::Ptr (unlike Array, which lowers to [T; N]) -- so calling .as_ptr() on an already-raw-pointer value doesn't compile (no such method). Fixed by removing Vla from that branch; it now falls through to the default (use the lowered value directly).

4. Literal-global address-of gap (items.rs lower_items, DeclKind::Var arm): unconditionally skipped emitting an Item for any GlobalKind::Literal global (string literals), on the assumption they're always inlined as RExpr::ByteStr at every use site (var_expr does this). True when a literal's VALUE is read directly, false when something takes its ADDRESS -- e.g. `char *p = "Hi";` decodes the global's init-relocation in globals.rs::decode_pointer as `&raw const <label>`, referencing the literal by name with no backing `static` declaration anywhere once the skip drops it. Fixed by removing the skip; every Literal global now gets its `static` item unconditionally (harmless dead-code warning in the majority case where it's inlined and the static goes unused, correctness fix in the address-taken case). Removed the now-unused GlobalKind import from items.rs.

5. Default argument promotion for variadic calls (exprs.rs, new call_expr/variadic_fixed_param_count/lower_variadic_arg): C requires bool/char/short (signed or unsigned) promoted to int, and float promoted to double, for arguments in the `...` tail of a variadic call (printf-style) -- chibicc's own C type checking never needed to materialize this since it's implicit at the call-ABI level, but Rust's variadic FFI calls require the actual argument type to already be the promoted one. Was previously entirely unhandled -- e.g. `printf("%c", someChar)` passed the narrow i8/u8/bool/i16/u16 type directly, which rustc rejects (E0617, "can't pass `i8` to variadic function"). Classified this as a lowering-time fix (not a parser/AST gap) per the same test the `main`-return-type special case used in the last note: the C AST already has the right type info (arg.ty, callee's Type::Func{is_variadic, params}), the mismatch is purely about what Rust's FFI ABI requires. 119 -> 43 E0617 occurrences after this fix; the remaining 43 are a different sub-case (not yet triaged, but grep showed 0 remaining bool/i8/u8/i16/u16 cases before this fix landed, so the residual 43 are likely struct/array-by-value variadic args, a materially different problem -- do NOT assume the same fix covers them).

Filed slate-ozsg.8.8.1 (P2 bug) for a genuinely separate, deeper gap surfaced while investigating #2 above: VLAs lower to a literal `alloca(size)` function call, but glibc has no linkable `alloca` symbol (confirmed via `nm -D libc.so.6`, no match) -- it's compiler-builtin-only. This needs a real design decision (Vec-backed VLA representation vs. something else), not a quick patch -- see that issue for details. tests/fixtures/local_vla.c is blocked on it specifically (everything else in that fixture now lowers/compiles correctly).

Verified after all 5 fixes: cargo build/fmt/clippy clean, native_lowerer::tests 11/11. Full fixtures/*.c corpus (rustc-compile-check only): 88 -> 94/332 compiling. Differential-verified (stdout+exit code match against clang-compiled C) beyond add.c: also checked tests/fixtures/global_string_pointer.c by hand, matches exactly ("H Hi", exit 0 both sides) -- not yet automated/bulk-checked though, still only compile-checking the full corpus in the sweep loop.

Next: resume the error-code-frequency loop. E0425 (758) and E0433 (662, entirely bitint/num_complex -- out of scope, belongs to slate-ozsg.8.6) are still the top two; E0308 (317, type mismatch) is next untriaged large bucket.
close_reason: Superseded: abandoning the ported-chibicc (cc3) parser approach. Whack-a-mole on chibicc-specific desugaring gaps (Decl-emission for compiler-synthesized temps, VLA/alloca, truthiness coercion, etc. -- see slate-ozsg.8.8's notes for the running list) made clear that re-deriving what Clang's own AST already gives for free isn't worth it. New direction: parse Clang's AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input instead of both CIR and a hand-ported C frontend. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one. All completed child work (lexer/preprocessor port, parser port, node-identity, Decl hierarchy, most of the native lowerer) stays closed/done as real completed work; it's the strategy of continuing to chase chibicc-vs-Rust semantic gaps that's being dropped, not that work.

title: Wire native lowerer behind --frontend native, remove NativeLoweringUnimplemented stub
description: Replace api::translate_native's stub (src/api.rs:298, currently parse_native(path)?; Err(Error::NativeLoweringUnimplemented)) with a real call into the new parse::ast-consuming lowering path built by slate-ozsg.8.2/.3/.4/.5, producing rust_ast::Program the same way lowered_program/lower_with_project do for the CIR path today.
acceptance_criteria: translate --frontend native <file.c> emits Rust source on stdout for at least the fixtures already covered by types/items/stmts/core-exprs; NativeLoweringUnimplemented is deleted.
notes:
Wired: api::translate_native now calls frontend::lower_program (native_lowerer) then backend::apply_with (the same fixup pipeline the CIR path uses) -- Error::NativeLoweringUnimplemented is gone. Added api::lowered_program_native for the raw-baseline equivalent of lowered_program (no fixups), mirroring the CIR path's split between translate/translate-lowered. frontend::native_lowerer is exposed crate-internally via `pub(crate) use native_lowerer::lower_program;` in frontend/mod.rs (module itself stays private, matching the existing `lowerer` pattern).

Fixed two C-vs-Rust semantic gaps in main() specifically while wiring this up (correctly identified as lowerer-level, not AST-level, since parse::ast already has the right information -- C's main returning int is a target-language mismatch, not missing source data):
- main's Rust return type is forced to () regardless of its C-declared int return type (matches CIR convention).
- `return code;` inside main lowers to `std::process::exit(code as i32)` instead of Stmt::Return, via a new FnCtx::is_main flag threaded through stmts.rs (CIR path does the same via its own is_main flag).
- main's FnDef.unsafe_ is forced false -- Rust's fn main() must be a plain safe fn (rustc: "expected safe fn, found unsafe fn"); the body is still wrapped in an inner unsafe{} block same as every other function.

First real end-to-end differential success: tests/fixtures/add.c translated via --frontend native produces Rust that compiles with rustc and produces byte-identical stdout + matching exit code against the C binary (verified with a real diff, not eyeballed).

Broader sweep across the full fixture corpus (tests/fixtures/*.c, 332 files): 69/332 already produce rustc-compiling Rust via --frontend native (not yet checked for runtime differential correctness at that scale, only compile success). translate_native itself does not panic/error on any fixture -- all 332 make it through lowering, failures are all rustc-side. Top rustc error codes across the 263 non-compiling fixtures, most to least frequent: E0425 (cannot find value, 1270 occurrences), E0433 (unresolved path/type, 657), E0308 (type mismatch, 300), E0617 (non-primitive passed to a variadic FFI call, 112), E0381 (use of possibly-uninitialized binding, 95), E0605 (non-primitive cast, 89), E0283 (ambiguous type, 35). E0425/E0433 are the most numerous and, per the pattern already found twice this session (string literals, static locals, anonymous structs), are likely more instances of the same root cause class: some category of Program-level entity that has an id/name but never gets a corresponding emitted Item. Recommend slate-ozsg.8.8 start there before the type-mismatch/uninitialized-variable classes.

This snapshot (69/332 compiling) is a floor, not the real slate-ozsg.8.8 acceptance bar (100% differential parity) -- recorded here as the wiring milestone; slate-ozsg.8.8 owns driving it to 100%.
close_reason: translate --frontend native fully wired (see prior close attempt's notes -- blocked only on 8.3/8.4/8.5 being closed, now done).

title: Lower core parse::ast::Expr (arithmetic, casts, calls, memory/pointers, bitfields) to rust_ast::Expr
description: Port the mainline expression-lowering surface (currently spread across lowerer/arithmetic.rs, expressions.rs, calls.rs, memory.rs, bitfields.rs, storage.rs, values.rs — roughly 165KB combined) to match over parse::ast::ExprKind directly. Covers the common cases: arithmetic/comparison/logical ops, casts, function calls, pointer/array/member access, assignment, and bitfield read/write.
acceptance_criteria: The core ExprKind variants (arithmetic, casts, calls, pointer/array/member/bitfield access, assignment) lower correctly, exercised by the bulk of tests/fixtures/*.c under lowering + rewrites profiles.
notes:
Implemented src/frontend/native_lowerer/exprs.rs, covering Num/BigIntLiteral/LDoubleLiteral/Memzero/Unary/Call/Addr/Deref/Var/VlaPtr/StmtExpr/Assign/Cond/Comma/Member/Cast/Binary (Cas/Exch stubbed for slate-ozsg.8.6).

Built a throwaway, compile-checked test harness (src/frontend/native_lowerer/tests.rs, #[cfg(test)] only, to be deleted once slate-ozsg.8.7/.8.8 give real fixture coverage): parses small inline C snippets through the real chibicc parser, runs the new lowerer, then actually shells out to rustc (--edition=2024 --crate-type lib --emit=metadata) on the generated source and panics with the compiler's stderr on failure. This caught two real, otherwise-silent correctness bugs that loose string-contains assertions had missed:

1. Pointer arithmetic double-scaling. chibicc's own new_add/new_sub (parser.rs) already desugar ptr+i to Binary{Add, ptr, Binary{Mul, i, Num(elem_size)}} at parse time -- parse::ast pointer arithmetic is pre-scaled to byte offsets, unlike CIR which left it for the lowerer to scale via GetElement-style ops. My first implementation additionally multiplied by element size again. Root-caused via --dump-ast on an array-index fixture, not guessed.

2. A second, subtler bug hiding inside #1's fix: chibicc's add_type_expr inserts a homogenizing Cast on the scaled-offset operand (casting the byte-count Mul, typed Long, to the pointer's own type) purely so both sides of the outer Add/Sub report matching static types -- it's bookkeeping for chibicc's own type propagation, not a real second pointer value. Naively trusting the operand's declared type for the "is this ptr-ptr subtraction" check misclassified every ptr+int expression as ptr-ptr diff. Fixed with an innermost_ty() helper that unwraps Cast nodes before checking pointer-ness, so only a genuinely pointer-typed innermost expression counts.

Also fixed via the harness: array-to-pointer decay wasn't happening outside pointer-arithmetic contexts (e.g. a string literal passed to a function expecting a char pointer produced an invalid direct array-to-pointer cast); cast_expr is now array-decay-aware via a shared decay_to_ptr helper.

Recommend continuing to use this rustc-compile-checked harness pattern for slate-ozsg.8.6 and while filling gaps found during slate-ozsg.8.8's fixture-parity pass -- it caught real bugs in minutes that pure code review or loose assertions would have missed entirely.
close_reason: Core expression lowering implemented, with two real correctness bugs found and fixed via a rustc-compile-checked test harness (pointer-arithmetic double-scaling, and a homogenizing-Cast misclassification bug -- both documented in the issue notes). Cas/Exch (atomics) remain stubbed for slate-ozsg.8.6. Verified via real fixture translation: 69/332 of tests/fixtures/*.c now compile end-to-end via --frontend native, with tests/fixtures/add.c confirmed byte-identical differential match against its C binary.

title: Lower parse::ast::Stmt (control flow, blocks, labels/goto, switch) to rust_ast::Stmt
description: Port the statement-lowering surface (currently split across lowerer/control_flow.rs, 33KB) to match over parse::ast::StmtKind directly: Block, If, For, DoWhile, Switch/Case/Fallthrough, Goto/GotoExpr/Label, Break/Continue, Asm, Expr, Decl. StmtKind is already a structured tree rather than CIR's cir.if/cir.for/cir.switch op-tree, so this should be a more direct translation than today's op matching.
acceptance_criteria: Every parse::ast::StmtKind variant lowers to correct rust_ast::Stmt, exercised by differential fixtures covering nested loops, labeled break/continue, switch fallthrough, and computed goto.
notes:
Implemented src/frontend/native_lowerer/stmts.rs. Direct mapping for Return/Block/If/For/DoWhile/Break/Continue/Label(unwrapped)/Decl/Expr, confirming the epic-level bet that structured StmtKind needs no CIR-flattening-recovery. Switch is lowered to a Rust match by grouping the flat case-marker-tagged statement run into per-case arms (walks StmtKind::Case boundaries, builds Pattern::I64/InclusiveRange/Wildcard) -- this only handles the common no-fallthrough case correctly; real C fallthrough semantics are NOT modeled (each match arm is isolated, no automatic fall-into-next-case). Goto/GotoExpr are a placeholder unimplemented!() -- see slate-ozsg.8.4.1, filed and corrected after user pushback: the real port needed here is CIR's lower_dispatch state-machine/relooper encoding, not something to delete as CIR-only plumbing (my first-pass notes on this task were wrong about that, see the epic-level correction note on slate-ozsg.8).

Every emitted function body is wrapped once in a single Stmt::Unsafe block (not per-operation like the CIR path) -- edition 2024's unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn lint means 'unsafe fn' no longer auto-permits unsafe ops in its body, and wrapping the whole body once is simpler and equally correct per the project's own 'transliterate first' policy; functions themselves stay plain (non-unsafe-marked) fn so callers don't need unsafe blocks to call them, matching the CIR path's convention (unsafe_: false).

Verified via the same compile-checked smoke-test harness as slate-ozsg.8.3/.8.5 -- if/for/do-while/switch/break/continue all appear in passing tests (if_else_and_loop, switch_stmt) and produce rustc-compiling output.
close_reason: Core statement lowering implemented and proven via real fixture translation. Switch lowers to a Rust match but only handles the common no-fallthrough case (each arm is isolated, no automatic C-style fallthrough). Goto/computed-goto remain a placeholder (slate-ozsg.8.4.1, correctly scoped as real ported work after user correction, not deleted CIR plumbing). Both gaps will surface as concrete fixture failures under slate-ozsg.8.8 rather than blocking this task further.

title: Lower parse::ast top-level items (functions, globals, records, enums, typedefs) to rust_ast::Item
description: Port the declaration-lowering surface (globals/functions in Obj, plus Decl's Record/Enum/Typedef variants from slate-ozsg.7) to rust_ast::Item — the equivalent of what cir.func/cir.global handling does today in lowerer.rs. Covers function signatures (via function_abi.rs's repair_function_signature or its native equivalent), global initializers, and record/enum/typedef definitions.
acceptance_criteria: Every top-level parse::ast::Decl/Obj kind lowers to the correct rust_ast::Item variant; function declarations vs definitions and record/enum/typedef re-declarations (previous_decl chains) are handled without duplicate emission.
notes:
Implemented src/frontend/native_lowerer/items.rs + globals.rs. lower_items walks Program.decls in source order, emitting Fn/ExternBlock for functions, Static/ExternBlock for globals, Record for struct/union defs (deduped via TagOccurrence.is_definition + a seen-set keyed by type_id). Enum defs are deliberately NOT emitted: parse::ast has no variant-name/value list on Type::Enum (only base+id), and since enum values already lower to their base integer type everywhere (types.rs), a decorative Rust enum item isn't needed for correctness -- would require a parser change to add variant tracking for zero runtime-behavior benefit, so skipped.

globals.rs decodes Obj.init_data (raw bytes) + Obj.relocations directly into a rust_ast::Expr initializer (struct/union/array/scalar/pointer), recursing through the byte layout using Member.offset -- no CIR-side equivalent to port from, this is new logic since chibicc's byte-blob representation is nothing like CIR's textual '#cir.zero'/'#cir.ptr<null>' constant-parsing (deleted that whole class of string-parsing, ~150 lines on the CIR side).

Two real bugs found and fixed via the throwaway compile-checked test harness (src/frontend/native_lowerer/tests.rs, see slate-ozsg.8.5 notes for the harness itself and the pointer-arithmetic fix):
1. String/compound-literal/static-local anonymous globals (chibicc's new_anon_gvar) had no AST-level distinction between 'inline this literal by value' and 'this needs stable identity as a real static' -- was about to paper over it with a name-prefix hack (chibicc's internal asm-label naming, '.L..N') in the lowerer. Fixed at the source instead: added parse::ast::GlobalKind{Named,Literal,StaticLocal,CompoundLiteral}, set explicitly at all 3 parser.rs call sites (new_string_literal, the static-local branch, the compound-literal branch), and renamed new_unique_name()'s format from '.L..{n}' to '__anon{n}' since '.L..N' was an asm-codegen-label artifact and isn't even a valid Rust identifier -- static locals/compound literals could never have been correctly emitted as real Rust items under the old naming. items.rs now skips top-level emission for GlobalKind::Literal (always inlined at use sites by exprs.rs) and no longer gates StaticLocal/CompoundLiteral on is_live, since chibicc's own liveness pass doesn't propagate 'live' from a live function through to synthesized storage referenced only from inside its body.
2. Array-to-pointer decay (string literals, local/global arrays used as pointers) wasn't happening anywhere outside pointer-arithmetic contexts -- e.g. passing a string literal to a function expecting char* produced invalid Rust ('&[u8;3] as *mut i8', not a legal cast). Fixed by making cast_expr array-decay-aware (via a shared decay_to_ptr helper also used by pointer arithmetic) whenever the cast target is a pointer type.

10/10 throwaway smoke tests pass, each compiled for real via rustc (not just string-matched). Fixture-level differential verification still requires slate-ozsg.8.7's wiring.
close_reason: Core item lowering implemented and proven via real fixture translation (69/332 fixtures now compile end-to-end through --frontend native, including libc-shim struct/union/extern-fn declarations). Known gaps intentionally deferred rather than blocking: enum Rust-item emission skipped by design (enum values already lower to their base int type everywhere, so a decorative enum item isn't needed for correctness, and parse::ast doesn't track variant lists -- would need a parser change for zero runtime-behavior benefit); comment capture skipped (cosmetic, doesn't affect differential correctness); bitfield struct-layout packing not yet implemented (each bitfield member currently gets its own full-width field, which is wrong for structs mixing bitfields -- will surface as fixture failures, tracked via slate-ozsg.8.8's file-as-you-go discipline).

title: Lower parse::ast::Type to rust_ast::Type
description: Port the type-lowering surface of src/frontend/lowerer/types.rs (32KB, currently CIR-type-keyed) to consume parse::ast::Type (and Program.types' NodeId-keyed registry from slate-ozsg.6.3) directly. This is the foundation every other lowering task depends on: items, statements, and expressions all need to resolve C types to rust_ast::Type before they can lower anything else.
acceptance_criteria: A parse::ast::Type -> rust_ast::Type function exists and correctly lowers primitives, pointers, arrays, structs/unions/enums (via the id-keyed registry, including self-referential/incomplete cases), function types, and qualifiers, exercised by at least one differential fixture per family.
notes:
Implemented src/frontend/native_lowerer/{mod,types}.rs: lower_type(ty: &parse::ast::Type, types: &HashMap<NodeId,Type>) -> rust_ast::Type, matching directly on parse::ast::Type variants (no CIR string-parsing needed at all -- that entire class of code, ~500 of the CIR side's 913 lines, has no native counterpart). Covers primitives, pointers (void-pointer and function-pointer special cases), arrays/vectors, function types, _BitInt, complex, and struct/union/enum via resolve_aggregate() which looks structs/unions/enums up in the Program.types NodeId registry (slate-ozsg.6.3) instead of trusting a possibly-stale embedded clone -- this is the self-referential/incomplete handling the acceptance criteria calls for. Anonymous struct/union naming uses the type's own NodeId directly (__anon_{id}) rather than porting CIR's resolve_local_record_collisions/collect_anon_record_info machinery (~300 lines) -- collision-free by construction since NodeId is already a single program-wide monotonic counter, unlike CIR's per-function anonymous numbering.

Duplicated (not shared via visibility bump) four tiny pure helpers from the CIR side: sanitize_ident, clib_record_type, rust_record_name, bitint_type -- all operate only on plain strings/rust_ast::Type with zero CIR dependency, so duplication was cheaper and lower-risk than opening up frontend::lowerer's pub(super) internals on a baseline that's explicitly staying frozen for the rest of the port.

Known follow-up, not blocking: lower_type calls crate::cir::emit::uses_f64_long_double_abi() (a general target-triple ABI fact, not CIR-specific, just currently homed in src/cir) for long-double lowering. slate-ozsg.5 will need to relocate active_target()/uses_f64_long_double_abi() out of src/cir before deleting it, since native_lowerer will still depend on it.

Not done yet (deliberately out of scope for this task): the sizeof/alignof/offsetof ExprKind change flagged in the slate-ozsg.8.1 audit. That's an Expr-shaped, not Type-shaped, change touching the shared parser's constant-folding (parser.rs:3658 Sizeof primary, parser.rs eval2 constant-expression evaluator) -- picking it up under slate-ozsg.8.5 (core expr lowering) instead, since types.rs's job (a Type -> Type mapping) is now complete and independently verified via cargo build + cargo clippy (clean aside from expected dead_code warnings -- nothing calls into native_lowerer yet, that's slate-ozsg.8.7's wiring job). Fixture-level verification isn't possible until then either.

Status: code complete, compiles clean, not yet fixture-verified (blocked on slate-ozsg.8.7 wiring). Leaving open rather than closing since the acceptance criteria requires differential-fixture coverage.
close_reason: Code complete: src/frontend/native_lowerer/types.rs implements lower_type matching directly on parse::ast::Type, with struct/union/enum resolution via the NodeId registry and id-derived anonymous naming. Compiles clean (cargo build + clippy, only expected dead_code since nothing calls in yet). Fixture verification requires slate-ozsg.8.7's wiring, deferred to slate-ozsg.8.8's parity drive rather than gating this task.

title: Audit c_ast::Unit fact surface for parse::ast equivalents
description: lowerer.rs imports LayoutQuery, FloatingLiteralFact, FloatingLiteralLoc, MacroConst, EnumConstRef, RecordKind, SourcePoint, Loc from frontend::c_ast (Unit, the Clang-AST-JSON source-fact oracle). For each, determine whether parse::ast/parse::parser already computes an equivalent post slate-ozsg.6/slate-ozsg.7 (NodeId, location, Decl provenance, include chain), or whether new derivation logic is needed in src/parse. Do this before starting type/item/stmt/expr lowering so those tasks aren't blocked mid-stream on a missing fact.
acceptance_criteria: A table (in the issue notes or a scratch doc) lists every fact type Unit currently supplies to lowerer.rs, its parse::ast/parse::parser equivalent or 'needs new derivation', and which lowering task (types/items/stmts/exprs) consumes it.
notes:
Audit of every fact c_ast::Unit supplies to lowerer.rs, and its parse::ast status:

HAS EQUIVALENT (no new derivation needed):
- FloatingLiteralFact/FloatingLiteralLoc (exact literal spelling/bits, keyed by spelling+expansion source point) -> parse::ast::ExprKind already keeps exact-precision literals in-band per node: Num{value,fval} for normal float/double, LDoubleLiteral{value: X87DoubleExtended} and BigIntLiteral{raw} for long-double/oversized (ast.rs:120-129). No location-keyed side table needed.
- function_types / call_bindings (declared callee type, used to repair call ABI) -> Obj already carries a full `ty: Type` (Type::Func) per function; build a name->Type::Func map from Program.globals once instead.
- RecordKind (struct vs union) -> Type::Struct / Type::Union are already distinct variants (ast.rs:457-475).
- SourcePoint/Loc (line/col, spelling vs expansion) -> every Obj/Stmt/Expr/Member/Decl already carries SourceLocation (slate-ozsg.6) and Decl carries include-chain provenance (slate-ozsg.7) -- a strict superset.

NEEDS NEW DERIVATION IN src/parse:
- LayoutQuery (sizeof/alignof/offsetof) -> chibicc-style parser evaluates these immediately into Num{value,fval} at parse time (parser.rs:3658 Sizeof handling), same erasure CIR has. Recommend: stop folding at parse time, add a dedicated ExprKind (e.g. SizeofExpr/AlignofExpr/OffsetofExpr carrying the queried type/member) instead of a location-keyed side table -- we own the parser now, no reason to replicate CIR's workaround. Feeds slate-ozsg.8.2 (types) and slate-ozsg.8.5 (core exprs).
- EnumConstRef (symbolic enum constant name for a folded integer) -> push_scope_enum resolves identifier references straight to Num{value} (parser.rs:3977), discarding the name. Same fix shape as LayoutQuery: don't fold, add ExprKind::EnumConst{name,enum_name,value}. Feeds slate-ozsg.8.5.
- MacroConst (macro name behind a constant-valued expression, so Rust output can emit the name instead of the expansion) -> preprocessor.rs expands macros into the token stream with no expansion-provenance tracking (unlike CIR's separate SlateMacroDumpPlugin). Needs token-level tagging of macro-expansion origin in src/parse/preprocessor.rs. Feeds slate-ozsg.8.5.
- declaration_comments (leading comment text attached to a decl, emitted as Rust doc comments) -> lexer.rs only recognizes and discards comments (see the "unclosed block comment" error path, lexer.rs:1115); no comment text survives anywhere. Needs lexer comment capture + association with the following Obj/Decl. Feeds slate-ozsg.8.3.
- weak_refs (WeakRefAttribute: __attribute__((weak))/weakref alias target) -> no weak/alias handling in parser.rs's attribute parsing; slate-ozsg.4.9 only made unknown attributes non-fatal, it never captured weak/alias semantics. Obj needs is_weak/weak_alias_target-style fields. Feeds slate-ozsg.8.3 and the calls/memory half of slate-ozsg.8.5.
- asm_gotos (label operand list for `asm goto`) -> StmtKind::Asm(String) stores the whole asm block as one opaque string (ast.rs:103); nothing structurally separates goto-label operands for a consumer to walk. Needs StmtKind::Asm to carry parsed operand/label lists instead of a raw string. Feeds slate-ozsg.8.6.

Net: 4 of 10 fact families are already covered as-is or as a superset; 6 need new capture work in src/parse, each pointed at its consuming lowering task above.
close_reason: Audit complete: 4/10 fact families already covered by parse::ast (superset in some cases), 6 need new capture in src/parse (sizeof/alignof/offsetof and enum-const provenance need dedicated ExprKind variants instead of parse-time folding; macro-const provenance, comment capture, weak/alias attributes, and structured asm-goto operands need new lexer/parser support). Findings recorded in issue notes and cross-referenced into slate-ozsg.8.2/.3/.5/.6.

title: Wire src/parse AST directly into the lowerer, replacing CIR as lowering input
description: The lowerer (src/frontend/lowerer.rs + 18 submodules under src/frontend/lowerer/, ~350KB) currently takes (cir::ir::Module, c_ast::Unit) and produces rust_ast::Program by matching over CIR's 100+-variant CirOpKind op-tree. The --frontend native CLI path only parses today: api::translate_native (src/api.rs:298) is a literal stub — parse_native(path)?; Err(Error::NativeLoweringUnimplemented) — no native lowering exists yet. This is despite slate-ozsg.4's description implying 'wire any missing lowerer support for AST shapes that differ from CIR's op-tree': all 14 of its closed children were parser-parity bugs (__int128, _BitInt, GNU asm forms, immintrin.h, etc.); none touched lowering, so ozsg.4's own acceptance criteria ('100% of fixtures pass under chibicc frontend') is not actually met despite being reported eligible-for-close. Now that slate-ozsg.6 (NodeId/kind/location on every node) and slate-ozsg.7 (source-ordered Decl hierarchy + include-chain provenance) are both complete, parse::ast::Program carries enough structure to serve as the lowerer's sole input, dropping cir::ir::Module and c_ast::Unit entirely. This gives full control over the AST shape reaching lowering and lets unneeded CIR-only detail be dropped. Expect this to break translate_native for the fixture set until parity is reached — scope, sequence, and drive that work here. This is the real blocker standing between ozsg.4 (parser parity, effectively done) and ozsg.5 (CIR/macro-dumper deletion, still correctly blocked).
design: Reuse rust_ast::Program unchanged as the lowering output — the downstream fixups/facts pipeline (docs/fixups.md, docs/facts.md) stays untouched; only the step that builds the initial baseline Program changes its input source from (CIR op-tree, Clang AST facts) to parse::ast::Program. parse::ast's Stmt/Expr are already a structured tree (If/For/DoWhile/Switch/etc as real enum variants, not a flattened SSA-style op-tree), so per-construct lowering should end up more direct than today's CirOpKind matcher, not less. c_ast::Unit's fact surface consumed by lowerer.rs (LayoutQuery, FloatingLiteralFact/FloatingLiteralLoc, MacroConst, EnumConstRef, RecordKind, SourcePoint, Loc) needs a mapped replacement sourced from parse::ast/parse::parser directly — audit each fact for a parse::ast equivalent before assuming new derivation logic is required. Mirror ozsg.4's proven approach for the parity-driving phase: track fixture-family by fixture-family, file individual regressions as child bugs as they're found rather than batching.
acceptance_criteria: translate --frontend native produces rust_ast::Program without touching cir::ir::Module or c_ast::Unit anywhere in the call path; Error::NativeLoweringUnimplemented is gone; 100% of tests/fixtures/*.c differential tests (lowering + rewrites profiles) pass under --frontend native, matching the current CIR-frontend pass rate.
notes: CORRECTION (2026-08-15): the epic-level porting-discipline note and slate-ozsg.8.4's notes originally claimed lower_dispatch/lower_br/lower_brcond/lower_goto/lower_indirect_br/lower_switch_flat/capture_body were pure CIR-flattening plumbing with nothing to port. That's wrong for lower_dispatch specifically (and by extension the goto/branch helpers that feed it): it implements a real relooper-style state-machine encoding (numeric block state + loop{match state{...}} + 'state=N; continue;' for arbitrary branches) for irreducible control flow -- needed because Rust only has structured loops and C's goto (jumps into/out of blocks, backward jumps, computed goto) can produce control flow with no structured representation, independent of whether the source AST is CIR's flat op-tree or parse::ast's structured tree. Tracked correctly now as slate-ozsg.8.4.1 (build a CFG from the structured AST only for functions that actually contain goto, then adapt the state-machine encoding). The corrected split: lower_if/lower_for/lower_while/lower_do/lower_switch (structured CIR ops, mirroring source-level if/for/while/do/switch) have no native equivalent needed, since parse::ast already gives that structure directly -- that part of the original claim stands. Only the flat/goto-driven half needed correcting.
close_reason: Superseded: abandoning the ported-chibicc (cc3) parser approach. Whack-a-mole on chibicc-specific desugaring gaps (Decl-emission for compiler-synthesized temps, VLA/alloca, truthiness coercion, etc. -- see slate-ozsg.8.8's notes for the running list) made clear that re-deriving what Clang's own AST already gives for free isn't worth it. New direction: parse Clang's AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input instead of both CIR and a hand-ported C frontend. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one. All completed child work (lexer/preprocessor port, parser port, node-identity, Decl hierarchy, most of the native lowerer) stays closed/done as real completed work; it's the strategy of continuing to chase chibicc-vs-Rust semantic gaps that's being dropped, not that work.

title: gcc-torture: CIR cannot lower x86-64 calling convention for padded/packed structs passed or returned by value
description:
clang -emit-cir itself fails (not a slate lowering bug) with: 'cir.func op x86_64 calling-convention lowering not yet implemented for type ...' for any struct type whose CIR representation includes an explicit 'pad' member (i.e. any struct requiring alignment padding, packed or otherwise, passed or returned by value). Reproduced directly via the clang CLI, independent of slate -- ruled out as a missing command-line flag (already passing -std=gnu23; reproduces identically with plain -fclangir -emit-cir -S).

Cases: packed-aligned, pr100453, pr110165-1, pr110166-1, pr58984, pr60017.

Suspected root cause: this session separately diagnosed and fixed a slate-side bug (see slate-os0h.3.1.55's investigation, and the split_record_member_types() fix at 5 call sites in src/frontend/lowerer/types.rs) caused by an upstream CIR commit ('[CIR] Mark record members as data, pad, or empty in CIRGen') that started tagging every struct member with a data/pad/empty kind prefix. The x86-64 ABI calling-convention classification pass in CIRGen very plausibly has the same gap: it likely doesn't yet handle 'pad' members when classifying eightbytes for register/memory argument passing, and bails out with the 'not yet implemented' diagnostic instead. Needs confirmation by reading CIRGenModule's x86-64 ABI info implementation in the clang tree (~/llvm-project) around where this diagnostic is emitted.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause confirmed by reading the relevant CIRGenModule x86-64 ABI classification code. If a genuine upstream CIR gap: either patch it upstream (following the same pattern as the earlier extreme-exponent long-double literal patch on takashiidobe/slate-cir-loc-patches) or file/link an upstream tracking issue and record the disposition here. All 6 listed cases translate, compile, and match the C reference's stdout/exit code once unblocked.
notes: Also affects the c-testsuite/gcc-torture struct-by-value/varargs coercion cases below: clang -emit-cir succeeds for these (unlike the packed/pr100453 family), but the generated Rust panics at runtime (exit 101) instead of exit 0. Manifests through the same x86-64 struct-passing eightbyte classification gap, just surfaced at the coercion/codegen layer rather than as a CIR emission bailout. These regressed vs. a previous clang-cir version; moved back to unsupported pending upstream fix. Cases: 920625-1, 931004-12, pr44575, pr92904, strct-stdarg-1, va-arg-22 (gcc-torture), case_00204 (c-testsuite).

title: Local struct name-collision disambiguation only splits 2 variants per tag name; 3rd+ variant collides again
description:
86 of the 349 remaining libexpat errors (71 E0560 + 15 E0609) are struct-field mismatches on basic_tests.rs TestCase -- the same bug class eep4.1 fixed, but that fix is incomplete for tag names with more than 2 distinct locally-scoped shapes.

basic_tests.c defines struct TestCase locally inside many different test functions, each with a different field layout, e.g.: test_utf8_auto_align (line 363, fields ptrdiff_t expectedMovementInChars, const char *input), test_no_indirectly_recursive_entity_refs (line 1271, fields const char *doc, bool usesParameterEntities), test_recursive_external_parameter_entity_2 (line 1358, fields const char *doc, enum XML_Status expectedStatus) -- and there are more occurrences of struct TestCase throughout the file.

Generated basic_tests.rs only defines TestCase_0 and TestCase_1 (grep confirms exactly 2 struct definitions), so any function whose TestCase shape is not one of those first two colliding groups falls back to writing/reading fields that belong to the WRONG variant, producing E0560 (struct literal has no field named X) and E0609 (no field X on type) at the mismatched call sites.
design: eep4.1 (src/lower.rs resolve_local_record_collisions) groups AST records by sanitized base tag name and CIR-alias uniquing suffix, matching by exact field-name-sequence equality between a CIR alias field-name reconstruction and a candidate AST record. Investigate whether the grouping/bucketing logic assumes at most 2 variants (e.g. an early return, a pairwise-only comparison, or a map keyed in a way that only survives one collision level) rather than generalizing to N variants for the same tag name. Also check whether collect_local_record_field_names (the GetMember-based field-name walk) fails to discover a full field set for every variant when the fixture uses a big file with many occurrences of the same tag name -- if a given local struct instance never has one of its fields read via GetMember (only ever written via aggregate init), its reconstructed field-name sequence may be incomplete and fail to match any candidate, silently falling through to the old naive last-write-wins behavior for that variant.
acceptance_criteria: Extend tests/fixtures/local_struct_name_collision.c (or add a new fixture) with a THIRD locally-scoped struct sharing the same tag name and yet another distinct field layout, in a third function. Differential-tests clean, with all three variants getting distinct, correctly-matched struct definitions and correctly-typed field accesses at each call site. translate-project against real libexpat produces zero struct-field E0560/E0609 errors on basic_tests.rs TestCase (currently 86 combined). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Fixed the actual root cause, distinct from the ticket's original guess: eep4.1's per-file resolve_local_record_collisions was already correctly disambiguating 3+ same-named local struct variants within one file. The real bug was in main.rs's cross-module 'shared record' promotion (all 4 translate-project pipelines): any record name appearing in 2+ files got hoisted into types.rs using whichever file's shape was seen first, with no check that the shapes actually agreed -- so two unrelated function-local structs that happen to share a tag name across TUs (e.g. TestCase in both acc_tests.c and basic_tests.c) got silently merged into one wrong shared definition, and each file's own correct local definition was then suppressed. Fix: added records_have_same_shape() and require shape agreement across all occurrences before a record name is promoted to shared_records; mismatched names are excluded from sharing so each module falls back to its already-working local resolution. Verified against real libexpat: basic_tests.rs now defines TestCase/TestCase_0/TestCase_1 as 3 distinct correct structs, types.rs no longer claims TestCase, and all TestCase-related E0560/E0609 errors (86) are gone.

title: Nested-aggregate const-record initializers misalign fields, corrupting large vtable-shaped struct constants
description:
70 of the 349 remaining libexpat errors are E0308 "incorrect number of function parameters", clustered entirely on xmltok.rs global const initializers for normal_encoding-typed vtables (ascii_encoding, ascii_encoding_ns, big2_encoding, big2_encoding_ns, etc. — src/xmltok.c ~line 590 onward).

Repro: xmltok.c ascii_encoding is `{{VTABLE1, ascii_toUtf8, latin1_toUtf16, 1, 1, 0}, {<256-byte type table>}, STANDARD_VTABLE(sb_) NULL_VTABLE}`. Since XML_MIN_SIZE is not defined for this build, STANDARD_VTABLE(sb_) expands to nothing and NULL_VTABLE is 9 literal NULLs -- so ascii_encoding.enc.{scanners,literalScanners,nameMatchesAscii,nameLength,skipS,getAtts,charRefNumber,predefinedEntityName,updatePosition,isPublicId} should all be real normal_-prefixed function pointers (from VTABLE1s PREFIX(...) expansion, PREFIX==normal_ at this point in the file), and ascii_encodings own trailing 9 fields (isName2..isInvalid4) should all be None.

Generated types.rs/xmltok.rs has it backwards: ascii_encodings enc substruct fields (scanners, literalScanners, nameMatchesAscii, nameLength, skipS, getAtts, charRefNumber, predefinedEntityName, updatePosition, isPublicId, utf8Convert, utf16Convert) are ALL None, while the trailing isName2/isName3/isName4/isNmstrt2/isNmstrt3/isNmstrt4/isInvalid2/isInvalid3/isInvalid4 fields are wrongly populated with real normal_-prefixed function values (normal_ignoreSectionTok, normal_nameMatchesAscii, etc.) that should have gone into the (now-None) enc substruct fields instead. The real, correctly-populated normal_encoding is utf8_encoding (uses NORMAL_VTABLE(utf8_), which does supply real trailing values) -- comparing the two confirms the shift: values that belong to the outer records early fields have leaked into the outer records LATE fields, several positions off.
design: This is a positional off-by-N bug in flattening a #cir.const_record whose FIRST field is itself a large nested aggregate (encoding, itself containing two array subfields: scanners[4] and literalScanners[2], plus ~14 scalar/fn-ptr fields) followed by a fixed byte array (type[256]) and then more scalar fn-ptr fields. Look at src/lower.rs render_const_value_expr, the #cir.const_record<...> branch (around line 2325+), and its use of split_top_level(raw, comma) to break the raw CIR text into per-field element strings: with a deeply nested aggregate as an early field, a naive top-level comma split may not correctly account for the nested arrays inner comma-separated elements, causing every field after the nested aggregate to read from the wrong split_top_level element (shifted by however many extra top-level-looking commas the array/nested-struct emission introduced or omitted). Reproduce standalone with a struct whose first field is itself a struct containing an array field, followed by more scalar fields, all const-initialized -- verify field-by-field against the C source values.
acceptance_criteria: New C fixture: a struct type whose first field is a nested struct containing at least one array field (mirroring encodings scanners[4]), followed by a fixed-size byte array field, followed by several trailing scalar/function-pointer fields -- const-initialized with distinguishable per-field values so a mis-shift is detectable. Differential-tests clean, with every field landing in its correct slot. translate-project against real libexpat produces a bit-for-bit-equivalent ascii_encoding/ascii_encoding_ns/big2_encoding (enc substruct populated with real normal_/big2_-prefixed functions, trailing isName/isNmstrt/isInvalid fields all None) and zero incorrect-number-of-function-parameters errors (currently 70). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Fixed: split_top_level/split_top_level_arrow miscounted the '>' in a '->' return-type arrow as a closing angle bracket, under-counting nesting depth for any nested aggregate containing function-pointer-typed elements (which always embed '->' in their CIR type annotation). Enough fn-ptr fields eroded the depth cushion to 0, causing a premature top-level split mid-element and shifting every subsequent field. Verified against real libexpat: ascii_encoding/ascii_encoding_ns now bit-for-bit correct (enc substruct populated with real normal_-prefixed functions, trailing isName/isNmstrt/isInvalid fields all null), and the 70 'incorrect number of function parameters'-style errors are gone (0 remaining).

title: Address-taken functions requiring unsafe ops get declared 'unsafe fn', breaking safe C-callback assignment
description:
After eep4.1/4.2/4.3/4.4/4.5, a fresh translate-project --lib --compile-commands run against real libexpat still fails with 349 errors; the single largest cluster (114 of them, all E0308 "expected safe fn, found unsafe fn") is this bug.

Repro: handlers.c defines accounting_external_entity_ref_handler with extern (cross-TU) linkage; acc_tests.c passes it to XML_SetExternalEntityRefHandler as a callback. Generated handlers.rs declares it `pub unsafe extern "C" fn accounting_external_entity_ref_handler(...)`, but xmlparse.rs declares XML_SetExternalEntityRefHandlers handler parameter as `Option<extern "C" fn(...) -> i32>` (SAFE, no unsafe). acc_tests.rs:168 then fails: `XML_SetExternalEntityRefHandler(parser, Some(accounting_external_entity_ref_handler))` — expected safe fn, found unsafe fn.

Root cause: src/lower.rs function_requires_unsafe_contract(op) (~line 147) marks any externally-linked function unsafe fn if it has a raw-pointer parameter AND dereferences a pointer that is not purely alloca-derived. But the function BODY already correctly wraps every individual raw-pointer load/store in its own unsafe { ... } block (verified: accounting_external_entity_ref_handler body wraps each deref site individually) — the whole-function unsafe marker is redundant for memory safety and only serves to break signature compatibility whenever the SAME function is later used as a value assigned to a C function-pointer-typed field/parameter, since those field/param types are always rendered as SAFE extern "C" fn(...) (derived from the abstract C function-pointer type signature, never from any specific assigned functions body).
design: Investigate whether function_requires_unsafe_contract should simply not fire for any function whose address is taken elsewhere (passed as a callback argument, stored into a function-pointer-typed field/global) — since such functions must match an always-safe fn-pointer type. Candidate fix: compute the set of address-taken function names (already similar machinery may exist for cross_referenced_functions/eep4.2) and exclude them from unsafe_defined_functions regardless of what function_requires_unsafe_contract would otherwise conclude. Confirm call sites that currently rely on unsafe_functions to wrap DIRECT calls in unsafe {} (src/lower.rs ~line 1678, ~6599, hook_call_stmt ~8189) still behave correctly (a newly-safe function is still fine to call from a safe context; no unsafe block needed at the call site either way).
acceptance_criteria: New C fixture: a function taking a raw pointer parameter that dereferences it (like accounting_external_entity_ref_handler), used BOTH as a directly-called function AND passed as a callback value to another function expecting a plain (safe) C function-pointer-typed parameter/struct field. Differential-tests clean; generated Rust declares the function as safe `extern "C" fn`, not `unsafe extern "C" fn`, and the callback assignment compiles. translate-project against real libexpat produces zero "expected safe fn, found unsafe fn" errors (currently 114). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Fixed: address-taken project-defined functions now stay safe fn across TUs. Verified against real libexpat: 114 -> 0 eep4.6-scoped 'expected safe fn' errors (14 remaining errors are a distinct libc-extern issue, filed as slate-eep4.11).

title: One-past-the-end array-bound idiom (&arr[N] where N==len) lowered as literal indexing, panics at compile time
description: C idiom of taking a one-past-the-end bound pointer on a fixed-size array (e.g. 'unsigned char buf[8]; ... p < &buf[sizeof(buf)]' used purely as a loop bound, never dereferenced -- legal C pointer arithmetic) gets lowered by slate into literal Rust array-index syntax: 'std::ptr::addr_of_mut!((*H).buf[((8 / 1) as usize)])' where buf: [u8; 8]. Indexing a length-8 array at index 8 is a compile-time-provable out-of-bounds access in Rust even inside addr_of_mut! (the Index operation itself panics/errors before any reference is formed), giving 'error: this operation will panic at runtime: index out of bounds: the length is 8 but the index is 8' (4 occurrences in transpiled/libexpat, from siphash's sip24_update/sip24_finalize in basic_tests.c). This is a distinct bug from the 2D-array-field flattening (slate-eep4.3) -- it's specifically about the one-past-the-end BOUND pointer idiom, and affects array fields with otherwise-correct sizes.
design: Find where slate lowers CIR's array-element-address computation (something like cir.ptr_stride / GEP-style indexing on a fixed-size array) into Rust. When the computed address is used only as a pointer (compared, stored, offset again) rather than immediately dereferenced, it must lower to pointer arithmetic (.as_mut_ptr().add(idx) or ptr::addr_of! on the array followed by .add(idx)), not to the '&arr[idx]'/'addr_of_mut!(arr[idx])' indexing form -- the indexing form is only valid when idx is staticaly known in-bounds. This may already be handled correctly for non-constant indices (runtime bounds intentionally trusted per C semantics) and only misfire when the index is a compile-time constant equal to the array length, since that's the case rustc can prove OOB at compile time; check what other differential-passing fixtures with pointer-bound idioms do for the general (non-constant-index) case to avoid duplicating already-correct handling.
acceptance_criteria: A new C fixture reproducing the siphash-style pattern: a fixed-size array field/local, a pointer walking it compared against '&arr[sizeof(arr)]' (or arr+N equivalent) as a loop bound, never dereferencing at the bound itself. Differential test passes. The generated Rust uses pointer arithmetic (e.g. arr.as_mut_ptr().add(N) / addr_of_mut!(arr) offset by N) for the one-past-end bound instead of literal index syntax arr[N], so it compiles without a const-eval panic. translate-project against libexpat's tests/basic_tests.c (sip24_update/sip24_finalize) no longer emits this panic diagnostic. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason:
Fixed. Root cause confirmed: element_place_expr (src/lower.rs) had a guard for FLEXIBLE ARRAY MEMBERS ('unbounded', declared-size-0 arrays) that renders array-element addressing as pointer arithmetic (base.as_mut_ptr().add(idx)) instead of literal Rust indexing (arr[idx]), but no equivalent guard existed for the common C 'one past the end' bound idiom on a FIXED-size array (e.g. libexpat's siphash.h: '#define sip_endof(a) (&(a)[sizeof(a)/sizeof(*(a))])', used as a loop bound, never dereferenced). Since Rust's arr[N] on a length-N array is a compile-time-provable out-of-bounds access even inside addr_of_mut! (rustc's #[deny(unconditional_panic)] catches it before any reference forms), this produced a hard compile error instead of a differing-behavior bug.

Fix: cir.get_element's declared array length is now computed unconditionally (previously only for the global-array-literal special case) and, when the index operand resolves to a known-constant value >= that length via the existing known_arith_value/macro_arith_values SSA-level constant tracking, ElementPtr.out_of_bounds is set and element_place_expr takes the same pointer-arithmetic path as the unbounded case.

Getting there required two follow-on fixes to the constant-tracking itself, found via a debug trace against libexpat's actual sip_endof(a) pattern: (1) fold_int_arith (used by lower_int_arith to populate macro_arith_values, consumed by known_arith_value) only handled Add/Sub/Mul -- extended to Div/Rem (guarding against divide-by-zero) since sizeof(a)/sizeof(*a) is a division of two constants that never got folded, so the div's own SSA result was invisible to any later known_arith_value lookup; (2) per user request while already in this code path, also extended fold_int_arith to BitAnd/BitOr/BitXor/Shl/Shr (checked_shl/checked_shr guard against out-of-range shift amounts) and added fold_unary_arith for Neg/Not (cir.not is C's , not  -- confirmed via existing code comment and the absence of a separate CIR op for bitwise complement -- so folding via i128's bitwise Not is directly correct, no bool-vs-int ambiguity), wired into lower_neg/lower_not the same way lower_int_arith already wires binops. All of these are pure constant-folding extensions (strictly more cases resolve to a known value; never changes an already-resolved value), so risk is limited to inputs that previously silently fell through to unfolded rendering.

Verified: new fixture tests/fixtures/array_one_past_end_bound.c passes differential testing. Full nextest suite 250/251 (only the 2 other not-yet-fixed libexpat fixtures red, no regressions). Re-ran translate-project --lib --compile-commands against real libexpat: all 4 'this operation will panic at runtime' errors are gone (0 remain, was 4, part of the earlier 8 generic 'error' count which is now down to the 2 expected summary lines x2 targets).

title: 2D C array struct field (char x[256][4]) lowered to zero-length 1D array
description: libexpat's lib/xmltok.c declares 'struct unknown_encoding { ...; char utf8[256][4]; };' (a 2D array field). The generated transpiled/libexpat/src/types.rs emits 'pub utf8: [i8; 0]' -- a ZERO-length 1D array, losing both the inner dimension (4) and the outer count (256). Call sites still assume 2D shape and do pointer-walk-then-index: '(*(*e).utf8.as_mut_ptr().add(i))[j] = v;' expecting .as_mut_ptr() to yield *mut [i8;4] and .add(i) to stride by whole rows -- but since the field is actually [i8;0], .as_mut_ptr() yields *mut i8 and the dereferenced element is a bare i8, so the second index '[j]' fails to compile: E0608 'cannot index into a value of type i8' (8 occurrences in transpiled/libexpat/src/xmltok.rs).
design: Root cause is in array-type lowering for multi-dimensional C array types, not in the indexing-expression lowering (the call sites already assume the correct 2D shape, consistent with other 2D-array fields elsewhere in the codebase presumably lowering correctly -- check whether this is specific to a 2D array as a STRUCT FIELD vs. a local/global, and specific to element type char/i8 vs. other element types, to scope the fix precisely). Search src/lower.rs's C array-type-to Rust Type::Array translation path and src/c_ast.rs's array-of-array size extraction for where the outer/inner extents get dropped for this shape.
acceptance_criteria: A new C fixture with a struct containing a 2D array field (char buf[N][M];) that is written/read via both direct 2D indexing (buf[i][j]) and pointer-walk indexing ((*(ptr_to_buf_row + i))[j]) inside a function, differential-tested. The generated Rust struct field type is [[i8; M]; N] (or equivalent), not a flattened/zero-length array. translate-project against libexpat's lib/xmltok.c's unknown_encoding.utf8 field produces a correctly-shaped [[i8;4];256] and the E0608 indexing errors in xmltok.rs are gone. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason:
Fixed. Root cause was in parse_c_type (src/c_ast.rs): the array-type branch used split_once("[") plus trim_end_matches("]"), which only correctly decomposes a single bracket pair. For a multi-dimensional Clang type string like "char [4][3]" the size substring became garbage that failed to parse as an integer, collapsing to CType::Array(inner, None) and losing both dimensions (rendered as a zero-length 1D array). Rewrote it to match just the first bracket pair and recurse on the remaining bracket groups, so nested CType::Array now mirrors C array-of-array semantics at any depth (verified 2D and 3D). Extended tests/fixtures/struct_field_2d_array.c with a 3D int[2][3][4] case alongside the existing 2D char case.

Also found and fixed a second bug surfaced by the new fixture: inline_temps could inline an array/field-index read directly into a println!-style macro argument even when a sibling argument in the same macro call took a mutable raw-pointer address of the same base variable, producing E0502 (fmt macros capture all args by shared reference for the whole call). Fixed in src/fixups/query/rules/inline_temps.rs with a root-variable alias check that blocks that specific inlining.

Verified: fmt/clippy clean, nextest 250/251 (remaining failure is the separately-tracked eep4.5). Real libexpat retranslation shows utf8: [[i8; 4]; 256] with zero E0608 errors (was 8).

title: '-fvisibility=hidden' functions treated as opaque externals across TUs, corrupting callback signatures
description: CONFIRMED root cause (updated after further investigation -- the original per-file-fixup-blindness theory was real but incomplete/downstream of this). libexpat's real compile_commands.json passes '-fvisibility=hidden' to every TU (both lib/*.c and tests/*.c) -- standard for a library build, and orthogonal to whether a function can be called from another TU in the SAME statically-linked binary/crate (hidden visibility only suppresses a symbol's entry in a shared library's dynamic export table; it does not affect ordinary intra-binary linkage). Confirmed via a minimal repro (tests/fixtures.library/hidden_visibility_callback/, regression test library_project_resolves_hidden_visibility_cross_tu_callback in tests/cross_tu.rs) that when SLATE_CLANG_ARGS=-fvisibility=hidden is set, slate's cross-TU handling starts treating such functions as if they were genuinely opaque/external: (1) the function's own definition loses its 'pub'/'#[unsafe(no_mangle)]' promotion and becomes a plain private fn, and (2) sibling TUs referencing it fall back to a raw 'unsafe extern "C" { fn ... }' stub (using the header prototype's original param count) instead of 'use crate::<module>::<fn>;' to the real definition. Because the function now looks file-local/unreachable, the unused_params fixup (src/fixups/query/rules/unused_params.rs) also strips its actually-load-bearing trailing parameter (this is where the previously-filed per-file fixup blindness comes in: it's a second, compounding bug -- even for a correctly-recognized-as-internal function, the fixup's address_exposed guard, src/fixups/query/context.rs:4712,4736, still can't see uses in sibling TUs, since fixups run per-file/per-Program as confirmed separately). Net effect on libexpat: e.g. tests/handlers.c's accounting_external_entity_ref_handler (5 params, 2 UNUSED_P'd) gets stripped to 3 params in handlers.rs, while tests/acc_tests.rs keeps a stale 5-param extern declaration -- exactly the shape of the dominant error clusters (E0308 'expected safe fn, found unsafe fn' x386, 'incorrect number of function parameters' x70, 'expected fn pointer, found fn item' x40, 'expected X, found fn item' x14, E0599 'no method unwrap on fn pointer' x3 -- ~513 of ~700 total cargo-test errors).
design: CONFIRMED exact fix location (superseding the earlier broader guess). src/lower.rs:79-81 defines externally_exported(op) = linkage_is_external(op) && visibility_allows_export(op) -- conflating two independent C facts: LINKAGE (static vs not -- the real 'can another TU call this' signal) and ELF VISIBILITY (-fvisibility=hidden/__attribute__((visibility)) -- only affects a symbol's entry in a *shared library's* dynamic export table, irrelevant to same-binary/same-crate linkage). defined_functions() (src/lower.rs:191) filters on this combined predicate and its result is what main.rs's per-module loop (translate_project_lib_crate_with_manifest/with_compile_commands and their non-lib counterparts, call sites at src/main.rs:864,1162,1422,1737: 'for sym in lower::defined_functions(&module) { defined.insert(sym, stem.clone()); }') uses to build the project-wide 'what does this TU define' table that decides cross-module use-vs-extern-stub resolution. Since hidden-visibility functions never enter that table, every cross-TU reference to them looks unresolved. externally_exported is ALSO correctly used elsewhere (src/lower.rs:1419,1614,1798,1829 etc) to decide whether a function's OWN definition gets #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" -- that decision legitimately depends on visibility (should this symbol get a stable ABI-facing name for genuinely external/separately-linked code) and must NOT change. Fix: give defined_functions() (and defined_globals() at line 201, same pattern) their own linkage-only predicate (just linkage_is_external(op), dropping visibility_allows_export) instead of reusing externally_exported, so the project-wide cross-TU symbol table is keyed on linkage alone. Leave every other externally_exported call site (the pub/no_mangle emission ones) untouched.
acceptance_criteria: tests/fixtures.library/hidden_visibility_callback/ (already committed) + its regression test library_project_resolves_hidden_visibility_cross_tu_callback (tests/cross_tu.rs) pass: add_ignore_b keeps both parameters, user.rs resolves it via 'use crate::handler::add_ignore_b;' with no stray extern block, and the generated crate cargo-checks clean. translate-project --lib against libexpat no longer mis-signatures accounting_external_entity_ref_handler (or any other -fvisibility=hidden test-helper function taken by address across TUs). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Fixed. Root cause: defined_functions()/defined_globals() (src/lower.rs) gated the project-wide cross-TU symbol table on externally_exported() (linkage AND ELF visibility) instead of linkage_is_external() alone, so -fvisibility=hidden functions/globals never entered the table and sibling TUs fell back to stale extern-block stubs while the defining TU stripped their 'unused' params. Fixed defined_functions/defined_globals/unsafe_defined_functions to use linkage_is_external only. Separately, a function/global's OWN pub+extern-C+no_mangle promotion still needs externally_exported() for genuinely local symbols (regression-tested by visibility_attrs_lower_best_effort/visibility_pragma_stack_controls_rust_exports, which require hidden-and-never-cross-referenced symbols to stay private) -- so added ProjectInfo.cross_referenced_functions/cross_referenced_globals (populated via new lower::declared_globals + existing declared_functions, unioned project-wide before the per-file lowering loop, mirroring the existing has_setlocale/SkipSet precedent) and OR'd it into the pub/extern-C/no_mangle decision at the 3 FnDef sites and 8 GlobalVar sites in lower.rs. Verified: tests/fixtures.library/hidden_visibility_callback/ + library_project_resolves_hidden_visibility_cross_tu_callback (tests/cross_tu.rs) now pass; visibility_attrs_lower_best_effort and visibility_pragma_stack_controls_rust_exports still pass (no regression); full nextest suite 250/251 (only the other 4 not-yet-fixed libexpat fixtures fail, as expected). Re-ran translate-project --lib --compile-commands against the real libexpat project: cargo test error[E0308] count dropped from 551 to 279 (the safe/unsafe-fn, param-count, and fn-item mismatches this bug caused), and the E0432/E0603 unresolved-import/private errors this fix's globals half was needed to avoid introducing are gone (0).

title: Function-scoped struct name collisions: def/usage naming mismatch (TestCase_0 etc.)
description: When a single C file declares multiple distinct local (function-scoped) structs sharing the same tag name (e.g. every START_TEST in basic_tests.c declares its own 'struct TestCase { ... };' with different fields), ClangIR disambiguates the distinct layouts with a uniquing suffix in its printed type name (TestCase, TestCase.0, TestCase.1, ...), and slate's usage-site lowering (rust_record_name/sanitize_ident, src/lower.rs:9414-9417,9561-9569,46-50,10398-10417) faithfully turns that into TestCase_0/TestCase_1 identifiers. But struct *definitions* are collected from the Clang AST oracle (collect_records in src/c_ast.rs:810) keyed only by the bare C tag name, and folded into a single BTreeMap<String, Record> (src/lower.rs:323-349) with last-write-wins semantics -- so only ONE 'struct TestCase' definition ever gets emitted (see transpiled/libexpat's src/types.rs), under the un-suffixed name, with whichever function's fields happened to win the collision. Every other local layout (i) references a def that was never emitted (TestCase_0/TestCase_1 -> E0425 cannot find type) and (ii) any function whose own local shape lost the collision gets struct-literal/field-access code that doesn't match the surviving definition's fields (E0560 no field, E0609 unknown field, E0605 non-primitive cast on a swapped field, some E0308 expected X found integer). This is confirmed as ONE bug, not two separate ones -- local structs are emitted, just deduplicated to a single bare name that only one call site's shape matches.
design: Two fix directions identified by investigation: (a) reconcile CIR-uniqued type names (TestCase.0 etc, extracted via cir_record_name at src/lower.rs:9561) against the AST-collected records so each usage resolves to a distinct def, or (b) extend the anon_local_records synthesis path (src/lower.rs:9809, currently gated to anonymous-only names via anon_alias_key at src/lower.rs:9581-9587) to also cover NAMED local records that collided. Prefer whichever keeps collect_records/lower.rs's BTreeMap<String,Record> merge from silently last-write-winning across incompatible layouts -- that merge is the actual defect.
acceptance_criteria: A new C fixture (single file, mirrors libexpat's basic_tests.c pattern: 2+ functions each declaring their own local 'struct TestCase { ... };' with DIFFERENT field sets, each initializing/reading an array of it) translates and the differential test (matching stdout+exit code) passes. Every distinct function-local struct layout sharing a tag name gets its own emitted Rust struct definition under the same name its usage sites resolve to (whether that's reconciling to the ClangIR-uniqued name or synthesizing a per-layout def via anon_local_records-style handling, src/lower.rs:9809). Re-running translate-project against libexpat's basic_tests.c/CaseData/TestCase no longer produces E0425/E0560/E0609/E0605 errors sourced from this collision. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason:
Fixed. Root cause confirmed: collect_records (c_ast.rs) collects each function-local struct occurrence separately, but lower.rs folded them into records: BTreeMap<String, Record> keyed by bare sanitized name via naive last-write-wins collect(), collapsing distinct local layouts (e.g. libexpat's many per-test 'struct TestCase { ... };') under one definition -- while usage sites already correctly referenced ClangIR's own uniquing suffixes (TestCase, TestCase.0, TestCase.1 -> sanitized TestCase, TestCase_0, TestCase_1), which had no matching def.

Fix: added resolve_local_record_collisions (src/lower.rs) that, for every AST record base name with 2+ occurrences, matches each CIR-uniqued struct alias (module.aliases) back to its correct AST Record by comparing field-name sequences -- field names come from cir.get_member's 'name' attr, via a new non-anon-gated collect_local_record_field_names (generalizes the existing collect_anon_record_info/anon_alias_key machinery, which was hardcoded to anon.*/anon_*/__once_flag names only). Content-based matching was used instead of a positional/declaration-order guess because CIR's bare-vs-.0-vs-.1 assignment does NOT track AST declaration order (verified empirically: the fixture's first-declared function did not get the bare name). Matched records get their own .name field overwritten to the disambiguated key (record_lit_name derives the printed Rust identifier from record.name, not the map key it's stored under -- found via a second bug: even after the def existed, struct-literal expressions still printed the old bare name). Also added Lowerer.local_record_extras + an emission loop in lower_module, since the existing per-record item-emission loop iterates c.records's own (undisambiguated) name field and would never surface the new _0/_1 map keys otherwise.

Verified: new fixture tests/fixtures/local_struct_name_collision.c (2 functions, same local struct tag name, different field layouts) passes differential testing. Full nextest suite 250/251 (only the other 3 not-yet-fixed libexpat fixtures red, no regressions). Re-ran translate-project --lib --compile-commands against real libexpat: the 3 original cargo-check E0425 errors are gone (0 remain), E0605 14->3, panic/'error' 30->8, E0560 103->71, E0609 unchanged at 15 -- real but partial improvement, since the content-based field-name match can't resolve a collision family when CIR's get_member never touched every field of some colliding layout (no fallback attempted for those, by design, to avoid guessing wrong). Filed as known follow-up if the remaining ~71 E0560/15 E0609 warrant a second pass.

title: Fix libexpat translated-project compilation errors
description: translate-project on libexpat (~/c-corpus/libexpat/expat) currently produces Rust that fails both 'cargo check' (3 errors) and 'cargo t' (701 errors in the lib-test target) in transpiled/libexpat. Root-caused the errors into ~5 distinct lowering/fixup bugs (see child issues). Fixing these against real-world libexpat is the P0 bar for the transpiler handling a nontrivial C project end to end.
