Verified against real libexpat (~/c-corpus/libexpat/expat): 'cargo check' and 'cargo test --no-run' (the lib-test target) both now compile with zero errors, down from the epic's original baseline of 3 check errors / 701 test-target errors. The transpiler now handles this nontrivial real-world C project end to end.

title: assert() with a runtime-false condition is silently dropped instead of aborting
close_reason: Closed

title: (EPIC) Correctness fixes
description:
## Why
Beyond idiomization gaps (ugly-but-correct Rust), differential testing can surface actual semantic divergences between the C source and the generated Rust: cases where baseline lowering silently drops or misrepresents a side effect. These are correctness bugs, not readability work, and belong in a separate top-level epic so they never get deprioritized behind fixup/idiomization backlog.

## What to do
- Track and fix confirmed semantic divergences between C and generated Rust behavior (differing stdout, differing exit code, differing abort/panic behavior) discovered during any exploration, fixture audit, or fuzzing session.
- Each child bug must include a minimal C repro, the actual C binary behavior (stdout/exit code), and the actual generated Rust behavior, demonstrating the divergence concretely.
- Fixes must restore differential equivalence and land with a fixture under tests/fixtures/ that would have caught the regression.

## Success Criteria
- Every confirmed divergence has a landed fix plus a differential fixture pinning the corrected behavior.
- No open P0 bug lingers without an assigned root cause investigation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each child bug closes with a fixture demonstrating C/Rust equivalence restored.
- cargo nextest r --release passes with the new fixture included.

title: Thread proven function identity through lowering and semantic passes
description:
Why: every consumer that currently infers libc behavior from a function name can independently recreate the miscompile even after provenance exists in the frontend and AST types. Proven identity must become the sole authorization for idiomization and semantic summaries throughout Slate.

Scope:
- Thread typed function identity through baseline lowering, symbol tables, facts collection, fixup analysis, rewrite passes, effects summaries and interpreter models, and unused-extern pruning.
- Replace or gate every name-only standard-function classifier, including string_libc, call semantics, effect purity and summaries, allocation and I/O handling, and extern removal.
- Preserve ordinary call behavior for unknown, project-defined, indirect, aliased, or otherwise unproven functions.
- Add diagnostics or fact-debug output explaining why a same-name call was accepted or rejected where useful.
- Add end-to-end differential and effects regression coverage for trusted and adversarial same-name functions.
- Update provenance guarantee documentation and its link-time/runtime interposition boundary.
design: Downstream code may inspect symbol spelling for rendering and diagnostics, but semantic rewrites and summaries must require the typed proven identity. Remove compatibility adapters introduced by the type-system child once all consumers migrate. Default branches preserve baseline calls rather than assuming libc behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The epic reproducer translates and prints 5, with no constant strlen substitution. Trusted <string.h> strlen calls retain current valid idiomizations. Project strings.h declarations, project definitions, shadow headers, indirect calls, aliases, and unknown provenance never receive libc rewrites or effects. Project functions named like allocation, memory, string, and I/O APIs are not assigned standard semantics or pruned as unused externs. Repository search finds no semantic libc classification based only on callee string names unless it is explicitly limited to rendering or diagnostics. cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Rename KnownLibc to Known and expand it across all supported external standard APIs. Use one consolidated adversarial fixture covering every supported function, with exit last. Runtime interposition such as LD_PRELOAD is explicitly unsupported because it changes semantics out of band.
close_reason: Threaded Known function provenance through lowering, fixups, effects, and extern pruning; consolidated adversarial differential/effects fixture; documented interposition boundary; all gates pass

title: Represent external function provenance in the typed AST model
description:
Why: plugin evidence is useless if lowering collapses every callee to an untyped symbol name. The internal model needs an exhaustive distinction between proven standard functions and ordinary or unknown functions before any fixup can consume libc semantics.

Scope:
- Define typed identities for proven external functions, including an explicit unknown or ordinary classification.
- Add provenance-bearing call or callee nodes to the compact Clang AST facts and Rust AST instead of parallel string maps.
- Define the source-location join that attaches plugin call-site evidence to the corresponding Clang AST and CIR operation.
- Preserve direct versus indirect call identity and canonical signatures.
- Make printers, walkers, equality helpers, effects inputs, and test builders exhaustive over the new representation.

This child changes representation and transport boundaries only. Downstream passes may continue using compatibility adapters until the next child removes name-only behavior.
design: Use a strongly typed enum or equivalent AST node owned by the call/callee representation. Keep spelling and semantic identity separate: the source symbol remains available for baseline emission while optional proven semantics carry KnownLibc variants. Unknown must be the default, and constructing a known identity must require plugin evidence rather than a matching string.
acceptance_criteria: The compact Clang AST and Rust AST can represent two calls spelled strlen with distinct identities: KnownLibc::StrLen and unknown project function. Plugin facts join to calls by physical source location without assigning identity to unrelated same-name calls. Direct and indirect calls remain distinguishable. AST walkers and renderers compile exhaustively, baseline Rust emission is unchanged when provenance is unknown, and focused representation/join regression tests pass.
close_reason: Added typed call provenance to compact and Rust ASTs, joined plugin evidence through CIR source locations, distinguished direct and indirect calls, and added the differential strlen collision fixture.

title: Extract trusted function provenance in the Clang plugin
description:
Why: CIR and the rendered Rust AST retain external symbol names but not enough information to distinguish a standard-library declaration from a project declaration with the same name. Provenance must be captured while Clang still has the preprocessor include graph, physical file identities, declaration bindings, and redeclaration chains.

Scope:
- Extend the existing out-of-tree macro-dump plugin with PPCallbacks::InclusionDirective data for resolved physical FileEntryRef identities, include edges, written header names, angle-versus-quote form, and Clang header characteristics.
- Add an ASTConsumer that inspects direct CallExpr bindings, FunctionDecl canonical declarations and redeclarations, declaration expansion locations, bodies, and symbol-changing attributes.
- Establish a conservative trust policy for toolchain standard-header instances, including internal-header forwarding and project wrapper headers, without trusting basename or isInSystemHeader alone.
- Emit stable machine-readable call-site provenance facts keyed by physical source file and offset for later AST/CIR joining.
- Treat indirect calls and incomplete evidence as unknown.

The plugin gathers evidence only. It must not assign Rust fixup behavior or perform source rewriting.
design: Share one provenance collector between PPCallbacks and the translation-unit ASTConsumer. Build the resolved include graph during preprocessing, classify declaration chains after parsing, and emit call-site records only when the exact direct callee and trusted declaration ancestry are proven. Keep raw evidence distinguishable from semantic classification so diagnostics and future policies can explain rejection.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin output distinguishes a libc strlen declared through the toolchain-resolved <string.h> from a project-defined or project-header-declared strlen. Tests cover direct trusted calls, the epic reproducer with a project definition, an independent project strings.h declaration, a wrapper that includes trusted <string.h>, a shadow string.h on a normal project include path, internal libc header forwarding, macro-generated declarations, compatible redeclarations, symbol-changing attributes, and indirect calls. Unknown cases emit no trusted-function classification. The plugin builds against the configured CIR-enabled Clang and its output is deterministic.
close_reason: Implemented Clang plugin include/function provenance with physical header identities, AST redeclaration evidence, conservative rejection reasons, and 13 integration regressions. Verified plugin rebuild, cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo nextest r --release (736 passed). Merged into main as 44bf4c7.

title: Guarantee provenance for idiomized external functions
description:
Why: Slate currently assigns libc semantics and performs fixups by function name. A project-owned function with a reserved-looking name can therefore be replaced as though it were the standard-library function. The demonstrated case defines size_t strlen(const char *s) { return 5; }, but Slate folds strlen("hello world") to 11. This violates the projects correctness requirement and can affect string, memory, allocation, I/O, effects, and extern-pruning logic.

Scope:
- Establish trusted-header identity from the exact Clang invocation using an out-of-tree plugin and PPCallbacks::InclusionDirective. Record resolved physical file identity and include ancestry rather than trusting basename, angle-bracket spelling, or isInSystemHeader alone.
- Use Clang AST binding for direct calls and referenced declarations. Correlate CallExpr::getDirectCallee, canonical declarations, and redeclaration chains with trusted include provenance.
- Define conservative known-function identities such as KnownLibc::StrLen and preserve them through Clang AST extraction, CIR/source-location joining, baseline Rust AST lowering, fixup facts, effects summaries, and unused-extern pruning.
- Replace name-only semantic classification throughout the pipeline. Unknown, indirect, project-defined, aliased, weak, ifunc, asm-labeled, or otherwise unproven callees must retain ordinary external or project-call behavior.
- Document the guarantee boundary: source-level declaration provenance under the selected toolchain and normal libc linkage. Header provenance alone does not prove the link-time or runtime implementation under symbol interposition.
- Cover standard headers that re-export declarations through internal headers and project wrapper headers that include trusted standard headers.

Reproducer:
#include <stdio.h>
size_t strlen(const char *s) { return 5; }
int main() { printf("%ld\n", strlen("hello world")); }

Current wrong result: generated Rust replaces the project call with the known literal length 11 instead of calling the project strlen and printing 5.
design: Treat function semantics as typed provenance established before lowering, never as a property inferred from a rendered symbol name. InclusionDirective supplies resolved include identity; the completed Clang AST supplies call-to-declaration binding. Classify only direct calls whose compatible redeclaration chain contains a declaration exported through a trusted standard-header instance and contains no untrusted definition or symbol-changing attribute. Emit call-site facts keyed by physical source location so the CIR/AST join can carry the semantic identity into Rust AST nodes. Default to Unknown and decline idiomization whenever proof is incomplete.
acceptance_criteria: The reproducer prints 5 after translation and the generated Rust does not substitute strlen("hello world") with 11. A project header named strings.h that independently declares strlen is not classified as libc. A project wrapper header that includes the toolchain-resolved <string.h> preserves libc classification. A shadow string.h from an ordinary project include path is not trusted. Compatible redeclarations, macro-generated declarations, internal libc header forwarding, and direct versus indirect calls have differential regression coverage. All name-only libc semantic matching in fixups, effects, and extern pruning is removed or gated by typed known-function provenance. Unknown provenance always preserves baseline call semantics. cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.

title: Lower generic CIR scalar op spellings
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.binop and cir.unary as P0 unsupported generic scalar spellings that can block ordinary C emitted by newer/different CIR producers.

What to do:
- Add parsing/lowering for cir.binop and cir.unary spellings.
- Reuse existing scalar arithmetic, bitwise, logical, and unary lowering semantics where possible.
- Add differential fixtures that force these spellings.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md when the ops are supported.
close_reason: cir.binop/cir.unary are incubator-only generic spellings; upstream ClangIR (our producer) emits split named ops (cir.add, cir.minus, ...) instead and never emits these, so they can't be differentially tested. Not implementing. Documented in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.

title: Lower low-level CIR branch variants
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.brcond and cir.switch.flat as P0 unsupported control-flow variants. Slate supports structured branch/switch forms, but these lower-level forms can appear and should not block ordinary C.

What to do:
- Add parser and lowerer support for cir.brcond.
- Add parser and lowerer support for cir.switch.flat.
- Prefer structured Rust output when the CFG shape permits it; use conservative state-machine style only when needed.
- Add differential fixtures and update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: cir.brcond/cir.switch.flat come only from --cir-flatten-cfg, which Slate never runs. Verified: if/else, ternary, &&, ||, for, while, do-while, switch, goto all stay structured through Slate's emit pipeline (0 brcond/switch.flat). Supporting them would be untestable dead code. Documented in docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.

title: Op::Fmuladd always lowers to .mul_add(), but cir.fmuladd permits unfused legalization (target-dependent)
description:
Found while verifying slate-0ar5.2 (FP_CONTRACT allowlisting). Live on
main today, reachable with zero pragmas -- C99's default contraction
state is already "ON within a statement", so ordinary `a * b + c` already
emits `cir.fmuladd` (from clang's `llvm.fmuladd.f64`) with no pragma
required. Confirmed with both host clang and SLATE_CLANG.

lowerer.rs:4816-4823 lowers Op::Fmuladd to Rust's `.mul_add()`, identically
to Op::Fma (from explicit fma()/__builtin_fma). That's wrong: the two CIR
ops have different semantics.

- `cir.fma` (explicit fma() call) -> LLVM `llvm.fma.f64` -> mandatory,
  correctly-rounded, single-rounding fused result, unconditionally (falls
  back to a software-fused implementation if the target lacks hardware
  FMA). Rust's `.mul_add()` also compiles to `llvm.fma.f64` (confirmed:
  `declare double @llvm.fma.f64(...)`, `memory(none)` speculatable) -- so
  `.mul_add()` is the CORRECT match for Op::Fma.

- `cir.fmuladd` (implicit contraction of `a*b+c`) -> LLVM
  `llvm.fmuladd.f64` -> LangRef explicitly permits the backend to
  legalize this to separate unfused fmul+fadd when the target lacks a
  fast/legal FMA instruction. This is NOT an optimization-level choice
  (same at -O0 and -O3) -- it's driven by each backend's
  isFMAFasterThanFMulAndFAdd, a target-feature check.

Repro (values chosen so fused vs unfused rounding differs -- from the
classic FMA cancellation example, x = 0x1.fffffffffffffp+0, y = x,
z = -(x*x), result = x*y+z):
  real C (clang -O0, baseline x86-64, no -mfma):  0.00000000000000000000e+00
  Slate's generated Rust (.mul_add()):            4.93038065763132378382e-32
Both host clang and SLATE_CLANG confirmed emitting llvm.fmuladd.f64 for
this pattern with zero pragmas involved.

Confirmed via rustc --emit=llvm-ir that Rust's `.mul_add()` always compiles
to `llvm.fma.f64`, never `llvm.fmuladd.f64` -- so this is not fixable by
matching compiler flags between the C and Rust builds; it's a genuine
choice of which LLVM intrinsic gets targeted, baked into which Rust
surface Slate emits.
design:
Rejected: shimming Op::Fmuladd out to a C helper (the FENV_ACCESS pattern
from slate-0ar5). User's call: this is fundamentally different from
FENV_ACCESS's problem. FENV_ACCESS needs a shim because the correct
behavior depends on *dynamic* runtime state (the live rounding mode) that
Rust has no way to observe/express natively. Op::Fmuladd's correct
behavior is a *static* fact of the target triple/target-features, fully
known at translation time -- shimming every f64 arithmetic op to C for a
static target fact is unidiomatic, costs real readability for consumers
of the generated Rust, and actively works against later idiomization/
rewrite passes recovering native Rust operators.

Correct fix: target dispatch in the lowerer, same shape as
is_quad_long_double/uses_f64_long_double_abi in the long-double lowering
path (see docs/src/long-double.md, "Picking the right long double"). Ask
whether the target's backend would legalize llvm.fmuladd to a fused
instruction; if yes emit `.mul_add()`, if no emit decomposed `a * b + c`.

Per-arch legality conditions, pulled directly from each backend's
isFMAFasterThanFMulAndFAdd (f32/f64 case) in the local llvm-project
checkout:

- X86ISelLowering.cpp:36487 -- Subtarget.hasAnyFMA() (FMA3/FMA4/AVX512F).
  False at baseline x86-64 (SSE2 only); true with -mfma/-march=haswell+ or
  AVX512.
- AArch64ISelLowering.cpp:20278 -- Subtarget->hasFPARMv8(). Effectively
  always true -- FPARMv8 is the mandatory baseline FP extension for
  AArch64 (fmadd is not a separate opt-in extension the way x86 FMA3 is).
- ARMISelLowering.cpp:19594 -- Subtarget->useFPVFMx64(). Needs
  VFPv4/NEON-VFPv4; not guaranteed at ARM baseline.
- RISCVISelLowering.cpp:27773 -- Subtarget.hasStdExtDOrZdinx(). Tied to
  the D extension itself -- RISC-V's D extension mandates fmadd.d as part
  of the extension, unlike x86 where FMA is wholly separate from SSE2.

Slate needs a `target_has_native_fma(arch, features) -> bool`-shaped query
(mirroring the existing target-query pattern in long-double lowering) fed
by whatever target-triple/target-feature info the lowerer already carries
for other target-dependent choices.
acceptance_criteria:
- Op::Fmuladd lowering checks a target_has_native_fma-style query instead
  of unconditionally emitting .mul_add()
- x86-64 baseline (no +fma) case: decomposes to `a * b + c`, matches the
  stdlib_fp_contract.c differential repro
- AArch64 baseline case: still emits .mul_add() (fmadd is unconditional
  there) -- needs its own repro/verification since only x86-64 was
  directly tested this session

title: Verify extern "C" calls act as an optimizer barrier for float reordering
description:
The whole FENV_ACCESS shim design (slate-0ar5) rests on: does an
unannotated extern "C" call in generated Rust actually block rustc/LLVM
from reordering, CSEing, or constant-folding neighboring float ops across
it, in both directions, at -O2/-O3? This is currently only asserted by
analogy to the long-double shim's existing (informally trusted)
correctness -- never independently confirmed.

Build a minimal fixture: two ordinary float ops flanking a shim-style
extern "C" call adjacent to an fesetround() change. Emit LLVM IR for the
generated Rust (cargo rustc --release -- --emit=llvm-ir) and confirm no
reassociation/hoisting crosses the call boundary at -O2/-O3. Use Alive2
(see the alive2 skill) if manual inspection is ambiguous.

See handoffs/floating-point-env.md, "Open question to resolve before
implementing" section, for full context.
acceptance_criteria: Written up finding (pass/fail) with the LLVM IR or Alive2 evidence, either in the handoff doc or a follow-up bd note. If the barrier doesn't hold, the shim design in slate-0ar5 needs revisiting before any further subtask proceeds.
notes: Blocks the C-shim-writing and FenvAttr-parsing subtasks -- do this first.
close_reason: Confirmed via generated LLVM IR at rustc -C opt-level=2 and opt-level=3: an unannotated extern "C" call is never inferred readnone/readonly by rustc/LLVM (attribute group is just 'nounwind'), so LLVM treats it as an unknown-side-effect boundary and preserves source order across it in both directions -- verified with both a data-dependent op (indep computation feeding into a value used after the call) and a fully data-independent op (w*x with zero dependency on the call's args or result), neither got hoisted/sunk across the call at either opt level. Full detail + reproducer IR written to handoffs/floating-point-env.md.

title: Regression: trust_cir array-type override clobbered bitfield storage/wrapper field types
description: 6a8b252f ('start generating intrinsics') widened lower_record_def's trust_cir heuristic to trust CIR's resolved field type whenever it's an Array and the AST-derived guess wasn't already CType::Array (added to correctly type GNU vector-attribute struct fields like __storeu_si512's __v: [i64;8]). This over-applied to bitfield storage fields two ways: (1) synthesized __bitfield_N storage fields from bitfield_storage_fields() carry a deliberate CType::Record("__slate_bitfields::__SlateBitfield_*") sentinel that must not be second-guessed by CIR's raw byte-array member type; (2) real un-collapsed bitfield fields (bit_width: Some(_)) that fall through bitfield_storage_fields() (e.g. union bitfields -- that function only handles CirType::Struct, not CirType::Union) got their scalar-cast-friendly type replaced by a raw [u8;N] array. Broke 7 gcc-torture batch bins (bitfld_6, bitfld_7, pr23324, pr52979_1, pr52979_2, pr58570, pr70602, pr79737_1) under gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c.
design: Fixed by (a) never passing cir_field_types at all for lower_record's synthesized storage_record path (its field.ty already carries the fully-resolved intended type), and (b) excluding any field with bit_width.is_some() from the trust_cir override for the non-synthesized path. Both are needed -- they cover the two distinct code paths bitfields can take.
acceptance_criteria: cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering passes gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c
close_reason: Fixed in src/frontend/lowerer.rs: trust_cir now excludes bit_width.is_some() fields, and the synthesized storage_record path (lower_record) passes cir_field_types=None instead of re-deriving from CIR. Verified: gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c passes (was failing on 7 bins), full lowering nextest profile passes (7/7), AVX512 mask.expand intrinsics repro from this session still compiles/runs/matches clang byte-for-byte (confirms the original GNU-vector-field fix this heuristic exists for is untouched). Root cause found via git worktree bisection: confirmed passing at 0faa7b51's parent (e25a0003) and first broken at 6a8b252f.

title: Lower CIR vector types to std::simd, not plain Rust arrays, at extern/FFI boundaries
description: slate lowers every CIR <N x T> vector value to a plain Rust array [T; N] (Type::Array), which is correct for arithmetic done in-crate but is an LLVM *array* type, not an LLVM *vector* type. This has never mattered before because nothing round-tripped a slate-generated vector value through a real extern "unadjusted"/#[link_name="llvm.*"] call boundary (the call_llvm_intrinsic support from slate-os0h/x86-intrinsics-lowering work). Confirmed via direct repro: declaring an intrinsic shim with [i32; 16] params for __m512i, even with the correct #[link_name] (including legacy/stdarch-mined overrides, see handoffs/x86-intrinsics-lowering.md), still fails with 'rustc-LLVM ERROR: Cannot select: intrinsic %llvm.x86.avx512.mask.expand' because LLVM's Intrinsic::lookupIntrinsicID falls back to prefix-matching the array-typed declare against the generic overloaded family instead of resolving the legacy fixed-type ID. Fix requires lowering intrinsic-call operand/result vector types (at minimum) to std::simd::Simd<T,N> (#![feature(portable_simd, simd_ffi)]), confirmed working standalone for llvm.ctpop.v4i32 and llvm.x86.avx512.pmul.dq.512 (no mask arg). A hand-rolled #[repr(simd)] newtype was tried and confirmed to be a dead end (MIR validation ICE, only works inside core/std itself).
design: Scope narrowly to call_llvm_intrinsic operand/result types first (not all vector values project-wide) to avoid destabilizing existing array-based vector codegen; widen later if needed.
acceptance_criteria: AVX512 mask.expand repro (both _epi32 and _pd overloads, tests/fixtures or /tmp/overload_src in handoffs/x86-intrinsics-lowering.md) compiles and runs, matching clang output byte-for-byte.
close_reason: Fixed: lower_call_llvm_intrinsic now wraps vector-typed operand/result positions in std::simd::Simd<T,N> at the extern shim boundary (Simd::from_array/.to_array conversion at the call site, arrays unchanged everywhere else), and auto-emits #![feature(portable_simd, simd_ffi)] alongside the existing link_llvm_intrinsics/abi_unadjusted. Verified end-to-end: the AVX512 mask.expand repro (both _epi32 and _pd overloads) now compiles and produces byte-identical stdout/exit code vs clang -mavx512f.

title: Phase 1: swap slate's generic CIR layer onto clang-ir's typed ast layer
description: Replace Op/Attr/Module/Region/Block in src/cir/ir.rs with clang-ir's ast::{Operation,Type,Attribute,GenericModule}; delete src/cir/parse.rs (933 lines) entirely. Keep CirOpKind dispatch as-is since it only needs op.name - no dispatch-shape change in this phase. Rewrite src/frontend/lowerer/types.rs (currently ~900 lines of strip_prefix/strip_suffix string surgery reimplementing CIR's type grammar) to match against the real Type enum instead. Rewrite src/frontend/lowerer/constants.rs's ~18 parse_cir_* functions to match against the real Attribute enum instead of re-parsing Attr::Raw strings. src/cir/emit.rs and src/cir/flatten.rs stay slate-owned (target/libc-shim plumbing, goto-flatten orchestration) - wire them to hand already-normalized generic-form text to clang-ir's parser directly (using the pre-normalized-text entry point from the loc/signature task) rather than letting clang-ir's Toolchain re-invoke cir-opt a second time.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build succeeds with src/cir/parse.rs deleted and lowerer/types.rs + lowerer/constants.rs rewritten against typed Type/Attribute; relevant nextest profile(s) (lowering, rewrites, libc as applicable) pass; cir-opt is invoked exactly once per compilation unit, not twice.
notes:
Session 4: fixed the two remaining regressions from the typed-CIR migration and got all three nextest profiles (lowering, rewrites, libc) fully green.

1. alloca_group_is_lowerable (storage.rs) didn't exclude hoisted allocas (goto-target locals declared above the dispatch loop/closure). Consecutive same-line alloca groups (e.g. 'T *t1, *t2;') that were also goto-hoisted got merged into a __SlateAllocaFrameN tuple struct declared inside the wrong (inner) scope, producing 'cannot find value in this scope' errors when referenced from sibling blocks. Fix: also check !self.hoisted.contains(result) before grouping; hoisted allocas now fall through to the existing per-op lower_alloca path, which already handles them correctly.

2. Same function also grouped allocas whose pointee type contained core::ffi::VaList in any form (raw VaList, *mut VaList, [*mut VaList; N], **VaList) into the tuple-struct frame, which doesn't compile - a struct field with an elided VaList<'_> lifetime needs a named generic lifetime, unlike a let-binding's inferred '_'. Added a recursive type_contains_va_list() check (Ptr/Ref/Slice/Array/Complex/Generic) and excluded any such alloca from grouping, matching the existing exclusion for the direct-va_list-record case. Considered switching these to the boxed __SlateVaArgs representation (existing idiom for plain va_list allocas) but these are va_list POINTERS/arrays-of-pointers (repro: gcc-torture va-arg-21.c's 'va_list *ap_array[3], **ap_ptr;'), not va_list values, so __SlateVaArgs's owning Rc-based representation doesn't apply - falling back to individual non-grouped lets (which already compile fine with elided lifetimes) was the right fix, not a representation change.

3. anon_local_records (types.rs) filtered CIR struct members down to RecordMemberKind::Data only, silently dropping RecordMemberKind::Pad members. This broke over-aligned struct fields inside compiler-synthesized anonymous local structs (e.g. 'struct { _Alignas(16) char x, y; } a;') - the padding bytes CIR inserts between x and y to satisfy the 16-byte alignment were never emitted as a field, so the struct fell back to natural i8/i8 layout and &a.y - &a.x came out as 1 instead of 16 (chibicc alignof test). Fix: include Pad alongside Data in the filter, keeping the existing __slate_anon_{i} synthetic naming for the padding field (index i already counts over the full unfiltered member list, so no renumbering needed) - now matches pre-migration output byte-for-byte.

All three regressions were pre-existing-code interactions exposed by the migration making previously-uncompilable code compile for the first time, not new bugs in the typed-AST rewrite itself. Bug 7 (anon ABI-coercion structs collapsing to i32) from the prior session's handoff was already fixed when this session started (record_struct_type takes alias_key). cir-opt-invoked-once acceptance clause verified satisfied: src/cir/flatten.rs calls clang_ir::parse_generic_str(text) directly on slate's own already-normalized generic-form output, never clang-ir's own Toolchain (which would re-invoke cir-opt). src/cir/parse.rs is gone.

cargo fmt clean. cargo clippy --release --all-targets: 3 pre-existing dead_code warnings (unrelated, pre-dates this session) + 4 pre-existing style warnings (redundant_closure/needless_borrow in arithmetic.rs/calls.rs/intrinsics.rs, not touched this session) - none introduced by this session's changes.

Not committed - conservative git policy. title: Implement missing CIR ops in clang-ir's model layer
description: Against clang-ir's own 2,571-file real-CIR corpus, 472 files (18%) hit at least one unmodeled op in the model::Instruction enum (falls back to Instruction::Other). Biggest gaps by occurrence count: bitfields (cir.get_bitfield/set_bitfield - largest by far, 1881+1568 hits), varargs (va_arg/va_start/va_end/va_copy), complex numbers, vectors, atomics, inline asm, and math builtins (fabs, copysign, ctz/clz, overflow-checked arithmetic). Also investigate cir.ternary specifically: it already has a try_lower match arm but still silently degrades to Other 306 times in the corpus because the real-world op shape doesn't match the parser's structural assumption - fix the assumption, don't just add a variant.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running clang-ir's snapshot_fixtures test shows near-zero <unmodeled: ...> ops for the mnemonics slate actually needs (cross-check against slate's CirOpKind list); cir.ternary lowers structurally instead of falling back to Other.
close_reason: Closed the highest-value gaps: added typed Attribute::BitfieldInfo to the ast layer plus Instruction::GetBitfield/SetBitfield to the model layer (the single largest gap at 1881+1568 unmodeled occurrences), fixed the cir.ternary silent-fallback bug (Instruction::Ternary.result is now Option<(ValueId,Type)> to handle statement-position ternaries with no result), and added 15 more op families: Fmuladd, Copysign, MathUnary{Fabs,Floor,Ffs,Clz,Ctz,Abs,Signbit}, FrameAddress, ReturnAddress, Prefetch, VaStart/VaEnd/VaCopy/VaArg, MulOverflow/AddOverflow, ComplexCreate/ComplexReal/ComplexImag. Also fixed a real architectural bug found along the way: model::Instruction lowering (try_lower) only ever saw a bare Operation with no access to the module's alias table, so any attribute passed by #name reference (bitfield_info = #bfi_a is the common case, but also e.g. #true/#false-hoisted const values) silently failed to structurally match and fell back to Other - added an alias-resolution pass (resolve_op/resolve_attribute in model/module.rs) that inlines Attribute::Named references before lowering. Net effect on clang-ir's 2571-file real-CIR snapshot corpus: unmodeled-op occurrences dropped from ~6300 to ~400, concentrated in a long tail of ~45 low-frequency mnemonics (vectors, atomics, complex real_ptr/imag_ptr/add/sub, inline asm, misc single-digit builtins) filed as slate-cevu.5 for follow-up rather than blocking here. title: native lowering: switch/case has no break target and no real fallthrough
description:
9 fixtures fail to compile with E0268 "break outside of a loop or labeled block", all switch-related: gnu_case_ranges, goto_into_later_switch_case, goto_into_later_switch_case_bitint, goto_into_later_switch_case_i128, switch_break_inside_if, switch_default, switch_fallthrough, switch_no_default, switch_sparse. A 10th, switch_loop_control, now *compiles* (after this session's loop-label fix let a stray `break` inside a switch bind to the enclosing loop's label instead of erroring) but produces wrong stdout -- direct evidence the bug is semantic, not just a compile error.

Root cause: src/frontend/native_lowerer/stmts.rs lowers `switch` straight to a Rust `match` (SwitchStmt handler) with case bodies built by lower_switch_arms/push_case_chain/push_arms (~line 261-344). Any `BreakStmt` lexically inside a case is lowered via env.break_label (the *loop's* label, if any) or bare `Break(None)` -- there is nothing that gives the switch itself a break target. So:
  - A `break;` ending a switch case, when the switch isn't inside any loop, has nothing to bind to -> E0268.
  - When the switch IS inside a loop, that `break;` now incorrectly breaks the outer loop instead of just the switch (switch_loop_control's wrong-stdout case).
  - Separately, real C fallthrough (case N falling into case N+1's *own* statements without an intervening break) isn't modeled at all -- push_case_chain only merges directly-chained empty labels (`case 1: case 2: body`), not "case 1 has statements, no break, falls into case 2's statements" (switch_fallthrough).

The mature CIR lowerer already solves both problems for cir.switch: src/frontend/lowerer/control_flow.rs, `lower_switch` (~line 261-360). Technique: wrap the whole switch in `'switchN: loop { match state { ... } }` with an explicit i64 state variable; each case arm that doesn't end in control flow assigns the *next* case's index and does `continue 'switchN` (fallthrough), the last case (or an explicit break) does `break 'switchN`; loop_stack gets `LoopFrame{break_label: Some(switchN), continue_label: None, is_loop: false}` pushed while lowering case bodies so nested breaks bind to the switch, not any enclosing loop. Porting this (adapted from CIR case ops to Clang CaseStmt/DefaultStmt) is the recommended fix rather than patching around the current match-arm approach.

Verify each fixture with `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=<name> cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`; switch_fallthrough is the best functional check since it requires real fallthrough, not just compiling.
notes:
Implemented: ported the mature CIR lowerer's switch-as-dispatch-loop technique (src/frontend/lowerer/control_flow.rs lower_switch) to native_lowerer/stmts.rs. Switch now lowers to: a selector match picking a case index, a mutable __switch_caseN variable, and a labeled 'switchN: loop { match __switch_caseN { ... } } -- case bodies that don't end in break/continue/return get a synthesized 'assign next index + continue switchN' (real fallthrough) or 'break switchN' (last case). env.break_label is overridden to the switch's own label while lowering case bodies, so a bare C break correctly targets the switch instead of bubbling to an enclosing loop (previously: E0268 compile errors, or silently broke the wrong loop -- switch_loop_control's stdout differed before this fix, now passes).

Found and fixed two more bugs while landing this:
1. A real hang (while_switch_continue spun at 100% CPU): my earlier continue/break loop-labeling assumed a while loop's bare  always correctly falls through to loop-top with no wrapping needed -- true only when nothing else introduces an intervening loop construct. The new switch dispatch loop IS such a construct, so a bare continue inside a switch-in-a-while now bound to the switch's loop instead of the while's, looping forever. Fixed by applying the same loop_labels_if_needed/lower_loop_body wrapping to WhileStmt that ForStmt/DoStmt already had -- now always safe regardless of what's nested inside.
2. case_label_value() didn't handle negative case labels (case -3: is a UnaryOperator node, not covered by the match, silently defaulted to 0) -- switch_sparse was silently misrouting to the wrong case. Added a UnaryOperator{opcode:"-"} arm.

Not fixed (separate, pre-existing, real limitation): GNU case ranges (case 1 ... 4:) aren't handled by case_label_value at all -- gnu_case_ranges fails. Small enough to fold into slate-ypjt.2.11 (long tail) rather than its own bead.

139->145/332 passing (some of that delta is switch fixtures that were already compiling as plain FAIL before, now genuinely fixed).
close_reason: Switch dispatch-loop technique ported from the mature lowerer; break/fallthrough/case-in-loop all correct now. Also fixed a real infinite-loop regression (while+switch+continue) and a negative-case-label bug found along the way. 139->145/332 passing.

title: native lowering: sizeof/alignof (UnaryExprOrTypeTraitExpr) not lowered
description:
Largest single translate-failure bucket: 40 of 114 are `unsupported expr node kind: Some("UnaryExprOrTypeTraitExpr")` (sizeof/alignof/_Alignof/__alignof).

Root cause: src/parse/clang_ast.rs's `Clang` enum (the typed subset of clang-ast-crate node kinds this project bothers to deserialize -- see the enum around line 169) has no dedicated variant for UnaryExprOrTypeTraitExpr, so it falls into Clang::Other, which only carries {kind, name, tag_used, qual_type, loc} -- no operand type. src/frontend/native_lowerer/exprs.rs then rejects any Clang::Other that isn't in its `is_transparent_wrapper` allowlist (~line 97).

The old (being-replaced) src/frontend/c_ast.rs scraper already reads the fields you need, at ~line 1546 (`collect_layout_queries_at`): the JSON has `name` ("sizeof" | "alignof" | "_Alignof" | "__alignof") and, for the type-operand form (`sizeof(int)`), `argType.qualType`. For the expr-operand form (`sizeof(x)`), there's a single child expression instead and no argType -- confirmed via `cargo run --release -- dump-clang-ast` on a throwaway fixture with both forms.

Suggested approach:
  1. Add a typed variant to the Clang enum in src/parse/clang_ast.rs (mirror the existing MemberExpr struct pattern) capturing `name: Option<String>` and `arg_type: Option<QualType>` (serde rename "argType").
  2. In native_lowerer/exprs.rs, lower it to `std::mem::size_of::<T>()` / `std::mem::align_of::<T>()` where T comes from either arg_type (type-operand form) or the child expression's static type (expr-operand form) -- IMPORTANT: C's sizeof/alignof never evaluates its operand expression (VLA operand types aside, out of scope here), so lower from the operand's *static type* only, never lower_expr the child and take its runtime value/size_of_val.
  3. Result type is size_t -- match existing CType/int-literal-width conventions used elsewhere in this file for the produced value's type.

Affected: 40 fixtures across many features (aligned_struct, allocation_attribute_metadata, array_one_past_end_bound, and many more) -- this single fix is likely the highest-leverage item in the whole epic.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=aligned_struct cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`.
notes:
Implemented: added typed Clang::UnaryExprOrTypeTraitExpr(SizeOfAlignOfExpr) variant to src/parse/clang_ast.rs capturing name+argType, plus a dump_tree arm. In native_lowerer/exprs.rs, lowers to std::mem::size_of::<T>()/align_of::<T>() cast to the result type -- T from arg_type (type-operand form) or the unevaluated child's static type (expr-operand form), never lower_expr'ing the operand (sizeof doesn't evaluate it).

Important correction to my own original plan: I initially added a new Expr::SizeOf AST variant (touched 21 files across backend/facts+query for exhaustive-match fallout) before discovering the codebase already has a dormant, purpose-built convention for exactly this: Expr::Call{func: Expr::Var("std::mem::size_of::<T>"), args: []} -- a call whose Path is a single Ident holding the whole turbofish text verbatim, already recognized by src/backend/query/sort_search.rs's layout_size_type and src/backend/query/context.rs's unused_item_collect_layout_call_type_ref (both previously dead code, evidently pre-wired for this exact feature). Reverted the new-variant approach (git checkout on the 21 files) and used the existing convention instead -- zero blast radius, and gets free interop with sort_search.rs's qsort/bsearch layout reasoning.

126->139/332 passing.

title: native lowering: DeclRefExpr can't resolve global variables or enum constants
description:
33 of the 114 translate-time failures are LowerError::UnresolvedDecl, e.g.:
  [anonymous_enum_record_field] lower ...: unresolved decl reference 0x55590035e1e0
  [global_vars] (same shape)

Root cause: src/frontend/native_lowerer/exprs.rs DeclRefExpr handling (~line 74-80) resolves names ONLY through env.vars, a HashMap<Id, VarInfo> populated by items.rs's collect_locals, which walks a FunctionDecl body and registers only ParmVarDecl and non-static local VarDecl. Two decl kinds referenced from function bodies are never registered anywhere:
  1. Top-level global VarDecl (e.g. tests/fixtures/global_vars.c) -- lower_global (items.rs) lowers the global item itself but never inserts its Id->name into ctx.vars, so referencing it back from a function is UnresolvedDecl.
  2. EnumConstantDecl (e.g. tests/fixtures/anonymous_enum_record_field.c, array_indexed_struct_field_named_enum.c, local_named_enum_declaration.c) -- never registered at all.

Confirmed via `cargo run --release -- dump-clang-ast tests/fixtures/anonymous_enum_record_field.c`: the DeclRefExpr's referencedDecl points at an EnumConstantDecl/VarDecl outside the function.

Suggested approach:
  - Globals: in whatever collects top-level items (items.rs, near collect_top_level/lower_global), also insert each global VarDecl's Id -> its lowered name into ctx.vars, same as a local.
  - Enum constants: check whether the EnumConstantDecl node exposes its computed integer value in the clang-ast JSON (dump-clang-ast --dump-ast or the raw -ast-dump=json) -- if so, prefer resolving a DeclRefExpr to an EnumConstantDecl directly to an integer literal (RExpr::Value) rather than a named Var, since C enum constants are compile-time constants and CIR (the mature lowerer's input) folds them the same way, which is presumably why src/frontend/lowerer never needed this case at all.

Affected fixtures (partial list, all "unresolved decl reference"): anonymous_enum_record_field, array_indexed_struct_field_named_enum, global_vars, global_array_pointer_decay, global_string_pointer_array, local_named_enum_declaration, enum_ptr_signedness, enums, typedef_ptr_signedness, and ~24 more -- rerun the profile after fixing to get the exact remaining set.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=global_vars cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture` and same for anonymous_enum_record_field.
notes:
Fixed: (1) top-level global VarDecl was already registered in ctx.vars (no change needed); (2) EnumConstantDecl values were never computed/registered at all -- added Ctx.enum_values: HashMap<Id, i128>, populated by walking each EnumDecl's children (top-level AND nested inside RecordDecl bodies, for enums declared inline as a struct field type) computing C's implicit-increment enum value rule, using the constant-folded value Clang exposes via a ConstantExpr's 'value' JSON field when there's an explicit initializer. DeclRefExpr in exprs.rs now falls back to this map and emits an integer literal. Went from 120/332 to 126/332 passing.

Two things found and split into new beads rather than fixed here (different root causes): slate-ypjt.2.13 (CType::parse misparses anonymous enum/struct qualType strings like 'enum (unnamed at ...)' as a function type -- blocks anonymous_enum_record_field even after this fix), and slate-ypjt.2.14 (remaining unresolved-decl failures are __builtin_* function references, deliberately excluded by items.rs's is_implicit guard -- needs builtin-to-Rust-intrinsic mapping, not a DeclRefExpr fix).
close_reason: Global var + enum constant DeclRefExpr resolution fixed (120->126/332 passing). Residual unresolved-decl failures split into slate-ypjt.2.13 and slate-ypjt.2.14 as separate root causes.

title: native lowering: drive generated_differential_native to parity
description:
Follow-up to slate-ypjt.1, which explicitly deferred full fixture parity. Tracks closing the gap on the native (clang-ast-crate) lowerer's differential suite.

Baseline (this session, after fixing an infinite-loop hang in src/frontend/native_lowerer/stmts.rs's continue/break loop-labeling -- see notes): 120/332 fixtures passing.

Reproduce: `cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --no-fail-fast --nocapture 2>&1 | tail -5` prints "native lowering parity: X/332 fixtures passing". The nextest.toml profile filters to `test(generated_differential_native)`, the single #[test] in tests/native_lowering.rs that iterates every tests/fixtures/*.c, translates with the native frontend, and differentially runs C vs Rust.

Isolate one fixture: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=<name> cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`. Inspect raw output: `cargo run --release -- translate --frontend native tests/fixtures/<name>.c`.

OPERATIONAL WARNING: do not trust nextest --nocapture's captured panic dump when several fixtures fail to compile in the same run. tests/support/mod.rs's BatchBuild::error_for falls back to the *entire* shared batch cargo stderr whenever a specific bin's error isn't found in the per-target JSON map, so the panic message repeats that whole blob once per affected fixture -- a run with ~85 compile failures produced a ~930k-line log. Instead rebuild target/difftest-native-generated/batch_cargo directly:
  cd target/difftest-native-generated/batch_cargo && cargo build --quiet --keep-going --message-format=json --manifest-path Cargo.toml | jq -r 'select(.reason=="compiler-message" and .message.level=="error") | "\(.target.name)\t\(.message.rendered)"'
See child bead for fixing error_for itself.

213 failures were triaged into the child beads below by root cause (translate-time "unsupported expr/stmt kind" vs rustc compile errors vs runtime stdout/exit mismatches), using this technique. Each child lists its exact fixture set, the confirmed error text, and a concrete suggested approach -- often "port the equivalent handling already in src/frontend/lowerer/ (the mature CIR-based lowerer), which solves the same problem against CIR input instead of Clang AST input."

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (whole epic): 332/332 fixtures pass under `cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering`, or remaining gaps are explicitly demoted/documented with rationale (mirroring how tests/fixtures.gcc-torture.unsupported/ demotions are handled elsewhere in this project).
close_reason: Abandoning the native clang-ast-crate lowering experiment: reverted main back to the pre-migration commit (7f50e296) and parked the in-progress work on branch experiment/clang-ast. Decision (2026-08-16): the CIR-based lowerer is much further along (many more fixtures + gcc-torture cases passing), and the AST-only rewrite wasn't shaping up to be more readable/maintainable despite fixing several real bugs along the way. Resuming CIR-based work on gcc-torture (slate-os0h.22, slate-os0h.3.1) instead. All 22 child issues closed.

title: Hook native_lowerer up to clang-ast crate output
description: native_lowerer/{items,exprs,stmts,types,globals}.rs were written against the now-deleted chibicc-ported parse::ast::Program (ast.rs/lexer.rs/parser.rs/preprocessor.rs, deleted in 66677221). Rewrite native_lowerer to consume clang_ast::Node<Clang> (the clang-ast crate's typed deserialization of clang -ast-dump=json) directly as its lowering input: parse qualType strings into a Type representation (no more precomputed offsets/sizes -- let rustc's #[repr(C)] layout do that), resolve locals/globals by clang_ast::Id instead of Obj array index, and lower initializers from InitListExpr/literal expression trees instead of byte-blob decode. Wire src/api.rs (parse_native/translate_native/lowered_program_native) and the CLI (--frontend native, parse-only, native-frontend-report) to the new clang_ast-based path. Get differential fixtures passing incrementally; full 338-fixture parity is not in scope for the first pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: [EPIC] Replace CIR + hand-parsed Clang AST JSON with the clang-ast crate as the sole lowering input
description:
Supersedes the closed slate-ozsg epic tree (ported-chibicc parser attempt -- see slate-ozsg's closing note for why that was dropped: whack-a-mole on chibicc-vs-Rust semantic gaps that Clang's own AST already resolves for free).

New direction: drop both CIR (the MLIR generic-form op-tree from src/cir/) and the ad-hoc serde_json::Value-based scraping in src/frontend/c_ast.rs (2352 lines, currently used only as a secondary "source-fact oracle" joined to CIR by source location -- see docs/architecture.md). Replace both wholesale with the clang-ast crate (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast), which gives typed Serde deserialization of `clang -Xclang -ast-dump=json` output instead of hand-walking untyped JSON. The resulting typed Clang AST becomes the single, primary lowering input -- no more joining two IRs by location, no more CLANG_ENABLE_CIR build requirement.

Why this is expected to be materially easier than both prior approaches:
- CIR path: requires a custom CLANG_ENABLE_CIR clang build, format churns across clang versions, structured control flow already flattened by the time it reaches CIR.
- chibicc-port path (slate-ozsg, closed): we owned every desugaring decision (compound assignment, VLA/alloca, truthiness coercion, default argument promotion, goto/computed-goto dispatch, etc.) and had to rediscover/reimplement each one by hand, one differential-fixture failure at a time.
- clang-ast path: Clang's own AST already has this all resolved correctly (ImplicitCastExpr nodes make default argument promotion and truthiness coercion explicit, real Decl/Stmt/Expr hierarchy, no synthesized-Obj-with-empty-name problem) -- we consume Clang's own semantic analysis instead of re-deriving it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (draft, refine when scoping children): a typed clang-ast-crate-based frontend exists, is wired in as the primary (eventually sole) lowering input, is driven to at least parity with the current CIR-frontend differential fixture pass rate, and CIR/src/cir + the old c_ast.rs scraping are removed once parity is reached.

Needs child issues for: standing up the clang-ast crate dependency + a minimal typed-AST dump/round-trip smoke test; designing the typed-AST -> rust_ast lowering pipeline (can likely reuse much of src/frontend/lowerer/'s existing rust_ast-emission logic and runtime_support.rs, since only the *input* IR is changing, not the Rust-emission target); a migration/parity plan against the differential fixture suite; and finally removing src/cir + the old c_ast.rs once the new path reaches parity.
close_reason: Closed

title: Port goto/irreducible-control-flow dispatch-loop encoding to native_lowerer
description:
Corrects a mischaracterization in slate-ozsg.8.4's original notes: lower_dispatch/lower_br/lower_brcond/lower_goto/lower_indirect_br/lower_switch_flat in src/frontend/lowerer/control_flow.rs are NOT pure CIR-flattening plumbing to delete. lower_dispatch (control_flow.rs:544) implements a real relooper-style algorithm -- assign each basic block a numeric state, lower arbitrary branches to 'state = N; continue <dispatch-loop>;' inside a loop{match state{...}}, matching the classic Duff's-device/state-machine encoding for irreducible control flow. This is needed because Rust only has structured loops, and C's goto (including jumps into loop bodies, backward jumps to arbitrary points, and computed goto via &&label) can produce control flow with no structured representation at all -- this problem is independent of whether the source was CIR or a real AST; parse::ast having structured If/For/While/Switch nodes does NOT remove the need for this, it only removes the need for it on the (common) functions that never use unstructured goto.

Currently src/frontend/native_lowerer/stmts.rs's StmtKind::Goto/GotoExpr handling is a placeholder (emits unimplemented!()) -- functions using goto will compile but panic at runtime under --frontend native until this lands.
design: CIR's lower_dispatch takes an already-flat CIR basic-block Region (Br/Brcond/Label ops) as input -- that CFG already exists because CIR emission flattens control flow at the clang level. parse::ast has no equivalent flat CFG: StmtKind::Goto/Label are embedded directly inside the structured Stmt tree (nested in blocks/ifs/loops), not as a separate block graph. Porting this requires two layers, only the first of which is new: (1) build a basic-block CFG from the structured AST for functions that actually contain a Goto/Label/computed-goto (scan for label/goto boundaries within the Stmt tree, including fallthrough edges) -- gate this construction on actually needing it, most functions have zero gotos and should keep going through the direct structured lowering in slate-ozsg.8.4's main path; (2) adapt lower_dispatch's state-variable/loop/match encoding to whatever that native CFG representation ends up being -- the state-machine encoding itself ports largely as-is once fed a block list and branch targets, CIR-shaped or not.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture using goto to jump into/out of nested blocks (forward and backward), and a fixture using computed goto (&&label / void* jump table), both lower correctly under --frontend native and pass their differential test. unimplemented!() is gone from StmtKind::Goto/GotoExpr handling.
close_reason: Superseded: abandoning the ported-chibicc (cc3) parser approach. Whack-a-mole on chibicc-specific desugaring gaps (Decl-emission for compiler-synthesized temps, VLA/alloca, truthiness coercion, etc. -- see slate-ozsg.8.8's notes for the running list) made clear that re-deriving what Clang's own AST already gives for free isn't worth it. New direction: parse Clang's AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input instead of both CIR and a hand-ported C frontend. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one. All completed child work (lexer/preprocessor port, parser port, node-identity, Decl hierarchy, most of the native lowerer) stays closed/done as real completed work; it's the strategy of continuing to chase chibicc-vs-Rust semantic gaps that's being dropped, not that work.

title: Fold Vec<Obj> + tag-occurrence log into a source-ordered Vec<Decl>
description: Add a post-parse pass (not a parser-internal restructuring -- keep Obj and its chibicc-derived stack-layout machinery untouched, since that's what slate-ozsg.4's parity suite just validated) that classifies each Obj by its existing is_function/is_definition/is_local flags into DeclKind::Function/Var, merges in the Record/Enum/Typedef occurrences from the tag-occurrence log, and orders the combined list by source location/declaration sequence to match how they appeared in the original source. Expose the result as Program.decls: Vec<Decl>.
acceptance_criteria: Program.decls reproduces tests/fixtures/add.c as: Function(add, definition), Function(main, definition), in source order, plus whatever the libc shim headers pull in; a struct-bearing fixture shows Record decls interleaved with function/var decls in the right source positions. lowering/rewrites profiles pass unchanged (CIR path untouched, this is additive).
close_reason: Added fold_decls(globals: &[Obj], tag_decls: &[Decl]) -> Vec<Decl> in ast.rs: maps each Obj to a Decl via obj_to_decl (is_function picks DeclKind::Function vs Var; obj.is_definition.then(...) gives Function its Option<FunctionBody>; the shared DeclAttrs is built once and reused), concatenates with the tag-occurrence log from slate-ozsg.7.3, and sorts by Decl.id. Sorting by id rather than comparing SourceLocations directly works because NodeId is one global monotonic counter (unified across Obj/Stmt/Expr/Member/tag-Decls back in slate-ozsg.6.1) assigned at the same 'declarator/tag encountered' moment for every kind -- so id order already is parse/source-encounter order, including correctly interleaving across files (headers pulled in partway through parsing land at their true position, not shoved to the end). Program.tag_decls was removed in favor of Program.decls (the merged, sorted result); wired into parse_program right before constructing the final Program, using the not-yet-taken self.globals/self.tag_decls. Verified against tests/fixtures/add.c: Function(add) then Function(main) in source order (plus interleaved string-literal Var noise, a preexisting Obj.location quirk unrelated to this task). Verified interleaving with a scratch fixture (var, struct forward-stub+definition, var, function): produced before -> S(stub) -> S(complete) -> after -> make in exact source order. Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied. This closes out slate-ozsg.7's core deliverable; .7.5 (include-chain provenance on Decl) remains.

title: Log every struct/union/enum tag occurrence, not just completions
description: parse_struct_union_decl (parser.rs ~2217) only persists a tag's Type into Program.types/scope on completion or first incomplete-stub creation; a bare forward declaration like 'struct S;' after a tag already exists in scope leaves no trace of that specific source occurrence. Add a per-occurrence log (Vec<Decl> entries, or an intermediate list the fold pass in slate-ozsg.7's other task consumes) recording one Record/Enum Decl per tag mention -- including bare forward decls -- each chained via previous_decl to the prior occurrence of that tag in the current scope chain. This is the parser-side source of truth the fold pass needs to make Program's ordered Decl list one-per-occurrence like Clang's RecordDecl mentions.
acceptance_criteria: Every struct/union/enum declaration site in a source file (forward decl or full definition) produces one logged occurrence with correct previous_decl chaining; a fixture with a struct forward-declared then defined later shows two occurrences linked by previous_decl. Existing parse behavior/output unchanged (purely additive logging).
close_reason: Added Parser::tag_decls: Vec<Decl> and last_tag_decl: HashMap<NodeId, NodeId> (type_id -> most recent Decl.id for that tag), plus a log_tag_decl helper that both structs use. Logs one occurrence at each place a struct/union tag gets a genuinely new (never-before-seen-in-this-scope) incomplete stub (is_definition: false, in both the bare-forward-ref and ensure-exists-before-members branches of parse_struct_union_decl), and one at completion (is_definition: true, previous_decl chained from the prior occurrence of the same type_id). Enums log once at their single completion point (parse_enum_specifier has no forward-decl-without-body path). Deliberately does NOT log a new occurrence when a tag is merely referenced as an already-known type (find_tag succeeds, e.g. 'struct S s;' once S is defined) -- matches Clang's RecordDecl-per-declaration-not-per-reference semantics. Exposed as Program.tag_decls (provisional name; slate-ozsg.7.4 folds this together with Obj-derived Function/Var decls into the final source-ordered Program.decls). Verified with a scratch fixture (struct S; then struct S {...} with a self-referencing member, plus an enum): produced exactly 3 occurrences -- forward decl (is_definition:false, previous_decl:None), completion (is_definition:true, previous_decl:Some(<forward decl's id>), same type_id as the forward decl per slate-ozsg.6.3's id-stability fix), and the enum (single occurrence). The self-reference inside the struct body and the later plain-use 'struct S s;' correctly produced no extra entries. Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied.

title: Define Decl/DeclKind types
description: Add a new Decl { id: NodeId, name: String, location: SourceLocation, kind: DeclKind } to ast.rs, with DeclKind::{Function, Var, Record, Enum, Typedef} carrying only the fields relevant to that kind (see slate-ozsg.7's design note for the sketch). Model definition-vs-declaration as Option<Body>/Option<Initializer> rather than an is_definition bool -- structurally distinct instead of one flag away from each other, matching Clang's inner-present-or-absent convention. Record/Enum variants carry previous_decl: Option<NodeId> to link re-declarations of the same tag in source order (populated by slate-ozsg.7's per-occurrence logging task).
acceptance_criteria: Decl/DeclKind compile with no behavior wired up yet (pure type definitions, ready for the fold pass and the per-occurrence logging task to populate).
close_reason: Defined Decl { id, name, location, kind } and DeclKind::{Function(FunctionDecl), Var(VarDecl), Record(TagOccurrence), Enum(TagOccurrence), Typedef{ty}} in ast.rs, each payload struct carrying only fields relevant to that kind (FunctionDecl has no stack-layout fields when body is None; VarDecl has no function fields at all). Shared DeclAttrs groups the four attributes (const/deprecated/nodiscard/maybe_unused) that both Function and Var use identically today. TagOccurrence{type_id, is_definition, previous_decl} is the shape slate-ozsg.7.3's per-occurrence logging will populate: type_id points into Program.types (always resolvable, even for a bare forward decl since the parser always mints/reuses a Type id), is_definition distinguishes a full '{ ... }' from a bare mention, previous_decl chains to the prior Decl.id for the same tag. Added #[derive(Default)] to every leaf struct (DeclAttrs, FunctionDecl, FunctionBody, VarDecl, TagOccurrence) per request, so callers can use ..Default::default() the way Obj construction already does; Decl/DeclKind intentionally left without Default since no variant is a sensible default kind. Pure type definitions, nothing wired up yet (that's .7.3/.7.4). Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied.

title: Track include-chain provenance in preprocessor.rs
description: lexer::File records a file's own name/file_no/display_name but not who included it. preprocessor.rs's include_file (parser.rs ~1747) tokenizes and registers the included file with no link back to the includer. Add that link: when include_file registers a new File via tokenize_file, record the includer's file_no and the SourceLocation of the #include directive (filename_tok's location) alongside it -- either as new fields on File or a parallel HashMap<usize, (usize, SourceLocation)> keyed by file_no. Expose a lookup (e.g. fn include_chain(file_no) -> Vec<File>) that walks parent links back to the primary file (file_no == 1), mirroring Clang's loc.includedFrom.
acceptance_criteria: Given a file_no for a declaration pulled in through nested #includes, the chain back to the primary translation unit file is recoverable (which header, and the location of the #include that pulled it in, at each hop). No change to preprocessing behavior/output, purely additive bookkeeping.
close_reason: Added File.included_from: Option<(usize, SourceLocation)> (parent file_no + the #include directive's location), threaded through a new tokenize_file_with_provenance helper -- tokenize_file (root TU) passes None, the new tokenize_included_file passes Some, and preprocessor.rs's include_file now calls tokenize_included_file with the includer's file_no/location instead of tokenize_file. Added lexer::include_chain(file_no) walking parent links back to the primary file. Verified against tests/fixtures/add.c via a throwaway example (not committed): printf's file_no resolves through libc-shim/include/stdio.h back to add.c with the exact #include location; add's own chain is trivially itself. Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied.

title: Restructure Obj into a Clang-like Decl hierarchy with include-chain provenance
description: slate-ozsg.6 gave every node an id/kind/location, but Obj itself is still a 27-field god object shared by function decls, function defs, globals, locals, and params -- most fields are meaningless (false/None/0) for any given kind, and several (offset, align, stack_size, alloca_bottom, va_area) are chibicc's own stack-layout bookkeeping, not source-level AST facts, left over because slate deliberately did not port codegen.rs. Compared against a real Clang -ast-dump=json RecordDecl (id, kind, loc, range, name -- nothing else), our Debug output is unusably noisy for anything downstream to consume. Also, no declaration currently records which header pulled it in; location.file_no resolves to a filename but not an include chain, so the lowerer can't ask 'is this printf decl from stdio.h' the way Clang's loc.includedFrom answers it.
design: Two independent halves that land together: (1) a Program-level, source-ordered Vec<Decl> with a DeclKind enum (Function/Var/Record/Enum/Typedef) built by a post-parse fold over the existing Vec<Obj> plus a new per-occurrence log of struct/union/enum tag declarations (including bare forward decls like 'struct S;', each linked to its previous_decl: Option<NodeId> the way Clang chains RecordDecl re-declarations) -- the existing Program.types id-keyed map stays as-is underneath for cycle resolution, this just adds an ordered, kind-discriminated view on top. Do this as a post-pass over Obj rather than restructuring the parser's internal representation: Obj/stack-layout machinery is exactly what the chibicc-parity suite (slate-ozsg.4) just validated, and touching it risks that parity. (2) include-chain tracking in preprocessor.rs's include_file: record the includer's file_no and the #include directive's SourceLocation alongside each newly registered File, so a decl's provenance can walk back to 'included from <stdio.h>:1 <- main.c:1', mirroring Clang's loc.includedFrom.
acceptance_criteria: Program exposes a source-ordered Vec<Decl> covering functions, vars, and every struct/union/enum tag occurrence (forward decls included) with previousDecl-style chaining; Decl's Debug output for a plain forward struct decl is comparable in size to the Clang JSON example (id/kind/loc/name, no chibicc stack-layout noise); every Decl can answer its include chain back to the primary translation unit file. lowering/rewrites profiles pass unchanged (CIR path untouched, this is additive).

Whack-a-mole on chibicc-specific desugaring gaps (Decl-emission for compiler-synthesized temps, VLA/alloca, truthiness coercion, etc. -- see slate-ozsg.8.8's notes for the running list) made clear that re-deriving what Clang's own AST already gives for free isn't worth it. New direction: parse Clang's AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input instead of both CIR and a hand-ported C frontend. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one. All completed child work (lexer/preprocessor port, parser port, node-identity, Decl hierarchy, most of the native lowerer) stays closed/done as real completed work; it's the strategy of continuing to chase chibicc-vs-Rust semantic gaps that's being dropped, not that work.

title: Add a Program-level id-keyed type registry backing tag resolution
description: find_tag/push_tag_scope/update_tag_in_current_scope (parser.rs ~4624-4660) clone Type by value into scope chains. This means parse_struct_union_decl's self-reference handling (parser.rs:2266) captures an incomplete stub for a struct's own pointee member that is never patched once the tag completes (parser.rs:2289 only rewrites the tag-scope copy, not prior clones already embedded in member types). struct_ref (parser.rs:3543-3560) works around this today with an ad hoc 'is_incomplete? refetch by tag name via find_tag' fallback. Add a Program-level registry (HashMap<NodeId, Type>, keyed by the Struct/Union/Enum id) that is the single source of truth: push_tag_scope/update_tag_in_current_scope write through to it, and lookups resolve through it rather than trusting whatever Type value happens to be embedded at a given AST position.
design: Depends on: Add monotonic NodeId to Obj, Stmt, Expr, and Member (same NodeId space).
acceptance_criteria: A Program-level (or parser-level, exposed on the final Program) registry maps NodeId -> Type for every struct/union/enum; update_tag_in_current_scope updates the registry entry in place so all holders of that id see the completed definition; existing lowering/rewrites fixture profiles pass unchanged.
close_reason: Added Program.types: HashMap<NodeId, Type> and a matching Parser::type_registry, written through by push_tag_scope/update_tag_in_current_scope (both call a shared register_type helper) so every push or completion of a struct/union/enum tag records the current definition under its id. Also fixed a real correctness gap found while wiring this up: Type::complete_struct/complete_union previously minted a brand-new id on completion, different from the incomplete stub's id that self-referential members (e.g. struct Node { struct Node *next; }) had already captured -- so the registry entry those members' ids pointed at would never receive the completed definition. parse_struct_union_decl now captures the in-scope stub's id before parsing members and overwrites the completed type's id to match, so a self-reference's id always resolves to the up-to-date registry entry once a consumer looks it up (wiring that lookup up is slate-ozsg.6.4). Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied.

title: Add location to Obj
description: Obj (globals, locals, functions in ast.rs) has no location field, unlike Stmt/Expr/Member which already carry SourceLocation. The declarator token position is available wherever Obj is constructed in parser.rs; thread it through.
acceptance_criteria: Obj carries a location: SourceLocation field populated at every construction site in parser.rs; cargo build clean.
close_reason: Added location: SourceLocation to Obj. Populated at all 7 construction sites in parser.rs via self.last_location() (the declaration-site convention already used for Member's anonymous-field location), including the synthetic per-param Objs built in new_function_decl's params extraction. Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied. Not wired to any consumer yet.

title: Add monotonic NodeId to Obj, Stmt, Expr, and Member
description: Stmt/Expr have kind+location but no id; Obj and Member have neither an id. Generalize the existing TYPE_ID AtomicUsize counter (ast.rs:5, currently only used by next_type_id() for Struct/Union/Enum) into a single NodeId counter shared across all AST node kinds, and add an id field to Obj, Stmt, Expr, and Member. Type::{Struct,Union,Enum}'s existing id field is reused as-is (already the right shape), just backed by the shared counter.
acceptance_criteria: Obj, Stmt, Expr, Member each carry an id: NodeId field, populated at construction time in parser.rs; cargo build clean; no fixture regressions (ids are additive, not yet consumed by anything).
close_reason: Added a shared NodeId counter (renamed from TYPE_ID/next_type_id) and threaded id fields through Obj, Stmt, Expr, and Member; all construction sites in parser.rs populate it via next_node_id(). Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied. Lowering not yet wired to consume it (expected, per slate-ozsg.6.3/.6.4).

title: Add stable node identity (id/kind/location) to src/parse AST
description: The eventual native lowerer (slate-ozsg's end goal) needs to consume src/parse::ast::Program directly, but today only Stmt/Expr carry an id-shaped kind+location; Obj (functions/globals/locals) has neither, and Type::{Struct,Union,Enum}'s id is used only for equality, not lookup. Worse: struct/union tag resolution clones Type by value (find_tag/push_tag_scope), so a self-referencing struct's pointee member (parser.rs:2266) captures a permanently-stale incomplete stub once the tag is later completed (parser.rs:2289 only patches the tag-scope copy). The parser papers over this today with an ad hoc is_incomplete-refetch-by-name fallback in struct_ref (parser.rs:3543-3560); a standalone lowerer has no equivalent scope to fall back to. Reshape the AST so every node is addressable by a stable id and cyclical/repeated declarations are referenced by id instead of by a possibly-stale value copy, mirroring how Clang's own -ast-dump=json models repeated declarations (full body on first mention, id-only stub thereafter).
design: One monotonic NodeId space (generalizing the existing TYPE_ID atomic counter) assigned to every Obj, Stmt, Expr, Member, and Type::{Struct,Union,Enum}. Add a Program-level registry (HashMap<NodeId, Type>) that push_tag_scope/update_tag_in_current_scope write through, so a struct/union/enum has exactly one canonical, always-current Type value; self-referential member/pointee positions store the id and resolve through the registry instead of embedding a clone. Obj gains a location field (currently absent). Stmt/Expr keep their existing kind+location shape (StmtKind/ExprKind enum variants already serve as 'kind') and just gain id. Var/Call references (ExprKind::Var{idx,is_local}) already reference by index rather than cloning — leave that scheme as-is unless it turns out to need unifying with the new NodeId space.
acceptance_criteria: Every Obj/Stmt/Expr/Member carries a NodeId; Obj carries a location; struct/union/enum resolution goes through a single Program-level id-keyed registry with no remaining is_incomplete-refetch-by-name workarounds (struct_ref and any similar call sites simplify to a registry lookup); a differential fixture with a self-referencing struct (linked-list style) proves the pointee's member list is never stale. lowering/rewrites profiles still pass unchanged (CIR path untouched).
close_reason: Superseded: abandoning the ported-chibicc (cc3) parser approach. Whack-a-mole on chibicc-specific desugaring gaps (Decl-emission for compiler-synthesized temps, VLA/alloca, truthiness coercion, etc. -- see slate-ozsg.8.8's notes for the running list) made clear that re-deriving what Clang's own AST already gives for free isn't worth it. New direction: parse Clang's AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input instead of both CIR and a hand-ported C frontend. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one. All completed child work (lexer/preprocessor port, parser port, node-identity, Decl hierarchy, most of the native lowerer) stays closed/done as real completed work; it's the strategy of continuing to chase chibicc-vs-Rust semantic gaps that's being dropped, not that work.

title: Recursive-descent parser stack-overflows on deeply nested input (deep_ast.c)
description: tests/fixtures/deep_ast.c crashes the process with a real stack overflow ('thread main has overflowed its stack, fatal runtime error') rather than a parse error. cc3's parser.rs is a plain recursive-descent parser with no explicit depth limiting, so sufficiently nested expressions/statements blow the native OS thread stack. This is a crash-class bug, same severity concern as the long-double panic above (slate-ozsg.4.4) — uncontrolled crashes are worse than clean parse failures for any batch tooling built on top of this frontend.
design: Two options worth weighing: (1) run parsing on a thread with an explicitly large stack (cheap, doesn't fix the underlying unboundedness, just raises the ceiling), or (2) add an explicit recursion-depth counter that bails cleanly past some threshold in the hot recursive paths (expression precedence climbing, statement blocks). Check what depth deep_ast.c actually needs before picking a fixed stack size.
acceptance_criteria: deep_ast.c either parses successfully or fails with a clean CompileError (e.g. 'expression nesting too deep') — never a stack overflow abort.
notes: Fixed via the 'run on a bigger-stack thread' option from the design note: added parse_native_tokens() in api.rs which spawns parse::parser::parse() on a std::thread with a 256MB stack (Token/Program/CompileError have no interior-mutability types, so all Send, no Sync-safety concerns). deep_ast.c's 128-deep nested-paren expression (from STEP_8's 2^7 macro-expanded STEP_1 applications) now parses successfully end-to-end (OK: 141 globals) rather than crashing -- didn't need the depth-limit-with-clean-bail alternative since a modest stack bump was enough for every fixture in the corpus. native-frontend-report: 323/332 (up from 322; deep_ast.c off the failing list, no new failures). cargo fmt/clippy clean. Root unboundedness (arbitrarily deep input could still theoretically exceed even 256MB) is unchanged, but matches this ticket's acceptance bar and how real recursive-descent parsers (e.g. rustc's own parser) typically handle this class of pathological input.
close_reason: Stack overflow fixed by running the native parser on a large-stack thread; deep_ast.c now parses cleanly.

title: Fix long double literal parsing panic ('Invalid size: 16' at parser.rs:5638)
description: long_double_literal_edge.c and long_double_literal_precision.c crash the process (Rust panic, not a CompileError) at src/parse/parser.rs:5638 with 'Invalid size: 16' — some code path pattern-matches on a type's size() and doesn't handle LDouble's 16-byte size. This is a real crash, not just an unimplemented-feature error, so it should be prioritized above ordinary parse-error gaps: a panic in native-frontend-report or any future batch tooling is more disruptive than a clean failure. long_double.c and float128.c ('invalid numeric constant') may be related — check together, they're all in the long-double/f80/f128 literal family.
design: Read the match/switch at parser.rs:5638 that panics on size 16 — it's almost certainly missing an LDouble (or LDoubleComplex, 32 bytes) arm rather than needing new logic.
acceptance_criteria: long_double_literal_edge.c and long_double_literal_precision.c parse (or fail cleanly with a CompileError, never panic) via 'slate parse-only'. No fixture in tests/fixtures crashes the process.
notes: Fixed properly (not just patched around the panic): long double literals now carry their exact 80-bit x87 value through the AST instead of round-tripping through f64.
