Added TokenKind::Num.ldouble: Option<X87DoubleExtended> (lexer.rs), populated by parsing the literal's cleaned source text directly via rustc_apfloat's X87DoubleExtended FromStr (which natively handles both decimal and C99 hex-float syntax) when the suffix is L/l -- no f64 intermediate, so precision beyond f64's 52-bit mantissa (e.g. 0x1.0000000000000001p0L, 3.141592653589793238462643383279L) survives intact. The parser wraps this into a new ExprKind::LDoubleLiteral{value: X87DoubleExtended} (ast.rs), mirroring the existing BigIntLiteral{raw} precedent for _BitInt. write_gvar_data's new Type::LDouble branch writes value.to_bits() directly into the 16-byte global-init buffer (10 significant bytes + 6 zero-padding) when the initializer is a literal -- verified bit-exact against clang's own compiled output for both long_double_literal_edge.c and long_double_literal_precision.c (memcpy'd bytes match exactly). For non-literal long-double constant expressions (e.g. computed via +/-/*), eval_double still folds through f64 as before (a pre-existing ceiling on constant-folding precision, not attempted here) and write_gvar_data falls back to reparsing that f64's shortest round-trip decimal as X87DoubleExtended. Also generalized read_buf/write_buf to handle any size (not just 1/2/4/8) instead of panicking, so no future oversized-type initializer can crash the process. native-frontend-report: still 322/332 (same as before minus these two now-passing fixtures); the remaining 10 failures are unrelated clean CompileErrors or the already-tracked deep_ast.c stack overflow (slate-ozsg.4.6). cargo fmt/clippy clean.
close_reason: Panic fixed; long double global-initializer literals now parse cleanly, no crashes remain in tests/fixtures.

title: Register/special-case GNU and clang builtin functions the native frontend treats as undeclared
description: cc3's parser hard-rejects calls to any identifier with no prior declaration ('implicit declaration of a function', src/parse/parser.rs:3505) — correct strict behavior for ordinary functions, but it also blocks the many __builtin_* compiler intrinsics real C code calls without an explicit declaration. Only 'alloca' is registered today (declare_builtin_functions, parser.rs:142) and __builtin_types_compatible_p is special-cased (parser.rs:3390) as the only precedent for polymorphic-signature builtins. Affected fixtures, all currently failing with exactly this error: atomic_explicit_orderings.c, control_flow_builtin_ops.c, gnu_builtin_addressof.c, gnu_builtin_atomic_flag.c, gnu_builtin_debugtrap.c, gnu_builtin_return_address.c, gnu_builtin_source.c, integer_bit_builtin_ops.c, long_double_complex.c, math_builtin_ops.c, mem_bcopy_overlap.c, mem_bitcast_copy.c, mem_bzero.c, mem_memchr.c, memchr_nullable_pointer.c, target_stack_builtin_ops.c, complex.c, complex_equality.c, complex_lvalue.c, stdlib_complex_cx_limited_range.c, constant_object_query_ops.c, overflow_scalar_ops.c.
design: Biggest single cluster of remaining native-frontend parse failures (~22/43). Worth doing before the smaller family-specific bugs since it likely also unblocks parts of the atomics and complex-number families listed separately below once headers stop hitting this first.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed fixture parses via 'slate parse-only'. Fixed-signature builtins (memcpy/memset-family, __builtin_expect, __builtin_clz-family, __builtin_return_address, __builtin_debugtrap, etc.) get real declarations in declare_builtin_functions(); polymorphic ones (__builtin_add/sub/mul_overflow, __builtin_constant_p, __builtin_object_size, __builtin_complex) get parser special-cases following the __builtin_types_compatible_p pattern at parser.rs:3390.
close_reason: All 22 fixtures now parse. Registered ~35 fixed-signature builtins (bit-counting, bswap/rotate, libm, memcpy-family, source-location, control-flow hints, __atomic_test_and_set/__atomic_clear) via a new push_builtin_fn() helper in declare_builtin_functions(). Special-cased the 5 genuinely polymorphic ones in the primary-expression parser (matching the existing __builtin_types_compatible_p/__builtin_compare_and_swap pattern): __builtin_add/sub/mul_overflow (lowered to '*result = a op b, 0' as a parsing-only stand-in -- real overflow detection needs a lowerer that doesn't exist yet), __builtin_complex (Comma of the imaginary part discarded + a Cast of the real part to the right *Complex type), __builtin_bit_cast (represented as an ordinary Cast), __builtin_addressof (Addr). Also fixed two adjacent gaps found along the way: is_lvalue() didn't accept __real__/__imag__ expressions as assignment targets (blocked complex_lvalue.c), and stdatomic.h/preprocessor init_macros() were missing the _explicit compare-exchange macros and __ATOMIC_* ordering constants (blocked atomic_explicit_orderings.c, gnu_builtin_atomic_flag.c). Also fixed CompileError's Display to include line:column -- it was silently dropping the location it already carried, which had been slowing down every diagnosis in this epic.

title: Drive src/parse frontend to 100% parity with the CIR frontend
description: Using the parity test command from slate-ozsg.3, fix bugs uncovered in the ported lexer/preprocessor/parser and wire any missing lowerer support for AST shapes that differ from CIR's op-tree, until every currently-passing CIR-frontend differential fixture also passes through --frontend=chibicc. File individual fixture regressions as child bugs under this epic as they're found rather than batching them into one issue.
design: Blocked on slate-ozsg.3. This is expected to be the largest and longest-running sub-epic; track it fixture-family by fixture-family rather than as one monolithic pass.
acceptance_criteria: 100% of tests/fixtures/*.c differential tests (lowering + rewrites profiles) pass under the chibicc frontend, matching current CIR-frontend pass rate.
close_reason: Superseded: abandoning the ported-chibicc (cc3) parser approach. Whack-a-mole on chibicc-specific desugaring gaps (Decl-emission for compiler-synthesized temps, VLA/alloca, truthiness coercion, etc. -- see slate-ozsg.8.8's notes for the running list) made clear that re-deriving what Clang's own AST already gives for free isn't worth it. New direction: parse Clang's AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input instead of both CIR and a hand-ported C frontend. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one. All completed child work (lexer/preprocessor port, parser port, node-identity, Decl hierarchy, most of the native lowerer) stays closed/done as real completed work; it's the strategy of continuing to chase chibicc-vs-Rust semantic gaps that's being dropped, not that work.

title: Wire src/parse as an alternate frontend behind a CLI flag
description: Expose a new frontend selector (e.g. --frontend=chibicc alongside today's CIR-based default) and a new test command/harness that runs the differential fixture suite through the src/parse frontend instead of clang+CIR. Reuse the existing lowering pipeline (src/frontend/lowerer.rs and submodules) where the ported AST shape allows; this issue is about plumbing the two frontends side by side, not about reaching parity yet.
design: Blocked on slate-ozsg.2 (needs a working parser producing Program). Keep the CIR frontend as the default/untouched baseline throughout — this is additive plumbing, not a replacement yet.
acceptance_criteria: New CLI flag selects src/parse as the frontend; a new test command runs tests/fixtures/*.c through it end to end and reports pass/fail counts, independent of and comparable against the existing CIR-frontend baseline.
close_reason: Wired src/parse as a selectable frontend and added a parity-measurement tool. Concretely: api::parse_native()/translate_native() (translate_native parses via the new frontend, sets libc-shim include paths from cir::emit::libc_shim_dir(), then returns Error::NativeLoweringUnimplemented since .4 hasn't built a lowerer for the new AST yet — no pretending). CLI: 'translate --frontend native <file.c>' selects it (default stays cir, clang passthrough args unaffected); new 'parse-only <file.c>' subcommand runs frontend-only and reports OK/error via exit code; new 'native-frontend-report [dir]' subcommand spawns parse-only as a subprocess per *.c fixture (default tests/fixtures) and tallies pass/fail — subprocess-per-fixture is required, not just convenient, because src/parse's include-path/file-registry state (BASE_FILE OnceLock etc.) is process-global and latches to the first file if reused across a loop. Baseline measured: 5/332 tests/fixtures/*.c parse cleanly today. That number plus the failing-file list is .4's starting point.

title: Port cc3 parser + AST into src/parse
description: Port ~/Projects/cc3's src/parser.rs (recursive-descent parser, parse()/const_expr()) and src/ast.rs (Program/Obj/Member/Stmt/StmtKind/Expr/ExprKind/Type) into slate's src/parse/. cc3's AST is already fully resolved: struct/union layout with bitfields, VLAs, atomics (Cas/Exch), _BitInt(N), complex numbers, inline asm, goto/labels/switch with case ranges. Expose Program as the structured frontend output; do not port codegen.rs (cc3 walks this AST to emit its own assembly, which slate does not need — slate's lowerer will walk it to emit Rust instead).
design: Depends on the lexer/preprocessor port for its Vec<Token> input.
acceptance_criteria: src/parse::parse(tokens) -> Program compiles and runs standalone against representative fixtures; size/align/offset queries the lowerer currently gets from CIR (src/cir/ir.rs) are all recoverable from the ported Type/Member types.
notes: parser.rs and ast.rs are already copied into src/parse as a byproduct of .1 (preprocessor.rs calls parser::const_expr directly, so it couldn't be separated). Remaining scope here: confirm Program is fully exposed the way lowerer.rs needs, decide whether to strip cc3's codegen-prep bindings (Obj::offset/stack_size/alloca_bottom/va_area, Call::ret_buffer, Vla::size_var — kept as-is from the raw copy, unused by anything yet).
close_reason: Program is fully exposed: added src/parse::parse_file(path) tying lexer::tokenize_file -> preprocessor::preprocess -> parser::parse into one entry point. Verified end-to-end against a real fixture (tests/fixtures/add.c) with libc-shim/include on the search path via preprocessor::set_include_paths — it runs the full pipeline and reaches a real parse error deep in a transitively-included header (CompileError at file_no 82), confirming the wiring works and giving .4 a first concrete parity bug to chase. Left the codegen-prep bindings (Obj::offset/stack_size/alloca_bottom/va_area, Call::ret_buffer, Vla::size_var) untouched — stripping them is cleanup, not blocking, deferred to whenever .3/.4 touches that code.

title: Port cc3 lexer + preprocessor into src/parse
description: Port ~/Projects/cc3's src/lexer.rs (tokenize_file/tokenize_builtin/tokenize_string_literal/tokenize) and src/preprocessor.rs (preprocess, directive handling: #include, #define, #if/#ifdef family, #pragma, search_include_paths) into slate's src/parse/. Adapt cc3's CompileError/SourceLocation types to slate's existing error and location conventions where the two need to interoperate (slate's diagnostics currently key off Clang AST source points in src/frontend/c_ast.rs's Loc/SourcePoint).
design: Do not port codegen.rs or main.rs. Keep directive/pragma recognition at parity with cc3 rather than reusing slate's existing src/frontend/preprocess.rs (which only records directive activity for diagnostics and still shells out to clang for actual preprocessing).
acceptance_criteria: src/parse::tokenize/preprocess compiles standalone and tokenizes+macro-expands a representative sample of tests/fixtures/*.c identically to cc3's own behavior on the same inputs.
close_reason: Ported lexer.rs, preprocessor.rs into src/parse (plus parser.rs/ast.rs, pulled in by preprocessor's direct dependency on parser::const_expr for #if evaluation and both files' dependency on ast::Type). Compiles clean across the whole crate. Codegen-prep bindings in ast.rs (Obj::offset/stack_size/alloca_bottom/va_area, Call::ret_buffer, Vla::size_var) left in place, untested, flagged for removal consideration in .2/.3.

title: Replace ClangIR frontend with ported chibicc (cc3) parser
description: The C frontend currently depends on a custom CLANG_ENABLE_CIR clang build for CIR emission plus a separately-built macro-dump-plugin (also requires building against system clang) for macro provenance. CIR's format also churns across clang versions, and both build requirements block shipping a portable single binary. Port the lexer/preprocessor/parser/AST from ~/Projects/cc3 (a mature from-scratch Rust chibicc reimplementation: lexer.rs 2022 lines, preprocessor.rs 2197 lines, parser.rs 6554 lines, ast.rs 702 lines) into src/parse as a new, self-contained C frontend. This removes both custom-clang build requirements, makes the shipped slate binary self-contained (clang remains only as a differential correctness oracle in tests, not a runtime dependency), and — since we'd own the parser — lets us add GCC-semantics compliance for the ~500 gcc-torture-suite tests currently excluded because clang doesn't execute them the same way gcc does.
design: Source: ~/Projects/cc3 (Rust chibicc port). Only port lexer.rs, preprocessor.rs, parser.rs, ast.rs — do NOT port codegen.rs (2953 lines, emits its own asm, not needed) or main.rs (CLI-specific glue). Target: src/parse in this repo, exposing cc3's Program/Obj/Stmt/Expr/Type as the structured output src/frontend/lowerer.rs will eventually consume instead of the CIR op-tree (src/cir/ir.rs's Module/Op/Region/Block).
acceptance_criteria: src/parse exists as a working lexer+preprocessor+parser+typed-AST frontend ported from ~/Projects/cc3; it is wired in as a selectable frontend and driven to 100% parity with the existing CIR-based differential fixture suite; a documented plan exists for recovering the previously gcc-excluded tests.
close_reason: Superseded: abandoning the ported-chibicc (cc3) parser approach in favor of parsing Clang's own AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input. See slate-ozsg.8.8's closing note for full rationale. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one.

title: gcc-torture: runtime exit-code mismatches after clang/CIR upgrade (uncategorized)
description:
7 previously-supported gcc-torture fixtures now translate and compile, but their compiled Rust binary's exit code no longer matches the C reference's (mostly Rust exit=None, meaning the binary crashed/aborted rather than exiting normally, plus one plain mismatch).

Cases and observed symptom:
  20021118-1: exit code differs, C=Some(0) Rust=None
  20040703-1: exit code differs, C=Some(0) Rust=None
  921123-2: exit code differs, C=Some(0) Rust=None
  931004-11: exit code differs, C=Some(0) Rust=None
  950628-1: exit code differs, C=Some(0) Rust=None
  990525-1: exit code differs, C=Some(0) Rust=None
  pr57130: exit code differs, C=Some(0) Rust=None

None of these have been individually root-caused yet -- filed as a single bucket pending per-case triage. Reproduce one case with SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=<case> cargo nextest r --release --test gcc_torture_suite -E 'test(gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c)' --nocapture. Note 931004-11 is distinct from the already-tracked 931004-10/12/14/2/4/6/8 in slate-os0h.3.1.40 (va_arg aggregate reconstruction) -- confirm whether it shares that root cause or is a separate bug before assuming so.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 7 cases is individually triaged: either fixed (translates, compiles, matches C stdout/exit code) or re-filed as its own focused ticket with a confirmed root cause if it turns out to be a distinct bug from the others in this bucket.
close_reason:
Fixed all 7 cases via two root-cause fixes:

1. Alignment tracking for record-typed "coerce" ABI-bridging locals. type_alignment()
   (src/frontend/lowerer.rs) returned a hardcoded 1 for any Type::Custom (record) because
   it has no field layout to consult, so every caller comparing a CIR-supplied alignment
   against it explicitly excluded Type::Custom from the over-alignment check
   (`!matches!(ty, Type::Custom(_))`), meaning a record-typed local was NEVER wrapped to
   satisfy a higher CIR-declared alignment. Added effective_type_alignment(), which looks
   up the record's true natural alignment via the existing record_natural_align() (used
   elsewhere for sizeof/alignof), and wired it into the two real call sites (the standalone
   alloca path in storage.rs, and collect_global in lowerer.rs -- the alloca-group path
   never sees Custom types, already filtered out upstream). Fixes 20021118-1, 20040703-1,
   921123-2, 950628-1, 990525-1, pr57130, and (as a byproduct, since it also affects
   over-aligned globals) pr22141-2 plus unblocked 4 more previously-unsupported fixtures
   (20010518-2, 20050215-1, 20090113-1, pr44164).

2. bitint::{BInt,BUint}<N,LIMBS> wrapper types are always u64-limb-backed (align 8)
   regardless of the requested bit width N, but CIR's own alignment for the coercion
   buffer reflects the *natural* C representation (e.g. align 4 for a 24-bit-in-one-
   eightbyte coercion), which can be narrower. Reading such a buffer through a reinterpret
   pointer cast to a bitint type was therefore doing a plain (aligned) dereference on a
   pointer the wrapper type's own alignment requirement disallowed. Fixed by routing loads
   whose CIR result type maps to a bitint::{BInt,BUint} generic through
   std::ptr::read_unaligned instead of a plain deref, in lower_load's fallback branch
   (src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs). Fixes 931004-11.

3. Found and fixed a third, related gap while verifying #1 against the wider corpus:
   address_expr()'s global branch (src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs) built
   std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(*global) for any over-aligned static/global (now correctly
   Aligned<>-wrapped per fix #1) without wrapping the expression in unsafe, even though
   dereferencing through the Aligned wrapper's Deref impl requires it (unlike a bare
   addr_of_mut!(global), which the macro exempts). This surfaced as a regression on
   pr22141-2 while re-verifying the full suite -- now fixed alongside the others.

All 7 originally-listed cases plus pr22141-2 and 4 additional previously-unsupported
fixtures now translate, compile, and match the C reference. Full gcc_torture_suite
(both supported-match and unsupported-still-fail) is clean except for the 6 already-
tracked va_arg aggregate-reconstruction cases in slate-os0h.3.1.40.

title: gcc-torture: regressions from clang/CIR toolchain upgrade
description: A recent clang/CIR toolchain pull (see commit 943ed2e6 'new changes for long double that came in from updating clang ir version') appears to have regressed a batch of previously-supported gcc-torture fixtures. Running the full (unfiltered) gcc_torture_suite test -- not filtered to a single fixture via SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE -- surfaces 19 distinct failing fixtures aggregated into one test failure, most of which are NOT explained by any in-progress work this session and were presumably passing at some earlier point since they live in tests/fixtures.gcc-torture/ (the supported directory). Filed as three child buckets by symptom; see each for details.

title: gcc-torture: disambiguate colliding anonymous-struct names between AST and CIR-derived records
acceptance_criteria: The mix() repro above translates, compiles, and matches the C reference's stdout and exit code (no SIGSEGV, no garbage). Anonymous-struct naming no longer silently collides across unrelated AST- and CIR-derived records in the same translation unit -- either by disambiguating names or by detecting and correctly resolving shape conflicts. Existing gcc-torture and long-double-complex fixtures relying on anon_struct-shaped coercion (20081103-1, pr87053, 920625-1, pr44575) continue to pass.
notes:
Root cause was NOT a name collision -- corrected diagnosis.

Re-investigated with the exact mix() repro from the description. Instrumented
lower_with_project (temporarily) to print any AST-derived (c.records) entry
named "anon_struct" alongside the CIR-derived one before the merge: for this
repro, and for the real long_double_complex.c fixture, there was NO AST-side
"anon_struct" entry at all. Only the CIR-derived one existed, and it *already*
had the wrong fields (i32, i32) at the point anon_local_records() built it --
before the AST/CIR merge in lower_with_project ever ran.

Actual bug: cir_type_to_ctype() (src/frontend/lowerer/types.rs) recognizes
long double member types only via is_long_double(), which requires the
"!cir.long_double<...>" wrapper. The x86-64 SysV ABI return-coercion struct
for `_Complex long double` (`!rec_anon_struct = !cir.struct<{data !cir.f80,
data !cir.f80}>`) spells its member type as the bare "!cir.f80", not wrapped
-- the same bare-spelling gap already fixed for
is_complex_long_double_coercion_type() in the ctanl/ctanhl fix (see
slate-os0h.3.1.8/.16). cir_type_to_ctype() had the same gap in a different
call site (anon_local_records' field-type decoding) and fell through to the
generic default `CType::Int { signed: true, bits: 32 }`, producing (i32, i32)
instead of (f80, f80).

Fix: added `|| ty == "!cir.f80"` alongside is_long_double() in
cir_type_to_ctype() (one line). mix() now translates, compiles, and matches C
stdout/exit (verified via SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=long_double_complex). No SIGSEGV,
no garbage.

Searched for a genuine collision to justify the original theory: instrumented
the records.entry(name).or_insert_with(...) merge point in lowerer.rs to flag
any case where an AST-derived record and a CIR-derived record share a
sanitized name but have different field shapes (count or type-level, via
CType's derived PartialEq). Ran this across the entire test corpus
(differential, gcc-torture supported, c-testsuite supported, chibicc
supported, full libc-shim suite -- lowering + rewrites + libc nextest
profiles). Zero collisions detected anywhere in the corpus, with or without
the fix applied.

Conclusion: the AST-vs-CIR merge-order "first wins" behavior
(or_insert_with) is still structurally fragile in principle, but there is no
live evidence it causes any observed bug today, and speculatively rebuilding
it without a reproducing case would be scope creep. Recommend closing this
ticket as resolved by the cir_type_to_ctype fix; if a genuine shape collision
ever surfaces (different repro), it should get its own ticket with a concrete
failing case rather than reopening this one on a disproven theory.
close_reason: Root cause was a missing bare-!cir.f80 case in cir_type_to_ctype (types.rs), not an AST/CIR anon-struct name collision. Fixed with one line; mix() repro now passes end-to-end. Exhaustively searched the full test corpus for genuine shape collisions under the or_insert_with merge and found none.

title: gcc-torture: lower cir.fmuladd (fused multiply-add intrinsic)
description:
Why: Clang lowers fused-multiply-add patterns (from __builtin_fma or FP-contraction of a*b+c) to a dedicated cir.fmuladd op, distinct from an ordinary fma() library call. Slate's lowerer has no handler for it at all -- hits emit_todo("cir.fmuladd") unconditionally, producing an unresolved-SSA-reference compile error at every call site (todo!() emits the todo statement but never materializes the result, so downstream uses of that value reference a nonexistent local).

Cases: cbrt, pr58574 (128 occurrences in pr58574 alone -- a big table of FMA-based math routines).

Reproduce: SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=cbrt cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test gcc_torture_suite -E 'test(gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c)' --nocapture

This is a distinct gap from slate-04q.47.6 (idiomatizing __builtin_fma/hypot/fdim/cbrt as explicit library-call builtins under a different epic) -- that ticket is about recognizing fma() as a call; this one is about the compiler-synthesized cir.fmuladd op that Clang emits for contracted a*b+c expressions regardless of whether fma() was called explicitly.

Discovered while running the full lowering profile test suite for the first time this session, unrelated to the long-double/complex-long-double work in progress at the time.
acceptance_criteria: cbrt and pr58574 translate, compile, and match the C reference's stdout/exit code; both promoted into tests/fixtures.gcc-torture/; cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test gcc_torture_suite passes for both.
close_reason: Already implemented in 7f50e2963 (cir.fmuladd -> CirOpKind::Fma -> lower_ternary_method mul_add); verified cbrt and pr58574 both translate and pass individually

title: Preserve aggregate types in long-double link shim generation
description: The ignored link_fixture_runs_match_c test reconstructs C shims from mangled names through render_shim_c_source_for_names. Aggregate arguments and returns are tagged x, reconstructed as void *, and ext_box_roundtrip/ext_nested_roundtrip/ext_pair_make are called without typed prototypes. Use typed program signature data for the link harness or otherwise preserve record signatures.
acceptance_criteria: link_fixture_runs_match_c is unignored and passes end-to-end; generated C shims declare and pass ld_box, ld_pair, and ld_nested by value with the correct ABI; existing long-double project/cross-TU tests remain green.
notes: Implemented typed aggregate shim generation, exact AST floating-literal facts, macro spelling/expansion CallSiteLoc joins, and long-double extern function-pointer shims. Unchanged link suite passes long_double, long_double_callback, and long_double_aggregate.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with the full release lowering profile

title: Promote newly passing GCC torture fixtures and enable the unsupported guard
description: The ignored gcc_torture_unsupported_tests_still_fail check now identifies 76 of 210 unsupported fixtures that pass end-to-end. Promote those fixtures, update TRIAGE.md and affected child-bead case lists/status, then remove the ignore so future newly supported cases fail the regular rewrites profile.
acceptance_criteria: All 76 identified fixtures are in tests/fixtures.gcc-torture; the supported suite passes; the unsupported invariant is no longer ignored and passes; TRIAGE.md maps only remaining unsupported cases.
close_reason: Promoted 76 fixtures, updated the 134-case triage index, and enabled the passing unsupported-bucket guard

title: Emit ABI-correct strfroml C shim prototype
description: The generated long-double C shim redeclares strfroml with void pointers and unsigned long long, conflicting with stdlib.h's char pointers and size_t.
acceptance_criteria: The generated declaration matches int strfroml(char *, size_t, const char *, long double), and the cross-TU C23 strfrom library integration test passes.
notes: Generalized after initial closure: ABI repair now reads Clang-declared function type spellings for all externs and restores pointer-sized typedefs and pointer constness. strfroml is only coverage, not a repair special case. GNU malloc/obstack coverage exercises the same path.
close_reason: Added trusted function signature repair registry shared by extern and long-double shim lowering; strfroml prototype and integration pass

title: Restore long-double stdlib and variadic shim declarations
description: The rewrites profile fails stdlib complex/functions and strtold probes and long_double_variadic because required f80 runtime declarations are absent or inconsistent after rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: The complex/functions and strtold probes compile and pass; long_double_variadic declares and links its printf/scanf f80 shims; the focused differential tests pass.
close_reason: Restored long-double shim declarations; stdlib strtold and long-double variadic regression now pass

title: Keep goto dispatch state in scope for c-testsuite case 00051
description: The rewrites profile emits case_00051 state assignments and a continue outside the generated dispatch loop, producing undeclared state and label errors.
acceptance_criteria: case_00051 generates a scoped dispatch loop and c_testsuite_supported_tests_match_c passes.
close_reason: Rejected goto structuring when a dispatch-arm prefix still writes the state variable inside nested control flow, preserving the correct fallback state machine for case_00051. The full c-testsuite run no longer reports case_00051; remaining failures are separate runtime signature work.

title: Fix mutable bitfield parameter stores in gcc-torture rewrites
description: The rewrites profile fails gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c because generated functions mutate bitfield storage through by-value parameters emitted without mut. Affected cases include 930126-1, pr110166-1, and bf64-1.
acceptance_criteria: The affected generated Rust parameters are mutable when written; the focused gcc-torture supported suite passes without changing C behavior.
close_reason: Preserved mutability for parameters whose generated bitfield storage receives a setter call. Verified 930126-1, pr110166-1, and bf64-1 with focused rewrites-profile gcc-torture runs.

title: Expose rewrite failures by resolving generated-Rust warnings
description: Capture the current rewrites-profile warning set. Add narrowly scoped allow attributes for intentional C-to-Rust artifacts, fix diagnostics that reveal invalid ABI types or unsafe runtime declarations, and rerun the profile to reveal the underlying failures.
acceptance_criteria: The rewrites profile output is no longer obscured by known generated-Rust warnings, valid diagnostics are fixed instead of allowed, and all remaining failing tests are enumerated under the epic.
close_reason: Added targeted generated-Rust lint allows, corrected trusted runtime ABI signatures and unsafe C function pointers, and preserved string rewrites across repaired size_t boundaries

title: Fix failing rewrite differential tests
description: Restore the rewrites profile by first eliminating generated-Rust warning noise, then triaging and fixing every exposed compile or differential failure. Legitimate ABI and safety diagnostics must be corrected rather than suppressed.
acceptance_criteria: cargo nextest r --release --profile rewrites --no-fail-fast passes; generated Rust has targeted allow attributes only for intentional translation artifacts; invalid runtime symbol types and safety declarations are corrected; cargo fmt and cargo clippy pass.
close_reason: All six rewrite failures resolved; full rewrites profile, formatting, and release clippy pass

title: Prevent rustc stack exhaustion in generated stress builds
description:
## Problem
The dense and serial temporary-chain fixtures translate successfully, but nightly rustc overflows its stack while producing DWARF for the generated programs. Affected fixtures: dense_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time and serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run either fixture through SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE and generated_differential under the lowering profile. rustc terminates with SIGSEGV in DwarfCompileUnit scope construction and recommends RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216.
design: Disable debug information in generated batch crates with profile.dev debug = 0. These crates exist only for compile-and-run differential checks, so their DWARF is unused. Measurement showed raw Slate translation completes in about 0.14 seconds and the same generated dense program compiles on the default rustc stack when debug info is disabled; the failure was LLVM recursive DWARF scope emission, not Slate value-graph complexity.
acceptance_criteria: Both stress fixtures compile, run, and differentially match C through generated_differential in the lowering profile, while their dedicated translation-time bounds continue to pass.
notes: The lowering representation maps CIR SSA ids through a BTreeMap<String, Val> to Rust AST expressions/locals; it is a flat SSA name map, not a polynomial expression or union-find graph. Dense raw lowering emits 3217 Rust temporaries and roughly 402 unsafe scopes; serial emits 6759 temporaries. Both differential fixtures pass with generated-crate debug info disabled, and their bounded translation tests pass under the release lowering profile. cargo fmt, release clippy, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Generated differential crates omit unused DWARF, so both stress fixtures compile and match C without increasing rustc stack size.

title: Initialize goto-crossing VLAs after size evaluation
description:
## Problem
Goto dispatch hoists a dynamic alloca initializer above the SSA value that computes its length. Affected fixture: c-testsuite case_00207.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test c_testsuite_suite -E "test(c_testsuite_supported_tests_match_c)" --nocapture. case_00207 emits a Vec length using an undeclared temporary before the argc-derived size is materialized in dispatch state zero.
design: When a VLA must be hoisted for dispatch, declare empty storage before the dispatch loop and allocate or resize it at the original cir.alloca position after the size operand is available. Preserve the pointer binding used by later blocks.
acceptance_criteria: case_00207 compiles and differentially matches C under the lowering profile. Generated Rust never references a VLA size temporary before its declaration.
notes: Follow-up: only dispatch-prepass dynamic allocas are initialized empty; ordinary dynamic allocas encountered inside a dispatch state retain direct sized initialization. Genuinely hoisted VLAs call Vec::resize at the original cir.alloca, retaining capacity across goto loops. case_00207, 20040811-1, pr43220, and the full c-testsuite pass under lowering; cargo fmt, release clippy, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Hoisted VLAs resize after count evaluation while non-hoisted VLAs retain sized initialization, covering goto correctness and stress behavior.

title: Box aggregate varargs for internal variadic functions
description:
## Problem
Rust VaList::next_arg cannot retrieve arbitrary structs because aggregate types do not implement the sealed VaArgSafe trait. Affected fixture: c-testsuite case_00204.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test c_testsuite_suite -E "test(c_testsuite_supported_tests_match_c)" --nocapture. case_00204 fails for s7, s9, and the homogeneous floating aggregate record types passed through myprintf.
design: Use the existing boxed variadic representation for internal, non-address-taken variadic definitions and their direct generated call sites. Preserve true C ABI variadics for externally visible or address-taken functions.
acceptance_criteria: case_00204 compiles and differentially matches C under raw lowering, including structure and homogeneous floating aggregate varargs. Externally callable variadic definitions retain their C ABI.
notes: Follow-up: full lowering gate found vprintf-1 cannot use boxed arguments because its va_list is passed to external vprintf. Box eligibility now excludes any variadic definition with a call operand typed as va_list. Focused vprintf-1 and the full c-testsuite pass under lowering, preserving both native forwarding and case_00204 aggregate boxing.
close_reason: Boxed internal varargs are restricted to functions that do not forward va_list to native C ABI consumers.

title: Avoid parameter and global Rust name collisions
description:
## Problem
Function entry parameters bypass collision-aware local name allocation and can shadow module statics. Affected fixture: gcc-torture mode-dependent-address.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=mode-dependent-address cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test gcc_torture_suite -E "test(gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c)" --nocapture. rustc rejects parameters arg1 through arg4 because statics with those names exist.
design: Allocate Rust parameter names against global Rust names and existing parameters, then bind CIR entry SSA arguments to the allocated names. Keep the existing local spill naming behavior consistent with the renamed parameters.
acceptance_criteria: mode-dependent-address compiles and differentially matches C under the lowering profile, and generated function parameters do not shadow statics.
notes: Allocated non-main Rust parameter names against defined and extern globals plus earlier parameters, mapped entry SSA arguments to the allocated names, and seeded local-name collision tracking with those parameters. mode-dependent-address passes its focused release lowering GCC fixture. fmt, clippy, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Function parameters now receive collision-free Rust names and preserve their SSA bindings under raw lowering.

title: Lower arbitrary-width overflow arithmetic correctly
description:
## Problem
Raw lowering emits primitive Rust casts and overflowing methods for vendored bitint values. Affected fixture: gcc-torture pr71554.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=pr71554 cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test gcc_torture_suite -E "test(gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c)" --nocapture. rustc rejects primitive as casts into BInt<33,1> and the nonexistent BInt::overflowing_mul method.
design: Use bitint constructors or explicit conversion APIs rather than Rust as casts. Implement overflow arithmetic with the CIR result width, not merely the operand storage width. For pr71554, signed 33-bit operands multiply into an i32 result plus an overflow flag; truncation and overflow detection must follow __builtin_mul_overflow semantics.
acceptance_criteria: pr71554 compiles and differentially matches C under the lowering profile. The lowering supports non-native-width operands without primitive-only casts or nonexistent overflowing methods.
notes: Implemented explicit native-to-bitint constructors and bitint-to-wide conversions. Overflow operations on non-native integer operands up to 128 bits now compute in i128/u128, narrow to the CIR result type, and combine arithmetic overflow with result-width range overflow. Verified pr71554 and bitint_arith with the release lowering profile; cargo fmt, release clippy, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: pr71554 compiles and differentially matches C under raw lowering with destination-width overflow detection.

title: Add f80 shims for unary builtins and signbit
description:
## Problem
Raw lowering calls Rust floating-point methods on LongDouble.0, which is a [u8; 10] payload rather than a Rust float. Affected fixtures: gcc-torture 20080502-1 and stdlib math/long_double_builtins.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run 20080502-1 with SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE under gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c and the lowering profile. Run cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test stdlib_coverage -E "test(stdlib_coverage)" --nocapture to reproduce long_double_builtins.
design: Add f80 C shims and Rust extern declarations for signbit, abs, ceil, floor, round, and trunc. Route long-double CIR builtins through those shims while retaining native Rust methods for f32 and f64.
acceptance_criteria: 20080502-1 and math/long_double_builtins compile and differentially match C in the lowering profile. No generated operation invokes floating-point methods on the LongDouble byte array.
notes: Added f80 C bridge functions and Rust extern declarations for signbit, abs, ceil, floor, round, and trunc. Long-double unary CIR operations now call the ABI shims while f32/f64 retain native methods. GCC 20080502-1 and the release lowering stdlib profile pass; math/long_double_builtins is green and generated Rust no longer invokes float methods on LongDouble.0. fmt, clippy, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: f80 unary math and signbit operations now lower through C ABI shims and pass their lowering fixtures.

title: Preserve function-pointer types in raw lowering
description:
## Problem
Raw lowering loses AST-level function-pointer information at field loads and mishandles GNU old-style no-prototype function pointers. Affected fixtures: enum_return_type_function_pointer_field, enum_wrapper_unwind_abi_propagation, indirect_call_enum_return_capture, and c-testsuite case_00087, case_00089, case_00095, case_00210.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run each generated fixture with SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE and generated_differential under the lowering profile. Run cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test c_testsuite_suite -E "test(c_testsuite_supported_tests_match_c)" --nocapture for the GNU cases, or inspect one case with NEXTEST_PROFILE=lowering slate translate -std=gnu17 tests/fixtures.c-testsuite/<case>.c.
design: Materialize function-pointer field loads with the recovered AST field type instead of the erased CIR result type. Preserve enum return types through indirect calls. Represent or explicitly transmute GNU no-prototype pointers without taking addr_of_mut of a function item, and cast function items directly when converting to void pointers.
acceptance_criteria: All seven affected fixtures translate, compile, and differentially match C under raw lowering with -std=gnu17 where required. Generated Rust contains no invalid function-item address expressions or mismatched variadic/non-variadic Option function-pointer assignments.
notes: Preserved AST function-pointer field types when materializing loads and propagated those types through compatible CIR casts. Named function items now remain named across no-prototype casts, typed transmutes handle genuine function-pointer/data-pointer representation changes, and stores coerce to the recovered destination function-pointer type. All three generated enum-return fixtures pass under the release lowering profile. The full GNU17 c-testsuite batch no longer reports case_00087, case_00089, case_00095, or case_00210; only the separately tracked aggregate-varargs and VLA cases remain. fmt, clippy, and diff checks pass.
close_reason: Function-pointer field loads, enum returns, no-prototype casts, and function-item pointer conversions now compile and match under raw lowering.

title: Fix raw record identity and dependency emission
description:
## Problem
Raw lowering emits duplicate Rust record definitions for distinct or repeated C tags and can emit records without their dependent definitions. Affected fixtures: gcc-torture 930930-2; generated local_struct_name_collision; libc-functional popen, search_hsearch, search_insque, search_tsearch; c-testsuite case_00044, case_00053, case_00209.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run the affected generated, GCC, and libc fixtures with their SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE, SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE, or SLATE_LIBC_TEST_FIXTURE selector and the lowering profile. Run cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test c_testsuite_suite -E "test(c_testsuite_supported_tests_match_c)" --nocapture for the c-testsuite cases.
design: Emit records once by CIR identity rather than iterating duplicate C AST names. Preserve distinct block-local tag identities, compute a transitive dependency closure across source and header records, and synthesize opaque zero-sized Rust records for referenced incomplete tags such as struct S and struct __tab. Prune unrelated header records when they are not required by CIR or by a required record dependency.
acceptance_criteria: All nine affected fixtures translate, compile, and differentially match C under the lowering profile. Generated Rust has no duplicate type definitions and no unresolved record or typedef-backed field types.
notes: Record emission now prefers semantic names carried by named CIR struct/union aliases and falls back to !rec_* keys only for genuinely unnamed CIR-only aggregates. This retains synthesized multi-result records without bypassing anonymous/local collision reconciliation. Focused lowering fixtures gnu_extended_asm, x86_instruction_intrinsics, anon_local_struct, local_struct_name_collision, and long_double_union_representation pass; the complete generated differential lowering set passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix raw-lowering profile fixture failures
description: Make cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering pass without enabling backend fixups. Current raw failures: GCC 20080502-1, 930930-2, mode-dependent-address, pr71554; generated dense_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time, enum_return_type_function_pointer_field, enum_wrapper_unwind_abi_propagation, indirect_call_enum_return_capture, local_struct_name_collision, serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time; libc-functional popen, search_hsearch, search_insque, search_tsearch; c-testsuite case_00044, case_00053, case_00087, case_00089, case_00095, case_00204, case_00207, case_00209, case_00210; stdlib complex/functions (already known unsupported) and math/long_double_builtins.
acceptance_criteria: cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering passes with raw lowering active and no fixture failure suppression or allowlist.
notes:
Triage 2026-08-13:

The 24 actionable raw-lowering failures reduce to eight child issues:
- slate-12js.9.1 record identity, dependency closure, and incomplete records: 930930-2, local_struct_name_collision, popen, search_hsearch, search_insque, search_tsearch, case_00044, case_00053, case_00209.
- slate-12js.9.2 function-pointer type preservation and GNU no-prototype pointers: enum_return_type_function_pointer_field, enum_wrapper_unwind_abi_propagation, indirect_call_enum_return_capture, case_00087, case_00089, case_00095, case_00210.
- slate-12js.9.3 f80 unary builtins and signbit: 20080502-1, math/long_double_builtins.
- slate-12js.9.4 parameter/global Rust naming: mode-dependent-address.
- slate-12js.9.5 arbitrary-width overflow arithmetic: pr71554.
- slate-12js.9.6 internal aggregate varargs: case_00204.
- slate-12js.9.7 goto-dispatch VLA initialization ordering: case_00207.
- slate-12js.9.8 rustc stack exhaustion in generated stress builds: dense_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time, serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.

Recommended implementation order: .1 record graph; .2 function pointers; .3 f80; .6 boxed internal varargs; .7 VLA dispatch; .4 naming; .5 bitint overflow; .8 generated-build stack. The children remain independently claimable and have no artificial dependency edges.

Focused selectors:
SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=<name> cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test differential -E "test(generated_differential)" --nocapture
SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=<name> cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test gcc_torture_suite -E "test(gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c)" --nocapture
SLATE_LIBC_TEST_FIXTURE=<name> cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --test libc_test_functional_suite -E "test(libc_test_functional_supported_tests_match_c)" --nocapture

The c-testsuite runner currently has no per-fixture selector because collect_cases ignores environment selection. Reproduce that group with the suite, or inspect individual raw output using NEXTEST_PROFILE=lowering slate translate -std=gnu17 <fixture> until a selector is added.

stdlib complex/functions is the pre-existing known-unsupported probe tracked by slate-nk3.25.2. Do not add it to these child fixes and do not add new lowering allowlists or suppressions.
Completed 2026-08-13: all eight lowering child issues are closed. Final cargo nextest r --release --profile lowering --no-fail-fast passed all 6 suites (GCC torture, libc functional, c-testsuite, chibicc, stdlib coverage, generated differential), with 257 tests skipped by the lowering profile. cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --release --all-targets -- -D warnings, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Split completion gates into libc, rewrites, and lowering profiles
description: Evolve the existing nextest libc/lang profiles into task-specific completion gates: retain libc, rename lang to rewrites, and add a raw-lowered runtime differential profile. Update repository documentation so frontend, backend rewrite, and libc work require only their respective profile.
acceptance_criteria: The three named profiles select the intended test sets; lowering translator subprocesses run with SLATE_RAW_LOWER and exclude fixup shape assertions; repository instructions replace the universal nextest completion gate with profile-specific commands; profile lists and focused tests validate the configuration.
notes: Evolved existing profiles: retained libc (6 selected tests), renamed lang to rewrites (241 non-libc tests), and added lowering (6 aggregate runtime differential tests). NEXTEST_PROFILE=lowering disables backend fixups through backend::apply_with; no failures are suppressed. Updated CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md symlink, fixup docs, and corpus READMEs so only the changed subsystem's profile is required. Validation: profile list counts libc=6/lowering=6/rewrites=241; raw project/directive regressions 2/2 pass; cargo fmt --check, git diff --check, and clippy -D warnings pass. Strict lowering profile runs in 17.16s warm and currently fails 5/6 aggregate tests on the fixtures tracked in slate-12js.9.
close_reason: Configured and documented the libc, rewrites, and strict raw-lowering nextest profiles; validated selection and raw-mode behavior.

title: Measure differential suites without Rust fixup passes
description: Temporarily bypass backend fixup/rewrite passes while retaining CIR/AST parsing, baseline lowering, Rust emission, Cargo compilation, Rust execution, and C/Rust comparison. Exclude output-shape assertion tests, measure representative corpus and full-suite timing, record which fixtures cease to compile or match, then remove the benchmark bypass.
acceptance_criteria: Record rewrite-disabled timings and fixture pass/failure counts against normal runs; identify whether rewrites dominate translation; remove all benchmark-only code before handoff and verify formatting/status.
notes: Measured the same six runtime differential corpora with and without backend fixups. Warm rewritten run: 61.00s. Warm raw-lowered run: 31.74s, a 29.26s/48.0% reduction. Raw lowering preserved 1995/2020 fixture results (98.8%); rewritten output currently preserved 2005/2020 (99.3%). Isolated GCC improved from roughly 24-28s rewritten to 8.11s warm raw; generated_differential improved from about 10.03s to 8.99s. SLATE_RAW_LOWER was centralized in backend::apply_with so translate, translate-directives, and every translate-project mode respect it; fixup-debug remains explicit. Added project/directive end-to-end regressions.
close_reason: Measured rewrite cost and kept uniform SLATE_RAW_LOWER support with passing regressions.

title: Tune test concurrency and verify sub-10-second incremental gate
description:
## Problem
Internally parallel corpus tests can run concurrently under nextest, causing oversubscription, while conservative per-suite worker limits can also leave CPUs idle. The best policy must be chosen from measured phase data.

## Work
Tune nextest scheduling, suite job limits, or phase concurrency after the caching changes land. Measure warm no-change and representative small-change workflows, then address the dominant remaining costs without adding custom Rust compilation caching.

## Target
The representative warm incremental full release suite should complete in less than 10 seconds on the reference development machine.
acceptance_criteria: The final configuration avoids measured oversubscription and idle phases; at least three final warm runs are recorded; cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and the unfiltered cargo nextest release gate are run; median representative incremental runtime is below 10 seconds, or a measured lower bound and concrete blocker are documented.
notes: Final 12-thread policy: nextest gives gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c threads-required=num-test-threads and priority 100 because it internally uses all available workers; other internally parallel compiler-heavy corpora default to 3 workers and reserve 3 nextest slots, with priorities starting the longest suites first. Final warm full-suite wall samples: 66.32s, 63.77s, 69.72s (median 66.32s); Cargo was fresh in 0.03s on the latter two. The current dirty lowering worktree produces 6 existing failures, so failed Rust bins correctly rebuild on every run. Measured lower bounds/blockers: GCC alone is about 23-26s in full runs (30.76s isolated earlier), and generated_differential is about 33-38s. Sub-10s cannot be reached while retranslating every fixture and rejecting failed Cargo artifacts; it would require translation/result caching or narrower suite scope, contrary to current epic scope. Validation: cargo fmt; cargo clippy --release --tests -- -D warnings; focused cache/stale-artifact regressions 3/3 pass; unfiltered cargo nextest r --release --no-fail-fast completed 245 tests with 239 pass, 6 pre-existing worktree failures, 16 skipped.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reject stale Rust bins while preserving Cargo freshness
description:
## Problem
The batch harness accepts an executable whenever its path exists, even when the current Cargo invocation failed to build that bin. Removing the generated crate avoids some stale reuse but destroys source timestamps and forces unnecessary Cargo work.

## Work
Keep generated batch crates stable across runs and determine per-bin success from the current Cargo build invocation, preferably through Cargo JSON artifact messages. Continue using one shared src/bin crate and let Cargo own Rust dependency and target caching.

## Correctness
A prior executable must never satisfy a fixture whose current generated Rust fails to compile. Successful bins from a keep-going build may still run and report independently.
acceptance_criteria: A regression reproduces an old executable followed by invalid generated Rust and proves the fixture fails; unchanged generated bins and dependencies remain Cargo-fresh across warm runs; current compile diagnostics identify the failing bin; the generated crate is no longer deleted wholesale.
close_reason: Batch builds now trust only per-bin artifacts reported by the current Cargo JSON invocation; a regression covers valid, fresh, then invalid generated Rust with an old executable present; the primary generated workspace is preserved.

title: Cache C oracle binaries by source freshness
description:
## Problem
Every differential fixture recompiles its C oracle on every run even though fixture sources rarely change and C compilation is outside the behavior under test.

## Work
Persist C executables per suite and fixture. Recompile when the executable is missing, the C input is newer, compilation arguments change, or the cache schema changes. For multi-file fixtures, use the newest relevant source input. Keep executing the cached C binary when comparison work is required; runtime-result caching is optional only if measurements show execution is material.

## Scope
Compiler or system-header upgrades do not need automatic invalidation. Clearing target artifacts is the explicit refresh mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive unchanged runs compile each C oracle only on the first run; touching or changing a fixture recompiles that fixture and no unrelated fixture; changing C compilation arguments invalidates the affected artifact; failed compilation cannot leave a stale binary eligible for execution.
close_reason: Single-file C oracle compilation now reuses a persistent executable when source timestamp and compiler arguments are unchanged, compiles atomically on misses, and invalidates authorization before failures; integration regression covers hits, argument changes, and failed rebuilds.

title: Measure incremental test-suite phase costs
description:
## Problem
The approximately 60 second baseline is anecdotal and does not separate translation, Cargo freshness checks and compilation, C compilation, execution, or scheduler contention.

## Work
Add low-overhead opt-in phase timing to the differential harnesses and record cold, warm no-change, and representative one-feature-change runs on the reference machine. Include per-suite timing and CPU/job settings so later changes are comparable.

## Constraints
Do not change test semantics or skip any work in this task.
acceptance_criteria: Run the standard unfiltered cargo nextest release command and record its total time. Repeat after optimization on a healthy worktree; no custom phase instrumentation or strict statistical benchmark is required.
notes: Baseline simplified per user direction: use only the standard full release nextest wall time, with no phase instrumentation requirement. Initial run on 12 logical CPUs: Cargo release compilation 19.04s; nextest reached fail-fast after 9.867s and 34/242 tests; shell wall time 28.999s. This is an incomplete baseline because existing dirty-worktree changes caused generated Rust compile failures and a cross-TU shim failure. User supplied the representative healthy baseline of roughly 60s. Further optimization will compare ordinary full-command totals once the tree is green.
close_reason: Coarse baseline recorded with the standard release command; existing dirty-worktree failures and the user-provided approximately 60s healthy baseline are documented.

title: Reduce incremental test runtime below 10 seconds
description:
## Problem
The full release nextest suite currently takes roughly 60 seconds even when a typical lowering change affects very few generated Rust fixtures. Translation must still run for correctness, but unnecessary C recompilation and defeated Cargo freshness add avoidable work.

## Scope
Measure the differential harness by phase, fix stale Rust artifact handling so persistent generated crates are safe, preserve Cargo-managed Rust caching, add a timestamp-based C oracle cache, and tune concurrency based on measurements. Do not add a custom Rust executable or result cache; Cargo remains responsible for Rust compilation freshness.

## Goal
Bring a warm incremental `cargo nextest r --release` run from approximately 60 seconds to less than 10 seconds on the reference development machine when few or no generated Rust fixtures change, without weakening differential correctness or hiding current Rust compilation failures.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible baseline and final warm incremental benchmark are recorded; the final representative run completes in under 10 seconds or the remaining measured lower bound and blockers are documented; current Rust build failures cannot be masked by stale executables; the unfiltered release suite remains correct.
notes:
Implemented safe Cargo-managed Rust freshness, current-invocation artifact validation, timestamp/key-based C oracle reuse, libc-shim compile caching, and nextest-aware 12-thread scheduling. Final warm median is 66.32s, not under 10s. Required translation plus failing generated Rust recompilation dominate: GCC 23-26s and generated differential 33-38s. The target is blocked under the explicit constraint that all translation must run and no custom Rust/result cache is permitted. See child tasks for implementation and validation details.
Rust-only upper-bound follow-up slate-12js.6 measured 1,980 warmed differential C oracles at 5.069s aggregate worker time (2.56ms/oracle), translating to roughly 0.65s summed wall contribution after per-suite parallelism and likely less under full-suite overlap. Rust-only full wall samples were too noisy to expose this small delta.
close_reason: Closed

title: Provide C-ABI trampolines for user-defined callbacks with long double parameters
description:
.4 and .8 handle Rust-generated code calling OUT to C with a long-double argument (solved by wrapping the call site in a C-compiled shim). This ticket is the reverse direction: a translated Rust function whose address is taken and handed to C as a callback -- a qsort/qsort_r comparator, a signal handler, a project-defined function-pointer slot, anything where C calls back INTO Slate-generated Rust -- and whose signature includes a long double parameter or return.

If such a function is translated naively as `extern "C" fn cmp(a: F80, b: F80) -> i32` and its address handed directly to C, the caller (compiled with the real C ABI) expects a true C `long double` argument, which is X87/X87UP-classified and passed on the stack. Our F80 bridge struct is deliberately INTEGER-classified (see .2/.3's design) so it can safely cross the Rust/C boundary in normal call position -- but that's exactly the mismatch here: the callback slot expects X87 classification, not INTEGER. Taking the address of the Rust function directly and registering it as the callback would silently corrupt the argument.

Fix: generate a small C-compiled trampoline with the TRUE C signature (real `long double` parameters/return, correctly X87-classified by the C compiler), whose body packs/unpacks through the F80 bridge struct and calls the Rust-defined function by its Rust ABI. Register the TRAMPOLINE's address as the callback, never the Rust function's address directly. Same "always shim, never idiomize" principle as the rest of this epic (see epic DESIGN).

Related but distinct: slate-3f8g.5.6 (Use the C ABI for GNU libc callbacks) and slate-3f8g.5.4 (obstack allocator callbacks) fix extern "C" fn-pointer *typing* generally (rustc improper_ctypes) but neither addresses the long-double classification mismatch specifically -- this ticket is additive to those, not a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: A project-defined callback (e.g. a qsort comparator or a plain function pointer passed to another function) with a long double parameter or return type is registered and invoked correctly, bit-exact vs the C reference, in a differential fixture -- proving the trampoline's address, not the Rust function's address, is what gets passed to C.
close_reason: Generated C-ABI trampolines for long-double callbacks and fixed outgoing shim prototypes for unknown externs; focused callback link fixture passes.

title: Extend variadic call handling (printf/scanf-style) to the F80 bridge
description:
.4's shim generator covers fixed-signature extern functions taking/returning long double directly. It does not cover variadic call sites -- printf("%Lf", x), scanf("%Lf", &x), and similar -- which currently go through a structurally different mechanism (try_fixed_long_double_call_shim / try_long_double_i32_shim in calls.rs) that only handles i32-returning format calls and still uses the lossy f64 'ld' tag.

Relation to existing tickets:
- slate-5exy.3.10 (under the older slate-5exy.3 C23 epic) already lists "variadics" as an explicit acceptance-criteria item and is NOT linked to this epic. That requirement is currently orphaned -- confirm this ticket subsumes it, and consider superseding slate-5exy.3.10 once this lands.
- slate-os0h.3.1.41 (gcc-torture) covers *inbound* va_arg retrieval of long-double values inside translated variadic functions -- a different direction from this ticket, which is about Slate-generated code *calling out* to variadic functions with a long-double argument.
- slate-os0h.3.1.40 covers aggregate variadic arguments generally; long-double-specific aggregate variadic passing should cross-check against .6-equivalent (aggregate by-value) work too.

Note for implementers: a real C `long double` variadic argument is X87-classified and always passed on the stack, both for fixed and variadic calls -- there's no extra ABI wrinkle from the SysV classifier itself. The actual risk is Slate emitting a direct Rust-side call that mimics printf's signature using the F80 bridge struct's (INTEGER-classified, register-eligible) convention instead of routing through a real C-compiled variadic call site, which would place the argument in the wrong location. Any generated shim must contain the actual variadic call in C so the C compiler performs the X87 classification.
acceptance_criteria: printf/scanf-style calls with %Lf (and any other variadic extern call taking/returning long double) round-trip bit-exact values through a differential fixture, replacing the current f64-truncated format-call shim path. slate-5exy.3.10's variadics requirement is confirmed covered or explicitly linked.
close_reason: Variadic printf/sscanf long-double arguments now route through real C-compiled call shims using F80 values and long-double pointers; slate-5exy.3.10's variadics requirement is covered.

title: Lower long-double literals (source + static/global) to exact 80-bit F80 bit pattern
description:
.6 only fixes the finite float.h macro-constant table (currently just LDBL_TRUE_MIN) to gate on target. A general source-level FloatingLiteral like `long double x = 3.141592653589793238462643383279L;` is a different AST node and has no coverage anywhere in this epic. Without this, .2 (storage) and .3 (arithmetic) are moot -- there's no way to construct a full-precision F80 value from source in the first place.

This is NOT solvable by routing through __slate_ld_from_f64 at runtime: a literal with more than f64's 53 bits of precision would already be truncated before it reaches the 80-bit type. The exact 80-bit bit pattern must be computed at Slate translation time (host-side), not via a runtime FFI call. Reuse the APFloat value Clang's AST already carries for the literal (c_ast.rs already parses Clang AST JSON) rather than hand-rolling a decimal-to-extended-precision parser -- consistent with .3's ban on hand-rolled float math.

Also covers static/global storage-duration initializers (e.g. `static long double pi = 3.14L;`): these have the added constraint that a Rust `static` initializer must be const-evaluable, so the result must bottom out in a plain byte-array literal, not a sequence of runtime calls. Same underlying capability as the local-variable case, just consumed differently at codegen time.

Target-aware: on f64-abi/quad-abi targets the same literal lowers to a plain f64/f128 constant, consistent with .5's compile-time-only dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: A source fixture with a long double literal exceeding f64 precision (e.g. 20+ significant digits) round-trips through Rust and prints the same digits as the C reference, both as a local variable initializer and as a static/global initializer, on x87, f64-abi, and quad-abi targets.
close_reason: Threaded AST FloatingLiteral values through c_ast/lowering, replaced runtime/native long-double conversion with rustc_apfloat X87DoubleExtended parsing, and added precision/edge differential fixtures.

title: Fix long-double macro-constant lowering to gate on target
description: next_long_double_macro_const_expr (storage.rs:750-770) unconditionally wraps any MacroValue::LongDouble macro constant (currently just LDBL_TRUE_MIN) in a call to the LongDouble(...) wrapper constructor, with no check against uses_f64_long_double_abi() or is_quad_long_double. On an f64-abi target (MSVC/Darwin) this should lower to a bare f64 literal -- there is no LongDouble wrapper type constructed on that target at all -- and on the quad target (Bionic) it should become an f128 literal. Same bug shape as the .1 layout hardcoding fix, different file: a raw-string/table-driven site that doesn't consult the single uses_f64_long_double_abi()/is_quad_long_double dispatch that lowerer.rs:2969 already uses correctly.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture exercising LDBL_TRUE_MIN (or another float.h long-double macro) lowers to the correct target-specific literal/type on x87, f64-abi, and quad-abi targets.
close_reason: Added target-aware LDBL_TRUE_MIN lowering for x87/f64-abi/quad, expanded macro source matching for f64/f128 spellings, and covered all three targets with explicit differential tests.

title: Extend extern-call long-double shim generation to arbitrary signatures
description: try_fixed_long_double_call_shim / try_long_double_i32_shim (calls.rs) only fire for op_result_type == !s32i (int-returning, primarily format-string/fixed-arg calls). Any extern function taking or returning long double needs a __slate_<fn_name> C trampoline generated on demand, using the bit-exact F80 bridge struct (from the F80 storage task) instead of the current f64-truncating 'ld' tag, so libc calls (strtold, sinl, etc.) and arbitrary user extern declarations preserve full 80-bit precision across the FFI boundary.
design: Same memcpy-transducer pattern as the arithmetic shims: shim signature uses the F80 byte struct (INTEGER-classified on both sides), shim body casts to/from real long double before calling the true target, so the true target sees a correctly X87/X87UP-classified call.
acceptance_criteria: Extern C function taking/returning long double with non-i32 return type gets a generated shim and round-trips bit-exact values through a differential fixture. The existing __slate_strtold shim is explicitly migrated off the lossy f64 'ld' tag onto the F80 bridge struct as a concrete, required part of this task -- not left as an incidental side effect of the general mechanism.
close_reason: Implemented arbitrary-signature long-double C trampolines with F80 return/arg tags, migrated __slate_strtold to return F80 directly, added strtold and sinl differential fixtures, and updated cross-tu shim-name expectations.

title: Route F80 arithmetic and conversions through generated C helper shims, not hand-rolled softfloat
description:
Implement Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Neg/PartialEq/PartialOrd for F80 by calling small fixed extern "C" helper functions (e.g. __slate_f80_add) that unpack the bridge struct to a real long double, perform the operation on real x87 hardware via the C compiler, and repack the result -- reusing the same INTEGER-classified byte-struct ABI trick already used for call-boundary shims. Explicitly avoid a from-scratch extended-precision softfloat implementation: x87 rounding (guard/round/sticky bits, denormals) is exactly the kind of thing that silently diverges by 1 ULP from a real x87 unit, and this project's correctness bar is bit-identical stdout under differential testing. Getting the op executed by a real compiler on the real target keeps bit-for-bit parity by construction.

Also cover the full finite set of scalar to/from-long-double casts as fixed (not generated-on-demand) runtime helpers in the same C file: from_{i32,u32,i64,u64,f32,f64} and to_{i32,u32,i64,u64,f32,f64} at minimum, symmetric in both directions. Unlike .4's arbitrary extern-call shims (which are generated per-signature for un-translated C functions), this set is bounded and known in advance, so it should be hand-written once here rather than deferred to codegen. strtold-style string parsing is NOT in scope here -- an __slate_strtold shim already exists (see epic description) but currently narrows through the lossy f64 'ld' tag; reworking it to use the bit-exact F80 bridge struct belongs to .4 since it's an extern libc call, not a scalar cast.
design: Byte-transducer ABI: bridge struct classifies INTEGER on both Rust and C sides, C helper internally memcpy's to/from a real long double so clang emits the true X87/X87UP-classified call under the hood.
acceptance_criteria: F80 +,-,*,/,-,==,<,> match real x87 long double results bit-for-bit on existing long_**double*.c differential fixtures, replacing the current f64-truncated behavior. Full symmetric set of scalar casts (i32/u32/i64/u64/f32/f64, both directions) implemented as fixed C helpers -- not just the subset needed by whatever fixture happens to exist yet.
close_reason: Implemented fixed F80 arithmetic/comparison/cast C helpers, wired shared renderer through c_shim, updated lowering and shared-type extern handling, added raw-byte differential fixture, and cleaned the differential cache.

title: Design bit-exact F80 storage type (16-byte x87 memory representation)
description: Replace the lossy LongDouble(f64) newtype (runtime_support.rs:56-86) with a #[repr(C, align(16))] struct wrapping [u8; 16] (or equivalent) that stores the real x87 80-bit extended value's bit pattern exactly, matching the memory representation clang uses for long double on x86-64 SysV. This is storage-only in this task -- arithmetic and conversions land in follow-up tasks. Do not implement software extended-precision float math by hand; see the arithmetic-shim task for why.
acceptance_criteria: F80 struct exists with correct size_of==16/align_of==16, and can round-trip an arbitrary 80-bit bit pattern through memcpy without loss.
close_reason: LongDouble is now an align(16) 10-byte F80 payload; layout and memcpy round-trip fixtures pass. Arithmetic/literal lowering remains for follow-up tickets.

title: Fix long-double layout hardcoding for MSVC/Darwin (f64-abi) targets
description: c_layout() (lowerer.rs:3035) and ctype_uses_long_double() (lowerer.rs:3164) match CType::Float{bits:80} unconditionally and return size 16/align 16, ignoring uses_f64_long_double_abi(). On MSVC/Darwin the real long double is a double (size 8/align 8), so any struct or union with a long double field gets miscomputed layout there even though lowerer.rs:2969 already picks the correct f64 value type. Fix both functions to consult uses_f64_long_double_abi() the same way lowerer.rs:2969 does.
acceptance_criteria: New/extended fixture: struct or union containing a long double field, differential-tested (or layout-asserted) on an f64-abi target as well as the default x87 target, sizeof/alignof match the C reference on both.
close_reason: c_layout and ctype_uses_long_double now consult uses_f64_long_double_abi; added default and macOS/MSVC layout fixtures plus macOS translation check.

title: Target-aware long double: fix layout hardcoding, add bit-exact f80 type, drop tier-1 f64 truncation
description:
LongDouble handling has three gaps, discovered while reviewing an ABI-shim proposal for FFI calls into libc long-double functions:

1. Layout hardcoding bug: c_layout() (lowerer.rs:3035) and ctype_uses_long_double() (lowerer.rs:3164) pattern-match CType::Float{bits:80} unconditionally and hardcode size 16/align 16, even though lowerer.rs:2969 already knows (via uses_f64_long_double_abi()) that MSVC/Darwin long double is really f64 (size 8/align 8). Structs/unions containing a long double field get the wrong computed layout on those targets.
2. The x86-64 SysV (glibc/Linux) x87 long double is currently a lossy tier-1 approximation: LongDouble(f64) in runtime_support.rs truncates both storage and arithmetic to f64 (53-bit mantissa) instead of the real 64-bit x87 mantissa, and __slate_strtold/the i32-return call-shim family (calls.rs try_long_double_i32_shim) narrow to double at the Rust/shim boundary. This risks differential-test divergence whenever a C program's result depends on x87-precision rounding.
3. The extern-call shim mechanism only covers int-returning / format-string calls (try_fixed_long_double_call_shim requires op_result_type == !s32i). Arbitrary long-double-returning/taking extern calls into un-translated C aren't covered.

f64 (MSVC/Darwin) and f128 (Bionic quad) need no ABI glue at the value-passing level once (1) is fixed: both are native LLVM scalar types on the Rust and Clang side, so calling-convention classification already matches (confirmed by c_shim.rs's plain 'long double' passthrough for the quad tag, and uses_f64_long_double_abi()'s early-return skipping shim generation for MSVC/Darwin entirely). Only the x87 case needs new machinery.
design:
Governing rule for every child task: never idiomize a function signature or expression that touches long double into native Rust long-double math or a native-ABI Rust type. Always route through a small extern "C" shim, compiled by the real C compiler, that does the memcpy-into-a-real-long-double trick and calls the actual operation/function -- whether that's arithmetic (.3), an extern call (.4/.8), a struct member (.9), or a callback (.11). The F80 bridge struct (.2) is deliberately INTEGER-classified specifically so it's safe to pass across the Rust/C boundary in either direction; anything that tries to reason about long double natively in Rust reintroduces the exact softfloat-divergence risk .3 already rules out.

Cross-target testing infrastructure already exists and should be reused, not reinvented: tests/differential.rs has run_cross_target_fixture/compile_for_target with fixture directories at tests/fixtures/{bionic,msvc,macos}/ and per-target defines already wired up (Android API level, MSVC LLP64, etc). The existing long_double*.c fixtures currently only live at the top level (tests/fixtures/) -- extending coverage to the f64-abi/quad-abi targets means adding fixtures under those target-specific directories and running them through the existing harness, not building new cross-target machinery.
acceptance_criteria: Struct/union layouts containing long double are correct on x87, f64-abi, and quad-abi targets. x87 long double round-trips through libc calls and arithmetic at true 80-bit precision (bit-exact vs C reference), not f64-truncated. f64/f128 targets remain zero-glue passthrough.
close_reason: All target-aware long-double work and lowering/rewrite regressions verified

title: gcc-torture: promote setjmp and longjmp execution cases

title: gcc-torture: lower GNU vector arithmetic, comparison, and bitwise operations
description:
GNU vector arithmetic, comparison, division, negation, and bitwise operations are emitted as unsupported Rust array operators.

Cases: `20050604-1`, `20060420-1`, `ieee__fp-cmp-cond-1`, `pr23135`, `pr60960`, `pr94412`, `scal-to-vec1`, `scal-to-vec2`, `scal-to-vec3`, `simd-1`, `simd-2`, `simd-5`

Reproduce one case with `SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=<case> cargo nextest r --release --test gcc_torture_suite -E 'test(gcc_torture_unsupported_triage_report)' --run-ignored ignored-only --nocapture`. This issue was discovered by `slate-os0h.3.1` from the preserved `TRIAGE.log.gz`.
acceptance_criteria: All listed cases translate, their generated Rust compiles and matches the C reference's stdout and exit code, the files are promoted into `tests/fixtures.gcc-torture/`, and `cargo nextest r --release --test gcc_torture_suite` passes. If an upstream CIR limitation is the only remaining cause, record the upstream disposition and keep the cases mapped here until promotion or an explicit non-Slate exclusion.
notes:
Fixed:
1. cir.fmuladd already handled separately.
2. Global vector-typed initializers (#cir.const_vector<[...]>) fell through to the scalar fallback and only kept the first lane -- added an explicit branch in render_const_value_expr.
3. Unary neg/not (cir.unary minus/not) didn't expand elementwise over vector operands -- added vector branches to lower_neg/lower_not mirroring lower_int_arith's existing vector_binary_expr pattern.
4. Float vector arithmetic (fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv) went through lower_binary, which had no vector check at all (only lower_int_arith did) -- added the same vector_binary_expr branch to lower_binary.
5. cir.vec.create, cir.vec.splat, cir.vec.cmp had no handler at all (fell to emit_todo) -- added CirOpKind variants + lowerer methods. vec.cmp expands to per-lane (cmp as elem_ty).wrapping_neg() to match GCC vector-compare mask semantics (-1/0 per lane), only kinds 0-5 (lt/le/gt/ge/eq/ne); ordered/unordered kinds 6/7 still fall to unsupported.
6. Passing &local_vector to a function expecting a pointer-to-whole-vector (not decayed to element pointer) used to always emit local.as_mut_ptr() based purely on the slot's Rust type being Type::Array -- now call_arg_expr checks whether the CIR pointee type is itself an array/vector type (non-decayed) and uses &mut slot in that case.

All 12 listed cases pass, plus 7 bonus gcc-torture unsupported cases fixed by the same general changes (20080519-1, pr123625-2, pr126405, pr126405-2, pr85169, pr94524-1, pr94524-2). All 19 promoted via git mv. Full lowering + rewrites nextest profiles pass, fmt/clippy clean. Nothing committed yet -- conservative git profile.

title: gcc-torture: lower GNU vector construction, splats, and reinterpret casts
description:
