title: Preserve weak alias binding in cross-TU GNU pragma output
description: The required full release suite persistently fails cross_tu::gnu_symbol_pragmas_preserve_cross_tu_linkage because the generated pragma_weak_alias symbol has STB_GLOBAL binding instead of the expected weak binding. Reproduces independently with cargo nextest r --release --test cross_tu -E 'test(gnu_symbol_pragmas_preserve_cross_tu_linkage)' --nocapture.
acceptance_criteria: The isolated cross-TU test and the full release nextest suite pass; generated GNU weak aliases retain the expected ELF binding.
close_reason: Root cause was not in Slate's weak-alias codegen itself (symbols.rs's 'core::arch::global_asm!(".weak pragma_weak_alias\n.set pragma_weak_alias, pragma_weak_target")' correctly mirrors clang's own per-TU output for #pragma weak) -- it was that this raw asm text is invisible to rustc's own #[no_mangle] symbol-uniqueness frontend check, so a same-named strong definition elsewhere in the same combined crate (strong.rs's real pragma_weak_alias fn) only collides at the assembler stage, and only if both land in the same object file. Verified #[linkage="weak"] as an alternative fails unconditionally (rustc's frontend rejects duplicate #[no_mangle] names regardless of linkage), so the raw-asm approach is the only one that can work, and its correctness is entirely contingent on codegen-unit partitioning keeping the two modules in separate objects -- which neither generated_crate_manifest (tests/support/mod.rs, used by every differential/cross_tu/chibicc harness) nor lib_crate_manifest (src/main.rs, the real translate-project --lib output) guaranteed, since neither set an explicit codegen-units and this rustc/cargo installation doesn't default to enough units for a crate this small. Bisected empirically: codegen-units=1/2 reproduce the STB_GLOBAL failure, =16 and =256 both avoid it. Fixed by adding codegen-units = 256 (Cargo's own traditional dev-profile default, well above the empirically-necessary 16 for headroom) to [profile.dev] in both manifest generators -- this is a real end-user-facing robustness gap, not just a test artifact, since translate-project --lib would hit the identical nondeterministic failure for any real C project combining a #pragma weak alias TU with a strong-override TU into one crate. Un-ignored gnu_symbol_pragmas_preserve_cross_tu_linkage. cargo fmt/clippy clean, cargo nextest r --release fully green at 212/212 (2 skipped are the pre-existing intentionally-ignored diagnostic tests).

title: Generalize query engine around matchable Rust items
description: Refactor the query engine so rules iterate matchable Rust AST items, bind stable semantic identities, query generic facts including def-use relationships, and produce anchored edit sets independently of candidate type. Capture the architecture and migrate final_return_temps as the first vertical slice.
acceptance_criteria: A design note documents the target model and migration. A first vertical slice matches locals using semantic facts rather than generated names, exposes stable binding/def-use information, rewrites every matching final-return temporary, and the release nextest suite, clippy, and fmt pass.
notes: Completed statement, definition, function, and binding slices. FunctionRef exposes the complete FnDef; BindingRef exposes function, kind/index, type, BindingId, and generic def-use/value facts. unused_params migrated from a whole-program recipe to QueryRule<Binding> with explicit signature and call-expression edits. Full differential suite passes 90/90 including all 245 fixtures; full release has only slate-8h8f and slate-jqvc baseline failures.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add StmtWindowRule for statement-window matching and splice
description:
Why: the query engine has no way to match more than one AST node at a time or replace N statements with M statements. This structurally excludes most of the remaining legacy Fixup-trait rewrites tracked under slate-04q.75 (range_loop, slice_loop, goto, singleton_scopes, dead_locals, ptr_copy, and others) from ever using the engine, since they match adjacent statement runs against a fact (e.g. range_loop matches a Let immediately followed by a Loop against a CountedLoopFact) and splice in a replacement. This is the single highest-leverage addition for closing the gap between the query engine and the ~1000-rewrite target.

What to do: add a StmtWindowSite (item_index, path to the containing Vec<IndentStmt>, range into it) as a new Site/EditTarget (depends on the generic Plan<E> work), and a StmtWindowRule with a fixed width that slides over every Vec<IndentStmt> in the program (reusing the existing shared body-vec walker in src/fixups/support/walk.rs - no new traversal code). Case functions get a StmtWindowCaseContext exposing structural access to the window (case.stmts::<N>()) plus the same Proof/Rejection-returning fact-query pattern as CallCaseContext. Recipes return Vec<IndentStmt> (0 = delete, 1+ = splice).
design: See matcher-plan.md section 2 for the full sketch, including a ~15-line worked example of range_loop rewritten through StmtWindowRule (down from range_loop.rs's current 148 lines of hand-rolled recursive walk + hand-rolled pair match + hand-rolled splice + hand-rolled trace event). Build this on top of the generic Plan<E: EditTarget> engine rather than as a fourth bespoke plan/apply implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A StmtWindowRule can match a fixed-width run of adjacent IndentStmt against a QueryContext fact query, and its recipe can splice a replacement Vec<IndentStmt> with the same conflict-detection and trace-event guarantees ExprPlan has today. Proven end to end by at least one real rule (see the dependent range_loop migration ticket). cargo fmt, clippy, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason:
Implemented StmtWindowSite/StmtWindowRule/StmtWindowPlanBuilder/StmtWindowPlan in a new src/fixups/query/stmt_window.rs, built on the generic Plan<E: EditTarget> engine from .1: candidates are every width-N run of adjacent statements anywhere in the program (reusing facts::walk's traversal shape), cases get structural access via case.stmts::<N>() plus the same Proof/Rejection fact-query pattern as CallCaseContext (case.reject()/case.require() replace CallCaseContext's per-predicate methods since a statement window can hold any Stmt shape, unlike a call's fixed arg list), and recipes return Vec<IndentStmt> (0=delete, 1+=splice).

Proved it end to end by migrating range_loop.rs onto it (src/fixups/query/rules/range_loop.rs, ~55 lines vs the old 147-line hand-rolled Fixup impl), wired into fixups/mod.rs in place of the legacy pass, legacy module deleted. Both exact-string differential tests (counted_varargs_loop_uses_range_for, array_init_literal_counted_loop_uses_range_for) pass unchanged; full nextest r --release (191 tests incl. chibicc_suite/stdlib_coverage/generated_differential) passes.

One design tradeoff surfaced and deliberately not solved here: two candidate windows in a strict ancestor/descendant relationship (e.g. nested counted loops) are treated as a genuine overlap by plan.rs's generic conflict resolution and both get dropped in a single pass, rather than resolving inner-then-outer across a fixpoint. This matches existing, already-accepted behavior for nested CallRule targets (also drop-both, no retry) and is not a correctness risk since range_loop is a pure idiomatization fixup - confirmed safe by the full differential suite. Documented in docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md's new "Statement window rules" section rather than silently left unmentioned.

Also added crate::fixups::support::walk::nested_body_vecs_with_path - a read-only sibling of the existing nested_body_vecs_mut_with_path with an explicitly named lifetime, since the existing nested_bodies_with_path's elided-HRTB closure signature can't return borrowed data tied to the caller's chosen lifetime (needed to collect &'snapshot [IndentStmt] windows across the scan). Reusable by future StmtWindowRule-style consumers.

cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest r --release all pass. Not committed per standing instruction - left for review.

title: Collapse rewrite.rs/program.rs/definition.rs into a generic Plan<E: EditTarget> engine
description:
Why: ExprPlanBuilder/ExprPlan (rewrite.rs), ProgramPlanBuilder/ProgramPlan (program.rs), and DefinitionPlanBuilder/DefinitionPlan (definition.rs) each independently implement the same conflict-resolution algorithm: collect proposals, run cases in order, take the first Replace, group by target site, flag AmbiguousTarget/OverlappingTargets/MissingTarget/CandidateRejected, apply, log. ~85% identical, ~250 loc apiece, parameterized only by what "target" and "apply an edit" mean for that node kind.

What to do: introduce Site (Ord + Clone + overlaps()) and EditTarget (site() + apply()) traits, and a single generic Plan<E: EditTarget>/PlanBuilder<E> that all three current builders become thin instantiations of. RuleIdentity/RuleCaseIdentity/CaseRejection/PlanDiagnostic are already node-kind-agnostic and should be reused as-is, generalized to be generic over Site where they currently hardcode ExprSite/DefinitionLocation.
design: ExprSite::overlaps becomes the existing sites_overlap path-prefix check; DefinitionLocation::overlaps becomes the existing item/extern-decl overlap check. This is the prerequisite for adding StmtWindowSite later without writing a fourth parallel builder. Expect this to net-shrink LOC (three ~300-line builders collapse to one ~350-line generic one plus three ~30-line trait impls), not grow it.
acceptance_criteria: Existing memchr, libc_exit, anonymous_structs, and PruneUnusedDefinitions passes produce byte-identical trace output and differential test results after the collapse. rewrite.rs/program.rs/definition.rs total loc decreases. cargo fmt, clippy, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Collapsed rewrite.rs/program.rs/definition.rs conflict-resolution into a generic plan.rs (PlanSite/EditTarget traits, PlanBuilder<E>/Plan<E>, generic PlanDiagnostic<S>). apply() mechanics kept per-module since they genuinely differ; only the grouping/ambiguity/overlap algorithm and diagnostic enum were actually shareable. Net LOC roughly flat (1373->1370), not the larger reduction originally estimated - value is correctness/maintainability (one conflict-resolution implementation instead of three), not size. cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest r --release all pass.

title: Redesign query/rewrite engine core for scale
description:
Why: src/fixups/query/ (CallRule/DefinitionRule/ProgramRule) proved the declarative-rule approach on memchr, libc_exit, and anonymous_structs, but the engine only supports three hand-built shapes: a single call expression, a whole named definition, and one hardcoded whole-program selector. Most of the remaining ~45 legacy Fixup-trait rewrites tracked under slate-04q.75 (range_loop, slice_loop, goto, singleton_scopes, dead_locals, ptr_copy, ...) match a *window* of statements, not a single expression or item, so they cannot move onto the query engine as it exists today - the gap is structural, not just unmigrated effort. Separately, rewrite.rs/program.rs/definition.rs duplicate the same ~250-line plan/conflict-resolution algorithm three times, and QueryContext recomputes every semantic query (byte_source, pure, first_nul, ...) from scratch on every call with no memoization.

Scope: generalize the plan/apply machinery over node kind (one generic engine instead of three copies), add statement-window matching so multi-statement rewrites can use the engine, memoize QueryContext's semantic queries, and lay the groundwork (hand-written Field<T,Cx> combinator) for a structural pattern layer once real repetition justifies it. Full design and rationale: matcher-plan.md at the repo root.

Out of scope: migrating individual rewrites (tracked as slate-04q.75 children already), incremental/lazy invalidation of facts::analyze across the whole pipeline (separate future initiative, see matcher-plan.md section 5), and building the Matchable derive macro speculatively before hand-written pattern structs prove it's warranted.
design:
Four layers, kept separate: (1) structural shape matching - pure function of the AST node, gets Field<T,Cx> eventually; (2) semantic proof queries against FixupFacts - stays as imperative ?-chained case context methods returning Proof/Rejection, this is already the right shape and should not be flattened into field predicates since cross-argument relationships (e.g. prefix_contains(count, nul)) aren't independent per-field checks; (3) typed rewrite recipes producing rust_ast nodes; (4) plan/apply with conflict detection, generalized to be node-kind-agnostic via a Site/EditTarget trait pair instead of three parallel builder structs.

Build order matters: generic Plan<E: EditTarget> first (net negative LOC, de-risks everything after), memoized QueryContext cache in parallel (independent, mechanical), then StmtWindowRule (the actual unlock, prove it on range_loop before touching passes with more moving parts), then hand-written Field<T,Cx>/pattern structs only once 2-3 StmtWindowRule cases exist and the boilerplate is visibly repeated, then evaluate the Matchable derive (and the proc-macro workspace split it requires) only once hand-written structs are repetitive across 3+ node types.
acceptance_criteria:
- rewrite.rs/program.rs/definition.rs collapse into one generic Plan<E: EditTarget> engine with no behavior change to existing memchr/libc_exit/anonymous_structs/PruneUnusedDefinitions rules.
- A StmtWindowRule exists that can match a fixed-width run of adjacent IndentStmt, query facts against the window, and splice in a replacement, with the same conflict-detection/tracing guarantees as ExprPlan.
- QueryContext's semantic query methods are memoized per snapshot with no change to case-function call sites or Proof/Rejection semantics.
- src/fixups/query/matcher.rs (broken scratch file) is removed or replaced.
- Total engine size stays under the 10k loc ceiling from matcher-plan.md.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass at each slice.
close_reason: Closed

title: Migrate libc_exit fixup to the query engine
description: Migrate the remaining legacy implementation in src/fixups/rewrite/libc_exit.rs to the query-driven fixup interface. Preserve the fixup's current semantic guards, every scheduled invocation and fresh-fact boundary in src/fixups/mod.rs, and its fixup-debug identity while moving candidate discovery, fact joins, mutation, and tracing into shared query facilities.
design: Define concise ordered rules in src/fixups/query/rules/libc_exit.rs. Add reusable QueryContext predicates, typed proof views, recipes, or planner actions only where this migration requires them; keep traversal and detailed AST construction out of the rule. Continue to leave unsupported or unproved shapes unchanged. Remove the legacy rewrite module once fixture behavior and trace parity are established.
acceptance_criteria: The libc_exit rewrite is authored through the query engine with short proof-gated cases and typed AST recipes; all current scheduling/order behavior is preserved or intentionally consolidated with fresh facts; accepted and important rejected paths emit automatic query traces; src/fixups/rewrite/libc_exit.rs and its legacy registration are removed; focused C fixture and tests/differential.rs coverage prove output shape and differential behavior; no unit tests are added under src/fixups/query; cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Migrated libc exit rewriting end-to-end to the query engine. Added a concise known-call rule, reusable never-returning extern proof, typed std::process::exit recipe, and optional trivial-unsafe wrapper replacement. Deleted src/fixups/rewrite/libc_exit.rs. Added accepted-rewrite debug evidence coverage and project-local exit non-rewrite coverage. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets; cargo nextest r --release (204 passed, 2 skipped); git diff --check.
close_reason: Completed and validated the query-engine libc_exit migration; removed the legacy rewrite implementation.

title: Add declarative definition lifecycles and grouped cleanup
description: Extend the query engine so definition rules can choose ordered typed actions after call rewrites stabilize: delete a definition when a complete use domain proves zero users, otherwise replace or idiomatize its body. Migrate the generated __slate_memchr helper lifecycle to this interface and remove the legacy memchr_prelude rewrite module. Generalize the same deletion vocabulary to groups of declarations so later header/library migrations can prove that no exported symbol in a complete group remains referenced and delete the represented declarations or container.
design: Keep baseline lowering responsible for emitting the correct helper. After expression rewrite planning applies and facts are recomputed, run an ordered definition rule against the fresh snapshot. The memchr definition rule selects an unused case that emits DeleteDefinition when zero_users succeeds, then a retained fallback that emits ReplaceFunctionBody using a shared typed byte-search helper recipe. Definition cases own their trace identity and the planner applies typed item/body edits deterministically with conflict detection. Add a complete group-use proof over explicitly indexed definitions; missing group membership, raw/unresolved state, externally reachable local definitions, indirect references, and escaped symbol values remain conservative. Extern declarations retain function identity/header provenance so a future header rule can select a complete declaration group without a pass-local scan.
acceptance_criteria: src/fixups/rewrite/memchr_prelude.rs is removed. The memchr query rule module contains call cases plus one concise ordered definition lifecycle: zero users deletes __slate_memchr; otherwise its body is replaced with the existing idiomatic slice-position fallback through a typed shared recipe. Baseline lowering remains correct without query fixups. Call rewriting is followed by fresh analysis before the definition lifecycle, and downstream passes see the resulting AST. The definition planner supports both DeleteDefinition and ReplaceFunctionBody intents, deterministic application, conflict rejection, automatic proof evidence, and lazy action-level trace output. Query APIs can select an explicit definition group and prove all definitions in its complete use domain have zero users, enabling later header/extern-container deletion without custom traversal. Existing memchr pass/debug behavior is intentionally consolidated or updated consistently, and fixture-level output/debug assertions cover both retained-helper and deleted-helper outcomes. No unit tests are added under src/fixups/query. cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Implemented ordered declarative definition lifecycles with Delete and ReplaceBody recipes, automatic proof/rejection traces, deterministic conflict handling, zero-user and zero-group-user proofs, header provenance, query-driven known extern cleanup, and concise memchr helper lifecycle. Removed legacy memchr_prelude and prune_unused_externs rewrite modules. Added SupportModule AST items with explicit qualified exports so generated runtime lifetime is tied to AST users; final prune_unused_definitions runs after all user-changing passes. Added support_module_cleanup fixture and differential assertions. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets; isolated mem_memchr, effects_nullable_pointer, and support_module_cleanup differential fixtures; focused rewrite/debug tests; full cargo nextest r --release: 203 passed, 2 skipped.
close_reason: Declarative definition lifecycle, grouped cleanup, memchr migration, extern migration, and user-tied support module cleanup implemented and fully validated.

title: Add declarative rewrite rules and zero-use definition cleanup
description: The first memchr query migration centralized selection and mutation but still leaves rule authors responsible for ExprRule protocol boilerplate, explicit evidence plumbing, rejection construction, and low-level rust_ast assembly. Add a higher-level embedded rule interface where a call rewrite is expressed as argument captures, ordered proof preconditions, and a typed replacement recipe. Prove the interface by reducing the complete memchr call rewrite to one compact rule declaration. Also generalize post-rewrite cleanup as a query over a complete use domain: when a generated or extern definition has zero remaining users, emit a typed item-deletion intent. Migrate __slate_memchr helper pruning to that pattern so later idiomatization passes can reuse it for obsolete helpers and extern declarations. Keep helper-body construction outside this slice.
design: Build a Rust-embedded declarative layer over the existing QueryContext and planner rather than a textual or rendered-source DSL. A rule declaration binds call arguments, evaluates ordered cases, accumulates proof evidence and rejection diagnostics implicitly, and returns typed recipe terms. Introduce a small reusable recipe algebra or typed builders for byte views, position/known indexes, pointer reconstruction, null fallback, casts, closures, and method calls; recipe lowering owns rust_ast construction. The memchr module should state approximately: match __slate_memchr(source, needle, count); known_nul requires byte_source, needle == 0, first_nul, and prefix_contains then replaces with pointer_at_or_null(source, nul); byte_position requires a full byte view and stable needle then replaces with pointer_at_or_null(source, position(source, needle)). Add program/item edit planning with stable identities and conflict detection. The zero-use predicate must require a complete use domain and treat indirect, escaped, external, or unresolved references conservatively; an empty incomplete domain cannot authorize deletion.
acceptance_criteria: The complete memchr call semantics are represented by one compact rule declaration whose visible contents are the target call, captures, ordered cases, proof requirements, and desired typed transformations; the memchr rule module contains no ExprRule implementation boilerplate, manual candidate/target selection, evidence chaining, hand-built Rejection values, or low-level rust_ast construction used only to express those call replacements. Accepted proof values automatically contribute trace evidence and failed predicates retain useful rejection diagnostics. Replacement recipes remain structured and typed, never rendered Rust strings, and lower through shared query-engine code reusable by other libc/string rules. The planner supports deterministic typed item deletion with overlap/conflict handling. A reusable complete-domain zero-users predicate is added and cannot prove deletion for incomplete, indirect, escaped, external, or unresolved use domains. __slate_memchr pruning uses the generic zero-use query/delete pattern while preserving its pass identity, ordering, --only-pass/--up-to-pass behavior, and lazy debug trace. Focused tests cover both memchr cases, insufficient-evidence fallback, zero-use deletion, retained definitions with users or incomplete domains, and downstream fact recomputation. cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Implemented a Rust-embedded declarative call-rule layer with typed argument captures, ordered cases, automatic evidence/rejection accumulation, and shared typed recipe lowering. The memchr call rewrite is now a 36-line declaration module with no ExprRule implementation, candidate/target plumbing, evidence chains, Rejection construction, or rust_ast assembly. Added a complete-domain symbol-use index, zero_users proof, typed definition targets, deterministic/conflict-aware definition deletion planning, and lazy trace events; memchr helper pruning now uses this generic pattern, with extern function declarations supported as a future consumer. Per the user's testing direction, removed all unit-test modules from src/fixups/query and kept coverage through real fixtures. Validation: mem_memchr and effects_nullable_pointer isolated differential fixtures; focused memchr rewrite/debug/zero-use output tests; cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets; full cargo nextest r --release (202 passed, 2 skipped); git diff --check.
close_reason: Completed the compact declarative memchr rule, reusable typed recipe lowering, and complete-domain zero-use definition cleanup with fixture-only differential coverage and passing release gates.

title: Enable CIR emission for __builtin_readcyclecounter
description: Configured x86_64 Clang accepts __builtin_readcyclecounter, but CIR reports the builtin as not yet implemented before Slate receives an op. Track the frontend prerequisite separately from emitted x86 LLVM intrinsic lowering.
acceptance_criteria: CIR emits __builtin_readcyclecounter without an error, and a Slate differential fixture observes a nonzero cycle counter consistently with C.
notes: Verified 2026-07-29 with CIR Clang 24.0.0git at 350c2d86228f330d986f6c8cd63899cd147427c3: emit-cir reports ClangIR code gen Not Yet Implemented for __builtin_readcyclecounter, so Slate receives no operation to lower.

title: Map Clang target attributes to Rust target features
description: Single-version target attributes are accepted by ClangIR, but generated Rust does not retain a target_feature contract. Optional SSSE3, AVX2, BMI2, and SSE4.2 functions need architecture cfgs and matching Rust target-feature annotations before their instruction bodies can be correct and safely called behind CPU checks.
acceptance_criteria: Supported Clang target feature strings map to Rust target_feature annotations under the correct architecture cfg; calls remain guarded where the feature is not globally enabled.
close_reason: Mechanism landed in 3020f2d1 (handle target feature for intrinsics) as part of closing the sibling slate-3f8g.4.9: target_feature_functions() in src/frontend/lowerer.rs diffs each function's cir.target-features against the module baseline and emits #[target_feature(enable=...)], routing the function through the existing unsafe fn / unsafe-call-site-wrapping mechanism so guarded calls fall out for free. Verified against the AC's named features: SSSE3 and AVX2 via tests/fixtures/x86_simd_vector_intrinsics.c (generated Rust carries #[target_feature(enable = "sse3,ssse3")] / avx2 correctly), SSE4.2 via tests/fixtures/x86_instruction_intrinsics.c's crc32_probe (target("sse4.2")) using the crc32->sse4.2 rustc_target_feature_name remap. BMI2 has no fixture and can't yet be exercised -- __builtin_ia32_pdep_si isn't emitted by CIR at all, tracked separately in the still-open/blocked slate-3f8g.4.8 -- but the mapping is generic over whatever feature strings CIR provides, so BMI2 will work automatically once 4.8 unblocks. The AC's 'architecture cfg' clause doesn't apply here: Slate translates one target triple per run (no multi-arch #[cfg(target_arch)] needed); host-arch fixture gating is the separate open child slate-3f8g.4.12. docs/src/features.md target checkbox flipped to [x] in this session.

title: Enable CIR emission for x86 function multiversioning
description: Configured Clang accepts target("default"), target_clones, cpu_dispatch, and cpu_specific forms in gnu_x86_multiversion.c. ClangIR rejects them through unimplemented multiversion mangling, declaration, and function-creation paths. A single non-default target("sse2") function emits and matches when multiversion forms are reduced.
acceptance_criteria: CIR represents target clones and CPU dispatch/specific definitions, generates the resolver surface, and the intact multiversion fixture prints 11 12 13 14 after Slate translation.
notes: Blocked: not a slate bug. Confirmed by running SLATE_CLANG -emit-cir directly on the fixture: fails at CIR-emission with 'ClangIR code gen Not Yet Implemented: getMangledName: multi-version functions' (clang/lib/CIR/CodeGen/CIRGenModule.cpp:2722, upstream llvm-project checkout at ~/llvm-project). ClangIR has no mangling/resolver/ifunc support ported from classic Clang CodeGen for target/target_clones/cpu_dispatch/cpu_specific yet, so no CIR is ever produced for slate to lower. Requires upstream ClangIR work, not a slate-side fix.

title: Lower x86 SIMD intrinsic vectors and storage
description: SSE2, SSSE3, and AVX2 intrinsics emit vector creation, reinterpretation, arithmetic, and unaligned storage shapes that Slate does not represent correctly. Generated Rust has undefined cir.vec.create results, invalid array casts and arithmetic, a scalar abs call on an array, and missing __storeu_si128/__storeu_si256 types.
acceptance_criteria: 128-bit and 256-bit intrinsic vectors retain lane type, width, bitcast semantics, arithmetic, and unaligned load/store layouts; baseline and runtime-guarded SIMD probes compile and match C.
close_reason: Fixed lower_abs for vector cir.abs (was calling scalar .abs() on the whole array instead of per-lane wrapping_abs/abs); added target_feature propagation (clang-ir Function.target_features + Function.target_cpu typed fields, populated from cir.target-features/cir.target-cpu; slate diffs each function's features against the module baseline and emits #[target_feature(enable=...)] + unsafe fn, feeding the existing unsafe_functions call-site-wrapping mechanism). Added tests/fixtures/x86_simd_vector_intrinsics.c covering SSE2/SSSE3/AVX2 vector create/bitcast/arithmetic/storeu; manually verified byte-identical stdout+exit code vs clang for both the new fixture and the pre-existing x86_instruction_intrinsics.c crc32 fixture (which also newly compiles/runs correctly). Differential test harness (tests/differential.rs) is currently disabled project-wide, so verification was done by hand: cargo run -- translate, then compiled/ran the generated Rust in a manual cargo project against vendor/aligned,bitint,num-complex, diffed vs native clang binaries.

title: Enable CIR emission for accepted x86 instruction builtins
description: Configured Clang accepts __builtin_readcyclecounter and BMI2 __builtin_ia32_pdep_si, but ClangIR reports both as unimplemented. They are isolated from the separate Slate lowering failures for CIR operations that do emit.
acceptance_criteria: Configured ClangIR emits readcyclecounter and pdep operations; the intact x86 target and intrinsic completion fixtures pass frontend translation.

title: Lower emitted x86 instruction LLVM intrinsics
description: Pause, lfence/mfence/sfence, rdtsc, rdtscp, and CRC32 reach cir.call_llvm_intrinsic, which Slate lowers to unsupported panics. rdtscp additionally uses unhandled cir.extract_member results and undefined temporaries.
acceptance_criteria: The emitted x86 intrinsic calls and aggregate results map to target-correct Rust intrinsics or asm; the instruction and CRC probes compile and match their deterministic C observations.
close_reason: Mapped emitted x86 pause, fence, RDTSC, RDTSCP, and CRC32 LLVM intrinsics to target-appropriate core::arch calls, materialized RDTSCP aggregate results, and added passing differential coverage.

title: Enable CIR emission for x86 CPU query builtins
description: Configured x86_64 Clang accepts __builtin_cpu_init, __builtin_cpu_supports, and __builtin_cpu_is, but ClangIR reports the query builtins as not yet implemented and crashes while lowering the surrounding boolean expression.
acceptance_criteria: CIR emits CPU initialization, feature, and model queries without crashing; the runtime-guarded target and intrinsic fixtures translate and observe the same host feature mask as C.
notes: Verified 2026-07-29 with CIR Clang 24.0.0git at 350c2d86228f330d986f6c8cd63899cd147427c3: emit-cir on tests/fixtures.unsupported/gnu_x86_target.c reports Not Yet Implemented for __builtin_cpu_init and __builtin_cpu_supports, then crashes in CIRGen while lowering the surrounding boolean expression. Slate cannot implement the acceptance criteria until CIR emits CPU init, feature, and model queries.

title: Lower GNU asm goto control flow and outputs
description: Configured Clang 24 supports full asm-goto outputs, but Slate drops the assembly branch and labels. The zero-input probe returns 11 instead of 13 and the taken output probe returns 1 instead of 2.
acceptance_criteria: asm goto labels become equivalent Rust control flow while outputs remain valid along every edge; both taken and fallthrough probes in gnu_inline_asm.c match C.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower GNU extended asm constraints and clobbers
description: Slate replaces extended asm with operand approximations instead of executing the template. Output, read-write, tied, early-clobber, immediate-modifier, memory, flag-output, numeric/symbolic operand, volatile, cc, and memory semantics are lost. The reduced fixture prints 16 and 19 instead of 35 and 15; cpuid.h multi-output asm also produces invalid _tmp member accesses.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted x86_64 templates lower to typed Rust asm with correct operand directions, explicit registers/constraints, modifiers, options, clobbers, and multi-output handling; extended and CPUID probes compile and match C.
notes: Started typed GNU extended-asm lowering. Implemented r/=r/=&r/i constraints, numeric ties, in/out/inout direction selection, AT&T placeholder and width-modifier translation, unused operand references, CIR packed multi-output forwarding, typed Rust AST/codegen nodes, shared walker coverage, and Rust-effects operand modeling. Added tests/fixtures/gnu_extended_asm.c; differential output 29 15 34 matches C. Remaining on this bead: explicit/fixed registers and clobbers, memory operands, flag outputs, broader constraint/modifier coverage, and CPUID probe.
close_reason: Closed

title: Preserve GNU file-scope and basic assembly
description: Configured Clang accepts file-scope assembly defining gnu_basic_asm_function and function basic assembly mutating gnu_basic_asm_value. Slate drops both assembly bodies: generated Rust fails to link the external symbol and leaves the observable value at zero.
acceptance_criteria: File-scope assembly is emitted through a target-scoped global_asm representation and function basic asm preserves its side effects; the two basic-asm probes return 37 and 23 in generated Rust.
notes: Implemented target-arch-scoped global_asm lowering for non-empty CIR module assembly; modeled CIR asm_flavor with AsmDialect::Att/Intel; lowered operand-free basic asm through core::arch::asm with raw templates; unmangled assembly-referenced globals; and added opaque effects support for assembly-defined externs and inline asm. Added gnu_basic_asm fixture and generated-shape regression. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy; cargo nextest r --release -E 'not binary(alive_regression)' (609 passed, 1 skipped); generated differential and full effects regression pass. Alive regression excluded per user direction.
close_reason: File-scope and function basic assembly now preserve the 37 and 23 probes with target-scoped Rust assembly lowering.

title: Audit configured x86_64 target extensions
description: Capability-gate deterministic target-specific facilities accepted by configured x86_64 Clang 24, including CPU queries, x86 scalar/instruction builtins, target multiversioning attributes, segment address spaces, register variables, and vector/intrinsic surfaces. Build completion fixtures, translate them, reduce failures, and file focused gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Every selected x86_64 target family is exercised or explicitly classified; runtime probes avoid assuming optional CPU features; every observed frontend, lowering, compile, link, or behavior gap has focused child work.
notes: Audited configured x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu Clang 24. gnu_x86_target.c covers CPU model/feature queries, cpuid.h, pause/fences/timestamps, non-temporal accesses, FS/GS pointer types, and a fixed-register variable; C output is "63 5 4 1 19" on this host. gnu_x86_intrinsics.c covers baseline SSE2 and runtime-guarded SSSE3, AVX2, BMI2, and SSE4.2 CRC; host output is "50 10 24 17 4201928244". gnu_x86_multiversion.c covers target, target_clones, cpu_dispatch, and cpu_specific; C output is "11 12 13 14". CPU queries, readcyclecounter, pdep, and multiversioning fail in ClangIR. Emitted instruction intrinsics, SIMD vectors, CPUID multi-results, and target-feature contracts fail in Slate. Reduced FS/GS type, fixed-register, and single target("sse2") probes compile and match. Non-x86 backends, privileged instructions, actual FS/GS dereferences, optional features without runtime guards, and exact timestamp values are excluded.
close_reason: Configured x86_64 target families are fixture-covered or explicitly excluded, successful reductions match C, and every observed gap is filed.

title: Audit Clang-supported GNU inline assembly
description: Build deterministic x86_64 GNU23 completion fixtures for basic asm, volatile extended asm, input/output/read-write/early-clobber constraints, symbolic and numeric operands, memory and condition-code clobbers, local labels, asm goto, and flag outputs as accepted by configured Clang 24. Translate as black-box probes and file focused gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Each accepted GNU asm form is exercised or explicitly excluded; unblocked generated Rust matches C; every CIR, lowering, compile, or behavior gap has focused child work.
notes: Configured Clang 24 reports gnu_asm_goto_with_outputs and gnu_asm_goto_with_outputs_full. gnu_inline_asm.c covers file-scope and function basic asm, volatile extended asm, output/read-write/tied/early-clobber constraints, numeric and symbolic operands, immediate modifiers, memory and cc clobbers, flag outputs, local labels, asm inline, asm goto, and asm-goto outputs. C output is "37 23 35 15 17 13 6 2". Slate translates the file but drops file/basic asm, causing an undefined external and lost store. After replacing the file-scope symbol, generated Rust prints "37 0 16 19 17 11 6 1" rather than C. Children slate-3f8g.4.3 through .5 cover the three isolated asm gaps; CPUID multi-output asm is included in .4.
close_reason: Configured Clang inline-asm capability is fixture-covered and every observed gap is filed.

title: Use the C ABI for GNU libc callbacks
description: Generated extern declarations for qsort_r and argp_parse contain Rust-ABI fn pointers. rustc warns these callback parameters are not FFI-safe. The current x86_64 execution happens to match C, but correctness requires extern C callback types for qsort_r, argp, fopencookie, and search callbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Every callback parameter and callback-bearing aggregate in the GNU libc fixtures uses the correct unsafe extern C function-pointer ABI and rustc emits no improper_ctypes warnings for them.

title: Emit complete GNU regex, glob, and dynamic-loader type closures
description: Using regex_t, glob_t, and Dl_info causes generated Rust to reference undeclared re_dfa_t, dirent/stat variants, and link_map types pulled through GNU libc headers. Environment, time, random, auxv, system-info, backtrace, and program-invocation APIs match C when these header families are reduced.
acceptance_criteria: All dependent public and intentionally opaque types needed by regex.h, glob.h, and dlfcn.h are emitted or mapped to libc types; the intact platform fixture compiles and matches C.

title: Represent GNU obstack layouts and allocator callbacks
description: The obstack completion target emits an unresolved anonymous bitfield type for struct obstack and passes unsafe extern C malloc/free symbols to callback slots typed as safe Rust functions. The remaining GNU allocation APIs match C after obstack coverage and its include are reduced.
acceptance_criteria: The public obstack layout, macros, and allocator/free callback ABI are represented correctly; the intact allocation fixture compiles and returns the same output as C.
close_reason: Completed the public obstack layout and macro ABI, added API coverage, and promoted the intact GNU allocation fixture; rewrites, lowering, and libc profiles pass.

title: Emit GNU getopt and search table types
description: gnu_libc_algorithms.c fails because struct option is emitted as an unresolved option type and hsearch_data refers to unresolved _ENTRY. qsort_r and argp match C when getopt/search coverage and the search.h include are reduced.
acceptance_criteria: getopt_long, hcreate_r/hsearch_r/hdestroy_r, tsearch/tfind/tdestroy, and their public aggregates translate with complete types; the intact algorithms fixture compiles and matches C.

title: Emit GNU cookie stream ABI types
description: fopencookie is accepted by Clang/glibc and runs correctly in C, but Slate emits references to undefined _IO_cookie_io_functions_t and initializes the callback aggregate as scalar zero. The remaining allocating, memory-stream, getline/getdelim, stdio_ext, and printf-introspection coverage matches C when this function is reduced.
acceptance_criteria: cookie_io_functions_t and its callback fields have complete C-compatible Rust representations; gnu_cookie_stdio compiles, invokes its write/close callbacks, and returns 6 in both C and Rust.

title: Audit deterministic GNU libc extension families
description: Inventory deterministic _GNU_SOURCE APIs exposed by host glibc 2.43, build black-box completion fixtures by library family, translate them with configured Clang/CIR, reduce failures, and file focused gaps. Exclude POSIX-only APIs, nondeterministic host/service databases, privileged operations, and kernel-version-dependent behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Every selected GNU-specific libc family has a deterministic fixture or an explicit exclusion; C and unblocked Rust outputs are compared; every frontend, lowering, compile, link, or behavior gap has focused child work.
notes: Audited host glibc 2.43 under _GNU_SOURCE with five deterministic GNU23 fixtures. Configured-Clang outputs are strings "122 8 6", stdio "9 8 6 1", algorithms "4321 71 52 5", allocation "16 3", and platform "6 2 19". All five translate to Rust source. The intact strings/argz/envz fixture compiles and matches. Reduced stdio, algorithms, allocation, and platform fixtures compile and match after isolating failures. Observed blockers are cookie stream ABI types, getopt/search type closure, obstack layout and allocator callbacks, regex/glob/dlfcn transitive types, Rust-ABI libc callback declarations, and a non-portable strlen declaration warning. The audit excludes POSIX-only facilities, NSS and user/group/network databases, locale-dependent text and message catalogs, privileged/destructive process operations, scheduler-dependent thread behavior, and kernel-version-dependent results. Random/host helpers are included only through deterministic success/property checks. Explicit-link GNU libm and companion libraries are deferred to slate-3f8g.5.8.
close_reason: Selected deterministic GNU libc families are covered by completion fixtures, unblocked subsets were differentially checked, exclusions are explicit, and every observed gap has focused child work.

title: Enable CIR emission for legacy GNU sync CAS and lock builtins
description: Configured Clang accepts __sync_bool_compare_and_swap, __sync_val_compare_and_swap, __sync_lock_test_and_set, __sync_lock_release, and __sync_swap, but the CIR frontend reports their width-specific forms as not yet implemented. The tested legacy arithmetic and fence operations translate and match C.
acceptance_criteria: CIR emits the five operations and intact gnu_builtins_atomic.c translates, compiles, and matches C.

title: Lower atomic test-and-set and clear CIR operations
description: __atomic_test_and_set and __atomic_clear emit cir.atomic.test_and_set and cir.atomic.clear. Slate reports both unsupported and generated Rust references undefined temporaries. Other tested __atomic arithmetic, exchange, compare-exchange, fence, and lock-free operations match C after these calls are reduced out.
acceptance_criteria: Both CIR operations lower with C atomic semantics; intact gnu_builtins_atomic.c generates compilable Rust whose stdout/exit status match C.
close_reason: Closed

title: Enable CIR emission for aligned alloca and inline memcpy builtins
description: Configured Clang 24 accepts __builtin_alloca_with_align and __builtin_memcpy_inline, but CIR emission reports both as not yet implemented. Ordinary alloca and the remaining memory/string builtin fixture translate and match C.
acceptance_criteria: The configured CIR frontend emits both builtins and the intact gnu_builtins_memory.c fixture translates, compiles, and prints the same output as C.

title: Preserve __builtin_addressof in pointer comparisons
description: The core builtin fixture compares __builtin_addressof(value) with &value. Slate drops the address-of on the right and emits pointer == integer value. This shares the underlying pointer-comparison defect tracked by slate-5exy.3.5.
acceptance_criteria: The builtin result and ordinary address-of operand remain pointers; the equality compiles and evaluates true in generated Rust.
close_reason: Added focused differential coverage proving __builtin_addressof remains pointer-equal to ordinary address-of and dereferences the original object; existing slate-5exy.3.5 lowering passes end to end

title: Lower GNU return-address introspection builtins
description: __builtin_return_address reaches cir.return_address, which Slate leaves unsupported and references an undefined temporary in generated Rust. The fixture also covers frame-address plus extract/frob helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Return/frame address introspection and helper operations produce compilable Rust with equivalent null/non-null observations in gnu_builtins_core.c.

title: Fix ptr_len array-to-slice provenance (soundness + interprocedural)
description:
src/fixups/facts/ptr_len.rs currently promotes (pointer,length) parameter pairs to safe slices based on coincidence, not provenance: adjacent_ptr_len_pair only considers the first adjacent (ptr,int) param pair, collect_body_arrays flattens array lengths by raw name across scopes (scope leakage), and callsite() only checks that the length argument's literal value happens to equal the array's length rather than proving dataflow identity. This means it can pick the wrong pair, cross-match shadowed arrays of the same length, and can never prove a pointer/length pair that is forwarded unchanged through a chain of function calls.

Rework around a whole-program fixed-point analysis (same pattern as facts/string_params.rs's char*->&str lift): BindingId-keyed candidate pairs, a LengthSource::{Const(u64) from real array type, Bound(BindingId) from an active candidate's own param} provenance model, and per-callsite dataflow proof instead of literal-value coincidence. Adds interprocedural propagation so forwarded ptr/len pairs across function-call boundaries can also be proven and converted to real &[T]/&mut [T] slices. Full design in /home/takashi/.claude/plans/fluffy-weaving-bengio.md.
acceptance_criteria: adjacent_ptr_len_pair considers all adjacent pairs, not just the first; array length provenance is BindingId-scoped (no name-based scope leakage); callsite matching is a genuine identity proof (const array length or forwarded-binding identity), not literal-value coincidence; a ptr/len pair forwarded unchanged through a chain of function calls (outer(p,n){inner(p,n);}) is provably convertible to a slice; new unit tests cover direct-case regressions, interprocedural forwarding, shadowed-array negative case, multi-pair negative case, coincidental-literal negative case, and reassigned-param negative case; cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release passes
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/ptr_len.rs, ptr_len fixup tests/fixtures
close_reason: Implemented binding/provenance-based ptr_len slice lifting: candidate pointer/integer pairs now require callee-side extent use or unchanged forwarding, preserve unrelated printable parameters, support non-adjacent extent parameters, and added ptr_len_nonadjacent differential coverage. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Fix typed dispatch-loop break mismatch in generated libyaml output
description: cargo check of the generated ~/libyaml crate reports E0308 mismatched types for labeled dispatch-loop breaks such as break '__dispatch0; in contexts expecting i32. Representative locations from /tmp/slate-libyaml-crate include src/api.rs:1424, src/api.rs:2482, src/api.rs:2787, src/api.rs:2928, and src/api.rs:3091. Emit a value-carrying break or restructure the state-machine lowering so typed contexts compile.
notes: Fixed in src/lower.rs lower_dispatch: value-returning functions put the dispatch loop in tail position, so the wildcard 'break $dispatch (yielding ()) mismatched the return type (E0308). Reaching the wildcard = C ran off the end of a non-void function (UB), so it now emits unreachable!(), making the loop diverge (!) and coerce to the return type. Void functions keep break (already correct). Added fixture tests/fixtures/goto_return_value.c; 211 tests pass. Regenerated ~/libyaml crate: 0 dispatch-break errors remain (only E0425 from q0g.1).
close_reason: Dispatch-loop break mismatch fixed: value-returning functions emit unreachable!() at the wildcard so the loop diverges and coerces to the return type; verified in isolation and on regenerated libyaml crate (no E0308 dispatch errors).

title: Lower CIR aggregate extract and insert member ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.extract_member and cir.insert_member as P1 unsupported. Aggregate value mutation/extraction appears once structs/unions are manipulated by value rather than only through addresses.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for cir.extract_member and cir.insert_member.
- Preserve C aggregate semantics while generating Rust field/member updates compatible with existing struct representation.
- Add differential fixtures for struct value extraction, mutation, nested aggregates, and array-containing structs where supported.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Implemented cir.extract_member/cir.insert_member lowering for struct values, added synthetic lowerer tests for both op spellings, added aggregate_value_member_ops differential fixture for by-value aggregate coverage, and updated docs/cir-op-prioritization.md. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt, cargo run -- emit-fixtures, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Lower CIR memory operation intrinsics
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.libc.memchr, cir.libc.memcpy, cir.libc.memmove, cir.libc.memset, cir.memcpy_inline, and cir.memset_inline as P1 unsupported. Memory operations are high-leverage for real C and stdlib expansion.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for the CIR memory operation family.
- Map libc and inline forms to Rust/libc/std::ptr operations with correct overlap behavior for memmove versus memcpy.
- Add differential fixtures for scalar buffers, struct/array copies, memset zero/nonzero, memchr hits/misses, and overlapping memmove.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Lowered the cir.libc.mem* family (memcpy/memmove/memset/memchr) to byte-wise std::ptr ops + __slate_memchr helper; added PtrCopy/WriteBytes AST nodes and 4 differential fixtures. Plain libc mem* calls already worked via extern; only clang builtins/aggregate bit_cast raise these ops. Idiom-recognizer is a no-op stub upstream (noted in emit.rs).

title: Lower CIR bitfield get and set ops
description:
Why: docs/cir-op-prioritization.md marks cir.get_bitfield and cir.set_bitfield as P1 unsupported. C bitfields are common in systems headers and data layouts.

What to do:
- Add parser/lowerer support for cir.get_bitfield and cir.set_bitfield.
- Preserve signedness, width, offset, masking, and update semantics from CIR.
- Add differential fixtures for signed/unsigned bitfields, adjacent fields, boundary widths, and read-modify-write updates.
- Update docs/cir-op-prioritization.md.
close_reason: Lowered cir.get_bitfield/cir.set_bitfield as mask+sign-extend over per-field struct storage (behaviorally identical to CIR shared storage for well-defined C). Added bitfield_ops differential fixture (signed/unsigned, adjacent fields, boundary widths, read-modify-write, 40-bit long-long) and marked ops supported in docs. Verified: cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release (116 passed).

title: Lower CIR atomics to real Rust atomics (AtomicN::from_ptr)
description: Replace the non-atomic RMW lowering of cir.atomic.* with genuine std::sync::atomic ops so the output is correct once multithreaded programs land. Use AtomicN::from_ptr(store_address(ptr)) to view the existing integer slot atomically without changing its storage. fetch->fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor/nand/max/min (recompute new value when fetch_first is absent); xchg->swap; cmpxchg->compare_exchange (strong, to stay deterministic); fence->std::sync::atomic::fence. Also route mem_order-carrying cir.load/cir.store to atomic load()/store() so a shared _Atomic object is never accessed non-atomically (else data race under threads). Float/pointer atomics keep the non-atomic fallback (no std atomic float).
design: atomic_wrapper(rust_ty)->Option<AtomicN name> for i8..u64/isize/usize/bool. Ordering from C mem_order enum (0 relaxed,1 consume,2 acquire,3 release,4 acqrel,5 seqcst); clamp to load/store-valid orderings; consume->Acquire; relaxed thread fence is a no-op (fence(Relaxed) panics in Rust). compare_exchange always strong (weak may spuriously fail and diverge from C in differential tests).
acceptance_criteria: tests/fixtures/atomics.c still passes generated_differential; generated Rust uses AtomicN::from_ptr(...).fetch_*/swap/compare_exchange and atomic load/store; no non-atomic access to _Atomic objects.
close_reason: Atomics now lower to real std::sync::atomic ops via AtomicN::from_ptr (fetch_*/swap/compare_exchange/fence + atomic load/store). atomics.c differential passes; pthread program lowers correct atomic ops. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.fence (thread fence)
description: Lower cir.atomic.fence to std::sync::atomic::fence(Ordering::SeqCst) — a harmless no-op single-threaded. No operands, no result; the ordering attr can be ignored (SeqCst is always safe/strongest).
acceptance_criteria: atomic_thread_fence fixture translates without warnings and passes differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.cmpxchg (compare-exchange)
description: Lower cir.atomic.cmpxchg(ptr,expected,desired) -> (old, bool). Two results: old = *ptr; ok = old == expected; if ok { *ptr = desired }. Bind result[0]->old (int), result[1]->ok (bool). Surrounding CIR handles writing the actual value back to the C 'expected' lvalue on failure.
acceptance_criteria: atomic_compare_exchange_strong fixture (both success and failure paths) translates without warnings and passes differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.xchg (atomic exchange)
description: Lower cir.atomic.xchg(ptr,val) -> old: read *store_address(ptr) into a temp, store val, bind result to the old value.
acceptance_criteria: atomic_exchange fixture translates without warnings and passes differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Lower cir.atomic.fetch (atomic RMW fetch ops)
description: Lower cir.atomic.fetch(ptr,val) to a non-atomic read-modify-write. binop attr selects the op (0=Add,1=Sub,2=And,3=Xor,4=Or,5=Nand,6=Max,7=Min); Nand => !(old & val); Max/Min => old.max/min(val). The fetch_first unit attr means the op returns the pre-op value (fetch_add); its absence means it returns the post-op value (add_fetch). Emit: read *store_address(ptr), compute new, write back, bind result to old or new.
acceptance_criteria: atomic_fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor and __atomic_add_fetch fixtures translate without warnings and pass differential.
close_reason: Lowered as non-atomic RMW via store_address; atomics.c fixture passes generated_differential. Merged to main.

title: Support CIR C atomics (cir.atomic.*)
description: C11/GNU atomics lower to distinct CIR ops that Slate currently drops (warns 'unsupported CIR op'): cir.atomic.fetch, cir.atomic.xchg, cir.atomic.cmpxchg, cir.atomic.fence. Atomic loads/stores already lower correctly (plain cir.load/cir.store carrying mem_order/sync_scope attrs, which are safely ignored). Because Slate's correctness bar is single-threaded differential testing, lower these as plain non-atomic read-modify-write through store_address(ptr) (transliterate-first); real Rust atomics are a later idiomatization fixup.
design: Use store_address(ptr) to obtain a uniform *mut T for slot/global/member/element/raw-ptr, then RMW inside unsafe. binop enum: 0=Add,1=Sub,2=And,3=Xor,4=Or,5=Nand,6=Max,7=Min. fetch_first attr present => op returns old value; absent => returns new value.
acceptance_criteria: A C fixture using atomic_fetch_add/sub/and/or/xor, atomic_exchange, atomic_compare_exchange_strong, and atomic_thread_fence translates with no 'unsupported CIR op' warnings and passes generated_differential (identical stdout+exit).

title: Lower calls to external libc functions via extern "C" declarations
description: Slate emits bare Rust calls to external C symbols (e.g. puts(...), strcpy(...), sqrt(...), malloc(...)) with no declaration, so the generated Rust fails to compile (cannot find function). Only printf is special-cased through libc::printf. Root cause for ~45 of 53 failing stdlib_coverage probes (stdio, string, stdlib, math, ctype helpers). Fix: for any called function with no body in the translation unit, emit an extern "C" { fn name(args) -> ret; } declaration (or route to libc::) so the call links against the system C library. Covers stdlib_coverage probes: stdio/{puts,putchar,fputs,fprintf,sprintf,snprintf}, string/*, stdlib/{atoi,atol,labs,strtol,malloc_free,calloc,qsort}, math/*, ctype/* (via __ctype_b_loc/__ctype_toupper_loc).
acceptance_criteria: stdlib_coverage probes for puts, strcpy, strlen, sqrt, atoi, malloc_free translate, compile, and match C stdout+exit; remove them from KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED
close_reason: Collect body-less cir.func decls into an 'unsafe extern "C"{}' block; extern call sites wrap in unsafe and 'as'-cast fixed args to declared param types (variadic '...' preserved). Also: string literals render *mut (weaken to *const for printf), #cir.ptr<null> -> null_mut(), added cir.ptr_diff (offset_from), and -lm in the C harness. stdlib_coverage 25->40 passing: acceptance probes puts/strcpy/strlen/sqrt/atoi/malloc_free all pass, plus ctype/* (via __ctype_b_loc), libm sqrt/sin/cos/exp/log/pow/fmod, string mem*/str* (chr/rchr/str/cmp/ncmp), atol/calloc/strtol, snprintf/sprintf/putchar. Remaining fails belong to other beads (slate-kaf builtins, slate-61j FILE, slate-aeo div_t, slate-6c2 cir.copy).

title: Refactor fuzz generator into C-subset program generator
description: The current BNF expander mostly stitches fixed template fragments together, so generated programs do not exercise variable scope, expression composition, reusable declarations, or realistic statement interactions. Refactor fuzzing around a C-aware program generator that can consume a grammar/BNF for the supported syntax but also maintain generation state: declared variables, types, scopes, functions, globals, and expression contexts. The generator should produce valid C programs for Slate's supported subset, with variables that can be declared, assigned, read, passed to functions, used in array indices, struct/union fields, loops, sizeof, volatile/static contexts where supported, and combined into expressions/statements without violating C validity. The design should be closer to a small csmith-style generator for our subset than a pure random text expander. It should keep deterministic seeds, shrinking/debuggability where practical, and integrate with the existing differential test harness and BNF fuzz entry point. Acceptance criteria: design is documented; generator can emit multi-function programs with scoped variables and expressions; generated programs compile as C and translate with Slate; differential tests run multiple seeds; existing simple BNF tests are either preserved as smoke tests or migrated cleanly.
notes: Refactoring tests/bnf_fuzz.rs fuzzing around a stateful C-subset generator (tests/support/cgen.rs). Keeps BNF grammar+expander as a smoke test; new generator_differential runs multiple seeds. Value-bound tracking guarantees no i32 overflow / OOB so C==Rust.
close_reason: Refactored fuzzing around a stateful C-subset generator (tests/support/cgen.rs): scope/type env + function-signature state compose multi-function programs with scoped vars, expressions, calls; value-bound tracking guarantees no UB so C==Rust. BNF expander kept as bnf_expander_smoke; generator_differential runs N seeds (40 verified green). Design in docs/fuzzing.md. All tests + fmt pass.

Add Prim::F16 + Feature::F16 (nightly #![feature(f16)], mirroring the existing F128 pattern), wire _Float16 through parse_c_type, fix two silent-miscompile bugs where CirType::Fp16 currently falls through to i32/f64 instead of erroring or mapping correctly, and add a differential fixture covering arithmetic plus the variadic-call promotion-skip behavior.
