title: Wire FenvAttr dispatch for Tier 1b ops (sin/cos/exp/pow/round/sqrt/fabs/fmax/fmin/copysign/fma)
description:
Verification is done (was the open question this issue originally posed) --
see handoffs/floating-point-env.md's "Tier 1b" section. Checked every
FenvAttr-carrying CIR op Slate lowers to an f32/f64 std method via
rustc --emit=llvm-ir, not just sqrt/fabs as originally suspected. Real
split:

Needs shimming (compiles to a foldable LLVM intrinsic, same hazard as
+/-/*): sin, cos, exp, exp2, log, log2, log10, pow, ceil, floor, round,
rint (round_ties_even), trunc, sqrt, fabs, fmax (max), fmin (min),
copysign -- plus Op::Fma specifically when FenvAttr is set (.mul_add() is
llvm.fma, also foldable; distinct from slate-kmao's Op::Fmuladd
target-dispatch fix, which doesn't touch this).

Already fine, no work needed: asin, atan, atan2, acos, acosh, asinh,
atanh, cosh, sinh, tanh, cbrt, exp_m1, ln_1p, hypot, tan -- these already
compile to real opaque extern libm calls.

All of the needs-shimming list's C helpers are already written in
src/frontend/shims/fenv.c (__slate_fenv_sin_f64 etc., landed alongside
slate-0ar5.3's closure). What's left here is the lowerer-side dispatch:
each Op::Sin/Op::Cos/Op::Exp/etc. handler in lowerer.rs (currently routing
unconditionally through lower_known_unary_method/lower_binary_method to
.sin()/.cos()/etc., see lowerer.rs:4476-4565 and neighboring arms) needs
the same per-op FenvAttr check slate-0ar5.4 is adding for the core
arithmetic ops -- same containment discipline applies (dispatch off the
op's own attribute, never a function/TU-wide flag).

Runs in parallel with slate-0ar5.4, not after it -- both depend on
slate-0ar5.3 (done) and slate-0ar5.1 (done), not on each other.
acceptance_criteria:
Each Tier 1b op (sin/cos/exp/exp2/log/log2/log10/pow/ceil/floor/round/
rint/trunc/sqrt/fabs/fmax/fmin/copysign, plus Op::Fma under FenvAttr)
checks its own FenvAttr and dispatches to the matching __slate_fenv_*
shim only when set; unconstrained call sites keep lowering to the current
Rust std method unchanged.

Same containment regression test shape as slate-0ar5.4: FENV_ACCESS ON
around exactly one Tier 1b call (e.g. one .sin()), ordinary calls to the
same method elsewhere in the function stay native.
close_reason:
Wired per-op FenvAttr dispatch for the full Tier 1b list identified during
scoping: Op::Cos/Exp/Exp2/Log/Log10/Log2/Sin/Sqrt (via lower_fenv_unary
wrapping the existing lower_known_unary_method path), Op::Fabs/Ceil/Floor/
Rint/Nearbyint/Round/Roundeven/Trunc (via lower_fenv_unary wrapping
lower_unary_method/lower_abs), Op::Pow/Copysign/Fmaxnum/Fminnum (via
lower_fenv_binary_op wrapping lower_known_binary_method/lower_binary_method),
and Op::Fma (inline dispatch, since it already always lowered to
.mul_add() -- now checks fenv first and shims when set, otherwise
unchanged). Same containment discipline as slate-0ar5.4: per-op
`.fenv.is_some()` check, generic fallback closures so the existing
non-constrained lowering path is untouched byte-for-byte when fenv is
absent.

Found two more shim gaps while wiring this: Op::Nearbyint and
Op::Roundeven both carry their own FenvAttr (confirmed in
CIRGenBuiltin.cpp) but have distinct semantics from Op::Rint/Op::Round
(nearbyint never raises FE_INEXACT; roundeven ties-to-even without
consulting rounding mode) -- added __slate_fenv_nearbyint_f{32,64} and
__slate_fenv_roundeven_f{32,64} to fenv.c. roundeven/roundevenf needed
`#define _GNU_SOURCE` before <math.h> to be declared (glibc gates the C23
addition behind that feature-test macro) -- added to fenv.c.

cargo build/fmt/clippy clean. Full lowering nextest profile: 7/7, no
regressions (expected -- FENV_ACCESS is still rejected upstream by
preprocess.rs, so none of this is reachable yet; that's slate-0ar5.5).

title: Allowlist FENV_ACCESS/FENV_ROUND/FENV_DEC_ROUND and add differential fixtures
description:
Once the shim exists and FenvAttr dispatch is wired in, remove
FENV_ACCESS/FENV_ROUND/FENV_DEC_ROUND from preprocess.rs's
UnsupportedSemantic classification (or otherwise allow translation to
proceed when active), update the pragma_inventory.c /
unsupported_directive rejection fixtures accordingly, and add new
fixtures under tests/fixtures/ that exercise FENV_ACCESS ON with an
fesetround() change straddling a Tier 1 op (add, cast, compare),
verified against C.

Note: tests/differential.rs's generated_differential harness is disabled
repo-wide (confirmed this session) -- verification here means the same
manual loop used for slate-0ar5.2/slate-kmao: `cargo run -- translate`,
compile both the C fixture and generated Rust directly, run both, diff
stdout/exit code by hand. Don't rely on the disabled harness for signal.

Depends on the FenvAttr-parsing/dispatch subtask (slate-0ar5.4), which
also carries the containment-strategy design note this issue's fixtures
need to verify.
acceptance_criteria:
pragma_inventory.c / unsupported_directive fixtures updated to reflect the
new supported set. New FENV_ACCESS fixtures manually verified (translate,
compile C + Rust, run both, diff stdout/exit code) to match C bit-for-bit.

Containment fixture included (see slate-0ar5.4's acceptance criteria):
FENV_ACCESS ON around exactly one op, ordinary arithmetic immediately
outside that scope in the same function, generated Rust inspected to
confirm only the scoped op became a shim call.

cargo fmt/clippy pass. Relevant nextest profile (lowering) passes with no
regressions.
notes: Found and fixed a containment bug before closing: dispatch was keyed on value.fenv.is_some(), but real Clang CIR attaches a #cir.fenv attribute to EVERY float op in a function once FENV_ACCESS ON appears anywhere in it -- not just to ops lexically inside the pragma block, contradicting handoffs/floating-point-env.md's stated assumption. Verified on tests/fixtures/stdlib_fenv_access.c: 'before = x + y' and 'after = x + y' (both outside the pragma block) got explicit fenv<dynamic_rounding_mode=tonearest, except_mode=masked, strict_except=false>, same as the constrained 'contended = x / y' inside the block getting fenv<unknown,unknown,strict_except=true>. Fixed by adding fenv_is_constrained() in src/frontend/lowerer/types.rs, keyed on strict_except=="true" || dynamic_rounding_mode=="unknown", and swapping all 27 call sites (src/frontend/lowerer.rs, arithmetic.rs, memory.rs) from bare .is_some(). Re-verified: only the pragma-scoped op now emits a shim call; before/after use plain native +. Differential (translate-project, cargo build, run C + Rust binaries) still bit-for-bit identical stdout/exit code. cargo fmt/clippy clean, lowering nextest profile: 7/7 pass, no regressions.
close_reason: Containment dispatch bug found and fixed; verified against acceptance criteria (differential match, containment fixture confirms only scoped op shimmed, fmt/clippy/lowering profile clean).

title: Parse cir::FenvAttr in src/cir/ and dispatch Tier 1 ops to the shim
description:
src/cir/ currently never reads a fenv/FenvAttr field on any op, so a
non-null FenvAttr (emitted under FENV_ACCESS ON / FENV_ROUND) is silently
dropped today. Add FenvAttr parsing to the CIR op-tree parser, and in
lowerer.rs, for each Tier 1 op (FAddOp/FSubOp/FMulOp/FDivOp/FRemOp,
CmpOp/VecCmpOp, CastOp), check for a non-null attr and dispatch to the
matching __slate_fenv_* C helper instead of the native Rust
operator/`as` cast.

NOT in scope here: FMAOp/FMulAddOp. Pulled out of Tier 1 -- that op's
FenvAttr handling is a separate, lower-priority compounding case (see
handoffs/floating-point-env.md); Op::Fmuladd's primary bug (target-
dependent fuse-or-not) was already fixed separately in slate-kmao via
lower_fmuladd's target dispatch, unrelated to this shim.

Depends on the C shim helpers subtask (needs the helpers to call into) and
the extern-call-barrier verification subtask (done, slate-0ar5.1).

CONTAINMENT STRATEGY (important, don't widen this): dispatch must read
each op's own FenvAttr field at its own match arm, the same way
Op::Fmuladd/type_mentions_long_double dispatch already works -- never
thread a self.constrained-style bool through FunctionLowerer for "we're
inside a FENV_ACCESS region right now." Clang's CIRGenFPOptionsRAII
(CIRGenFunction.cpp:1376) constructs FenvAttr from
e->getFPFeaturesInEffect() -- the FP-pragma state at that SPECIFIC
expression's lexical position -- so the attribute is already scoped per-op
by Clang, matching the C standard's own lexical (not reachability-based)
FENV_ACCESS contract. A same-op-kind instance two lines outside the pragma
block gets no attr and must keep lowering to the plain native Rust
operator. Any per-function/per-TU shortcut would taint more code than the
real C reference binary does, breaking differential parity, on top of
being exactly the readability regression this design is trying to avoid.
acceptance_criteria:
cir::FenvAttr is parsed and available on Tier 1 ops in the lowerer. Ops
with a non-null attr lower to the shim call; ops without one keep lowering
to native Rust as before (no behavior change for non-constrained code).

Containment regression test: a fixture/probe with FENV_ACCESS ON around
exactly one `+` (or other Tier 1 op), with ordinary arithmetic immediately
before and after it in the same function, outside the pragma's block.
Inspect the generated Rust and confirm only that one op became a shim
call -- the sibling ops before/after stay plain native operators. This is
the direct test that the taint doesn't leak past the pragma's lexical
scope.
close_reason:
Scope corrected from the original framing: no CIR parser changes were
needed in Slate itself for presence/absence detection (value.fenv.is_some()
already worked -- confirmed empirically via emit_module + a throwaway probe
that Fadd.fenv is Some(...) under FENV_ACCESS ON and None otherwise).
However, per user direction, went further and fixed the vendored clang-ir
crate properly rather than working around it: added fenv mnemonic handling
to parse_dialect_attr in clang-ir/src/parser/attrs.rs (parse_cir_fenv_attr,
mirroring parse_cir_bitfield_info's keyed <k=v,...> shape), so
value.fenv now decodes to the fully-typed Attribute::Fenv{dynamic_rounding_mode,
except_mode, strict_except} instead of the generic undecoded
Attribute::Dialect{raw: Some(...)} form -- useful to any other consumer of
the crate, not just Slate's presence check. Two new unit tests added
upstream (parses_fenv_attr_fields, parses_empty_fenv_attr), both pass.
Confirmed via git stash that a pre-existing, unrelated snapshot test
failure (alignment attribute drift, likely from a clang version bump) was
not introduced by this change.

Wired per-op FenvAttr dispatch for the core Tier 1 set: Op::Fadd/Fsub/
Fmul/Fdiv (lower_fenv_binary in arithmetic.rs), Op::Cmp for the six basic
predicates (lt/le/gt/ge/eq/ne; One/Uno ordered/unordered compounds and
non-float operand comparisons untouched, fall through as before), and
Op::Cast for the fenv-relevant kinds (float widen/narrow, float<->bool,
int<->float using i64/u64 carrier widths, try_lower_fenv_cast in
memory.rs). Each dispatches to the matching __slate_fenv_* shim only when
`op.fenv.is_some()` AND the type is Single/Double -- containment discipline
followed per the design doc: checked at each op's own match arm, no
function/TU-wide flag introduced.

Not done (explicitly out of scope, tracked elsewhere): VecCmpOp (SIMD
compares), FRemOp (no existing match arm reaches it -- C has no native %
on floats, unclear if reachable at all), f80/f128 fenv handling (existing
shim paths already always-opaque for unrelated ABI reasons). End-to-end
verification blocked on slate-0ar5.5 (pragma still rejected upstream of
lowering) -- deferred to that issue.

title: Write C shim helpers for FenvAttr-carrying ops (Tier 1)
description:
Following the __slate_f80_* pattern (docs/src/long-double.md), write C
helper functions for the Tier 1 op surface identified in
handoffs/floating-point-env.md: FAddOp/FSubOp/FMulOp/FDivOp/FRemOp (+ - * /
%), FMAOp/FMulAddOp (.mul_add()), CmpOp/VecCmpOp float comparisons, and
CastOp (bool_to_float, int_to_float, float_to_int, float_to_bool,
float-extend/trunc), each x {f32, f64}. ~14 functions plus comparison
predicates. f80/f128 should thread through the existing long-double/quad
shim paths rather than getting new helpers.

Each helper does the obvious real-C-arithmetic thing (e.g.
`return a + b;`) -- correctness comes from real hardware consulting the
live rounding-mode register, not from anything clever in the helper
itself. No rounding-mode parameter needed (FenvAttr's rounding field only
matters under FENV_ROUND, which pins a static mode; plain FENV_ACCESS ON
leaves it dynamic).

Depends on the extern-call-barrier verification subtask landing with a
positive result first.
acceptance_criteria: New __slate_fenv_* C helpers compiled alongside generated Rust, covering the Tier 1 matrix. Not yet wired into the lowerer (that's the next subtask) -- this is just the C-side helpers existing and compiling.
close_reason:
Added src/frontend/shims/fenv.c (new file, sibling to shims/long_double.c
as requested) with the Tier 1 op surface from handoffs/floating-point-env.md:
add/sub/mul/div/rem, six comparison predicates, and casts (int64/uint64 <->
float, float widen/narrow, float->bool), each x {f32, f64}. Named
__slate_fenv_<op>_<f32|f64> (or _to_/_from_ for casts), matching the
existing __slate_f80_* naming convention. rem uses fmod/fmodf (matching
LLVM's frem semantics; C has no native % on floats). int<->float casts use
i64/u64 as canonical carrier widths -- narrower int types widen/narrow on
the Rust call side before/after the call, same approach as the existing
typed-shim machinery already uses elsewhere in c_shim.rs.

Hooked into all three render entry points in src/frontend/c_shim.rs
(render_shim_c_source, render_shim_c_source_for_program,
render_shim_c_source_for_names), mirroring exactly how F80_SHIMS/has_f80
already works: a new FENV_SHIMS include_str!, a has_fenv-style name-prefix
check that includes the whole file when any __slate_fenv_* shim is
referenced, and a skip in the per-shim auto-render loop so
render_typed_shim/render_trampoline don't try to regenerate these
(they're hand-defined, like f80/cf80).

Verified: fenv.c compiles standalone (clang -Wall -Wextra -std=c11, clean).
cargo build --release clean. Smoke-tested render_shim_c_source_for_names
via a throwaway example binary (removed after) -- confirmed the FENV_SHIMS
block is included when a __slate_fenv_* name is present, and no bogus
auto-generated trampoline is emitted for it. cargo fmt clean (one
rustfmt-required wrap on the has_fenv any() closure, applied), no clippy
warnings. Full lowering nextest profile: 7/7 pass, no regressions
(expected -- nothing in the lowerer dispatches to these yet, that's
slate-0ar5.4).

Not done here (by design, per this issue's scope): no FenvAttr parsing,
no lowerer dispatch -- these functions aren't called from anywhere yet.
That's slate-0ar5.4, which is now unblocked.

title: Allowlist #pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT in preprocess.rs
description:
Unlike FENV_ACCESS/FENV_ROUND/FENV_DEC_ROUND, FP_CONTRACT doesn't need any
shim work. Clang's CIRGen (CIRGenExprScalar.cpp's tryEmitFMulAdd) already
resolves within-statement contraction into cir.fmuladd vs. plain
cir.fmul+cir.fadd before Slate ever parses the CIR -- the same "already
resolved by the time CIR arrives" shape as CX_LIMITED_RANGE. Slate already
lowers both resulting ops (Op::Fma/Op::Fmuladd -> .mul_add(),
lowerer.rs:4808-4823). It's rejected today purely because it isn't
allowlisted next to CX_LIMITED_RANGE in preprocess.rs's
is_clang_resolved_pragma.

Add an is_fp_contract_pragma alongside is_cx_limited_range_pragma
(preprocess.rs), matching "STDC FP_CONTRACT" ON/OFF/DEFAULT payloads, and
wire it into is_clang_resolved_pragma. Add a fixture exercising a*b+c
under FP_CONTRACT ON vs OFF and confirm the differential test produces the
same fused/unfused codegen behavior as C.

Independent of the rest of slate-0ar5 -- can be done in any order relative
to the other subtasks.
acceptance_criteria: FP_CONTRACT ON/OFF/DEFAULT pragma no longer rejected as unsupported-semantic. New fixture differentially verified. cargo fmt/clippy/lowering profile pass.
notes:
Core scope done: added is_fp_contract_pragma (preprocess.rs, mirroring
is_cx_limited_range_pragma) and wired it into is_clang_resolved_pragma.
Confirmed via `cargo run -- translate` on tests/fixtures/stdlib_fp_contract.c
that the pragma no longer triggers "unsupported directive" and both blocks
lower correctly per-CIR-op (ON block -> cir.fmuladd -> Op::Fmuladd, OFF
block -> separate cir.fmul+cir.fadd -> Op::Fmul/Op::Fadd), confirming
FP_CONTRACT's contraction decision really is fully resolved by Clang
before Slate sees CIR, as expected.

Manual differential verification (C vs generated Rust, since the
generated_differential test harness is disabled repo-wide) surfaced a
REAL, pre-existing, unrelated bug: slate-kmao (Op::Fmuladd always lowers
to .mul_add(), which is only correct on targets with unconditional
hardware FMA -- x86-64 baseline isn't one). That bug is live on main today
independent of this pragma (fires on ordinary a*b+c with zero pragmas,
since C99's default contraction state is already ON). Filed separately,
not blocking this issue's actual scope.

tests/fixtures/stdlib_fp_contract.c is added and correctly exercises both
FP_CONTRACT states, but will not differentially match C on x86-64 baseline
until slate-kmao is fixed (the ON block hits the .mul_add() bug). Left the
fixture in place as the regression test for both this pragma and
slate-kmao together -- once slate-kmao lands, this fixture should pass
cleanly with no further changes needed here.
close_reason: is_fp_contract_pragma added and wired into is_clang_resolved_pragma (preprocess.rs), mirroring is_cx_limited_range_pragma. Confirmed via translate output that FP_CONTRACT ON/OFF no longer rejects and both branches lower through the correct CIR ops (cir.fmuladd vs cir.fmul+cir.fadd), confirming the pragma's effect really is fully resolved by Clang before CIR the same as CX_LIMITED_RANGE. cargo fmt clean, no clippy warnings introduced. Fixture added (stdlib_fp_contract.c) but won't differentially pass until slate-kmao (found during this verification, filed separately) is fixed -- that's a pre-existing Op::Fmuladd bug unrelated to this pragma's scope.

title: Shim FENV_ACCESS/FENV_ROUND/FENV_DEC_ROUND-constrained float ops to C
description:
Slate currently hard-rejects #pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS/FENV_ROUND/FENV_DEC_ROUND
as unsupported semantic directives (preprocess.rs's DirectiveRecord::disposition
classifies them UnsupportedSemantic; directive_translate.rs/cross_tu.rs reject
any translation unit where one is active).

The reason: Clang's CIRGen attaches an optional cir::FenvAttr ("constrained
floating-point") to ops under these pragmas -- FAddOp/FSubOp/FMulOp/FDivOp/
FRemOp, FMAOp/FMulAddOp, CmpOp/VecCmpOp, CastOp, and ~30 libm-style builtins
(CIRGenExprScalar.cpp, CIRGenBuiltin.cpp, CIRGenBuilder.h in the local
llvm-project checkout). Slate's src/cir/ parser never reads a fenv/FenvAttr
field, and the lowerer has no notion of a constrained op distinct from an
ordinary one -- so a non-null FenvAttr would be silently dropped and lowered
to plain Rust arithmetic, which doesn't respect dynamic rounding-mode changes
(fesetround) or exception-flag semantics the way the source contract requires.
That's a silent-miscompile risk, hence the current hard rejection rather than
best-effort translation.

Proposed fix: shim the ops that carry FenvAttr to real C helper functions,
the same pattern already used for long double (docs/src/long-double.md,
the __slate_f80_* helpers). Real hardware FP instructions already consult
the live MXCSR/FPU control word rounding bits at execution time regardless
of source language, so a C helper like `return a + b;` gets correct dynamic
rounding and exception behavior for free. The actual value of the shim is
that an opaque extern "C" call blocks rustc/LLVM from reordering, CSEing, or
constant-folding the flagged op the way it's free to do with a native Rust
operator -- that's the actual hazard FENV_ACCESS exists to guard against, not
the numeric result on real hardware.

See handoffs/floating-point-env.md for the full scoping writeup (op surface,
which ops are already effectively shimmed via existing libm-calling lowering,
and the open correctness question that needs verifying before committing to
the design).
design:
Tier 1 (needs a new shim, done -- slate-0ar5.3): FAddOp/FSubOp/FMulOp/
FDivOp/FRemOp -> Rust + - * / %, CmpOp/VecCmpOp -> < > <= >= == !=,
CastOp (bool_to_float, int_to_float, float_to_int, float_to_bool,
float-extend/trunc) -> as casts. f80/f128 route through existing
long-double/quad shim paths already, so wiring FenvAttr through those is
cheap relative to building them fresh. FNegOp never carries FenvAttr
(CIRBaseBuilder.h: fneg raises no exceptions, is rounding-independent) --
skip it.

Tier 1b (needs a new shim, done -- slate-0ar5.3, dispatch tracked as
slate-0ar5.6): verified via rustc --emit=llvm-ir instead of assuming --
sin, cos, exp, exp2, log, log2, log10, pow, ceil, floor, round, rint,
trunc, sqrt, fabs, fmax, fmin, copysign all compile to foldable LLVM
intrinsics (llvm.sin/cos/exp/.../fabs/etc), same hazard class as native
operators. Op::Fma under FenvAttr is in this category too (.mul_add() is
llvm.fma). asin/atan/atan2/acos/acosh/asinh/atanh/cosh/sinh/tanh/cbrt/
exp_m1/ln_1p/hypot/tan already compile to real opaque libm calls, no shim
needed -- confirmed, not assumed.

Op::Fmuladd (implicit FP_CONTRACT-driven fusion) is NOT part of this shim
-- its bug (always fusing via .mul_add() regardless of whether the target
backend actually would) was a separate, static target-triple question,
fixed via lowerer target dispatch in slate-kmao, unrelated to FenvAttr.

Open question (resolved -- slate-0ar5.1): does an unannotated extern "C"
call in the generated Rust actually block rustc/LLVM from reordering or
folding neighboring float ops across it in both directions at -O2/-O3?
Confirmed yes via LLVM IR inspection -- see slate-0ar5.1's close notes and
handoffs/floating-point-env.md.

See handoffs/floating-point-env.md for full detail, including the
containment strategy (per-op FenvAttr dispatch only, never a function/TU-
wide flag -- Clang already scopes FenvAttr lexically per-expression via
CIRGenFPOptionsRAII, so Slate inherits that scoping for free) and why
softfp/arpfloat were considered and rejected in favor of the C shim.
acceptance_criteria:
- pragma_inventory.c / unsupported_directive fixtures updated: FENV_ACCESS ON
  (and FENV_ROUND/FENV_DEC_ROUND) translate instead of hard-rejecting, once
  the shim exists
- New C fixture(s) in tests/fixtures/ exercise FENV_ACCESS ON with a
  fesetround() change straddling a Tier-1 op, differentially verified
  (identical stdout/exit code between C and generated Rust) under the
  lowering profile
- Correctness of the "extern call blocks reordering" assumption verified via
  LLVM IR inspection or Alive2, not just asserted by analogy to long double
- cargo fmt / clippy / relevant nextest profile pass
close_reason: All children closed; FENV_ACCESS/FENV_ROUND/FENV_DEC_ROUND shim work complete and verified.

title: Retire Slate generic operation compatibility helpers
description: Remove generic mnemonic and attribute helper layers once typed model and operation consumers cover their uses.
acceptance_criteria: Generic Operation helpers are confined to normalization/flattening and no replacement for CirOpKind is introduced.

title: Upstream remaining CIR attribute and source-location decoding
description: Move builtin dense-array parsing, callsite/location alias structure, and reusable CIR literal decoding out of Slate and into typed clang-ir APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Slate no longer reparses supported clang-ir Attribute or SourceLocation payload strings, except lowering-policy grammars such as inline asm templates.
notes:
Three clusters, all done, split across clang-ir (sibling repo, path dep) and slate:

1. Literal decoding: clang-ir::decode_escaped_bytes made public, Slate's decode_cir_string now delegates to it (fixed a missing \"/\\n/\\t escape bug in Slate's copy). New cir.ptr/cir.block_addr_info parser support in clang-ir -> typed Attribute::ConstPtr/BlockAddrInfo (variants already existed in generated types, parser just wasn't constructing them); Slate migrated off the Attr::Dialect raw-string fallback for both. [committed by user separately]

2. Source-location resolver (biggest piece): new SourceLocation::Callsite{spelling,expansion} variant in clang-ir-types (template/src/ast/op.rs, hand-written/template-copied, not tblgen-generated); structural callsite(A at B) parsing in clang-ir's parser; Module::resolve_named_locs() eagerly resolves every #alias reference (including nested ones inside Fused/Callsite) in place at parse time, mirroring the existing resolve_named_attrs pattern. Slate's lowerer.rs deleted self.loc_aliases, self.source_locations, resolve_floating_literal_loc, resolve_source_point, source_location_text entirely - now just matches the crate's pre-resolved SourceLocation directly. Caught and fixed a real parser bug along the way: the raw-text alias-fallback capture included trailing whitespace before a terminator token (captured "#loc " instead of "#loc"), which would have silently broken every macro-expanded floating-literal lookup once callsite parsing landed - caught by a new clang-ir unit test (resolves_aliased_callsite_locations), not by Slate's own suite (tests/differential.rs is currently disabled). Added tests/fixtures/long_double_literal_macro.c in Slate exercising this exact path (macro-expanded long-double literal); inert until differential.rs is re-enabled.

3. Builtin dense-array accessor: Attribute::as_dense_array_ints() added to clang-ir-types-gen's fixed impl-block template (clang-ir-types-gen/src/attrs.rs, same place as as_int/as_bool - not a new tblgen-derived variant, just a parsing helper on the existing Dialect fallback), regenerated into clang-ir-types/src/attrs.rs. Slate's op_utils.rs builtin_dense_array_ints/int_array_attr now calls the typed accessor instead of hand-splitting raw dialect-attr text.

Verified throughout: cargo build/fmt/clippy clean in both repos (scoped to touched files; left ~2400 lines of pre-existing unrelated generated-file formatting debt untouched), clang-ir's own unit + snapshot test suite (8-10/10 unit tests pass; the one snapshot-fixture failure is a pre-existing toolchain-drift issue confirmed present on a clean clang-ir checkout too, unrelated to this work), Slate's lowering nextest profile 7/7 (rewrites profile and tests/differential.rs are both currently disabled project-wide per user, so only the lowering profile's suite tests give signal right now).
close_reason: All three clusters (literal decoding, source-location resolver, dense-array accessor) landed across clang-ir and slate; verified via build/fmt/clippy and lowering nextest profile in both repos.

title: Add a shared typed operation walker
description: Provide a small recursive walker over generated Op regions and migrate repeated parsing/lowering scans to it without introducing a visitor framework.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated hand-written region recursion is reduced and migrated analyses match generated Op variants directly.
notes: Added walk_region_ops/walk_block_ops in src/frontend/lowerer/op_utils.rs: a small recursive (region,block,op)->bool visitor over the typed clang_ir::model::Op tree, built on the crate's existing for_each_region primitive. Migrated the two duplicated hand-written recursions onto it: cross_block_live_values (analysis.rs) and region_has_direct_continue/ops_have_direct_continue, now inlined into region_has_direct_continue (control_flow.rs). transparent_region_ops in cir_ops.rs was left alone — it unwraps one transparent Scope level rather than doing a full tree walk, different shape. The untyped legacy Operation walkers (region_ops/collect_region_ops_recursive in analysis.rs, forwardable_temp_allocas in op_utils.rs, collect_function_bitfields in bitfields.rs, contains_goto/contains_label in cir/flatten.rs) are a separate migration — they predate/duplicate the typed conversion and are really slate-jedr.5's territory (retiring generic Operation compat helpers), not this issue's typed-walker scope.
close_reason: Shared typed-Op walker added and both duplicated region recursions migrated onto it; verified via build/fmt/clippy/lowering nextest profile.

title: Consume clang-ir model::Module after CIR normalization
description: Convert the post-flattening frontend boundary to clang_ir::model::Module and migrate top-level function/global/module analysis away from repeated generic Operation mnemonic scans. Add missing clang-ir model fields instead of introducing a new Slate operation taxonomy; retain raw operations only for attributes not yet modeled.
acceptance_criteria: emit/lowering boundary exposes model::Module; top-level collection uses typed functions and globals; relevant differential fixtures pass under the release lowering profile; cargo fmt and clippy pass.
close_reason: Converted the post-flattening boundary to clang_ir::model::Module; migrated top-level function/global indexing, feature analysis, lifecycle/used-symbol analysis, global collection, and defined-function body lowering to typed model fields and generated regions. Fixed clang-ir Function signature parameter typing with a regression test. Verified with clang-ir lib tests, Slate release clippy, and the full release lowering nextest profile (7/7).

title: Finish the typed clang-ir parsing boundary
description: Make clang-ir's model::Module and generated Op types the semantic parsing boundary for Slate. Eliminate Slate-side mnemonic classification and CIR/MLIR payload reparsing, centralize typed traversal, and then reorganize parsing/lowering files around the resulting pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Slate lowering consumes typed module/function/global/op structures after normalization; generic Operation is confined to normalization/flattening escape hatches; remaining CIR-specific textual decoding is upstreamed or explicitly justified; parsing/lowering organization reflects typed pipeline phases.

title: Phase 3: make Instruction self-sufficient for lowering (drop &Op dependency)
description:
Goal: make clang-ir's typed Instruction carry everything a lowering consumer
needs, so slate's lower_* helpers (and any other crate consumer) never have
to fall back to the generic &Operation for real work. Currently every
Instruction-passing conversion done in Phase 2.5 (slate-cevu.4) still keeps
op: &Op around as a second parameter because Instruction is missing two
categories of information:

1. Per-operand types. Instruction variants generally only carry the ty:
   Type of the *primary result* - not a type for each operand. slate leans
   on Operation::operand_types (the full function-type signature) heavily:
   ~139 call sites across src/frontend/lowerer/ (op_operand_types/
   op_result_type/op_result_types), used for things like distinguishing
   function-pointer operands, va_list operands, bitint operands, etc. This
   is the single largest reason op can't be dropped from a converted
   lower_* helper today.

2. Recursive body structure isn't consumed by the traversal engine. Control-
   flow Instruction variants (If/While/For/Switch/Ternary/Scope/
   CleanupScope) already carry a fully-typed Body/InstBlock tree
   (recursively Vec<Instruction>, not raw Op) - but slate's block/region
   walking (lower_region_ops, lower_block in src/frontend/lowerer.rs) still
   walks the generic Op/Region/Block tree, never the typed one. Rewiring
   that traversal engine to dispatch off Instruction/Body/InstBlock instead
   of Op/Region/Block is what would actually let lower_op(op: &Op) become
   lower_instruction(instr: Instruction) end to end. This is structural -
   it changes the engine underneath every op family at once, not one family
   at a time like the current Phase 2.5 work.

Also in scope, smaller items surfaced while investigating this:

- Correct a wrong claim in handoffs/cir-op-kind-migration.md (session 8):
  slate's Attr/CirType (src/cir/ir.rs) are literally `pub use
  clang_ir::ast::{Attribute as Attr, ..., Type as CirType}` - already the
  same types as Instruction's typed fields, not a separate representation
  needing reconciliation. Audit remaining direct op.attr(...) calls in
  already-converted lower_* helpers (e.g. lower_const's `value` lookup)
  that could use the already-typed Instruction field directly instead.
- Related prior art already landed in ~/Projects/clang-ir (uncommitted,
  local path dep): Module::resolve_named_attrs, called at the end of
  parse_module, eagerly resolves Attribute::Named (MLIR's #name alias
  hoisting for large/repeated attrs like #cir.bitfield_info<...>) against
  the module's attr_aliases table before any Instruction::try_lower runs.
  This was needed because try_lower(op: &Operation) has no access to the
  owning Module's alias table and so could never resolve aliases itself -
  same underlying theme as this ticket (Instruction/try_lower needing to
  see more context than a bare &Operation gives it).

Motivation: this benefits slate directly (finishes what Phase 2.5 started)
and is intentionally scoped as crate-level work so any other clang-ir
consumer gets the same benefit, not just slate's lowerer.

Out of scope for slate-cevu.4: this blocks the "drop op entirely" end state
but does NOT block continuing incremental CirOpKind->Instruction dispatch
migration in the meantime (family-by-family classification migration keeps
working fine with op kept alongside instr, as it does today).
notes: Completed the function-body migration to clang-ir generated operations. Op is now the primary generated enum; generic parser nodes are named Operation. Removed CirOpKind/OpKindExt, the raw lowering fallback, raw control-flow/value handlers, duplicate raw block traversal, TypedFoo aliases, and lower_*_typed naming. Multi-block dispatch now consumes generated Region/Block/Op for label discovery, alloca hoisting, liveness, divergence, block args, and lowering. Typed SwitchFlat was required by supported goto-flattening fixtures; fixed clang-ir-types generation to read case_operand_segments and regenerated 0.1.4-7. Validation: Slate cargo fmt, release clippy -D warnings, release lowering nextest 7/7; clang-ir library tests 7/7 and generator tests pass.
close_reason: Function lowering and CFG traversal now consume generated clang-ir Op data without generic Operation fallback; compatibility taxonomy and naming removed.

title: Implement remaining long-tail CIR ops in clang-ir's model layer (vectors, atomics, complex ptr/add/sub, asm, misc builtins)
description: After slate-cevu.2 closed the largest gaps (bitfields, fmuladd, varargs, math builtins, complex create/real/imag, frame/return_address, prefetch, overflow arithmetic - roughly 5900 of ~6300 unmodeled-op occurrences in clang-ir's 2571-file real-CIR snapshot corpus), a long tail remains, each individually low-occurrence but still needed for full coverage. Remaining <unmodeled: ...> counts as of this filing: cir.vec.splat(71), cir.vec.extract(45), cir.is_fp_class(40), cir.vec.create(30), cir.asm(29), cir.complex.real_ptr(24), cir.complex.imag_ptr(23), cir.atomic.fetch(16), cir.complex.add(14), cir.stacksave(12), cir.libc.memchr(11), cir.call_llvm_intrinsic(11), cir.vec.cmp(10), cir.cleanup.scope(9), cir.atomic.xchg(8), cir.case(7, standalone outside switch), cir.byte_swap(5), cir.vec.insert(4), cir.popcount(4), cir.parity(4), cir.fmaxnum(4), cir.complex.sub(4), cir.clrsb(4), cir.trunc(3), cir.trap(3), cir.sub.overflow(3), cir.modf(3), cir.eh.setjmp(3), cir.eh.longjmp(3), cir.ceil(3), cir.atomic.fence(3), cir.atomic.cmpxchg(3), cir.round(2), cir.rint(2), cir.objsize(2), cir.is_constant(2), cir.fma(2), cir.block_address(2), cir.atomic.test_and_set(2), cir.assume(2), cir.vec.shuffle(1), cir.nearbyint(1), cir.libc.memset(1), cir.libc.memmove(1), cir.libc.memcpy(1), cir.fminnum(1), cir.clear_cache(1), cir.bitreverse(1), cir.atomic.clear(1). Also noted: cir.extract_member shows 2 unmodeled occurrences despite already having a try_lower arm - likely a shape mismatch (possibly a multi-result or differently-typed variant) worth a quick look rather than a fresh implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running clang-ir's snapshot_fixtures test (CLANG_OPT/CIR_OPT env vars pointed at a CIR-enabled clang build) shows near-zero <unmodeled: ...> ops across the corpus for whichever of these mnemonics slate's own fixture/gcc-torture/libc-test corpora actually exercise; ops slate never emits (e.g. some GNU/vector extensions) can be deprioritized once cross-checked against slate's actual CirOpKind usage.
close_reason: Completed by clang-ir's TableGen-generated operation model, which covers the long-tail CIR operations tracked here.

title: Phase 2: incrementally migrate CirOpKind dispatch onto clang-ir's model::Instruction layer
description: Once Phase 1 is stable, migrate individual op families from slate's own CirOpKind dispatch (158 variants, 243 match sites across 20 lowerer submodules) onto clang-ir's typed model::Instruction where coverage is solid - one op family at a time, not a single cutover. clang-ir's op grouping differs from slate's (e.g. Binary{op: BinaryOp} collapses add/sub/mul/div/rem/and/or/xor rather than keeping them as distinct CirOpKind variants), so each family needs its own mapping/verification pass, not a mechanical rename.
acceptance_criteria: Each migrated op family has its own commit/PR with the relevant nextest profile passing; CirOpKind variants that migrate are removed only after their replacement is verified against real fixtures, not speculatively.
notes: Final completion supersedes the incremental migration state described in earlier notes: every runtime operation family now dispatches through clang-ir generated Op, CirOpKind and OpKindExt are deleted, and the full release lowering profile passes. Changes remain uncommitted under the conservative repository profile.
close_reason: All operation families migrated to clang-ir generated Op; CirOpKind removed entirely and lowering validation passes.

title: Migrate slate's CIR parsing to typed clang-ir crate
description: Replace slate's hand-rolled src/cir parser/generic-op-tree with the new ~/Projects/clang-ir crate to get a typed CIR representation (real Type/Attribute enums instead of raw-string reparsing in lowerer/types.rs and lowerer/constants.rs). Not a clean refactor - large coupling surface in src/frontend/lowerer/*.rs (243 CirOpKind matches, 151 variants). Sequenced as: fix clang-ir gaps first (loc + function-signature typing, missing op coverage), then swap slate's generic layer onto it (Phase 1), then incrementally migrate CirOpKind dispatch onto clang-ir's typed model::Instruction layer (Phase 2).
close_reason: All seven migration phases are complete: clang-ir owns parsing/types/generated operations, Slate function lowering consumes generated Op without generic Operation fallback, and compatibility dispatch/types are removed.

title: Local vector variable initializer drops all elements when a macro constant (e.g. INT_MAX) appears in the list
description: v4si va = {INT_MAX, 1, INT_MIN, 0}; as a LOCAL variable inside a function lowers to 'let mut va: [i32;4] = i32::MAX as [i32; 4];' -- an invalid cast of a scalar to an array type, dropping every element after the first. The same initializer at global scope lowers correctly to 'aligned::Aligned([2147483647, 1, -2147483648, 0])'. Repro: a local __attribute__((vector_size(N))) variable whose brace-init list contains at least one macro-expanded constant (INT_MAX/INT_MIN verified; likely any macro_arith_values-tracked constant) breaks; the same list with plain integer literals lowers correctly as a local. Discovered while validating slate-os0h.3.1.58 (saturating arithmetic) -- unrelated to that fix, worked around in the differential test by using plain literals instead of INT_MAX/INT_MIN in the vector initializer. Likely in the local-VarDecl vector-initializer path colliding with the macro-constant-folding path (macro_arith_values / next_macro_const_expr) that global-scope initialization doesn't go through.

title: Saturating add/sub (__builtin_elementwise_add_sat/sub_sat) silently lowered as wrapping arithmetic
description: Clang lowers __builtin_elementwise_add_sat/sub_sat (any int/_BitInt width, any signedness) to plain cir.add/cir.sub with a 'saturated' unit attribute rather than a distinct CIR op. Verified via direct clang -fclangir -emit-cir on unsigned __int128 and _BitInt(200)/unsigned _BitInt(200) fixtures: same cir.add/cir.sub shape, just with saturated set. grep over src/frontend/lowerer confirms nothing checks for a 'saturated' attribute anywhere, so lower_int_arith (or whatever handles plain cir.add/cir.sub) silently ignores it and emits ordinary wrapping addition/subtraction. This is not a build failure -- it is a silent wrong-runtime-answer bug: any C source using these builtins currently translates and runs, but produces the wrapped result instead of the saturated one. No __builtin_elementwise_mul_sat exists in Clang, so multiply is not part of this gap. Discovered while scoping slate-os0h.3.1.24 (checked-overflow builtins); kept separate since the failure mode (silent wrongness vs compile error) and required fixture work differ.
close_reason: Fixed. Root cause was two bugs: (1) missing lowering entirely -- Clang lowers __builtin_elementwise_add_sat/sub_sat (scalar or vector, any int/_BitInt width, any signedness) to plain cir.add/cir.sub with a 'saturated' attribute rather than a distinct op, and nothing in the lowerer checked for it, so it silently fell through to ordinary wrapping add/sub. (2) attr_bool(op, key) checked only key presence (op.attrs.contains_key), but CIR emits 'saturated = false' as an explicit key=value pair on the non-saturating path (not omitted), while the saturating path emits bare 'saturated' (parsed as Attr::Raw("true")) -- so my first attempt at wiring this up made EVERY plain add/sub spuriously saturating, caught by a differential test (u128 sub in a local var came out wrong). Fixed attr_bool globally to check the actual value (Raw("false") -> false, anything else present -> true) rather than just presence; verified this doesn't regress any of its other 12 call sites (is_volatile, isShiftleft, rotateLeft, noreturn, fetch_first, min) via the full lowering profile. Added saturating_add/saturating_sub to bitint::BUint (carry/borrow check) and bitint::BInt (sign-rule check + saturate to MIN/max_value()=!min_value(), reusing the overflowing_add/sub from slate-os0h.3.1.24) in vendor/bitint/src/lib.rs, verified via a standalone example harness. Added lower_saturating_arith in src/frontend/lowerer/arithmetic.rs (scalar: direct saturating_add/sub method call, reused for both native ints via std's inherent methods and bitint via the new crate methods since both share the same method names; vector: per-element method call building an ArrayLit, mirroring lower_int_arith's vector_binary_expr shape). Confirmed via clang that no other saturating-arithmetic builtin family exists (no __builtin_elementwise_mul_sat, no AMDGPU/HLSL builtins reachable from generic C, __builtin_sadd_overflow-family builtins reject vector args), and that these builtins are integer-only (reject float/double outright with a Clang diagnostic). Added tests/fixtures/saturating_arith.c covering scalar int/short/unsigned, u128, signed/unsigned _BitInt(200), and a v4si vector, both saturating and non-saturating cases. Verified end-to-end by hand (translate + compile + run generated Rust, byte-for-byte matching a clang-compiled reference binary across all 8 cases) since the generated_differential harness that would normally pick up new tests/fixtures/*.c is currently disabled; cargo fmt and cargo clippy --release are clean, and the full lowering profile passes (one chibicc failure was the known parallel-run batch-cargo cache flake, unrelated). Filed slate-os0h.3.1.59 separately for an unrelated pre-existing bug discovered during validation: local vector variable initializers drop all elements but the first when a macro constant (INT_MAX/INT_MIN) appears in the brace-init list.

title: gcc-torture: size flexible array members from their static initializer
description:
Slate lowers a trailing flexible array member (C99 struct-hack, e.g. char a3p[]; or int j[];) straight from its declared C length (0 or 1), producing a Rust field like [i8; 0] / [i32; 0]. When the global is initialized with more elements than that declared length (e.g. a3 = {'o', "wx"} or x = {1, {2, 0, 2, 3}}), the extra initializer elements are dropped and the field keeps zero (or one) elements of storage. Reads/writes through the member then land past the struct with no reserved bytes -- out-of-bounds UB in the generated Rust, not just a compile error.

Discovered while working slate-os0h.3.1.9 ("avoid Rust references when addressing mutable statics"): fixing that bug's mutable-static-reference issue unblocked compilation for 20010924-1 and pr33382, but both then fail at runtime (stdout/exit code mismatch) due to this separate root cause.

Cases: 20010924-1, pr33382 (both still in tests/fixtures.gcc-torture.unsupported/)

Reproduce one case with SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=<case> cargo nextest r --release --test gcc_torture_suite -E 'test(gcc_torture_unsupported_triage_report)' --run-ignored ignored-only --nocapture
acceptance_criteria: Both cases translate, their generated Rust compiles and matches the C reference's stdout and exit code, the files are promoted into tests/fixtures.gcc-torture/, and cargo nextest r --release --test gcc_torture_suite passes. The flexible array member's Rust field length must be widened to match its static initializer's element count (not left at the declared 0/1).
close_reason: Fixed: added widen_flexible_array_members pre-pass in src/frontend/lowerer.rs, run before required_record_defs. It scans cir.global ops for structs whose trailing field is a flexible-array-member candidate (declared C length None/0/1), resolves the CIR sym_type through cir.aliases to find the matching c_ast::Record (handles both named tags and Slate's anon_N-renamed anonymous structs), and widens that field's declared length to the initializer's actual element count when larger. Both cases (20010924-1, pr33382) now translate, compile, and match C stdout/exit code; promoted into tests/fixtures.gcc-torture/. cargo fmt/clippy clean; --profile lowering 7/7 passed (supported corpus grew by 2, unsupported_tests_still_fail confirms no spurious regressions).

title: alloca() calls need shared, non-moving per-function stack arena, not independent heap Vecs
description:
chibicc's alloca fixture (tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/alloca/alloca.c) asserts that consecutive alloca() results are contiguous and 16-byte spaced, matching real C stack layout (p1-p2==16, p2-p3==16, p3-p4==16).

ClangIR lowers __builtin_alloca()/alloca() to a dynamic-size cir.alloca op named literally "bi_alloca" (align 16, size = runtime SSA value) -- distinct from the user's own variable name, so the frontend/CIR does carry a signal to distinguish a real alloca() call from an ordinary VLA local (e.g. int arr[n]), which hits the exact same code path today.

src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs:165-197 (lower_alloca) currently handles ALL dynamic-size cir.alloca ops (VLAs and alloca() calls alike) by emitting an independent heap allocation:
    let mut bi_alloca: Vec<u8> = vec![0; n];
Each call gets its own separate Vec from the global allocator, so relative pointer arithmetic between separate alloca() results is allocator-dependent noise, not the required LIFO/contiguous stack semantics. This is why the fixture's differential run currently produces p2-p3 == -32 in Rust vs 16 in C -- not an off-by-sign bug, just allocator layout happening to differ.
design: Likely needs a per-function (or per-scope) bump-allocated arena buffer that alloca() calls draw from with 16-byte alignment padding between allocations, LIFO-ordered to match the real stack, and that must never reallocate/move once a pointer has been handed out to C code (a growing Vec would invalidate previously-returned pointers on reallocation) -- e.g. a fixed-capacity or leaked/boxed backing buffer per function activation. Distinguish real alloca() calls from VLA locals using the cir.alloca op's name attribute (literally "bi_alloca" for alloca()/__builtin_alloca, vs the user's variable name for a VLA declaration).
acceptance_criteria: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/alloca passes end-to-end under the lowering nextest profile and is promoted (git mv) to tests/fixtures.chibicc/supported/alloca.

title: gcc-torture: sret return-value copy aliases caller's destination slot (pr43784)
description:
pr43784 now translates and compiles cleanly after the global_view/constant-address-expression fix in slate-os0h.3.1.29 (q correctly computes v+4 via addr_of_mut! chain), but fails at runtime with a Rust UB check: 'ptr::copy_nonoverlapping requires that both pointer arguments are aligned and non-null and the specified memory ranges do not overlap' inside rp(), called from qp() -> *q = rp().

Root cause: rp() returns a 256-byte struct s by value via a hidden sret out-param. Slate's codegen lowers 'return *p;' as unsafe { std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(p, arg0, 1) } where arg0 is the caller-supplied destination slot. In qp(), the caller passes q directly as arg0 (q = v+4, p = v+0), so src and dst are two overlapping views into the same union storage v (both within its 256+ byte footprint). C semantics require the return value to be materialized into a temporary first, then assigned into *q -- collapsing that into a direct copy_nonoverlapping(p, q, 1) is only safe when the sret slot provably cannot alias the return expression's source, which isn't checked here.

Reproduce: SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=pr43784 cargo nextest r --release --test gcc_torture_suite -E 'test(gcc_torture_unsupported_triage_report)' --run-ignored ignored-only --nocapture -- then run the built debug batch binary directly (RUST_BACKTRACE=1) to see the panic; batch binaries land under target/*-batch-cargo/debug/<fixture>.

Fix direction: either use copy (memmove-safe) instead of copy_nonoverlapping for sret-return assignments, or detect potential aliasing between the sret destination and the return expression's source and route through a stack temporary in that case.
acceptance_criteria: pr43784 translates, compiles, and its generated Rust matches the C reference's stdout and exit code; the file is promoted into tests/fixtures.gcc-torture/ and cargo nextest r --release --test gcc_torture_suite passes.
close_reason: Fixed as a side effect of slate-os0h.3.1.37's fix: pr43784's sret-return-copy aliasing bug shared the exact same opaque-aggregate-copy fallback in lower_copy (storage.rs) that 20071219-1 hit. Switching that fallback from copy_nonoverlapping to overlap-safe ptr::copy resolved both. pr43784 now passes end-to-end and is promoted into tests/fixtures.gcc-torture/. Full lowering profile passes.

title: native lowering: struct stat's st_atime/st_mtime/st_ctime macros need field-access flattening for libc::stat
description: stat_struct and stat_mtime_member still fail after slate-ypjt.2.25's fixes (rust_record_name now correctly emits 'libc::stat' instead of colliding with the extern fn stat(), and mbstate_t/pthread_attr_t-style opaque zero-init now routes through std::mem::zeroed). struct stat itself needs one more piece: libc-shim's sys/stat.h defines 'struct stat' with NESTED 'struct timespec st_atim/st_mtim/st_ctim' fields plus '#define st_atime st_atim.tv_sec' (and mtime/ctime) macros for POSIX compat (libc-shim/include/sys/stat.h:29-31). title: native lowering: CType::parse doesn't resolve typedef'd anonymous union/struct types (e.g. mbstate_t)
description: uchar_conversions still fails after slate-ypjt.2.25's CLibType/rust_record_name fixes landed. Root cause is one level earlier than the CLib-record-mapping machinery: libc-shim's 'typedef __mbstate_t mbstate_t;' where __mbstate_t is itself 'typedef union { ... } __mbstate_t;' (see libc-shim/bits/types.h:229-251) never produces a CType::Record at all -- 'cargo run --release -- translate --frontend native tests/fixtures/uchar_conversions.c' shows mbrtoc16/c16rtomb/mbrtoc32/c32rtomb's mbstate_t* params lowering to bare '*mut i32' and their size_t return type lowering to 'i32' instead of the expected 'u64'/usize, meaning CType::parse (native_lowerer/types.rs) is falling through to some default int case for this qual_type spelling rather than recognizing the anonymous-union canonical form. title: native lowering: printf/variadic calls pass LongDouble raw through Rust's C-variadic ABI, needs f80 printf shim routing
description:
native lowering passes LongDouble (the f80 software-float shim struct, #[repr(C, align(16))] wrapping [u8;10]) straight through Rust's C-variadic `...` mechanism whenever a variadic call (printf/fprintf/snprintf/etc.) has a long-double argument -- e.g. tests/fixtures/long_double_complex.c's print_lc lowers `printf("%s=%Lax%Lai\n", name, creall(z), cimagl(z));` to a plain `printf(fmt, name, creall(z), cimagl(z))` call against `unsafe extern "C" { fn printf(_0: *mut i8, ...) -> i32; }`, passing LongDouble args directly through `...`.

This is wrong: Rust has no native f80 type, so a LongDouble struct pushed through a variadic call doesn't land in the x87-extended-precision argument slot glibc's `%La`/`%Lf`/`%Le`/etc. format expects -- confirmed by running long_double_complex.c under native lowering (after fixing slate-ypjt.2.38's __attribute__ parsing bug, which was blocking this fixture from compiling at all): every print_lc call that includes a long-double component prints `-nan` garbage instead of the correct value, even though the underlying arithmetic is now correct.

The mature CIR lowerer already solved this: src/frontend/lowerer.rs / calls.rs generates a family of typed, non-variadic shim wrapper functions per concrete printf-call shape actually used -- e.g. `__slate_printf__ri32_pi8_f80` (one f80 arg), `__slate_printf__ri32_pi8_f80_f80` (two), `__slate_printf__ri32_pi8_pi8_f80_f80` (a %s plus two f80 args) -- confirmed via `cargo run --release -- translate tests/fixtures/long_double_complex.c` (default CIR frontend), which declares exactly these three shim signatures matching print_lc's three call shapes. Search the mature lowerer for how it decides when a printf/scanf-family call needs shim routing (probably keys off the format string's %L conversions plus each variadic arg's CType, generating one specialized extern per distinct (format shape, arg types) combination actually called) and how the shim itself is implemented (real C code compiled in, or inline asm marshaling the x87 stack) -- check for a shim source directory or SLATE_LIBC_SHIM-adjacent build step, and whether libc-shim/ has a printf implementation already handling this.

This is NOT specific to _Complex -- confirmed independently: tests/fixtures/long_double.c (plain `long double`, no complex) doesn't even lower under the native frontend yet (fails earlier on an unrelated unresolved-decl issue from a different libm builtin), so this printf/f80-variadic-ABI gap has never actually been exercised by native lowering before. Whichever fixture is the first to get native lowering far enough to reach a `printf("%L...", long_double_value)` call site will need this.

Fix shape: extend native_lowerer's call-lowering (src/frontend/native_lowerer/exprs.rs's call_expr, or a new prepass alongside collect_math_builtin_externs in builtins.rs/items.rs) to detect variadic calls whose format string contains %L conversions or whose variadic args include LongDouble/Complex<LongDouble>, and route them through the same __slate_printf__* naming/shim mechanism the mature lowerer already established (port the CIR lowerer's shim-selection and extern-generation logic rather than reinventing it -- check whether it can be shared directly since it operates on already-typed args, not CIR-specific state).

Repro: SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=long_double_complex cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture -- once this bead is done, re-check whether long_double_complex fully passes (slate-ypjt.2.18's __builtin_complex support itself is already done and verified via complex, complex_equality, complex_lvalue, stdlib_complex_cx_limited_range; slate-ypjt.2.38 already fixes the __attribute__ parsing that was blocking this fixture from compiling at all -- this bead is the last known blocker for long_double_complex specifically, though other fixtures reaching a long-double printf call for the first time may hit it too).

title: native lowering: CType::parse mis-parses function types with trailing __attribute__((...))
description:
native lowering mis-parses any function type whose Clang qualType spelling carries a trailing GCC/Clang attribute with its own parens, e.g. `void (void) __attribute__((noreturn))` -- confirmed via -ast-dump=json that abort's FunctionDecl type is genuinely `void (void) __attribute__((noreturn))` in both tests/fixtures/bitint_arith.c and tests/fixtures/long_double_complex.c (both declare their own `void abort(void);` on top of libc-shim's `_Noreturn void abort(void);`, and Clang folds the noreturn spelling onto the type string either way).

Root cause: CType::parse's trailing_paren_params(s) (src/frontend/native_lowerer/types.rs) matches parens from the END of the string to find the function's parameter list. For "void (void) __attribute__((noreturn))", the string does end in ')', so trailing_paren_params walks backward and finds the matching '(' for the LAST ')' -- which is the outer paren of "__attribute__((noreturn))", not the function's own "(void)" parameter list. This makes CType::parse treat "void (void) __attribute__" as the return-type spelling (itself unparseable, falls through to CType::Unknown) and "(noreturn)" as the parameter list (a single bogus "noreturn"-named param). CType::Unknown(_) unconditionally lowers to Type::Prim(Prim::I32) (types.rs:372), which is why the generated signature comes out as `fn abort(arg0: Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(i32) -> i32>) -> i32` instead of `fn abort() -> !` / `fn abort()` -- every Unknown slot silently becomes i32.

This will hit any libc/user function whose declaration is annotated with __attribute__((...)) (noreturn, pure, const, malloc, format, nonnull, etc.) wherever Clang's canonical qualType spelling keeps the attribute suffix -- not just abort, and not specific to complex/long-double (confirmed by reproducing the identical wrong signature on bitint_arith.c, which has no complex/long-double content at all).

Fix: trailing_paren_params (or its caller in CType::parse) needs to strip trailing `__attribute__((...))` (and similarly-shaped GNU attribute suffixes) from the type spelling before doing paren-matching, rather than doing raw right-to-left paren balancing over the whole string. Simplest fix is probably a strip_trailing_attributes(s) pass (recognize and remove one or more trailing `__attribute__((...))` groups, respecting nested parens within the attribute's own argument list) run immediately after strip_qualifiers, mirroring how strip_qualifiers already strips const/volatile/etc.

Repro: cargo run --release --bin slate -- translate --frontend native tests/fixtures/bitint_arith.c 2>&1 | grep 'fn abort' -- compare against the correct `_Noreturn void abort(void);` prototype. Also blocks slate-ypjt.2.18's long_double_complex fixture from fully passing (the __builtin_complex/_Complex support itself is done and verified against complex, complex_equality, complex_lvalue, stdlib_complex_cx_limited_range -- this is the one remaining, unrelated blocker for long_double_complex specifically, which happens to declare its own `void abort(void);`).
close_reason: Fixed: added strip_trailing_attributes() to native_lowerer/types.rs, stripping trailing __attribute__((...)) groups (balancing nested parens) from a type spelling before CType::parse's trailing_paren_params does its right-to-left paren match, so __attribute__((noreturn))-suffixed function types (e.g. abort's 'void (void) __attribute__((noreturn))') no longer get misparsed as a function whose return type AND parameter list are garbage Unknown->i32 fallbacks. Verified: 'cargo run -- translate --frontend native tests/fixtures/bitint_arith.c' now emits the correct 'fn abort();' instead of 'fn abort(arg0: Option<unsafe extern C fn(i32)->i32>) -> i32;'.

title: native lowering: va_list / __builtin_c23_va_start+va_end unresolved (port __SlateVaArgs scheme)
description:
c89, varargs, va_list_vfprintf fail with 'unresolved decl reference' because va_start()/va_end()/va_arg() (via <stdarg.h> macros) resolve to implicit __builtin_c23_va_start/__builtin_va_end/__builtin_va_arg FunctionDecls/exprs, excluded by items.rs's is_implicit guard -- same root cause as slate-ypjt.2.14, but this is statement-shaped (mutates a va_list value across a sequence of calls), not a single-expression rewrite, so it does not fit builtins.rs's try_lower_builtin_call(node,name,env)->RExpr shape.

Studied the mature CIR lowerer's design (src/frontend/lowerer.rs:1640-1686, src/frontend/lowerer/calls.rs:827-871, src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs:198-211, src/frontend/lowerer/types.rs:204-221) -- it does NOT use Rust's native extern "C" variadic ABI for user-defined variadic C functions (Rust has no way to declare a variadic fn outside extern "C", and no portable way to walk a real C va_list). Instead:

- A user-defined variadic function whose va_list never escapes to a C-ABI boundary (!c_abi_functions.contains(name) && !function_forwards_va_list(op)) gets its varargs replaced with a single synthetic parameter carrying a __SlateVaArgs value (Rc<Vec<__SlateVaArg>>, index cursor) -- see the __SlateVaArg/__SlateVaArgs SupportModule literally emitted as a Rust source string at lowerer.rs:1643-1682: __SlateVaArg boxes each variadic arg as Box<dyn Any> + its size, __SlateVaArgs::next_arg::<T>() downcasts (falling back to unaligned raw-byte reinterpretation if the concrete type didn't downcast, e.g. after an integer-promotion mismatch).
- Call sites to such a function pack the trailing variadic arguments into __SlateVaArgs::new(vec![__SlateVaArg::new(arg)...]) (calls.rs:100-112) instead of passing them as trailing args.
- va_list ap; locals become a Type::Custom("__SlateVaArgs")-typed local (storage.rs:198-211, gated on the CIR type containing __va_list_tag/__builtin_va_list).
- va_start(ap, last_named_param) lowers to ap = <the function's va-args parameter>.clone() (calls.rs:827-846).
- va_arg(ap, T) lowers to unsafe { ap.next_arg::<T>() } (calls.rs:848-871).
- va_end(ap) appears to be a no-op (no lower_va_end found -- Rc-based storage needs no explicit teardown).
- Functions that DO need real C-ABI variadics (declared extern "C", or whose va_list is forwarded to another variadic call, e.g. vfprintf-style passthrough -- see function_forwards_va_list, analysis.rs:245) keep genuine ... Rust variadic signatures instead.

Native lowering (src/frontend/native_lowerer/) needs the equivalent: extend items.rs's function-signature emission to detect a variadic FunctionDecl and rewrite its trailing ... into a single boxed-args parameter (unless it's a C-ABI/forwarding case), extend call-site lowering in exprs.rs to pack trailing arguments into __SlateVaArgs::new(...), add a Type::Custom("__SlateVaArgs") case for va_list locals in items.rs's collect_locals/type lowering, and add statement/expr handlers for the three implicit builtins (__builtin_c23_va_start, __builtin_va_arg -- check exact Clang node shape, likely a dedicated VAArgExpr rather than a CallExpr, so it needs a Clang::* match arm in exprs.rs's lower_expr rather than builtins.rs's call dispatch -- and __builtin_va_end) mirroring lower_va_start/lower_va_arg above. The SupportModule literal itself (lowerer.rs:1643-1682) can likely be reused/shared rather than reimplemented -- check whether it's frontend-agnostic.

Verify: SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=varargs cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture (also re-check c89, va_list_vfprintf once varargs passes).

title: native lowering: float-classification __builtin_is*/signbit/huge_vall (long_double.c)

title: native lowering: compile-time arithmetic-overflow lint on literal expressions
description: 2 fixtures fail to compile with rustc's 'this arithmetic operation will overflow' diagnostic: mul, sub. Confirmed via 2026-08-16 native-lowering triage. C's wraparound/overflow semantics for a compile-time-constant arithmetic expression (e.g. INT_MAX + 1-style literal math) are being emitted as plain '+'/'-'/'*' on typed literals, which rustc's const-eval overflow check rejects at compile time even in release profiles when the operands are literal constants. Needs the same fix pattern used elsewhere in this codebase for runtime overflow (see slate-ypjt.2.14's overflowing_add/overflowing_sub/overflowing_mul builtin work) applied to plain arithmetic operators on other-wise-constant operands -- or emit .wrapping_add()/.wrapping_sub()/.wrapping_mul() instead of the bare operator when both operands are literal/constant-foldable, matching C's defined-but-implementation-specific wraparound. Verify: SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=mul cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture.

title: native lowering: libc-shim struct types unresolved (tm/stat/mbstate_t/obstack)
description: A cluster of compile failures where a libc-shim struct type isn't resolved in generated Rust, either colliding with a same-named function or missing entirely: pointer_compare_address (E0425 'cannot find type tm'), stat_mtime_member + stat_struct (E0573 'expected type, found function stat' -- name collision between the libc fn stat() and the struct stat type), uchar_conversions (E0422 'cannot find struct mbstate_t'), gnu_libc_allocation (E0425 'cannot find type obstack', additionally has an unrelated Option<fn> cast bug already covered by the sibling function-pointer bead). Confirmed via a native-lowering triage run's per-fixture rustc diagnostics (2026-08-16). Likely native_lowerer/types.rs's CType/record-registry handling doesn't register or properly qualify these libc-shim-provided struct types the way the mature lowerer does (check src/frontend/lowerer's equivalent record-tag resolution and whether it disambiguates struct-vs-function names, e.g. via a  qualified path). Start with one fixture (SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=stat_struct) to confirm the exact mechanism before generalizing a fix across all four.
close_reason: Fixed a real bug found while investigating stat_struct: native_lowerer's rust_record_name() returned CLibType::c_name() (the bare C tag, e.g. 'timespec') instead of ::path() (the qualified Rust path, e.g. 'libc::timespec') for every CLIB_RECORD_TYPES-mapped record -- this silently broke every already-mapped type (FILE/mbstate_t/pthread_attr_t/timespec), emitting unresolvable bare identifiers. Also taught native_lowerer/globals.rs's zero_value/lower_init to consult CLibInitializer (ScalarZero/Zeroed/Fields) for CLib-mapped records instead of always doing field-by-field construction from our own shim's RecordRegistry -- opaque libc types often rename or privatize fields relative to the C layout (e.g. libc::stat flattens/privates several), so field-by-field literals against them don't compile; this ports the pattern the mature CIR-based lowerer already used (lowerer.rs's default_value_expr). Added CLIB_RECORD_TYPES entries for 'tm' and 'stat' (both Zeroed). Net result: stat_struct now passes outright. uchar_conversions, stat_mtime_member, pointer_compare_address, and gnu_libc_allocation still fail, but each on a distinct, deeper, already-scoped-out root cause -- filed as slate-ypjt.2.44 (CType::parse doesn't resolve mbstate_t's anonymous-union typedef chain to a Record at all), slate-ypjt.2.45 (stat's st_atime/st_mtime/st_ctime POSIX macros need member-access flattening against libc::stat's real field names), and slate-ypjt.2.46 (obstack has no libc-crate equivalent and needs used-tag-reachability-gated emission, not the blanket is_shim_loc relaxation I tried and reverted after it caused a 225->3/332 regression by unconditionally emitting every transitively-included shim-internal struct, including incomplete ones). Verified via full native-lowering suite before/after: 225 -> 226/332, no regressions.

title: native lowering: __builtin_memchr/__builtin_bcopy/__builtin_bzero need extern passthrough decls
description: Clang silently rewrites plain calls to memchr()/bcopy() (via <string.h>) to reference the implicit __builtin_memchr/__builtin_bcopy FunctionDecl instead of the header-declared one, so native_lowerer/items.rs's is_implicit exclusion drops them the same way it dropped every other __builtin_* until slate-ypjt.2.14. Affects mem_bcopy_overlap, mem_memchr, memchr_nullable_pointer (confirmed via parse-only --dump-ast: DeclRefExpr referencedDecl -> FunctionDecl name="__builtin_memchr"/"__builtin_bcopy", is_implicit). Fix: extend the same pattern slate-ypjt.2.14 built in src/frontend/native_lowerer/builtins.rs (try_lower_builtin_call dispatch + collect_math_builtin_externs-style Clang-AST prepass that only emits extern decls for builtins actually referenced) to a second small table of libc passthroughs with real (non-f64) signatures: memchr(*const c_void, i32, usize) -> *mut c_void, bcopy(*const c_void, *mut c_void, usize) -> (). Unlike the math table, these builtins' call-site args are already correctly C-typed by Clang (no need to force-cast to f64), so args can likely pass through via plain lower_expr(arg) rather than the math table's Cast-to-f64 step. Verify: SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=mem_memchr cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture.
notes: Also covers mem_bzero.c (__builtin_bzero) -- same is_implicit passthrough shape, found in the 2026-08-16 follow-up triage.
close_reason: Added LIBC_PASSTHROUGH_BUILTINS table (memchr/bcopy/bzero) with extern decl prepass, mirroring MATH_BUILTINS pattern. All 4 fixtures (mem_memchr, mem_bcopy_overlap, mem_bzero, memchr_nullable_pointer) now pass native-lowering profile.

title: native lowering: __builtin_complex unsupported (complex number family)
description: complex, complex_equality, complex_lvalue, stdlib_complex_cx_limited_range, long_double_complex all fail on 'unresolved decl reference' from __builtin_complex(re, im), which constructs a C _Complex value from its real/imaginary parts -- excluded by items.rs's is_implicit guard like every other __builtin_* was before slate-ypjt.2.14. This is a distinct, larger feature area from the simple single-expression builtins that ticket handled: C _Complex support needs a representation choice (the project already depends on the num-complex crate per tests/support/mod.rs's generated_crate_manifest, so check whether the mature CIR lowerer already lowers _Complex types/ops to num_complex::Complex<T> -- if so, port that representation and wire __builtin_complex to a Complex::new(re, im) call; if the mature lowerer doesn't support complex at all yet, this may need to start from scratch for both frontends). Check the mature lowerer first: does 'cargo run --release -- translate tests/fixtures/complex.c' (default CIR frontend) already succeed? If yes, study its Complex-type lowering approach before implementing the native-frontend equivalent. Verify: SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=complex cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture.
close_reason: Added CType::Complex(Box<CType>) parsing (_Complex prefix, positioned after pointer/array/func structural checks to avoid corrupting function-type parsing), Type::Complex lowering, zero-value struct-lit default, __builtin_complex(re,im) struct-lit builtin, __real__/__imag__ GNU unary ops (opcodes __real/__imag -> .re/.im field access), and FloatingRealToComplex/FloatingComplexToReal/FloatingComplexCast cast-kind handling (routing scalar components through the existing long_double_conversion_shim for f80 precision changes). Verified: complex, complex_equality, complex_lvalue, stdlib_complex_cx_limited_range all pass. long_double_complex is blocked by an unrelated pre-existing bug (filed as slate-ypjt.2.38: CType::parse's trailing_paren_params mis-parses __attribute__((noreturn))-suffixed function types, corrupting abort()'s signature) -- confirmed unrelated to complex/long-double by reproducing the identical wrong signature on bitint_arith.c which has no complex content.

title: native lowering: va_list / __builtin_c23_va_start+va_end unresolved
description: c89, varargs, va_list_vfprintf all fail with 'unresolved decl reference' because their calls to va_start()/va_end() resolve (via <stdarg.h> macros) to the implicit __builtin_c23_va_start/__builtin_va_end FunctionDecls, excluded by items.rs's is_implicit guard -- same general is_implicit root cause as slate-ypjt.2.14, but va_arg/va_list machinery is statement-shaped (mutates a va_list value across a sequence of calls), not a single-expression rewrite like the builtins.rs table handles, so it doesn't fit that module's try_lower_builtin_call(node,name,env)->RExpr shape directly. Needs its own design: check how the mature CIR-based lowerer (src/frontend/lowerer/, search for 'va_list'/'VaArg'/'va_start') represents and lowers these, since CIR likely has dedicated cir.va.* ops distinct from a bare CallExpr -- the native (Clang-AST) frontend will need equivalent StmtExpr-level handling in native_lowerer/stmts.rs or exprs.rs for the VAArgExpr/va_start/va_end call forms. Verify: SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=varargs cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture.
notes:
c89, varargs, va_list_vfprintf fail with 'unresolved decl reference' because va_start()/va_end()/va_arg() (via <stdarg.h> macros) resolve to implicit __builtin_c23_va_start/__builtin_va_end/__builtin_va_arg FunctionDecls/exprs, excluded by items.rs's is_implicit guard -- same root cause as slate-ypjt.2.14, but this is statement-shaped (mutates a va_list value across a sequence of calls), not a single-expression rewrite, so it does not fit builtins.rs's try_lower_builtin_call(node,name,env)->RExpr shape.

Studied the mature CIR lowerer's design (src/frontend/lowerer.rs:1640-1686, src/frontend/lowerer/calls.rs:827-871, src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs:198-211, src/frontend/lowerer/types.rs:204-221) -- it does NOT use Rust's native extern "C" variadic ABI for user-defined variadic C functions (Rust has no way to declare a variadic fn outside extern "C", and no portable way to walk a real C va_list). Instead:

- A user-defined variadic function whose va_list never escapes to a C-ABI boundary (!c_abi_functions.contains(name) && !function_forwards_va_list(op)) gets its varargs replaced with a single synthetic parameter carrying a __SlateVaArgs value (Rc<Vec<__SlateVaArg>>, index cursor) -- see the __SlateVaArg/__SlateVaArgs SupportModule literally emitted as a Rust source string at lowerer.rs:1643-1682: __SlateVaArg boxes each variadic arg as Box<dyn Any> + its size, __SlateVaArgs::next_arg::<T>() downcasts (falling back to unaligned raw-byte reinterpretation if the concrete type didn't downcast, e.g. after an integer-promotion mismatch).
- Call sites to such a function pack the trailing variadic arguments into __SlateVaArgs::new(vec![__SlateVaArg::new(arg)...]) (calls.rs:100-112) instead of passing them as trailing args.
- va_list ap; locals become a Type::Custom("__SlateVaArgs")-typed local (storage.rs:198-211, gated on the CIR type containing __va_list_tag/__builtin_va_list).
- va_start(ap, last_named_param) lowers to ap = <the function's va-args parameter>.clone() (calls.rs:827-846).
- va_arg(ap, T) lowers to unsafe { ap.next_arg::<T>() } (calls.rs:848-871).
- va_end(ap) appears to be a no-op (no lower_va_end found -- Rc-based storage needs no explicit teardown).
- Functions that DO need real C-ABI variadics (declared extern "C", or whose va_list is forwarded to another variadic call, e.g. vfprintf-style passthrough -- see function_forwards_va_list, analysis.rs:245) keep genuine ... Rust variadic signatures instead.

Native lowering (src/frontend/native_lowerer/) needs the equivalent: extend items.rs's function-signature emission to detect a variadic FunctionDecl and rewrite its trailing ... into a single boxed-args parameter (unless it's a C-ABI/forwarding case), extend call-site lowering in exprs.rs to pack trailing arguments into __SlateVaArgs::new(...), add a Type::Custom("__SlateVaArgs") case for va_list locals in items.rs's collect_locals/type lowering, and add statement/expr handlers for the three implicit builtins (__builtin_c23_va_start, __builtin_va_arg -- check exact Clang node shape, likely a dedicated VAArgExpr rather than a CallExpr, so it needs a Clang::* match arm in exprs.rs's lower_expr rather than builtins.rs's call dispatch -- and __builtin_va_end) mirroring lower_va_start/lower_va_arg above. The SupportModule literal itself (lowerer.rs:1643-1682) can likely be reused/shared rather than reimplemented -- check whether it's frontend-agnostic.

Verify: SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=varargs cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture (also re-check c89, va_list_vfprintf once varargs passes).
close_reason: Abandoning the native clang-ast-crate lowering experiment: reverted main back to the pre-migration commit (7f50e296) and parked the in-progress work on branch experiment/clang-ast. Decision (2026-08-16): the CIR-based lowerer is much further along (many more fixtures + gcc-torture cases passing), and the AST-only rewrite wasn't shaping up to be more readable/maintainable despite fixing several real bugs along the way. Resuming CIR-based work on gcc-torture (slate-os0h.22, slate-os0h.3.1) instead. Parent epic slate-ypjt was already closed; this closes out its slate-ypjt.2 child epic and all remaining open sub-issues.

title: native lowering: __builtin_ia32_* x86 intrinsics unresolved
description: x86_instruction_intrinsics fails on 'unresolved decl reference' from __builtin_ia32_lfence/mfence/pause/rdtsc/rdtscp/sfence -- excluded by items.rs's is_implicit guard like every other __builtin_* was before slate-ypjt.2.14. These map to stable core::arch::x86_64 intrinsics: _mm_lfence/_mm_mfence/_mm_pause (all in core::arch::x86_64, stable), __rdtsc/__rdtscp (also stable in core::arch::x86_64). Likely a small addition to src/frontend/native_lowerer/builtins.rs's try_lower_builtin_call dispatch (same shape as the existing simple 0/1-arg builtins e.g. __builtin_debugtrap), no new machinery needed -- just map each __builtin_ia32_* name to the matching core::arch::x86_64:: call, wrapped in unsafe if the intrinsic requires it (function bodies are already fully unsafe-wrapped per native_lowerer's convention, so no extra unsafe block needed, matching how gnu_builtin_debugtrap/math builtins were done). Verify: SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=x86_instruction_intrinsics cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture.
