title: native lowering: DeclRefExpr can't resolve GNU/Clang __builtin_* function references
description:
Split out of slate-ypjt.2.1 after fixing the global-variable/enum-constant cases there -- this is a separate, distinct root cause hitting the same LowerError::UnresolvedDecl symptom.

Residual "unresolved decl reference" failures after .2.1's fix (rerun `cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture` to get the current exact list; as of this triage): c89, complex, complex_equality, complex_lvalue, constant_object_query_ops, control_flow_builtin_ops, gnu_builtin_addressof, gnu_builtin_debugtrap, gnu_builtin_return_address, integer_bit_builtin_ops, long_double, long_double_complex, math_builtin_ops, mem_bcopy_overlap, mem_memchr, memchr_nullable_pointer, overflow_scalar_ops, stdlib_complex_cx_limited_range, va_list_vfprintf, varargs, x86_instruction_intrinsics. (Not all individually confirmed to be this exact cause -- the fixture names strongly suggest __builtin_* usage, but verify each.)

Root cause (confirmed mechanism, not yet confirmed for every fixture above): src/frontend/native_lowerer/items.rs's collect_top_level only registers `Clang::FunctionDecl(d) if !d.is_implicit` into ctx.vars (~line 98). Compiler builtins (__builtin_popcount, __builtin_addressof, __builtin_expect, etc.) are synthesized, implicit FunctionDecls that Clang injects -- they're deliberately excluded by that `is_implicit` guard (presumably to avoid registering thousands of implicit library-function declarations as plain Rust functions), so any DeclRefExpr/CallExpr referencing one hits LowerError::UnresolvedDecl.

This needs different handling than a plain DeclRefExpr resolution fix: __builtin_* functions should map to Rust intrinsics/std library calls (e.g. `__builtin_popcount` -> `count_ones()`, `__builtin_expect` -> pass-through, `__builtin_memcpy` -> `std::ptr::copy`, etc.), not to a registered Var pointing at a real function definition -- there's no C-side definition to lower for these; they're compiler magic. Check whether src/frontend/lowerer (mature CIR lowerer) already has this mapping table somewhere (search for "__builtin_" or "Builtin" in src/frontend/lowerer/*.rs and src/frontend/intrinsics.rs if it exists) -- since CIR itself may already resolve builtins to a `cir.` builtin op before this ever becomes a DeclRefExpr problem, the mature lowerer's approach might not transfer directly, but the *mapping table* of which builtins to which Rust equivalents should be reusable.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=gnu_builtin_addressof cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`.
close_reason: Implemented direct Rust-equivalent codegen for the common __builtin_* families in a new src/frontend/native_lowerer/builtins.rs module (dispatched from call_expr before generic DeclRefExpr resolution): __builtin_addressof, debugtrap/trap, unreachable, expect, assume, return_address/frame_address, __clear_cache/prefetch, bitreverse32/bswap32/clz/ctz/popcount/parity/ffs/clrsb/rotateleft32/rotateright32, add/sub/mul_overflow, and the sin/cos/tan/log/log10/log2/exp/exp2/sqrt/pow/fmod/lround/llround math family (with a Clang-AST prepass that emits only the extern decls actually referenced). Also fixed a real, more general pre-existing bug this surfaced: ReturnStmt didn't cast a Rust-bool-shaped comparison result to the function's declared C return type when C's own type system doesn't insert an implicit cast (comparisons are already 'int' in C) -- added Env::ret_ty threaded through function lowering. Net effect: 200 -> 209/332 fixtures passing (9 fixed: control_flow_builtin_ops, gnu_builtin_addressof, gnu_builtin_debugtrap, gnu_builtin_return_address, integer_bit_builtin_ops, math_builtin_ops, overflow_scalar_ops, target_stack_builtin_ops, plus bonus fix logical_ops). Remaining unresolved-decl failures are NOT the is_implicit-exclusion root cause anymore -- they're distinct unimplemented builtin families, triaged and filed as new child beads: __builtin_complex (complex.c family), va_list/__builtin_c23_va_start+va_end (varargs family), __builtin_memchr/__builtin_bcopy (trivial libc passthroughs, same shape as the math table), __builtin_ia32_* (x86 intrinsics), __builtin_constant_p/__builtin_object_size (need compile-time constant analysis).

title: native lowering: CType::parse misparses anonymous struct/enum/union qualType as a function type
description:
Found while working slate-ypjt.2.1. Confirmed for anonymous_enum_record_field.c:
  struct Conditional { enum { IN_THEN, IN_ELIF = 4, IN_ELSE } ctx; };
lowers `ctx`'s field type to `Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(i32) -> i32>` instead of an integer/enum type.

Root cause: src/frontend/native_lowerer/types.rs, CType::parse (~line 190-241). Clang spells an anonymous enum's qualType as `"enum (unnamed at tests/fixtures/anonymous_enum_record_field.c:4:3)"`. The parse order checks `trailing_paren_params(s)` (~line 212, treats a trailing `(...)` as a function parameter list) BEFORE checking the `"enum "`/`"struct "`/`"union "` tag prefixes (~line 223-239) -- so the `(unnamed at ...)` location suffix gets misread as a parameter list, and the whole anonymous enum type is misclassified as `CType::Func`. The same bug plausibly affects anonymous struct/union field types that reach this same qualType-string parse path (not just RecordDecl's own dedicated collection path in items.rs, which handles named/tagged records separately).

Suggested fix: don't reorder the checks naively -- a function *returning* a struct/union/enum by value legitimately spells as e.g. "struct Foo (int)", so struct/enum prefix can't simply be checked first unconditionally. Instead, special-case the "(unnamed at " marker specifically: if the trailing paren group's contents start with "unnamed at ", it's an anonymous-tag location suffix, not a parameter list -- skip the trailing_paren_params branch for that case and fall through to the struct/union/enum prefix checks.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=anonymous_enum_record_field cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`. Also check anon_local_struct/anonymous_header_two_hop (already filed as slate-ypjt.2.8) in case this is the same root cause for some of those -- worth checking before fixing both independently.
close_reason: Fixed as a side effect of slate-ypjt.2.8: CType::parse's trailing_paren_params branch now bails when the text before the trailing parens is bare 'struct'/'union'/'enum' (no tag name), falling through to the tag-prefix checks that correctly parse '(unnamed at file:line:col)' as an anonymous-tag location suffix instead of a function param list. anonymous_enum_record_field now passes.

title: test harness: BatchBuild::error_for dumps entire shared stderr per unmatched fixture
description:
Not a lowering bug -- a test-harness DX problem that actively hampers triaging this epic's other children. tests/support/mod.rs, BatchBuild::error_for (~line 526-534): when a specific bin's name isn't found in the `errors` BTreeMap (populated only from JSON "compiler-message" entries that include a "target" name), it falls back to returning the *entire* shared `self.stderr` (the batch cargo invocation's raw process stderr, which can include every OTHER bin's linker errors, warnings, etc. concatenated). Every case in compare_batch that hits this fallback re-embeds that same giant blob into its own `[name] Rust batch build failed:\n<blob>` failure message.

Impact: a native-lowering profile run with ~85 compile-failing fixtures produced a `cargo nextest ... --nocapture` log of ~930,000 lines (measured this session) -- the same multi-hundred-KB stderr blob repeated ~85-100 times. This makes `--nocapture` essentially unusable for triage once more than a handful of fixtures fail to compile in the same batch, and will bite anyone working the other children in this epic.

Suggested approach: raw process stderr should only be used as the fallback for bins that have genuinely no per-target JSON message (e.g. real linker-only failures like "undefined symbol" that cargo doesn't attribute to a specific bin target in JSON) -- and even then, don't repeat it verbatim for every affected fixture; either dedupe (attach it once, referenced by name, not inlined N times) or scope it by grepping the blob for lines mentioning that specific bin's source path before falling back to the whole thing. Consider whether cargo has a way to attribute linker errors to bins more precisely (per-bin `--message-format=json` linker diagnostics, or building bins individually only for the ones missing an artifact, as a fallback pass).

This is independent of and can be picked up before/in-parallel-with the other children in this epic -- fixing it first will make every other child's triage faster.
close_reason: Stopped push_str'ing every compiler-message's rendered text into the shared BatchBuild::stderr blob (it was accumulating every OTHER bin's errors too); error_for now scopes the raw-stderr fallback to lines mentioning that bin's src/bin/<name>.rs path, falling back to the full blob only once (not per-fixture) when nothing matches. --nocapture log for a run with ~130 compile failures dropped from ~930k lines to 1627.

title: native lowering: anonymous/locally-scoped struct type names unresolved
description:
4 compile failures are E0425 "cannot find type \`X\` in this scope" for a *struct* type name (distinct from the sibling LongDouble bead -- different root cause, same rustc error code): anon_local_struct ("buffer_t"), anonymous_header_two_hop ("anonymous_header_state"), libyaml_type_shapes ("parser_t"), local_struct_name_collision ("TestCase").

Root cause (not yet root-caused, needs investigation): the common thread by fixture name is anonymous or locally-scoped struct/typedef declarations. Likely native_lowerer's RecordRegistry (src/frontend/native_lowerer/types.rs) registers named top-level RecordDecls but misses one of: (a) structs declared via typedef of an anonymous struct (`typedef struct { ... } buffer_t;`), (b) structs declared inside a function body (local scope), or (c) some name-collision/shadowing case between two same-named locally-scoped structs in different functions (local_struct_name_collision hints at this specifically). Start by dumping the AST for anon_local_struct.c and libyaml_type_shapes.c (`cargo run --release -- dump-clang-ast`) to see which RecordDecl/TypedefDecl shape isn't being walked into the registry, then compare against how items.rs's collect_top_level / RecordRegistry population walks the tree.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=anon_local_struct cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`.
close_reason: Generalized RecordDecl collection+emission to walk the whole AST (not just tu.inner): anonymous struct/union RecordDecls now derive their registry tag from the adjacent TypedefDecl/VarDecl/FieldDecl's own qual_type (via CType::parse, unwrapping through Array/Ptr), covering typedef'd anon structs (buffer_t, parser_t), locally-scoped structs inside function bodies (point), and nested anon members (union value). Also fixed: (1) CType::parse misparsing '(unnamed at file:line:col)' anon-struct tag spellings as function types (bare struct/union/enum before trailing parens no longer triggers the fn-ptr branch); (2) is_shim_loc path check no longer canonicalizes (libc-shim/include/bits is a symlink to ../bits, which broke prefix matching after resolution); (3) ImplicitValueInitExpr in aggregate initializers now zero-inits instead of erroring; (4) bool-typed comparison/logical subexpressions (including through ParenExpr) are now cast to i32 in arithmetic/bitwise binary ops, matching C's implicit promotion. Fixed anon_local_struct, anon_struct_array, anon_struct_name_collision, anonymous_enum_record_field, anonymous_header_two_hop, array_indexed_struct_field_named_enum, bitfield_storage, int128_arith, nested_anon_struct_fields, struct_init (178->188/332). Known unfixed limitation: local_struct_name_collision has three same-named 'struct TestCase' definitions in different function scopes with different fields -- the registry is a single flat tag->fields map with no scope disambiguation, so only the first-seen definition wins; the other two functions get wrong field layouts. Fixing this needs per-scope record renaming, a real architecture change. libyaml_type_shapes also still fails on unrelated typedef-desugaring gaps (typedef'd char array element type resolving to i32 instead of the underlying unsigned char, and a typedef'd function-pointer struct field not desugaring to a real fn-ptr type).

title: native lowering: nullptr / C23 CXXNullPtrLiteralExpr not lowered
description:
13 translate failures are `unsupported expr node kind: Some("CXXNullPtrLiteralExpr")`. Slate defaults to GNU C23 (see CLAUDE.md / docs/README.md toolchain section), which added the `nullptr` keyword; clang represents both the `nullptr` literal and (per c23_nullptr.c fixture name) related nullptr_t usage this way.

Root cause: same shape as the sizeof/alignof gap (sibling bead in this epic) -- src/parse/clang_ast.rs's `Clang` enum has no variant for CXXNullPtrLiteralExpr, so it falls into `Clang::Other` and gets rejected by native_lowerer/exprs.rs's `Other` fallback (~line 97) since it's not in `is_transparent_wrapper`.

Suggested approach: this one is simpler than sizeof -- no extra fields needed, just a leaf literal. Add a match arm in native_lowerer/exprs.rs's lower_expr for `Clang::Other(o) if o.kind.as_deref() == Some("CXXNullPtrLiteralExpr")` (or promote it to a first-class enum variant if that's the established pattern by the time this is picked up) that lowers to a null pointer expression at the target type -- check node_type(node)/qual_type for the pointee type and produce `std::ptr::null_mut()` / `std::ptr::null()` matching how the mature lowerer represents C NULL elsewhere (likely also worth checking whether ordinary `NULL` macro / integer-0-to-pointer already has a working path in this file to reuse its target type resolution).

Affected: 13 fixtures including c23_nullptr and others using nullptr in initializers/comparisons/returns -- get the exact list from a fresh triage run after the fix.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=c23_nullptr cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`.
close_reason: Added nullptr_t -> CType::Ptr(Void) mapping in CType::from, and a CXXNullPtrLiteralExpr leaf case in lower_expr producing RustValue::NullPtr (std::ptr::null_mut()), matching the mature lowerer's null-pointer representation. Parity went 162->178/332 (nullptr_t appears widely across fixtures beyond the 13 originally scoped).

title: native lowering: string literal initializer for fixed-size char array not decoded
description:
Confirmed for string_lift: generated code has
  let mut greeting: [i8; 4] = c"h303251";
  let mut mutate: [i8; 4] = c"abc";
i.e. rustc error "expected \`[i8; 4]\`, found \`&CStr\`" -- a C string literal used to initialize a fixed-size char array is being lowered as a C-string pointer/&CStr expression (the right form for a `char *` initializer) rather than decoded into an array-of-bytes literal (the right form for a `char buf[N] = "..."` initializer).

Root cause is presumably in src/frontend/native_lowerer/globals.rs's lower_init (used for both global and DeclStmt local initializers): the StringLiteral case likely always produces the pointer/CStr form regardless of the declared target type being an array vs a pointer. The mature lowerer (src/frontend/lowerer) must already special-case this (char-array-from-string-literal is extremely common C); find its equivalent (search for how it distinguishes InitListExpr/StringLiteral-into-array vs into-pointer) and mirror the same target-type-driven branch in globals.rs's lower_init.

Likely-affected fixtures (string_lift confirmed; others share the "mismatched types" E0308 symptom against similar initializer shapes but are NOT individually confirmed to be this exact cause -- verify each): array_init, memcmp, string_libc_fixup, string_param_lift. Re-triage after the fix to see what's left.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=string_lift cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`; check the generated Rust directly with `cargo run --release -- translate --frontend native tests/fixtures/string_lift.c`.
close_reason: Fixed: char-array string-literal initializers now decode into byte-array literals instead of &CStr; also fixed octal-escape (\ddd) decoding in unescape_c_string, needed for non-ASCII string literals like "hé". Fixed string_lift, string_libc_fixup, string_param_lift. array_init and memcmp fail for unrelated reasons (different array-init bug, and memcmp bool/i32 comparison mismatch).

title: native lowering: LongDouble type never defined/imported in generated programs
description:
9 compile failures are E0425 "cannot find type \`LongDouble\` in this scope": long_double_comparisons, long_double_extern_sin, long_double_f80_arithmetic, long_double_literal_edge, long_double_literal_precision, long_double_pointer_out, long_double_strtold_f80, long_double_struct, long_double_union_representation, long_double_variadic (some may additionally have their own follow-on errors once this is fixed).

Root cause: `LongDouble` is a real type used pervasively by the mature CIR lowerer -- see src/frontend/lowerer/{calls,types,runtime_support,constants,storage}.rs and src/backend/rust_ast.rs / codegen.rs (codegen presumably renders a `Type::LongDouble` variant as the bare identifier `LongDouble`). Generated programs from that path must therefore also emit or import the LongDouble struct definition somewhere (check runtime_support.rs -- likely a prelude/support item list appended to every generated program's `Item`s). The native lowerer's own type module (src/frontend/native_lowerer/types.rs, CType) either doesn't map `long double` to the same Type::LongDouble at all, or does but items.rs/lower_program never includes the definition-emitting step the mature path relies on.

Suggested approach: confirm CType::parse maps "long double" the same way the mature lowerer's rust_type() does (reusing Type::LongDouble, not inventing a parallel representation), then find wherever the mature path injects the LongDouble struct definition into a generated program's item list and do the same for native_lowerer::lower_program (mod.rs) / items.rs.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=long_double_struct cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`.
notes:
Root cause was actually two-fold (the bead title only named the first):

1. LongDouble type never emitted: the struct + operator-impl prelude (long_double_prelude()) and the __slate_f80_* extern shim declarations (f80_shim_decls()) already exist in the mature CIR lowerer (src/frontend/lowerer/runtime_support.rs), gated behind a uses_long_double flag and spliced into the program only when needed -- the native lowerer never called any of this. Relaxed visibility (pub(super) -> pub(crate)) on long_double_prelude/f80_shim_decls/f80_cast_from_name/f80_cast_to_name/f80_literal_expr and their containing modules (runtime_support, constants), and reused them directly rather than duplicating -- wired a program_uses_long_double() post-pass in native_lowerer/items.rs (walks all Fn/Static/Record/ExternBlock items and their bodies for any Type::LongDouble) and spliced the prelude+shim extern block into RustProgram.items in mod.rs when true.

2. Even with the type defined, no VALUE of that type could ever be constructed: FloatingLiteral always lowered to a bare RustValue::Float (f64), and casts always used plain 'as' -- neither type-checks against the LongDouble struct. Fixed by reusing the mature lowerer's exact machinery: FloatingLiteral for a long-double-typed literal now calls f80_literal_expr() (parses the literal's own decimal text via rustc_apfloat's X87DoubleExtended -- NOT a lossy round-trip through f64, which would truncate precision beyond f64's ~15-17 digits; Clang's JSON already gives clean, pre-rounded 80-bit-precision decimal text, confirmed via dump-clang-ast) with a __slate_f80_from_f64 fallback matching the mature lowerer's own fallback for whatever edge case that parser might reject. Casts to/from LongDouble now route through the f80_cast_from_name/f80_cast_to_name shim tables instead of a bare 'as'. zero_value() for CType::LDouble now uses long_double_zero_expr() instead of RustValue::Float(0.0).

Also fixed, found opportunistically and broadly impactful (not long-double-specific): comparison/logical expressions passed as variadic call arguments (e.g. printf("%d", a > b)) lower to Rust bool but Rust rejects passing bare bool to a variadic function (E0617) -- call_expr now detects variadic callees via the callee's own CType::Func{is_variadic} (itself only correctly parseable since slate-ypjt.2.4's pointer-to-function CType::parse fix) and inserts an  for any bool-typed argument landing in the variadic tail.

150->153/332, zero regressions (diffed full ok/FAIL list). Long_double_struct, long_double_comparisons, long_double_memcpy now pass. Most other long_double_* fixtures still fail on unrelated gaps found along the way, NOT re-diagnosed in depth: long_double.c pulls in _BitInt/__int128 casts and ~40 libm long-double extern functions (way beyond this bead's scope); long_double_variadic/long_double_pointer_out show stdout diffs (printf %La hex-float formatting and/or va_list-of-LongDouble passing, not verified which); long_double_extern_sin has an unexamined remaining compile error. These are real, separate gaps -- worth their own triage rather than folding into this bead.
close_reason: LongDouble type+value construction now fully wired (prelude struct, shim externs, precise literal parsing, cast conversions), reusing the mature lowerer's existing machinery instead of reimplementing. Also fixed a broadly-impactful bool-to-variadic-arg bug found along the way. 150->153/332, no regressions. Most other long_double_* fixtures remain blocked on distinct, unexamined gaps (BitInt/int128 casts, libm externs, %La formatting) -- noted but not chased further.

title: native lowering: function values aren't cast/wrapped for Option<extern fn> fields
description:
~15+ compile failures are E0308 "expected enum \`Option<unsafe extern \"C\" fn(...) -> ...>\`, found fn item \`unsafe fn(...) {name}\`" (or "found raw pointer"/"found type i64"). Sample fixtures: function_pointers, setjmp_recovery_extern_c_callback, indirect_call_void_ptr_param, nested_anon_struct_fields, ternary_function_pointer_select, function_pointer_presence, gnu_symbol_pragmas (a related "expected fn item ... found fn item" ABI-tag mismatch), and by name alone likely also: function_pointer_struct_init, function_pointer_to_void_ptr_cast, weakref_function, alias_function, indirect_call_unwind_abi_propagation, enum_return_type_function_pointer_field, pointer_to_function_pointer_field, struct_literal_null_function_pointer_field, void_ptr_function_pointer_cast, c11_callbacks, libc_address_taken_safe_callback -- confirm each individually, this list is by symptom-name pattern match, not all individually verified.

Root cause (hypothesis to confirm): this codebase represents C function-pointer-typed fields/locals as `Option<unsafe extern "C" fn(...) -> ...>` (nullable, ABI-tagged). When a plain function name (a FunctionDecl reference used as a value -- e.g. assigned into a function-pointer field, passed as a callback argument, compared, or selected in a ternary) is lowered, native_lowerer/exprs.rs's DeclRefExpr path just emits a bare `RExpr::Var(name)` (a function item reference), never wrapping it as `Some(name as <fn-ptr-type>)` the way a function-pointer-typed context requires. The `CallBinding`/`function_identity` machinery already imported in native_lowerer (see stmts.rs/exprs.rs imports) exists for *call* sites -- check whether it or an equivalent already has the right wrapping logic for non-call (value) contexts, or whether that only exists in src/frontend/lowerer/calls.rs (the mature CIR lowerer) and needs porting.

One entry (goto_into_later_switch_case_bitint) shows a *different*-looking E0308 against the same Option<fn> field type ("found type {integer}") -- likely an unrelated bitint/state-dispatch bug coincidentally touching a similarly-named field; don't fold it into this fix without checking, triage separately if it doesn't resolve.

Suggested approach: find where CType/native_lowerer's type lowering decides a C function-pointer type becomes `Option<unsafe extern "C" fn...>` (types.rs), and make every expression-context lowering of a FunctionDecl-valued DeclRefExpr against that target type wrap the function reference in `Some(name)` (with any needed `as` cast for extern "C" ABI-tagging), matching whatever src/frontend/lowerer/calls.rs already does for the mature CIR path.

Verify: `SLATE_DIFF_FIXTURE=function_pointers cargo nextest r --release --profile=native-lowering --nocapture`.
notes:
Found the actual root cause was different from my original diagnosis, plus a real second bug once fixed. Two separate fixes:

1. CType::parse's trailing_paren_params heuristic mis-parsed pointer-to-function declarator syntax entirely: qualType strings like 'int (*)(int, int)' were parsed by recursively treating the inner '(*)'  as ITS OWN function-type spelling (base 'int (*)' -> return_ty parsed AGAIN via the same heuristic, misreading '*' as a param list) instead of recognizing '(*)' as the pointer-to-function marker. Result: every function-pointer-typed value got a garbled, doubly-nested Option<fn> type. Fixed in native_lowerer/types.rs by detecting a base ending in '(*)' and wrapping the parsed function type in CType::Ptr instead of recursing into it as a return type.

2. Once the type was correct, two real gaps remained: (a) function names used as *values* (assigned/passed where a fn-pointer is expected) need Some(..) wrapping to satisfy Option<extern fn>, but a DIRECT call's callee must stay a bare callable function item -- Clang marks exactly this distinction via the FunctionToPointerDecay ImplicitCastExpr, which wraps a function name in every value-use including direct-call callees. Fixed in exprs.rs: FunctionToPointerDecay now wraps in Some(..) by default; call_expr's callee position specifically bypasses that wrapper (added lower_callee()) and calls through Option-typed values via .unwrap(). (b) Function *definitions* whose address is taken this way were still declared as plain `fn` (Rust ABI), not coercible to extern "C" fn pointer type -- added a collect_address_taken_fns() pre-pass (items.rs/mod.rs) that scans the whole TU for FunctionToPointerDecay-wrapped function references and tags those definitions abi: Some(Abi::C), matching how the mature CIR lowerer already does this (its c_abi_functions set, src/frontend/lowerer.rs ~line 2153).

145->150/332, zero regressions (diffed the full ok/FAIL list against the pre-fix run).
close_reason: Root cause was actually a CType::parse bug for pointer-to-function declarators (garbled nested Option<fn> types), plus missing Some(..)-wrapping and extern C ABI tagging for address-taken functions. Both fixed. 145->150/332, no regressions.

title: native lowerer: VLA/alloca translation has no real Rust target (alloca has no linkable symbol)
description:
The native lowerer translates C VLAs (int arr[n]) to a literal alloca(size) call (see parser.rs's declare_builtin_functions/new_alloca), which the generated Rust emits as a plain function call `alloca(sz)`. This has no real target: glibc does not export a linkable `alloca` symbol (confirmed via `nm -D libc.so.6` -- no match), it's a pure compiler builtin with no ABI-stable callable form. Even if declared via extern "C", it wouldn't link, and even if it somehow did, calling it through a real function-call boundary from Rust wouldn't reserve stack space in the caller's frame the way C's alloca() semantics require.

Found while fixing Decl-emission gaps in slate-ozsg.8.8 (tests/fixtures/local_vla.c): after fixing the VLA-local and VLA-size-temp Decl gaps (both now emit correctly) and a related decay_to_ptr bug (Vla-typed values were incorrectly treated like fixed arrays and given a spurious .as_ptr() call), this is the only remaining error on that fixture.

Needs a real design decision, not a small patch: options include (a) lower VLAs to a real Rust allocation (Vec<T> with runtime len, changing every use site from raw-pointer arithmetic to a Vec-backed pointer), (b) use an actual stack-allocation crate/intrinsic if one exists and is acceptable per the project's unsafe/libc conventions, or (c) something else. Whatever's chosen needs to preserve the raw-pointer/unsafe transliteration style used everywhere else in native_lowerer per CLAUDE.md's "transliterate first, idiomize later," while still being a real, linkable, semantically-correct translation.
close_reason: Superseded: abandoning the ported-chibicc (cc3) parser approach. Whack-a-mole on chibicc-specific desugaring gaps (Decl-emission for compiler-synthesized temps, VLA/alloca, truthiness coercion, etc. -- see slate-ozsg.8.8's notes for the running list) made clear that re-deriving what Clang's own AST already gives for free isn't worth it. New direction: parse Clang's AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input instead of both CIR and a hand-ported C frontend. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one. All completed child work (lexer/preprocessor port, parser port, node-identity, Decl hierarchy, most of the native lowerer) stays closed/done as real completed work; it's the strategy of continuing to chase chibicc-vs-Rust semantic gaps that's being dropped, not that work.

title: Attach include-chain provenance to Decl
description: Once slate-ozsg.7's include-chain task and the Vec<Decl> fold both exist, expose provenance on Decl -- e.g. a method or field answering 'is this from the primary translation unit file' and, if not, the include chain back to it (header name plus the #include location at each hop) -- so the eventual lowerer can decide whether to translate a declaration, map it onto an existing Rust/libc binding, or skip it, the way Clang AST consumers use loc.includedFrom.
acceptance_criteria: Given tests/fixtures/add.c (#include <stdio.h>), the printf FunctionDecl's provenance resolves to stdio.h via the include chain from main.c; a plain user-defined function in the primary file reports as primary-file-native with no chain.
close_reason: Added Decl::is_primary_file(&self) -> bool (location.file_no == 1) and Decl::include_chain(&self) -> Vec<PathBuf> (delegates to slate-ozsg.7.1's lexer::include_chain(location.file_no)) in ast.rs. Kept as methods rather than eagerly-populated fields deliberately -- storing the chain on every Decl would reintroduce the same per-node bloat this whole epic is fighting; computing on demand from the file_no already on every Decl costs nothing until asked. Verified against tests/fixtures/add.c exactly per the acceptance criteria: printf resolves is_primary_file=false, chain=[add.c, libc-shim/include/stdio.h]; add resolves is_primary_file=true, chain=[add.c] only. Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied. This closes out slate-ozsg.7 (Decl/DeclKind hierarchy + include-chain provenance) -- all 5 subtasks done.

title: Reference self-referential struct/union members by id instead of embedding a possibly-stale Type clone
description: Once the id-keyed type registry exists, stop embedding a cloned Type::Struct/Union (complete or not) inside pointer/member positions that refer back to a tag currently being defined. Store the NodeId and resolve through the registry on demand. Remove the now-redundant is_incomplete-refetch-by-name fallback in struct_ref (parser.rs:3543-3560) and audit other call sites doing the same workaround (grep for is_incomplete checks paired with find_tag, e.g. member.ty.clone() at parser.rs:6648, and the semantic-analysis uses around parser.rs:6872/6970).
design: Depends on: Add a Program-level id-keyed type registry backing tag resolution.
acceptance_criteria: A differential fixture with a self-referencing struct (linked-list style, e.g. traversing node->next->next->value) proves the pointee's member list is never stale/empty; struct_ref's is_incomplete fallback branch is deleted or proven unreachable; lowering/rewrites profiles pass unchanged.
close_reason: Replaced both is_incomplete-refetch-by-name workarounds with a single canonicalize_type(&self, ty: Type) -> Type helper that resolves a Struct/Union/Enum through the id-keyed registry from slate-ozsg.6.3. struct_ref (member/arrow access) and find_typedef's resolve_typedef_type now call it instead of hand-reconstructing the incomplete fallback via full field enumeration; resolve_typedef_type itself was collapsed away (its one caller now calls canonicalize_type directly). This is also strictly more correct than the old find_tag(&tag)-by-name fallback it replaced: name-based scope lookup can resolve to the wrong type if the tag name is shadowed in a nested scope between capture and use, whereas id-based lookup is unambiguous. Because struct_ref is the single point where -> and . resolve a member list, a chain like node->next->next->value self-heals through repeated canonicalization at each step even though the member's embedded pointee type (Member.ty) still carries its original possibly-incomplete clone -- only its id (stable per 6.3) needs to be current. Audited the other member.ty/member.offset call sites (is_array check, eval_rval/eval2 offset accumulation) -- unrelated to type staleness, no changes needed. Build + clippy clean, cargo fmt applied. No tests run per instruction; this closes out slate-ozsg.6.

title: float128.c: __float128 type and Q literal suffix unsupported
description: float128.c failed with 'invalid numeric constant' at the first Q-suffixed float literal (1.0Q) -- the lexer's convert_pp_number only stripped f/F (Float) and l/L (LDouble) suffixes, leaving a trailing Q it couldn't parse as f64. __float128 itself also wasn't recognized as a type at all (no Type variant, no declspec/is_typename_token wiring), the same gap __int128 had before slate-ozsg.4.3.
design: Fixed: added Type::F128 (size=align=16, is_flonum=true) to ast.rs; wired '__float128' as an identifier-spelled type specifier in parse_declspec and is_typename_token, mirroring __int128's precedent exactly; added q/Q suffix stripping in lexer.rs's convert_pp_number mapping to Type::F128. Reused the plain f64-backed ExprKind::Num representation (not the exact-precision X87DoubleExtended-style path built for LDouble) since every literal this fixture uses (1.0, 0x1p-100, 42.0, 42.75) is exactly representable in f64 -- no precision loss for this fixture's needs, though a future fixture exercising __float128 precision beyond f64 would need the same raw-value-preserving treatment LDouble got.
acceptance_criteria: float128.c parses via 'slate parse-only'.
close_reason: Added Type::F128, __float128 declspec/typename recognition, and Q/q literal suffix support; float128.c parses.

title: long_double.c: several __builtin_* math/classification functions unregistered
description: long_double.c failed with 'implicit declaration of a function' (misleadingly located at 59:30, which is not the real trigger site -- error-location tracking through nested macro expansion is imprecise here, bisection by truncating the file was needed to find the actual cause). isnan/isinf/isfinite/isnormal/signbit/islessgreater/isunordered expand (via libc-shim/include/math.h) to __builtin_isnan/isinf/isfinite/isnormal/signbit/islessgreater/isunordered, and HUGE_VALL/HUGE_VAL/HUGE_VALF expand to __builtin_huge_vall/huge_val/huge_valf -- none of these were registered via push_builtin_fn (parser.rs declare_builtin_functions), unlike the sin/cos/exp/etc. family that already was.
design: Fixed: registered __builtin_isnan/isinf/isfinite/isnormal/signbit (double->int) and __builtin_islessgreater/isunordered (double,double->int) and __builtin_huge_val/huge_valf/huge_vall (void->double/float/long double).
acceptance_criteria: long_double.c parses via 'slate parse-only'.
close_reason: Registered the missing __builtin_isnan/isinf/isfinite/isnormal/signbit/islessgreater/isunordered/huge_val family; long_double.c parses.

title: atomic_flag_ops.c: ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT / atomic_flag undefined in native frontend
description: atomic_flag_ops.c fails with 'undefined variable' at 5:22, pointing at 'ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT' in 'atomic_flag flag = ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT;'. The fixture also uses atomic_flag_test_and_set(_explicit) and atomic_flag_clear(_explicit). Likely the libc shim's stdatomic.h (SLATE_LIBC_SHIM) doesn't define the ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT macro and/or the atomic_flag type, or the native frontend doesn't special-case the atomic_flag builtins the way it does the general atomic_fetch_*/atomic_load/atomic_store family.
design: Check libc-shim/include/stdatomic.h for atomic_flag/ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT definitions first (this may be purely a missing-shim-macro issue, not a parser gap). If the macro exists but still fails, check whether atomic_flag_test_and_set/_clear are registered alongside the other atomic builtins (see slate-ozsg.4.1's builtin-registration work for precedent).
acceptance_criteria: atomic_flag_ops.c parses via 'slate parse-only'.
notes: Root cause was purely a libc-shim bug, not a native-frontend parser gap: libc-shim/include/stdatomic.h's ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT was defined as a function-like macro ('#define ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT(x) (x)'), but the fixture (and the C standard) uses it as a bare object-like macro ('= ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT;', no parens). A function-like macro name not followed by '(' is left untouched by the preprocessor per the standard, so the raw identifier leaked through to the parser as an undefined variable. Fixed by making it an object-like macro ('#define ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT 0'), which is a valid scalar initializer since this shim's atomic_flag is typedef'd to a scalar (_Atomic _Bool), not the struct type some libcs use. Confirmed via 'slate emit-cir' that this fixture doesn't even compile under the CIR/clang frontend today (separate pre-existing bug: atomic_exchange's shim macro calls a fake __builtin_atomic_exchange that isn't a real clang builtin) -- so this was never in the 'currently passing under CIR frontend' baseline the epic targets for parity, but the shim fix is still correct/shared and the ticket's own acceptance bar (native frontend parses it) is now met. native-frontend-report: 324/332.
close_reason: Shim bug fixed (ATOMIC_FLAG_INIT is now object-like); atomic_flag_ops.c parses via the native frontend.

title: atomic_fallbacks.c: 'invalid operands' on _Atomic(float)/_Atomic(int*) fetch_add/exchange
description: atomic_fallbacks.c fails with 'invalid operands' at 43:60 (a reported location past the fixture's own 20 lines, so likely from stdatomic.h shim macro expansion). The fixture exercises _Atomic(float) with atomic_fetch_add_explicit/atomic_load, and _Atomic(int *) with atomic_fetch_add_explicit/atomic_exchange_explicit/atomic_load -- i.e. atomic builtins on float and pointer operands, not just plain integers. Likely the native frontend's atomic-builtin type checking (whatever validates the fetch_add-family builtins' operand types) only accepts integer operands and rejects float/pointer, where C11 stdatomic explicitly allows both (pointer fetch_add does scaled pointer arithmetic; float atomics are a common extension).
design: Find where the native frontend type-checks atomic builtin calls (grep for atomic_fetch_add / __atomic or similar in parser.rs) and compare against how the equivalent CIR/libc-shim path allows float and pointer operands. May just need to broaden an is_integer()-style guard to also accept is_flonum()/pointer types, mirroring how normal +/- already handle pointer arithmetic.
acceptance_criteria: atomic_fallbacks.c parses via 'slate parse-only'.
notes: Root cause was two distinct bugs in parser.rs, both around Type::Atomic handling in arithmetic, found by tracing lhs.ty through to_assign()'s atomic-compound-assignment CAS-loop desugar (added and removed a debug eprintln to confirm which of the two atomic_fetch_add_explicit call sites -- float vs pointer -- actually failed): (1) new_add/new_sub classified operands by calling is_numeric()/.base() directly on possibly-Atomic-qualified types without first applying C11's lvalue-to-rvalue atomic decay (6.3.2.1p2), so e.g. plain '_Atomic int a; a + b;' (as in type_qualifiers.c, not just this ticket's fixture) misclassified both operands as pointer-like via Type::base()'s Atomic arm and rejected them. Fixed by adding Type::decay_atomic() (ast.rs) and calling it on both operand types at the top of new_add and new_sub. (2) to_assign()'s CAS-loop desugar for 'A op= B' on an atomic A declared its 'val' temp local with A's own unwrapped type (base_ty) rather than B's actual type -- wrong whenever they differ, which C11 requires for pointer atomics specifically ('_Atomic(T*) += n' takes an integer offset n, not a T*). For _Atomic(int*) p; p += 2, this forced the addend into an int* local, so new_add then saw two pointer-typed operands and correctly rejected THAT as invalid pointer+pointer arithmetic -- not a bug in new_add, but bad input from the desugar. Fixed by sizing 'val' from rhs.ty instead. Side effect: this also fixed tests/fixtures/type_qualifiers.c ('_Atomic int' arithmetic), which was independently failing under slate-ozsg.4.8 with the identical 'invalid operands' root cause -- removing it from that ticket's remaining scope (c23_nullptr.c only, now). native-frontend-report: 326/332 (up from 324; atomic_fallbacks.c and type_qualifiers.c both off the failing list, no new failures). cargo fmt/clippy clean.
close_reason: Both root causes fixed (atomic-decay in new_add/new_sub, and correct addend typing in the atomic op= CAS-loop desugar); atomic_fallbacks.c parses, and type_qualifiers.c was fixed as a side effect.

title: Fix _BitInt and oversized-integer literal parsing ('invalid numeric constant')
description: bitint_arith.c and goto_into_later_switch_case_bitint.c both fail with 'invalid numeric constant' — likely _BitInt literal suffixes (wb/uwb) or literal magnitudes that don't fit the lexer's u64-based pp-number-to-integer conversion (Token::convert_pp_int in lexer.rs). May share root cause with slate-ozsg.4's __int128 literal gap (goto_into_later_switch_case_i128.c has the identical error message) — check together.
design: Check lexer.rs's convert_pp_int (around the suffix-parsing block) for _BitInt suffix (wb/uwb) handling, and whether large decimal/hex literals overflow before suffix parsing even runs.
acceptance_criteria: bitint_arith.c and goto_into_later_switch_case_bitint.c parse via 'slate parse-only'.
close_reason: bitint_arith.c, goto_into_later_switch_case_bitint.c, goto_into_later_switch_case_i128.c all now parse. Root cause: wb/uwb-suffixed _BitInt literals weren't recognized at all in convert_pp_int, and their magnitudes (up to 512 bits in the fixture corpus) don't fit u128 anyway so the existing u128::from_str_radix parse would have failed regardless. Rather than truncating into eval2's i64 (which would silently bake a wrong value into the AST), added ExprKind::BigIntLiteral{raw} to ast.rs carrying the literal's exact source text, so a future lowerer can parse it with a real bignum type instead of losing precision now. The literal's Type::BitInt width is computed exactly (not guessed) via a new integer_literal_bit_width() helper in lexer.rs -- a manual divide-by-2 loop over the decimal digit string (repeated division, no bignum crate needed), matching the same rule C23 uses to pick an unwritten _BitInt literal's width. eval2 (the i64-bounded constant-folding evaluator used for e.g. switch-case distinctness) now wraps BigIntLiteral's digits into i64 the same lossy way it already handles every other constant in this evaluator -- consistent with existing precision ceiling, and the exact value stays recoverable from  regardless. Per user direction, did not invest further in eval2's correctness beyond this -- slate translates source-to-source and will likely pass the whole program (macros included) to the lowerer rather than depending on this evaluator being exactly right; noted in project memory (project_chibicc_const_eval_scope).

title: Add __int128 / unsigned __int128 as a representable type
description: ast.rs's Type enum has no 128-bit integer variant at all (BitInt{width,is_signed} is separate/generic-width, not the same as GCC/Clang's __int128). 3 fixtures fail: int128_arith.c ('expected \',\', found identifier \'add128\''), int128_struct.c ('typename expected'), goto_into_later_switch_case_i128.c ('invalid numeric constant', likely an oversized integer literal that only makes sense as __int128).
design: Could plausibly reuse the existing BitInt{width: 128, is_signed} representation instead of adding a new Type variant — worth checking whether BitInt's size()/align() (parser.rs Type::size, capped tiers) already produce correct 16-byte/16-byte-aligned results for width=128 before adding a dedicated variant.
acceptance_criteria: __int128/unsigned __int128 parse as a type in declarations, casts, and struct members; the 3 listed fixtures parse via 'slate parse-only'.
close_reason: int128_arith.c and int128_struct.c now parse. Reused Type::BitInt{width:128,is_signed} rather than adding a new Type variant -- its existing size()/align() already compute 16 bytes/16-byte alignment for width=128, exactly __int128's ABI, so no new match arms were needed anywhere else. __int128 isn't a lexer keyword; taught parse_declspec (and is_typename_token, for cast-expression contexts) to recognize it as an identifier-spelled type specifier that composes with signed/unsigned like _BitInt already did, following that exact precedent. goto_into_later_switch_case_i128.c's remaining failure ('invalid numeric constant' at a case label like 99999999999999999999999999999wb) turned out to be a _BitInt literal-suffix parsing gap, not an __int128 gap -- that's slate-ozsg.4.4's scope, left for that ticket.

title: Support GNU inline asm forms (asm goto, basic/extended asm, register asm operands)
description: 4 fixtures fail parsing GNU inline asm variants: gnu_asm_goto.c ('undefined variable'), gnu_basic_asm.c ('typename expected'), gnu_extended_asm.c ('undefined variable'), inline_asm_ops.c ('undefined variable'). ast.rs already has StmtKind::Asm(String) as a bucket for raw asm text, but these errors suggest the surrounding syntax (asm goto label lists, extended asm operand and clobber lists, or register-variable asm bindings) isn't fully handled by the parser.
design: Investigate each fixture's exact construct before assuming one shared root cause -- 'undefined variable' on 3 different files may be 3 different gaps: asm goto's jump-target label list being parsed as expressions, named asm operand syntax (bracketed name, string constraint, parenthesized variable), or a register-qualified local declaration with an asm register binding.
acceptance_criteria: All 4 fixtures parse via 'slate parse-only'.
close_reason: All 4 fixtures now parse. Root cause was two gaps: (1) __asm__ (GNU double-underscore spelling) wasn't macro-aliased to the asm keyword the way __volatile__/__const__/__inline__ already were in preprocessor.rs init_macros() -- added it. (2) parse_asm_stmt only handled the bare 'asm("...")' form; rewrote it to consume the full extended-asm grammar (optional goto keyword, output/input operand lists with [name] "constraint" (expr), clobber list, goto-label list for asm goto) and added file-scope asm(...) handling to parse_program's top-level loop, which had none at all. Operand expressions are parsed (so identifiers must resolve, catching real errors) but discarded -- ast.rs's StmtKind::Asm(String) has no operand-list slot, consistent with parsing-only scope until a lowerer exists.

title: Remove clang-AST/macro-dumper/CIR code paths, make chibicc the sole frontend
description: The gcc-torture-suite recovery goal (originally scoped here) is a much longer-term effort — roughly 30 tickets to work through the ~500 currently-excluded tests, and it also depends on codegen work that hasn't happened yet. Out of scope for this epic. Instead, once slate-ozsg.4 reaches parity, this issue is: delete the CIR pipeline (src/cir/*, cir-opt invocation, SLATE_CIR_OPT), the clang AST-JSON frontend (src/frontend/c_ast.rs's run_clang_ast_dump path), and the macro-dump-plugin build/invocation (tools/macro-dump-plugin, SLATE_MACRO_DUMP_PLUGIN), leaving the ported chibicc frontend (src/parse) as the only C frontend. Drop the --frontend flag added in slate-ozsg.3 once there's nothing left to select between.
design: Blocked on slate-ozsg.4. This is a deletion-heavy cleanup epic, not new-feature work — the risk is mostly in making sure nothing outside the frontend (docs, CLAUDE.md, CI, env var references) still assumes clang/CIR is required.
acceptance_criteria: src/cir/, the clang-ast-dump code path, and the macro-dump-plugin build/invocation are deleted; SLATE_CLANG/SLATE_CIR_OPT/SLATE_MACRO_DUMP_PLUGIN env vars and CLANG_ENABLE_CIR build requirement are gone from docs and code; slate builds and passes its full test suite using only the chibicc frontend; clang remains only as an optional differential oracle in test infra, not a build or runtime dependency.
close_reason: Superseded: abandoning the ported-chibicc (cc3) parser approach in favor of parsing Clang's own AST JSON directly (https://github.com/dtolnay/clang-ast) as the primary lowering input. See slate-ozsg.8.8's closing note for full rationale. Tracked under the new epic replacing this one.

title: gcc-torture: zero-initializing a record-typed local with bare 0 fails to type-check
description:
zero-struct-2 fails Rust compilation: 'let _v1: raw_spinlock_t = 0;' -- expected raw_spinlock_t (a record type), found integer. Some lowering path is emitting a bare integer literal 0 as the zero-initializer for a record-typed local instead of the record's proper zero-value construction (e.g. a struct literal with all-zero fields, or Default::default(), or an explicit zeroed() call), presumably regressed by the same clang/CIR upgrade as the other buckets under this epic.

Reproduce with SLATE_GCC_TORTURE_FIXTURE=zero-struct-2 cargo nextest r --release --test gcc_torture_suite -E 'test(gcc_torture_supported_tests_match_c)' --nocapture
acceptance_criteria: zero-struct-2 translates, compiles, and matches the C reference's stdout/exit code.
close_reason: Fixed. lower_const's final fallback (src/frontend/lowerer/storage.rs) hardcoded Expr::Value(RustValue::I64(0)) for any unrecognized cir.const value (e.g. #cir.poison for an empty struct, emitted when a call's result is ABI-classified as Ignore/void). For a record-typed result this produced 'let _v1: raw_spinlock_t = 0;', a type error. Fixed by falling back to self.parent.default_value_expr(&rust_ty) when the result type is Type::Custom (a record), reusing the existing zero-value-struct-literal machinery instead of a bare int literal. zero-struct-2 now translates, compiles, and matches C.

title: Lower long double complex libc calls in generated C shims
description: tests/stdlib/complex/functions.c still fails to build because generated long-double complex libc shims use the generic void* trampoline tag ('x'). render_trampoline/c_type_for_tag need a long-double complex bridge (and <complex.h>) so cacosl/casinl/... signatures match C ABI.
close_reason: Added cf80 long-double-complex bridge tag/type in c_shim.rs and runtime_support.rs; generated shims now use __slate_cf80 and complex.h. Also recognized __slate_printf__ shims in printf fallback so C/Rust stdout ordering matches. Verified with stdlib_coverage complex/functions, full lowering, and full rewrites.

title: Replace internal Complex struct with vendored num-complex
description: Replace the custom Complex<T> struct definition generated in the prelude with the standard num-complex crate, vendoring num-complex in vendor/ following the existing pattern used for aligned and bitint. Currently, Slate emits a hand-rolled #[repr(C)] Complex struct along with manual Add/Sub trait implementations in runtime_support.rs. Using num_complex::Complex provides standard complex representation and arithmetic in generated Rust output.
design:
Follow the established vendoring pattern for dependencies like aligned and bitint:
1. Vendor Crate: Place num-complex in vendor/num-complex with minimal configuration (e.g., default-features = false / no_std support).
2. Scaffolding (src/main.rs):
   - Update crate_manifest() to add num-complex = { path = "num-complex" }.
   - Add write_num_complex_support(crate_dir: &Path) to write vendor/num-complex files into <crate_dir>/num-complex/.
   - Call write_num_complex_support in init_crate().
3. Test Harness (tests/support/mod.rs):
   - Add num_complex_path() helper pointing to vendor/num-complex.
   - Include num-complex path dependency in generated_crate_manifest().
4. CIR Lowering & Codegen:
   - Remove hand-rolled Complex struct definition and Add/Sub impls from complex_prelude() in src/frontend/lowerer/runtime_support.rs.
   - Update Type::Complex emission in src/backend/codegen.rs, src/frontend/lowerer/expressions.rs (lower_complex_create, lower_complex_part, lower_complex_part_ptr, lower_complex_mul, lower_complex_div, lower_complex_conj), and src/frontend/lowerer/constants.rs to use num_complex::Complex.
   - Preserve C ABI layout compatibility (num_complex::Complex is #[repr(C)] with re, im).
acceptance_criteria:
1. vendor/num-complex is vendored in the repository.
2. Generated crates and test harnesses build with num-complex dependency.
3. Hand-rolled Complex struct in runtime_support.rs is replaced by num_complex::Complex.
4. All complex fixtures (tests/fixtures/complex.c, tests/fixtures/complex_equality.c, tests/fixtures/complex_lvalue.c, tests/fixtures.chibicc/supported/complex/complex.c, tests/stdlib/complex/functions.c, and gcc-torture complex tests) pass translation and differential tests.
5. Full test suite passes (cargo nextest run).
notes: Vendored num-complex 0.4.6 under vendor/num-complex; wired generated crate and test manifests; replaced hand-rolled Complex type/literals/prelude with num_complex::Complex; added component-wise add/sub lowering and promoted gcc-torture complex-2. Lowering and rewrites profiles pass. tests/stdlib/complex/functions.c still fails in the generated C shim for long-double complex libc calls (void* tag 'x'), tracked separately.
close_reason: Replaced hand-rolled Complex with vendored num-complex 0.4.6, wired generated/test manifests, updated all complex emission/lowering, added long-double-complex shims, and promoted gcc-torture complex-2. Verified with cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets, lowering profile (6/6), and rewrites profile (246/246).

title: Measure Rust-only differential-suite upper bound
description: Temporarily bypass C oracle compilation and execution while retaining C-to-Rust translation plus generated Rust compilation/execution. Run warm full nextest samples on the 12-thread reference machine, record the delta against the 66.32s median, then restore the benchmark-only harness edits.
acceptance_criteria: At least two warm cargo nextest r --release --no-fail-fast Rust-only measurements are recorded on slate-12js; temporary correctness bypass is removed before handoff; git diff confirms only the prior epic implementation remains.
notes: Rust-only temporary full-suite samples (translation + Rust build/run retained; C oracle compile/run skipped): nextest 55.277s warm-up, then 70.919s (71.05s wall) and 71.758s (71.92s wall), versus prior normal median 66.32s. Whole-suite variance exceeded the expected signal. Paired isolated GCC samples also crossed: Rust-only 25.49s vs normal 27.76s, then normal 23.99s vs Rust-only 27.24s. Direct in-process accounting on warmed C caches was stable: gcc 1228 oracles/4152.088ms aggregate/12 workers; generated 328/267.249ms/3; libc functional 37/315.094ms/3; c-testsuite 214/231.844ms/3; stdlib 140/86.452ms/3; chibicc 33/16.117ms/3. Total 1980 oracles and 5068.844ms aggregate, 2.56ms/oracle. Sum of per-suite aggregate/worker estimates is 651.6ms wall if suites are serial; full-suite overlap makes the actual critical-path saving likely smaller. All temporary skip/timing code was removed; rg found no benchmark markers and cargo fmt --check passed.
close_reason: Measured Rust-only full runs and direct C-oracle phase cost; restored benchmark-only changes and verified formatting/clean code state.

title: Apply safe batch caching across differential corpora
description:
## Problem
The primary fixtures, c-testsuite, GCC torture, libc-test, and multi-TU harnesses use related but inconsistent work-directory, cleanup, job, and batch-artifact behavior.

## Work
Apply the safe persistent-workspace and C-oracle caching patterns to every applicable differential corpus. Remove stale generated source entries selectively when fixtures disappear, without deleting valid Cargo state. Document intentional exceptions such as compile-only and cross-target checks.
acceptance_criteria: All applicable differential corpora reuse unchanged Cargo inputs and C oracle binaries; removed fixtures cannot leave runnable stale targets; suite-specific fixture selection remains correct; ignored unsupported guards preserve their existing semantics.
notes: Applied persistent Cargo source trees and timestamp/key-based C binary/object caching across the shared differential harness, including multi-source and linked-object inputs. Batch consumers now accept only compiler-artifact executables reported by the current Cargo invocation, so removed or failed targets cannot fall back to stale files. chibicc uses the same artifact contract. libc-shim compile-only checks use a content-addressed object cache including the shim header tree. Cross-target compile-only probes are intentionally uncached because they are not runnable host C oracles.
close_reason: Closed

title: Handle by-value passing of structs/unions containing a long double member through extern calls
description: .1 fixes size/align computation for structs/unions containing long double, but SysV classification of an aggregate that CONTAINS a long double member (as opposed to a bare long double parameter, which is .4's scope) is a separate concern. A struct with a long double field passed by value to/from an extern function needs correct eightbyte classification (typically MEMORY class once mixed with other fields or once the aggregate exceeds two eightbytes), which is a different code path from both .1 (layout math only) and .4 ("function takes/returns long double directly").

title: Confirm target dispatch stays compile-time (no runtime LongDouble enum)
description: Once F80 lands, LongDouble should keep resolving to exactly one concrete Rust type at lowering time -- f64 passthrough (MSVC/Darwin), F80 (x87 default), or f128 passthrough (Bionic/AArch64 quad) -- the same way is_quad_long_double/uses_f64_long_double_abi already select today (lowerer.rs:2969, types.rs:456-463). A single generated C program only ever targets one ABI, so introducing a tagged Rust enum LongDouble { F64(..), F80(..), F128(..) } in emitted code would be the wrong abstraction: unnecessary runtime tag overhead and a shape that doesn't match any real calling convention. This task is a design-review checkpoint, not new code -- audit the three prior tasks' patches to confirm none of them introduced a runtime enum.
acceptance_criteria: No runtime enum for LongDouble representation exists in generated code or lowerer output; the three concrete types are selected purely at lowering time based on target.
close_reason: Design review confirmed: LongDouble resolves to a single concrete lowering-time type (f64, F80, or f128), with no runtime enum in generated or lowerer output.

title: cir.switch.flat case values truncate/silently drop wide _BitInt magnitudes and use unrepresentable literal patterns
description:
cir.switch.flat is the flattened switch form ClangIR's structurizer falls
back to for irreducible control flow (goto jumping into/across switches or
loops in ways that can't be represented as nested cir.if/cir.switch --
slate re-emits with --cir-flatten-cfg --cir-goto-solver for translation
units that need it, see cir::flatten / emit_generic_with_args_flattened in
src/cir/emit.rs). It has the same two bugs slate-g3kp and slate-ryci just
fixed for the primary cir.switch path, unfixed:

1. Magnitude: lower_switch_flat (src/frontend/lowerer/control_flow.rs:841)
   reads case values via attr_i64_array(op, "caseValues")
   (src/frontend/lowerer/op_utils.rs:57-70), which parses each raw value
   with `parse_cir_int(raw).map(|n| n as i64)`. For a case value whose
   magnitude is between i64::MAX and i128::MAX this silently truncates
   (wraps via `as i64`) instead of erroring or preserving it -- worse than
   the g3kp bug, which only dropped values, never truncated them to a
   different in-range value. For magnitude beyond i128::MAX the value is
   dropped entirely via filter_map, which additionally desyncs the
   `case_values.iter().zip(case_states.iter()).zip(case_args.iter().zip(operand_groups))`
   chain in lower_switch_flat against the surviving successors/operand
   groups (those aren't filtered in step), so a dropped case value doesn't
   just disappear -- it can misalign every case after it in the same switch.

2. Representability: lower_switch_flat (control_flow.rs:~880) builds
   `MatchArm { pattern: int_pattern(*value as i128), .. }` and matches it
   directly against the raw `selector_expr` in a `Stmt::Match`. If the
   selector's Rust type is bitint::BInt/BUint (any _BitInt(N) outside
   {8,16,32,64,128}), this is not valid Rust for the same reason
   slate-ryci fixed in lower_switch: integer literal patterns don't
   typecheck against a custom struct scrutinee. lower_switch_flat never
   received the Pattern::Guarded treatment ryci added to lower_switch/
   lower_duff_switch.

Narrower blast radius than the original bug: cir.switch.flat only fires
for genuinely irreducible goto+switch/goto+loop combinations, not every
switch, so this needs a repro constructed specifically to force
--cir-flatten-cfg (hand-rolled goto+switch fixtures during slate-ryci's
investigation did not trigger it; needs a real cycle clang's structurizer
can't raise, e.g. a goto crossing into the middle of a switch from within
a sibling loop).
design:
Mirror both fixes already landed for cir.switch:

- attr_i64_array's caller here needs a decimal-string-aware sibling (or
  attr_i64_array itself needs to stop being used for caseValues) --
  build a caseValues reader parallel to switch_case's case_value_digits/
  bitint_case_value_pattern (src/frontend/lowerer/cir_ops.rs) that
  produces full-precision Pattern values instead of routing through the
  i64-truncating attr_i64_array. Whatever replaces it must not silently
  drop entries -- either propagate failure per case value (bailing the
  whole cir.switch.flat op like lower_switch now does via emit_todo) or
  otherwise keep case_values, case_states, and operand_groups in sync so a
  parse failure can't desync the zip chain.
- lower_switch_flat needs the same selector-type detection lower_switch
  gained in slate-ryci (op_operand_types(op.ty) + bitint_generic_parts) to
  choose between literal Pattern::I64/I128/U128 arms (primitive selector,
  unchanged) and Pattern::Guarded arms (bitint selector, reusing
  bitint_from_decimal_str_expr) -- Pattern::Guarded already exists in
  rust_ast.rs/codegen.rs from slate-ryci, this is purely a call-site change
  in lower_switch_flat, no new AST surface needed.

Constructing a fixture: needs an actual --cir-flatten-cfg trigger. Try a
goto from inside one loop into the middle of a switch's case body inside a
different loop/scope, or a goto backward across a switch boundary that
Clang's structured-CFG raiser can't represent as nested cir.if/cir.switch.
Confirm with `SLATE_CLANG ... -Xclang -fclangir -Xclang -emit-cir` (or
however slate's own cir::flatten path is invoked) showing cir.switch.flat
in the dump before relying on it in a differential fixture.
acceptance_criteria:
A cir.switch.flat-lowered switch (i.e. one reached via a genuinely
irreducible goto+switch combination) over a _BitInt(N > 128) selector,
with a case value whose decimal literal exceeds u128::MAX, translates to
compiling Rust and matches real GCC/Clang output via a differential
fixture. A case value strictly between i64::MAX and i128::MAX no longer
silently truncates to a wrong in-range i64 value for any switch.flat
switch (primitive or bitint selector). cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason:
Fixed both bugs in cir.switch.flat (the flattened-CFG switch form Clang's
structurizer falls back to for irreducible goto+switch/goto+loop control
flow -- confirmed reachable via tests/fixtures/goto_into_later_switch_case.c
already triggering it, and the exact same goto-into-later-case shape with a
_BitInt(200)/_BitInt(128) selector reproducing both bugs before this fix).

src/frontend/lowerer/cir_ops.rs: factored switch_case's per-value pattern
building into a shared case_values_to_patterns(raw_values, bitint_ty)
helper, and added switch_flat_case_patterns(op, bitint_ty) reading
cir.switch.flat's "caseValues" attr through it -- same layered
parse_cir_int -> parse_cir_uint128 -> bitint_from_decimal_str_expr/
Pattern::Guarded treatment switch_case already had, applied uniformly so
cir.switch and cir.switch.flat can't drift again.

src/frontend/lowerer/control_flow.rs::lower_switch_flat: replaced
attr_i64_array(op, "caseValues") (silently truncated magnitudes between
i64::MAX and i128::MAX via `as i64`, silently dropped anything beyond
i128::MAX and desynced the case_values/case_states/operand_groups zip
chain when it did) with switch_flat_case_patterns, which fails the whole
op to emit_todo on any unparseable value instead of desyncing case
alignment. Also added the same selector-type detection (op_operand_types +
bitint_generic_parts) lower_switch already had, so int_pattern(*value as
i128) literal arms (broken for a bitint::BInt/BUint selector) become
Pattern::Guarded arms when the selector is bitint-typed.

Verified against real clang: hand-built two repros forcing
--cir-flatten-cfg (goto jumping into a later switch's case label, mirroring
the existing goto_into_later_switch_case.c fixture) -- one with a
_BitInt(200) selector and a 45-digit case value, one with a _BitInt(128)
(native i128) selector and a case value between i64::MAX and i128::MAX.
Both compiled and ran identically to clang-compiled C before landing as
tests/fixtures/goto_into_later_switch_case_bitint.c and
tests/fixtures/goto_into_later_switch_case_i128.c respectively.

cargo nextest r --release passes (236/236), clippy clean.

title: switch/match dispatch on a bitint::BInt/BUint selector needs guard-based patterns, not literal ones
description:
_BitInt(N) outside {8,16,32,64,128} lowers to the vendored bitint::BInt/
BUint struct (types.rs::bitint_type), not a native Rust integer. Every
switch dispatch path that touches such a selector emits Rust `match`
arms with literal integer patterns (Pattern::I64/I128/U128/
InclusiveRange) matched directly against the raw selector value -- which
does not typecheck against a custom struct scrutinee at all. Verified by
hand-translating:

    int f(_BitInt(200) x) {
      switch (x) { case 5: return 1; default: return 0; }
    }

which currently produces `match *x { 5 => { return 1; } _ => { return 0; } }`
with `*x: bitint::BInt<200, 4>` -- not valid Rust, regardless of whether
the case value's magnitude parses correctly (see slate-g3kp, a
prerequisite for the magnitude side of this bug).

Two lowering paths both build these unrepresentable literal-pattern
matches and both need to change:

- lower_switch (src/frontend/lowerer/control_flow.rs, the baseline/
  original lowering, *not* a fixup) builds a two-stage dispatch: a first
  `match __switch_value0 { <case patterns> => <index>, _ => fallback }`
  to compute an i32 case index, then a second `match __switch_case0 { ... }`
  inside a `'label: loop` to run the matched body (supporting fallthrough
  via continue). Stage one already matches literal patterns directly
  against the raw (possibly bitint-typed) selector value, so the baseline
  form is *not* automatically safe just by virtue of being the loop form
  -- it has the same representability problem in miniature.
- src/backend/query/switch.rs is a query-driven fixup (see docs/fixups.md)
  that recognizes lower_switch's two-stage loop output when every case is
  fallthrough-free and single-pattern (is_eligible), and collapses it into
  one flat `match selector { <original case pattern> => body, ... }`,
  reusing the same literal Pattern values against the raw selector
  (case_pattern/build_match). This is the path that produced the `match
  *x { 5 => ... }` example above, but the root cause (literal patterns
  against a non-primitive scrutinee) is not specific to this fixup --
  fixing it there alone would leave stage one of the baseline lowering
  broken for any switch this fixup declines to collapse (fallthrough
  cases, multi-pattern cases).
design:
Fix representability at the source (lower_switch), not by special-casing
around it downstream: the collapsing fixup should stay type-agnostic and
correct automatically once stage one of the baseline lowering emits valid
Rust for every selector type, since it just copies whatever pattern
lower_switch already produced.

Recommended shape: teach Pattern/ExprMatchArm/MatchArm (src/backend/
rust_ast.rs) an optional match guard (`Pattern::Wildcard` bound to a name
plus `guard: Option<Expr>`, or a new `Pattern::Guarded` variant) so a case
label can compile down to `v if v == BUint::<N, M>::from_decimal_str("...")
=> body` instead of a bare literal pattern. This keeps the dispatch inside
an actual `Stmt::Match`/`Expr::Match` (minimal disruption to codegen.rs,
idents.rs, and the various backend/facts/*.rs passes that already walk
Pattern), and generalizes cleanly to InclusiveRange-style case ranges
(`v if v >= lo && v <= hi`) since bitint::BInt/BUint already implement
Ord. lower_switch picks literal Pattern::I64/I128/U128 for primitive
selectors (unchanged, keeps jump-table-friendly codegen) and guard-based
patterns only when the selector's Rust type is a bitint Generic
(bitint_generic_parts / is_cir_int_type-style check).

This is the switch instance of a wider gap: bitint::BInt/BUint needs to
be usable in every context a native C integer type is usable in the
generated Rust (comparisons -- already covered by PartialOrd/Ord --
dispatch, casts, printf-style formatting, atomics if ever reachable),
since _BitInt(N) is a first-class C integer type. Treat that as the
framing for this bead's scope: fix switch dispatch now, but implement it
in a way (guard-based Pattern, not a switch-only special case) that the
next context needing this doesn't reinvent the mechanism.

Depends on slate-g3kp for full-precision case values feeding the guard
comparison's from_decimal_str argument.
acceptance_criteria:
A switch over a _BitInt(N > 128) selector (signed and unsigned) with case
values inside and outside i128 range compiles and matches real GCC/Clang
output via a differential fixture (extend tests/fixtures/bitint_arith.c
or add a new fixture covering fallthrough and multi-value cases too, not
just the trivial single-return case). Existing switches over primitive
selectors keep their current match-based codegen unchanged (no regression
in the query/switch.rs collapsing fixup's applicability or the codegen it
produces for non-bitint switches). cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason:
Implemented guard-based match dispatch for bitint::BInt/BUint switch selectors,
per the design: added Pattern::Guarded { bind: Ident, cond: Box<Expr> } to
src/backend/rust_ast.rs, printed as `bind if cond` by codegen.rs's pattern()
-- no changes needed to the match-arm printers themselves (Stmt::Match/
Expr::Match), since they already just print `{pattern} => {body}` and a
guarded pattern is valid syntax in that exact position.

lower_switch/lower_duff_switch (control_flow.rs) now read the switch op's
own operand type signature (op.ty via op_operand_types, the same way
storage.rs/builtins.rs already recover operand types) to detect a
bitint-typed selector via bitint_generic_parts, and thread that through to
switch_case/duff_switch (cir_ops.rs). When present, case values build
`v if v == BInt::<N,M>::from_decimal_str("...") => idx` arms instead of
literal Pattern::I64/I128/U128, and case ranges build
`v if v >= lo && v <= hi => idx` -- both reusing bitint_from_decimal_str_expr
from the slate-58wk/slate-g3kp work, so full-precision case values (including
the ones slate-g3kp stopped dropping) now actually reach working codegen.

The collapsing fixup (src/backend/query/switch.rs) needed no changes: its
existing arm-classification match has a `_ => return None` catch-all, so a
Pattern::Guarded case naturally makes it decline to collapse, leaving the
switch in the baseline two-stage loop form -- which is exactly representable
Rust. Primitive/enum selectors are completely unaffected (bitint_ty is None,
same literal-pattern codegen as before).

Verified by hand-compiling and running a standalone crate (case value >u128,
multi-pattern case, case range, true fallthrough via continue, negative wide
literal) against real clang output -- identical stdout and exit code. Then
