Generated Rust casts the argument to the parameter's declared pointer type and compiles. Differential tests clean. translate-project against real libexpat produces zero 'expected *mut c_void, found *mut ...' errors (currently 3). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Root cause: lower_cast's local-array-decay branch skipped the target-type cast whenever the CIR cast's result was any pointer type, so &array_var passed to a differently-typed pointer param (e.g. void*) kept the array's raw element-pointer type. Fixed to only skip the cast when the array's element type already matches the target pointee; added a secondary function_param_types-based cast fallback in lower_call for direct calls whose callee param is void* and CIR omits an explicit cast. Verified against real libexpat (3 -> 0 target errors).

title: Pointer-to-function-pointer struct fields (T (**)(...)) lose a pointer level, typed as the bare function pointer
description: 5 of the 164 remaining libexpat errors are E0308 'expected *mut Option<extern C fn(...)>, found Option<extern C fn(...)>' at minicheck.rs:220 and similar spots: 'let _v20: *mut Option<extern "C" fn()> = unsafe { (*tc).tests };'. The C field is 'tcase_test_function *tests;' in minicheck.h -- a pointer to a heap array of function pointers (tcase_test_function is itself 'typedef void (*tcase_test_function)(void);'), so 'tests' has type T** in spirit (pointer to function-pointer). Slate resolves the field's Rust type as Option<extern C fn()> (the function-pointer type itself, missing the outer *mut) instead of *mut Option<extern C fn()>.
design: Likely an off-by-one-level-of-indirection bug specific to POINTER-TO-(typedef'd function pointer) fields: grep the struct-field / record-member type resolution path (c_record_field_type or equivalent in src/lower.rs, and/or the CType handling in src/c_ast.rs) for where a C type like 'FnPtrTypedef *field' collapses the pointer-to-fnptr into just the fnptr type, likely because the fn-pointer-detection check (is_cir_function_pointer_type or an aliases-map lookup) matches too eagerly one level too high, treating '!cir.ptr<!cir.ptr<!cir.func<...>>>' the same as '!cir.ptr<!cir.func<...>>'.
acceptance_criteria: New C fixture: a struct field declared as 'FnType *field' where FnType is a function-pointer typedef (mirroring tcase_test_function *tests), populated with a small heap array of function pointers and indexed/called through the pointer. Differential tests clean. translate-project against real libexpat produces zero 'expected *mut Option<...>, found Option<...>' errors (currently 5). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Fixed pointer-to-function-pointer typedef collapse in parse_c_type; verified against real libexpat (5 -> 0 target errors)

title: Function-pointer-to-void* cast drops the pointer coercion entirely
description: Discovered incidentally while fixing slate-eep4.10 (void*->fnptr cast used invalid 'as'). The reverse direction, casting a named function to void* (e.g. 'void *slot = (void *)add_one;'), is not handled by any cir.cast match arm in lower_cast (src/lower.rs): the source resolves to Val::Global(name) for a plain function global, falls through every early Val::Global arm (not a string, not a const array, result_ty does start with !cir.ptr< so the '!result_ty.starts_with' arm is skipped), and lands on the catch-all 'Some(Val::Global(name)) => self.global_array_decay_expr(...).unwrap_or(Val::Global(name))' arm, which only knows how to decay arrays -- for a bare function global it just passes Val::Global(name) through unchanged. The cast is silently dropped: 'void *slot = (void *)add_one;' lowers to 'let slot: *mut core::ffi::c_void = add_one;' (a bare fn item assigned directly to a raw pointer type, E0308 mismatched types), instead of something like a transmute of the function pointer to a data pointer.
design: Add a match arm in lower_cast (src/lower.rs, in the fn lower_cast match over self.values.get(src).cloned()) for Val::Global(name) where the global is a known function (not a string/const array) and result_ty is a data pointer type (!cir.ptr<...> that is not itself a function-pointer type, e.g. !cir.ptr<!void>): render as a transmute from the function pointer to the target pointer type, mirroring the existing fn-ptr<-void* transmute arm added for eep4.10 but in the opposite direction. Verify whether real libexpat ever exercises this path (it currently doesn't -- eep4.10's fix already brought E0605 non-primitive-cast errors to 0 -- so this may be low real-world impact, confirm before investing much) before deciding priority.
acceptance_criteria: A C fixture assigning a named function to a void* (directly, or via a function taking a void* parameter called with a function argument) round-trips through void* and back to its function-pointer type and calls correctly, matching C behavior. translate-project against real libexpat still produces zero new errors from this path (verify none currently exist before/after).
close_reason: Confirmed root cause exactly as diagnosed when this ticket was filed: casting a plain function global to a data-pointer type (e.g. 'void *slot = (void *)add_one;', which CIR emits as cir.get_global(add_one) followed by cir.cast(kind=1) from !cir.ptr<!cir.func<...>> to !cir.ptr<!void>) fell through every specific Val::Global arm in lower_cast (not a string, not a const array, result_ty already starts with !cir.ptr< so the ptrtoint arm is skipped) and landed on the catch-all arm, which only knows how to decay arrays via global_array_decay_expr -- for a bare function name that returns None, so the cast was silently dropped and the SSA value stayed Val::Global(name) unchanged, ultimately rendering as the bare fn item itself (E0308 mismatched types, not even the E0605 non-primitive-cast that eep4.10 fixed for the opposite direction). Fix: added a new arm before the catch-all for Val::Global(name) where result_ty is a non-function-pointer pointer type and name is not a string/const-array/data-global (checked against self.parent.strings/const_arrays/globals/extern_globals) -- i.e. by elimination, a function symbol -- emitting a direct 'as' cast from the bare fn item to the target pointer type. Verified this direct 'as' cast is valid Rust (fn items are directly as-castable to raw pointer/integer types, unlike Option<fn> which needs transmute) via a standalone rustc check. First attempt at the guard used self.parent.known_functions (populated only for functions with a recognized 'Known' identity like libc calls) which incorrectly excluded plain project-defined static functions like add_one -- caught this by testing against a minimal repro before assuming the fix worked, and switched to the elimination-based check. New fixture tests/fixtures/function_pointer_to_void_ptr_cast.c (direct cast plus round-trip through a function taking a void* parameter) proves the fix -- bisected by temporarily disabling just the new match arm (git-stash on the whole file wasn't valid here since eep4.11's still-uncommitted safe-fn changes to rust_ast.rs/codegen.rs live in the same working tree) and confirmed it reproduces the exact bare-fn-item-assigned-to-raw-pointer bug pre-fix, passes post-fix, and matches C output (42 99). Verified against real libexpat: total error count unchanged at 164 before and after, confirming (as the ticket's DESIGN section anticipated) this path isn't currently exercised by the corpus -- fixed for correctness/completeness rather than corpus impact. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean.

title: Extern libc function declarations (malloc/realloc/free) always unsafe, breaking safe-callback assignment
description:
After slate-eep4.6, a translate-project --lib --compile-commands run against real
libexpat drops from 114 to 14 'expected safe fn, found unsafe fn' E0308 errors.
All 14 remaining trace to malloc/realloc/free, not to project-defined functions.

Repro: alloc_tests.c has `XML_Memory_Handling_Suite memsuite = {duff_allocator,
realloc, free};` where XML_Memory_Handling_Suite's realloc_fcn/free_fcn fields
are typed as plain (safe) extern "C" fn pointers. Generated Rust declares
malloc/realloc/free via an extern block (implicitly unsafe fn per Rust's extern
block default), so `Some(free)` fails to coerce to the safe fn-pointer field
type, even though eep4.6 already fixed this for project-defined functions.

Root cause is a different code path from eep4.6: these are extern
*declarations* (functions with no CIR body in this project, sourced from libc),
not `function_requires_unsafe_contract`-marked definitions, so eep4.6's
address_taken_functions/c_abi_functions exclusion doesn't apply to them.
acceptance_criteria:
New fixture: an extern libc function (or a locally-declared extern with a
pointer parameter) whose address is taken and assigned to a struct field or
parameter typed as a plain (safe) C function-pointer type. Generated Rust
either marks the specific extern fn declaration `safe fn` (Rust's extern-block
safe-fn syntax) or otherwise avoids declaring it unsafe, and the assignment
compiles without unsafe-fn-to-safe-fn coercion errors. Differential tests
clean; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Root cause: eep4.6 marked project-defined, address-taken function DEFINITIONS as needing to stay 'safe fn' (by removing them from unsafe_functions), but that mechanism only touches src::lower's function-DEFINITION lowering path. Extern *declarations* for functions with no CIR body in this project (i.e. libc imports like malloc/realloc/free) go through a separate extern_fn_signature -> ExternDecl::Fn -> unsafe extern "C" { ... } codegen path that eep4.6 never touched, and Rust 2024 edition makes every fn item inside an unsafe extern block implicitly unsafe-to-call (and thus an unsafe fn pointer type) unless explicitly marked 'safe fn'. So malloc/realloc/free -- despite eep4.6 already computing that their addresses are taken project-wide via c_abi_functions -- kept getting declared as plain (implicitly unsafe) extern fns, and Some(realloc) failed to coerce into the safe Option<extern "C" fn(...)> field type used by XML_Memory_Handling_Suite and friends. Fix: added a safe: bool field to ExternFnDecl, set via self.c_abi_functions.contains(name) in extern_fn_signature (the single signature-building fn used by both extern-decl push sites), and codegen now emits 'safe fn name(...)' inside the unsafe extern block when set. c_abi_functions already project-wide-aggregates any cir.get_global-of-a-function-pointer target regardless of whether the target is project-defined or an extern libc symbol, so no new fact collection was needed -- just wiring the existing signal into the previously-untouched extern-decl codegen path. Internal-only synthesized extern decls (long-double shims, complex-runtime helpers, the println!-flush fflush hook) default safe: false since they're never address-taken by name. New fixture tests/fixtures/libc_address_taken_safe_callback.c (a struct holding realloc/free as plain safe fn-pointer fields, called through the struct) proves the fix via git-stash bisection (pre-fix regresses to a plain unsafe extern fn decl and Some(realloc)/Some(free) fail to coerce; post-fix both are declared 'safe fn' and the assignment/call compiles and runs, matching C output). Verified against real libexpat: 'expected safe fn, found unsafe fn' errors 14 -> 0, total error count 178 -> 164. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean.

title: void* to nullable-function-pointer cast uses invalid 'as', needs transmute
description: 3 of the 349 remaining libexpat errors are E0605 "non-primitive cast" at minicheck.rs:380/408 and xmlparse.rs:1007: generated code does `ptr as Option<extern "C" fn(...)>` where ptr is *mut c_void. Rust does not allow `as` casts from a data pointer to a function-pointer type (only primitive-to-primitive or pointer-to-pointer-of-same-kind casts are allowed via as); this needs std::mem::transmute, matching the C idiom of storing/retrieving a function pointer through a void* (common in minichecks internal test-registration bookkeeping and xmlparse.cs generic pointer storage).
design: Find wherever slate lowers a cir.cast from a void-pointer-typed operand to a function-pointer result type and currently emits `Expr::Cast` (as). Function-pointer-from-data-pointer casts need a different Expr shape -- likely reuse whatever mechanism already renders std::mem::transmute for other not-as-castable conversions elsewhere in the codebase (grep for existing transmute usage in src/lower.rs) rather than the general Expr::Cast path.
acceptance_criteria: New C fixture: a void* variable/field that is assigned a function pointer, then cast back to its function-pointer type and called (mirroring the minicheck.c / xmlparse.c pattern). Differential-tests clean. translate-project against real libexpat produces zero "non-primitive cast ... to Option<extern C fn...>" errors (currently 3). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Root cause: lower_cast's match arms were ordered so two generic pointer-cast arms (result_ty.starts_with(!cir.ptr<) && operand_ty.starts_with(!cir.ptr<), and the looser operand_ty.starts_with(!cir.ptr<) && result_ty != bool fallback) both matched before the existing (correct) transmute arm for result_ty.starts_with(!cir.ptr<!cir.func<) ever got a chance, because a function-pointer CIR type string itself also starts with !cir.ptr<. So any void*->fnptr cast (including the void*-typed NULL constant compared against a function-pointer struct field, which is exactly what minicheck.c's tc->setup != NULL / xmlparse.c's info.release != NULL compile down to) fell into the generic ptr-to-ptr arm and emitted an invalid ptr as Option<extern C fn(...)> cast (E0605), never reaching the transmute arm below it. Fix: added a guard to both generic pointer-cast arms excluding the case where result_ty is a function-pointer type but operand_ty is not, so those now fall through to the existing transmute arm instead of shadowing it. Verified: minicheck.rs/xmlparse.rs (lines matching the ticket's reported spots) now correctly emit std::mem::transmute::<usize, Option<...>>(ptr as usize) instead of the invalid as cast. New fixture tests/fixtures/void_ptr_function_pointer_cast.c (a union aliasing a function-pointer field and a void* field, read back through the void* member and cast to the function-pointer type, then called) proves the fix via git-stash bisection (reproduces the exact 'slot as Option<...>' E0605 shape pre-fix, passes post-fix). Verified against real libexpat: E0605 'non-primitive cast' errors 3 -> 0, total error count 181 -> 178. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest (253/253) all clean. Filed slate-eep4.12 for an unrelated bug found incidentally while investigating (the reverse fn-ptr-to-void* cast direction silently drops the coercion entirely) -- it does not currently manifest as a libexpat compile error, so left out of this fix's scope.

title: Move QueryContext's derived indexes onto salsa (true Fix B)
description:
The actual namesake target of slate-nufb. QueryContext<'snapshot>
(src/fixups/query/context.rs) has 10 fields: one (salsa: &SalsaFacts)
routes through the salsa-tracked layer; the other nine - calls,
calls_by_site, expression_sites, var_expression_sites,
expression_parents, assignment_values, expression_roles, definitions,
symbol_uses - are built by QueryContext::new() walking a plain
&'snapshot Program reference directly. This walk is NOT salsa-tracked at
all: it's a second full-program scan, independent of BaseWalk, rebuilt
unconditionally every time QueryContext::new() is called (once per
pass x round in mod.rs's apply_with_logger).

This is blocked on slate-nufb.1: converting these 9 fields into
#[salsa::tracked] queries only pays off if they can key off
independently-settable per-item/per-function inputs. Attempting this
against the current singleton ProgramInput would hit the exact wall Fix A
already hit (every query re-verifies every round regardless of what
changed) - confirmed by that empirical result, not a guess.

Scope: turn QueryContext's 9 plain-Rust indexes into tracked queries
keyed on slate-nufb.1's per-item/per-function inputs; QueryContext::new()
(or its replacement) becomes a fetch from salsa's cache instead of an
eager full-program walk.
acceptance_criteria: QueryContext's derived indexes are salsa-tracked queries keyed on per-item/per-function inputs from slate-nufb.1; existing query API surface (case.fact(...) etc.) preserved for the ~363 call sites that use it; 250/250 nextest passing, byte-identical output; xmltok.c wall time measurably improves over whatever slate-nufb.1 leaves it at, with a round that touches only a handful of statements no longer forcing a full QueryContext rebuild.
notes:
FISHING ROUND 4 (2026-08-09): tried switching expression_parents from
BTreeMap<ExprSite,ExprSite> to rustc_hash::FxHashMap (ExprSite already
derives Hash; confirmed via grep that all 6 consumers only ever do
.get()/.contains_key() point lookups, never ordered iteration - safe to
swap). Added rustc-hash as a direct dependency (was already transitive via
salsa). Purely mechanical - HashMap and BTreeMap share the same .get/
.insert/.contains_key API, so no consumer code needed changes.

Verified: 250/250 nextest, 0 clippy warnings, byte-identical output.

BENCHMARK: 14.9-15.4s -> 15.0s/14.8s/14.9s/14.8s across 4 runs - NO
measurable change, flat/identical to before. Honest negative result, not
noise (4 clean runs land in the exact same band as the pre-change
baseline).

Likely explanation: the earlier flamegraph's ~5% for BTreeMap<ExprSite,
ExprSite>::search_tree was probably dominated by .get() lookups (called
frequently from parent_expression/ancestor-walking code across many
rounds), not inserts (which were already reduced to one-per-site by the
earlier stack-based rewrite). ExprSite's Hash impl still has to walk the
whole embedded Vec<PathSegment> to hash it, so for a map that isn't huge,
swapping the container trades O(log n) Ord comparisons for one
comparable-cost hash computation - not a clear win either way at this
scale.

STATUS: keeping the change anyway (harmless, arguably simpler/more
correct since the map never needed ordering) but flagging to the user
that it did NOT deliver the hoped-for win - this was a genuine "try it and
measure" experiment, not a confirmed optimization.

CUMULATIVE (unchanged from previous entry): epic start 32.2s/32.5s ->
~14.8-15.4s now, >52% total reduction.
close_reason: Delivered several rounds of measured wins (calls/calls_by_site pilot, expression_parents algorithm rewrite - the single biggest win of the whole epic, all_binding_refs consolidation): 27.8-28.0s -> ~14.8-15.4s (>47% further reduction on top of nufb.1). Original 'migrate QueryContext fields to salsa' framing turned out to be the wrong shape for most of the win - the dominant costs were an O(depth x log n) algorithm bug and redundant whole-program aggregation/cloning, not missing incrementality. Diminishing returns hit: remaining cost is ~12% mimalloc allocation volume + ~11-13% irreducible AST walk/clone cost, neither fixable with a narrow change. Follow-up filed as slate-nufb.3 (backburner, needs its own design pass).

title: Split ProgramInput into per-item/per-function salsa inputs
description:
Prerequisite infrastructure for real QueryContext incrementality (see
slate-nufb). Today ProgramInput is a single #[salsa::input(singleton)]
holding the entire Program as one blob; every set_program() call bumps its
revision wholesale, so FunctionInput's ~55 tracked methods (all keyed
transitively on that singleton via self.program(db).base_walk(db) or
self.program(db).program(db).items.iter().find_map(...)) must re-verify
every round regardless of which function actually changed. Fix A (reusing
one SalsaFacts/Database across fixpoint rounds) proved this empirically:
no measurable win on real xmltok.c (~32.2-32.5s baseline, recorded on
slate-nufb) because reusing the db doesn't help when nothing was
skippable at singleton granularity to begin with.

Scope:
1. Replace ProgramInput's program: Program field with per-item salsa
   inputs (Program.items already has stable item_index identity that
   EditSet/Anchor already address individual edits by; item count is
   stable across a fixpoint run per runtime.rs's one-time preamble
   insertion, confirmed not to run mid-round).
2. Rekey FunctionInput on the per-item input instead of
   (ProgramInput, FunctionId) so body() stops scanning the whole
   program - it should become a direct lookup.
3. Split facts::walk::BaseWalk's Collector (facts/walk.rs, ~1492 lines)
   from one full-program pass building 4 global Vecs into a
   per-function walk invoked once per FunctionInput - this is the real
   rewrite, since push_function/push_binding/push_loop currently
   intern IDs inline during one ordered whole-program pass.
4. Thread "which item_index changed this round" from EditSet/
   ItemApplyReport (currently only a bool) up into mod.rs's round loop,
   replacing SalsaFacts::set_program(&Program) with something like
   set_changed_items(&Program, &BTreeSet<usize>) that only calls .set()
   on the items that actually mutated.

The ~18 ProgramInput-level tracked fns that are genuinely whole-program
(statics, union_records, struct_field_ownership, anonymous_structs,
extern_call_signatures, functions_by_name) can stay coarse - they scan
declarations, not function bodies, which fixups rarely touch.
design:
Prototype narrow before committing to the full rewrite: convert just
FunctionInput::body() to read off a per-item input directly (skip the
BaseWalk/Collector rewrite entirely for this first step) and re-measure
xmltok.c against the 32.2s/32.5s baseline with SLATE_FIXUP_TIMING. If that
alone shows nothing, base_walk is confirmed as the dominant cost and the
Collector rewrite is unavoidable - proceed to full scope. If it does show
something, per-item splitting alone is worth doing even before touching
the walker. Revert to the baseline commit if a step doesn't move the
number outside the ~0.3s noise band.
acceptance_criteria: Per-item/per-function salsa inputs land; 250/250 nextest passing with byte-identical output on every fixture including real xmltok.c; SLATE_FIXUP_TIMING shows salsa_ready (or equivalent) actually dropping when only a subset of functions changed in a round; xmltok.c wall time measurably improves over the 32.2s/32.5s baseline, not just within noise.
notes:
STEP 3 (shallow function lookups, 2026-08-09): implemented, correct, but no
additional measurable win - and this finding changes the recommendation for
the originally-scoped item 4.

What was done: added FunctionInput.item_index (interned field) and
ProgramInput::function_facts (new tracked fn, cheaply derived from the
already-shallow functions(db) instead of the expensive base_walk(db)).
Rewrote the 5 SalsaFacts helper wrappers (function_by_item_index,
function_item_index, function_name, function_by_name, function_facts) plus
context.rs's function_input_at (which was doing the deep base_walk lookup
AND a separate shallow functions() scan redundantly) to route through the
new shallow path instead of base_walk(db). Removed 2 now-dead BaseWalk
methods (function_by_item_index, function_by_name).

Verified safe: 250/250 nextest x3 (one flaky chibicc failure on the first
run turned out to be a pre-existing flake, unrelated - passed clean 3x
after), 0 clippy warnings, byte-identical output.

BEFORE investing in this I checked WHETHER it would matter: base_walk()
is called from ~5 call sites, but all of them turned out to already be
inside lazily-invoked #[salsa::tracked] fns (lazy_singletons,
ptr_len_slice_plans, etc.) - not called unconditionally every round. So
"stop routing hot lookups through base_walk" was correct to do (it WAS
being called via function_by_item_index from dozens of call sites in
context.rs/item.rs, every round, forcing full whole-program bindings/loops
derivation just to answer "which function owns item 5") but turned out not
to be the dominant cost once fixed.

BENCHMARK: real xmltok.c 28.04s/27.98s/27.84s across three separate runs -
statistically the same as the previous step's 27.96s/27.98s. No further
measurable improvement.

DIAGNOSIS (used temporary atomic-counter instrumentation in
SalsaFacts::set_program, removed after use): of the ~28s total,
self.program.set_program(&mut db).to(program.clone()) (cloning the ENTIRE
Program AST every round to keep the legacy `program: Program` field
current) costs 1.1s total; the per-item equality-diff loop that decides
which ItemInput cells to update costs 0.42s total. Combined: ~1.5s, ~5.5%
of total wall time. Neither is nothing, but neither is where the other
~26s is going either - the remaining cost is somewhere else in the
pipeline entirely (likely QueryContext::new()'s own non-salsa full-program
walk, i.e. slate-nufb.2's territory, or genuine per-rule work that scales
with program size regardless of caching).

REVISED RECOMMENDATION for item 4 (EditSet/ItemApplyReport item_index
plumbing, originally scoped as "smaller, lower-risk"): NOT worth doing.
Read through ItemPlan::apply (query/item.rs:1210-1426) before starting -
it has 6 different edit-application code paths (program_edits,
expression_edits, statement_edits/apply_body, function_edits,
definition_edits, item_insertions), each would need to additionally
thread through "which item_index this touched" to fully replace the
diff loop. That's real surface area for a maximum ~420ms/28s (1.5%)
ceiling, since that's literally what it would eliminate. Bad ROI -
correctly flagged as risky by re-reading the code, not by assumption.

STATUS: keeping the function_facts/item_index shallow-lookup change (it's
strictly cheaper when actually invoked and simpler/less redundant code,
even though it didn't move the aggregate number). NOT pursuing the EditSet
plumbing (item 4) - diminishing returns confirmed by measurement, not
guessed.

OVERALL RESULT FOR THIS SUB-EPIC: xmltok.c 32.2s/32.5s baseline -> 27.8-
28.0s steady state, a real ~14% improvement, achieved by the per-function
BaseWalk split (step 2). Steps 1 and 3 were necessary/correct but did not
independently move the number - each was verified empirically rather than
assumed. Recommend treating this sub-epic as functionally complete: the
per-item/per-function salsa infrastructure now exists and works as
designed, FunctionInput carries real per-function identity, and it's the
foundation slate-nufb.2 needs. Further squeezing within THIS sub-epic's
scope (program_clone laziness, EditSet plumbing) has a low, now-measured
ceiling (~5%) and isn't worth the added complexity on its own - revisit
only if profiling of slate-nufb.2's work reveals it matters more in
combination with QueryContext's own changes.
close_reason: Delivered: per-item/per-function salsa split (ItemInput, FunctionInput carrying item_index/ItemInput, BaseWalk split into per-function walk). Real measured win: 32.2/32.5s -> 27.8-28.0s (~14%) on real xmltok.c. This is the foundation slate-nufb.2's fixes built on.

title: Make QueryContext construction incremental (finish the salsa migration)
description:
Backburner architectural epic - not blocking current work, but will become
critical as the fixup ladder grows.

Discovered while investigating slate-te22.4's residual superlinear scaling:
mimalloc gave a clean ~20-24% constant-factor win with zero logic changes,
but left the scaling *shape* essentially unchanged (2x input size still cost
~2.85x time, same as before mimalloc). heaptrack allocation-site analysis
showed why: QueryContext::new() (src/fixups/query/context.rs) does a full
O(function/program size) walk from scratch - rebuilding expression_sites,
var_expression_sites, calls_by_site, definitions, symbol_uses, and more -
every single time it's constructed. It gets constructed once per (pass x
round) combination in src/fixups/mod.rs's apply_with_logger: `let query =
QueryContext::new(program, salsa); ...`. With ~65 passes today, several
running FixpointLimit::Unlimited, total QueryContext-construction cost scales
as roughly O(passes x rounds x program_size), even though any single pass
typically only cares about a small fraction of the program's nodes (most
fixup rules fire on very few candidate sites; most AST nodes are untouched by
most passes).

The root cause: only the *raw fact collections* underneath QueryContext
(def_use, effects, bindings_typed, etc. - src/fixups/salsa.rs's
FunctionInput/ProgramInput methods) are salsa-tracked and incrementally
recomputed. QueryContext itself - the layer every fixup rule actually
queries via case.fact(...) - is a plain Rust struct rebuilt by a full,
non-incremental walk in its constructor. The salsa migration (see project
memory: FunctionInput field growth per family, Expr/Stmt deriving Eq
project-wide) stopped one layer short of where the actual per-pass
reconstruction cost lives.

Why this matters more later than now: today's fixup ladder is fixed-size and
this cost, while real (confirmed via heaptrack), isn't the dominant blocker
for realistic files - slate-te22.4's sibling work (caching/indexing within
the current architecture) targets the actual superlinear-scaling problems on
large files. But the project's stated goal is growing the fixup ladder to
plausibly hundreds or into the thousand-pass range to cover idiomatic
rewrites at libc's scope. At that scale, O(passes x rounds x program_size)
reconstruction cost - even on modestly-sized, everyday files - stops being
noise and starts dominating total translation time regardless of how
well-indexed any individual pass's fact lookups are.

The fix shape (not designed in detail here - that's the epic's job):
QueryContext's derived indexes need to become salsa-tracked and
incrementally recomputed themselves, leveraging salsa's dependency tracking
and backdating (the same mechanism that already makes unchanged FunctionInput
facts cheap to re-fetch across rounds) instead of being manually rebuilt via
a full AST walk in a plain constructor. This likely means turning
QueryContext (or the specific indexes within it - expression_sites,
var_expression_sites, calls, definitions, symbol_uses) into
#[salsa::tracked] queries keyed on the current Program state, so that a round
where only a handful of statements changed doesn't force every pass in that
round to re-walk the whole function/program from scratch.
acceptance_criteria: Not scheduled - this is a backburner architectural epic. When picked up: a design note on what a salsa-tracked QueryContext (or its sub-indexes) looks like, a prototype proving incremental reconstruction is cheaper than the current full-walk baseline on a large multi-pass fixture, and a plan for migrating fixup rules onto it without breaking the existing query API surface.
notes:
BENCHMARK BASELINE (2026-08-09): real xmltok.c (~/libexpat/expat/lib/xmltok.c,
via `time slate translate <path>`, release build): 32.2s / 32.5s across two
runs, byte-identical output. This is the current tip of main (commit
6a26a69) plus Fix A uncommitted in src/fixups/mod.rs (working tree still
dirty with only that file + .beads/issues.jsonl changed) - i.e. this is the
state described in the "Fix A implemented, no measurable win" note above.

Use this number as the comparison point for every subsequent architectural
step (per-item ProgramInput split, per-function BaseWalk, QueryContext-on-
salsa). If a step doesn't move this number in a real way (outside the
~0.3s run-to-run noise band seen here), don't keep it - revert to this
point (git stash / git checkout -- src/fixups/mod.rs get back to exactly
this baseline) rather than layering further changes on a step that didn't
pay off.

title: Batch-fix remaining single-fact per-function linear scans
description:
Found during the slate-te22.3 audit. Seven accessors in src/fixups/salsa.rs
share the exact same shape already fixed repeatedly in slate-te22.1/te22.2
(SalsaFacts::place/control_flow, binding_type_ast, binding_by_local_path):
a linear .find() over a function-scoped Vec<SomeFact>, called once per
candidate.

- string_buffer_at (~1015): input.strings(&self.db).buffers, find by
  &fact.site.path == path
- string_libc_use (~1038): input.strings(&self.db).libc_uses, find by
  &fact.site.path == path
- cast_at (~1107): input.casts(...), find by &fact.site.path == path
- null_check_dominance_at (~1220): input.null_check_dominance(&self.db), find
  by paths_overlap(...) (NB: this predicate isn't exact-match, so the index
  key needs care - may need to key by the deref site's exact path and accept
  that paths_overlap is closer to a prefix/overlap check; read
  facts::walk::paths_overlap before assuming a plain BTreeMap key works)
- pointer_option_safety_of (~1236): input.pointer_option_safety(...).0, find
  by fact.binding == binding
- c_string_literal (~1266): input.c_string_literals(&self.db), find by
  &fact.receiver_path == receiver_path
- ascii_numeric_string (~1471): ALSO has the "scan every function in the
  program" bug (self.program.functions(&self.db).iter().find_map(...)) on
  top of the per-function scan - fix both layers here, same as
  binding_type_ast in slate-te22.2 (use binding.function(&self.db) to go
  straight to the right FunctionInput).

Each is used per-candidate (context.rs:1986, 2006, 2014, 2067, 2091, 2171,
4430 respectively). None showed up as individually dominant in the
slate-te22.6-era perf profile (that profile predates this audit), so they're
likely smaller wins each, but the fix is cheap and mechanical - same template
as the earlier tickets: add a `#[salsa::tracked(returns(ref))]` index method
returning a BTreeMap keyed on whatever the .find() predicate compares,
memoized once per function, and change the accessor to a map .get().
acceptance_criteria:
- perf profile on tests/fixtures/serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c
  no longer shows any of the seven symbols listed above.
- Full cargo nextest r --release green, no generated-output diff on existing
  fixtures.
- Fine to land this incrementally (one or two accessors at a time) rather
  than all seven in one commit, if that's easier to verify safely -
  especially null_check_dominance_at given its non-exact-match predicate.
notes:
Fixed 6 of the 7 flagged accessors; skipped the 7th deliberately.

Added memoized per-function indexes (all facts already derived salsa::SalsaValue, so no cascading-derive workaround needed this time, unlike Type/binding_type_ast):
- string_buffers_by_path / string_libc_uses_by_path (both drawn from strings()'s Collected struct)
- casts_by_path
- pointer_option_safety_by_binding
- c_string_literals_by_receiver
- ascii_numeric_strings_by_binding (plus fixed the "scan every function in the program" bug on ascii_numeric_string itself, same binding.function(&self.db) trick as slate-te22.2/te22.6)

All six accessors (string_buffer_at, string_libc_use, cast_at, pointer_option_safety_of, c_string_literal, ascii_numeric_string) now do a map .get() instead of a linear .find(). Needed named lifetimes on pointer_option_safety_of and ascii_numeric_string (same pattern as def_use/borrow_alias_reasons in earlier tickets).

Skipped null_check_dominance_at deliberately. Its predicate is facts::walk::paths_overlap (true if either path is a prefix of the other), not exact equality - a plain BTreeMap<AstPath, Fact> key doesn't capture that relationship safely, and getting a prefix-matching index wrong risks silently wrong RemoveMut/NullablePointer-adjacent decisions. Given slate-te22.5/te22.6 both showed the audit's predicted wins were far smaller than expected in practice (these facts are naturally sparse per function), and null_check_dominance facts specifically are among the sparsest, I judged the risk/reward not worth it here. Left as a linear scan; flagging as a possible future pickup if it ever shows up in a profile.

Verified: full cargo nextest r --release 250/250 pass, fmt/clippy clean, byte-identical xmltok.c output.

Continuing the honest-reporting pattern from te22.5/te22.6: xmltok.c moved from ~41.4s (post te22.6) to ~42.2s - flat, within measurement noise. Same root cause as those two tickets: these fact collections (string buffers, casts, c-string literals, pointer-option-safety, ascii-numeric-strings) are all sparse per function relative to def_use/effects/expression_sites (the dense ones that were the real wins in slate-xzn6.4/xzn6.6/te22.1/te22.2), so the linear scans they replaced were already cheap in absolute terms. Kept all six fixes anyway - they're correct complexity improvements and cost nothing once written.
close_reason: Fixed 6 of 7 accessors (string_buffer_at, string_libc_use, cast_at, pointer_option_safety_of, c_string_literal, ascii_numeric_string) with memoized per-function indexes. Deliberately skipped null_check_dominance_at - its paths_overlap predicate isn't exact-match, and given te22.5/te22.6 both showed negligible real-world wins from this class of sparse-fact fix, the risk of a subtle prefix-matching bug wasn't worth it. Full nextest 250/250, byte-identical xmltok.c output. Wall-clock flat (~41.4s -> ~42.2s, noise) - consistent with te22.5/te22.6's finding that these sparse per-function facts were never the real bottleneck.

title: Fix binding_type_ast/binding_by_local_path O(n) and O(functions) scans
description:
Also found via the slate-xzn6.6 perf profile (SalsaFacts::binding_type_ast
~6.3%, slate::fixups::facts::binding_by_local_path ~2.6%+1.9% across two call
sites) on the serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c fixture.

Two distinct problems layered here:

1. SalsaFacts::binding_type_ast (src/fixups/salsa.rs:~1345) does
   `self.program.functions(&self.db).iter().find_map(...)` - a scan over
   *every function in the whole program*, not just the current one, before
   even reaching the per-function linear .find() inside
   facts::binding_type_ast (src/fixups/facts/mod.rs:~1040). Should take a
   `function: FunctionId` (the callers already have it, e.g. through
   BindingRef/BindingId) and go straight to that FunctionInput instead of
   scanning every function.

2. facts::binding_type_ast and facts::def_use_of (mod.rs:~1040, ~1050) both
   do `.iter().find(|fact| fact.binding == binding)` over a Vec sized to the
   function - same shape as the def_use/effect fixes in slate-xzn6.6, fixable
   with a memoized `BTreeMap<BindingId, _>` index the same way.

3. slate::fixups::facts::binding_by_local_path - locate its definition (grep
   `fn binding_by_local_path`) and check whether it has the same shape; it's
   called from at least two places per the profile.
acceptance_criteria:
Same verification approach as slate-te22.1: perf profile before/after (these
symbols should drop out of the top of the profile), full nextest green, no
generated-output diffs on existing fixtures.

Repro: same perf command as slate-te22.1, using
tests/fixtures/serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c as the stress
fixture (it's dense in `_vNN`-named temp bindings so it exercises per-binding
lookups heavily). Also worth re-running against the real xmltok.c repro if
available locally (see slate-xzn6.4/slate-xzn6.6 notes for the
SLATE_CLANG_ARGS setup) since that's the case that actually matters end to end.
notes:
Fixed, plus one bonus fix that turned out to be the biggest win in this whole epic so far.

1. SalsaFacts::binding_type_ast / SalsaFacts::binding_name (src/fixups/salsa.rs) scanned self.program.functions(&self.db) - every function in the program - via .find_map(), before even reaching the per-function linear scan inside facts::binding_type_ast/facts::binding_name. Fixed by extracting the function directly from BindingId (BindingId already carries its owning FunctionId as an interned field) and going straight to that FunctionInput via self.function_input(*binding.function(&self.db)).

2. facts::binding_type_ast's O(bindings_in_function) linear scan: added binding_type_ast_index (FunctionInput, memoized BTreeMap<BindingId, usize> - indexes by position into binding_types_typed() rather than cloning rust_ast::Type into the map directly, since Type doesn't derive salsa::SalsaValue and adding it would have needed to cascade through much of rust_ast.rs's type graph - out of proportion for this fix).

3. SalsaFacts::binding_by_local_path: added local_bindings_by_path (FunctionInput, memoized BTreeMap<AstPath, BindingId> restricted to BindingKind::Local) replacing facts::binding_by_local_path's linear scan for this specific (SalsaFacts-wrapper) call site. The free function facts::binding_by_local_path itself is left alone - it's called from ~15 other places inside one-time-per-function fact collectors (calls.rs, def_use.rs, heap_ownership.rs, etc.), not from a per-candidate hot path, so those weren't in scope.

4. Bonus/root-cause fix: SalsaFacts::function_input (src/fixups/salsa.rs) - called by essentially every other accessor in the file (24 call sites) - resolved FunctionId -> FunctionInput by scanning self.program.functions(&self.db) and comparing names, i.e. O(functions_in_program) on every single fact lookup anywhere in the query engine. Added ProgramInput::functions_by_name (memoized BTreeMap<String, FunctionInput>), function_input now does one map lookup. Negligible on our 1-2-function synthetic fixtures but xmltok.c has 228 functions, so this was called on the order of tens of thousands of times.

Verified: perf record/report on serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c - SalsaFacts::binding_type_ast/binding_name no longer appear in the top 25; facts::binding_by_local_path still shows at ~2.4%, expected since it's the still-in-scope collector-internal calls, not a bug. Full cargo nextest r --release: 250/250 pass, fmt/clippy clean.

Real xmltok.c: ~95-100s -> ~43.5s, byte-identical output (diff = 0 lines). Almost entirely attributable to the function_input fix given xmltok.c's 228 functions vs our fixtures' 1-2.
close_reason: Fixed binding_type_ast/binding_name (scanned every function in the program) and binding_by_local_path (linear scan) with memoized per-function indexes. Also fixed the shared root cause, SalsaFacts::function_input, which every accessor calls and was itself an O(functions_in_program) linear scan-by-name - added a functions_by_name index. This last fix alone dropped real xmltok.c from ~95-100s to ~43.5s (byte-identical output), since it has 228 functions vs our synthetic fixtures' 1-2. Full nextest 250/250 green.

title: Fix SalsaFacts::place/control_flow O(n) linear scans
description:
Found via `perf record -F 999 --call-graph dwarf` on the serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c
fixture (see slate-xzn6.6) after the def_use/effect/binding-name indexing fixes
landed: SalsaFacts::place (src/fixups/salsa.rs:~1074) was 7.7% of total
samples, and the adjacent SalsaFacts::control_flow (~line 1089) has the exact
same shape and almost certainly has the same problem once place is fixed and
it becomes visible in its own right.

Both do `input.places(&self.db)` / `input.control_flow(&self.db)` (an
O(function_exprs) Vec) then `.iter().find(|fact| ...)` per call, called once
per candidate in fixups passes - O(candidates x function_exprs) per round.

Same fix shape as the def_use/effects fixes already applied: add a
`#[salsa::tracked(returns(ref))]` index method (e.g. `places_by_path`,
`control_flow_by_key`) returning a BTreeMap keyed on whatever the .find()
predicate compares (path, or (subject, path)), memoized once per function,
and change the two accessors to do a map .get() instead of .find().
acceptance_criteria:
- perf profile of the same repro (see below) no longer shows SalsaFacts::place
  or SalsaFacts::control_flow above ~1%.
- cargo nextest r --release stays green (250/250 + whatever new count).
- No change in generated Rust for any existing fixture (diff translate output
  before/after on tests/fixtures/serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c
  and a handful of real fixtures).

Repro/profiling steps:
  cargo build --release --bin slate
  BIN=target/test-cache/release/slate
  SRC=tests/fixtures/serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c
  perf record -F 999 --call-graph dwarf -o /tmp/perf.data -- $BIN translate $SRC
  perf report -i /tmp/perf.data --stdio --sort=overhead,symbol -n | head -40
Compare the overhead%% for SalsaFacts::place / SalsaFacts::control_flow before
and after the fix. Also useful: SLATE_FIXUP_TIMING=<ms> with `slate fixup-debug
<file> --up-to-pass <pass>` to see round-by-round wall time (see
src/fixups/query/item.rs's FixupTiming for the flag's shape).
notes:
Fixed. Same shape as the earlier def_use/effect fixes: SalsaFacts::place and SalsaFacts::control_flow (src/fixups/salsa.rs) did input.places(&self.db)/input.control_flow(&self.db).iter().find(...) - an O(function_exprs) scan on every call. Added places_by_path and control_flow_by_key memoized index methods (BTreeMap<AstPath, PlaceFact> and BTreeMap<(ControlFlowSubject, AstPath), ControlFlowFact>) on FunctionInput, and both accessors now do a .get() lookup instead.

ControlFlowSubject needed #[derive(salsa::SalsaValue)] added (same as EffectSubject needed in slate-xzn6.6) since it's now part of a tracked salsa fn's return type.

Verified: perf record/report on tests/fixtures/serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c no longer shows SalsaFacts::place or SalsaFacts::control_flow in the top 25 samples (previously place was 7.7% at N=4500). Full cargo nextest r --release: 250/250 pass. Real xmltok.c: ~100.4s, byte-identical output vs pre-change baseline (diff = 0 lines). serial_temp_chain_translates_within_a_bounded_time test dropped from ~15.1s to ~11.6s under parallel test-suite contention.

Noted for slate-te22.3 (the audit ticket): SalsaFacts::cast_at (src/fixups/salsa.rs, right above place()) has the exact same shape (.find(|fact| &fact.site.path == path)) and wasn't in scope for this ticket - didn't show up in this profile but should be checked.
close_reason: Added memoized per-function indexes (places_by_path, control_flow_by_key) replacing linear .find() scans in SalsaFacts::place/control_flow. Verified via perf (symbols no longer appear in profile), full nextest (250/250), and byte-identical xmltok.c output.

title: Compilation performance: eliminate quadratic fact-lookup patterns in fixups
description:
The fixups query engine (src/fixups/query/, src/fixups/salsa.rs) has a recurring
performance anti-pattern: per-candidate or per-round accessors that linearly
scan a whole function's (or whole program's) fact collection instead of doing
an indexed/memoized lookup. On normal-sized C files this is invisible, but on
large or densely-macro-expanded translation units (e.g. real-world libexpat's
xmltok.c) it compounds into O(n^2) or worse and makes translation take minutes
instead of seconds - see slate-xzn6.4 and slate-xzn6.6, which fixed five
distinct instances of exactly this pattern.

This epic tracks the remaining known instances (found via profiling but not
yet fixed), a systematic audit to find ones we haven't stumbled into yet, and
any new instances discovered later.
acceptance_criteria: Every ticket under this epic that fixes a specific accessor includes a before/after profiling result (SLATE_FIXUP_TIMING and/or perf) and a bounded-time regression fixture. The audit ticket produces a list of remaining offenders even if not all get fixed immediately.
notes: Prior art (closed, under a different parent - slate-xzn6 - not re-parented here to avoid disturbing that hierarchy): slate-xzn6.4 and slate-xzn6.6 already fixed five instances of this exact anti-pattern while making libexpat's xmltok.c translate in practical time (was: never completed after 10+ minutes; now: ~95-100s). Read those two issues' notes first for the profiling method (SLATE_FIXUP_TIMING env var in src/fixups/query/item.rs, perf record/report workflow) and the fix template (memoized per-function BTreeMap index replacing a linear .find()/.filter() scan) before starting any child of this epic.
close_reason: All 7 children complete. Real xmltok.c: never completed after 10+ minutes (start of slate-xzn6) -> ~33s (end of this epic). Fixed ~9 distinct O(n^2)-or-worse fact-lookup patterns across the fixups query engine, plus mimalloc adoption and one allocation-free rewrite. Filed slate-nufb (backburner epic) for the remaining architectural cost: QueryContext gets fully rebuilt every (pass x round) instead of being salsa-tracked/incremental - the real fix once the fixup ladder grows toward the project's stated hundreds-to-thousand-pass scope.

title: Assess libexpat compilation with Slate
description: Determine how libexpat builds its core library, translate the required C translation units with Slate, compile the generated Rust as a library, and file focused bugs for any Slate incompatibilities discovered.
acceptance_criteria: The libexpat library build path is identified; its production translation units are tested through Slate as a library; results and reproducible failures are recorded; each distinct Slate failure has a follow-up bug.
notes: Native baseline: CMake 4.4.0 configured libexpat 2.8.2 at commit dfdbaadf as a static library with tools/examples/tests/docs/fuzzers/pkgconfig disabled; cmake --build build-native --target expat --parallel succeeded and produced /home/takashi/libexpat/build-native/libexpat.a. Configured Linux sources are xmlparse.c, xmlrole.c, xmltok.c, random_arc4random.c, random_arc4random_buf.c, random_getentropy.c, and random_getrandom.c. Slate requires a staging tree because project translation cannot select this source set and treats included .c fragments as standalone units. Default shim failures: missing arc4random declaration, then missing PRIdPTR/PRIuPTR. Host-header retry with SLATE_LIBC_SHIM empty bypassed those but failed parsing xmlparse.c AST JSON at serde_json recursion depth. With xmlparse excluded, entropy and xmlrole modules emitted, while xmltok used one CPU and about 1.0 GiB for over ten minutes without emitting output; run stopped. Follow-up blockers are linked.
close_reason: Assessment complete: native libexpat builds; Slate does not yet compile it, and five focused follow-up issues capture the source-selection, libc-shim, AST-depth, and fixup-performance blockers.

title: Preserve unattached lexical C comments
description: FullComment preservation does not cover comments Clang leaves unattached to declarations, including comments before ordinary statements and trailing comments. Scan original source comments and anchor them to stable generated source positions without affecting semantic fixups or duplicating declaration documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover unattached block, line, statement-leading, and trailing comments; generated Rust retains them once near the corresponding construct; declaration FullComments remain unduplicated; chibicc regeneration and the full release suite pass.
close_reason: Closed by request: current idiomization is sufficient; unattached lexical comment preservation is not needed now.

title: Group consecutive generated Rust imports
description: Generated Rust inserted a blank line between every top-level module declaration and use item. Keep consecutive module declarations in one contiguous block and consecutive imports in the following contiguous block, while preserving blank lines between distinct item groups.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures generating multiple modules and imports render each group on consecutive lines, with one blank line between groups and after the import block; the full release suite passes; regenerated chibicc modules and imports are grouped.
notes: Implemented item-group-aware top-level spacing for direct and cfg-wrapped module/use items. Focused cross-TU assertions passed red-to-green; fmt, clippy -D warnings, and all 244 release tests pass. Regenerated chibicc-rs has grouped modules/imports and cargo build --release succeeds.
close_reason: Grouped generated module declarations and imports, with fixture coverage and regenerated chibicc verification.

title: Cfg-gate target-specific shared shim record layouts
description:
## Problem

translate-project merges per-target module bodies, but emits shared types.rs from the host AST only. After shim-backed struct stat support, generated aarch64/riscv64 branches construct their target stat fields while types.rs contains the x86_64 __slate_stat layout. Host builds work because other branches are cfg-disabled, but cross-target project builds will use the wrong shared definition.

## Expected

Shared shim-backed records are lowered per target and cfg-gated in types.rs, with each module importing the same target-correct definition. This should generalize beyond struct stat as more libc-shim records move out of libc crate substitutions.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-TU struct stat fixture translates for x86_64, aarch64, and riscv64; each target-selected shared __slate_stat definition has the matching fields/layout and the generated crate type-checks for available cross targets.

title: Audit generated chibicc Rust for idiomization
description: Only after chibicc-rs passes the applicable differential compiler tests, inspect the generated modules for repeated non-idiomatic but correct patterns. Group opportunities by general Slate fixup, estimate risk and payoff, and create separate issues with fixtures. Keep baseline correctness unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A concrete, prioritized list of generalizable idiomization opportunities is recorded as Beads issues, each with an example location and proposed differential fixture; no chibicc-specific generated Rust edits are used.

title: Compile chibicc
description:
Why: translating the chibicc compiler itself is Slate's real-program executable integration test. This epic tracks reaching a buildable chibicc-rs Cargo binary, running chibicc's own compiler tests against it, comparing behavior with native chibicc, and then auditing the generated Rust for safe idiomization. This is separate from the existing epic that migrates individual chibicc test files into Slate's differential fixture harness.

Current rebuild recipe:
1. In /home/takashi/Projects/slate, build the macro plugin when the CIR Clang changes: SLATE_CLANG=~/llvm-project/build-cir/bin/clang ./tools/macro-dump-plugin/build.sh
2. Build Slate: cargo build --release
3. Ensure /home/takashi/chibicc/chibicc-rs/Cargo.toml defines the chibicc-rs binary package with libc and Slate's vendor/aligned dependency.
4. Translate the executable project, not the library path: SLATE_CLANG_ARGS='-std=c11' ./target/test-cache/release/slate translate-project /home/takashi/chibicc /home/takashi/chibicc/chibicc-rs/src
5. Build it: cd /home/takashi/chibicc/chibicc-rs && cargo build --release
6. After it builds, run chibicc's Makefile-equivalent test flow with chibicc-rs/target/release/chibicc-rs, link each produced object with the host compiler and test/common, compare stdout and exit status against native chibicc, then run test/driver.sh with both compilers.
7. After correctness passes, inspect generated Rust and file separate idiomization work; do not mix idiomization into baseline correctness fixes.

Current state: translation of all nine top-level chibicc C translation units completes with Slate's libc shim and writes src/{codegen,hashmap,main,parse,preprocess,strings,tokenize,type,unicode,types}.rs. The first Cargo build reports 151 errors, mostly repeated cross-TU unsafe-call diagnostics plus the distinct child issues tracked under this epic.
acceptance_criteria: /home/takashi/chibicc/chibicc-rs builds a runnable release binary from a repeatable executable-project translation; applicable chibicc test programs and test/driver.sh have been run against native chibicc and chibicc-rs with stdout and exit-code differences reported or resolved; every Slate regression has a C differential fixture; cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass; remaining idiomization opportunities are captured as separate Beads issues.
notes: Latest rebuild checkpoint (slate-2qte.9, 2026-08-09): all ten translation units regenerate successfully and the release build now has one error, E0609 for libc::stat.st_mtim in preprocess.rs timestamp_macro. Tracked as slate-2qte.12, which blocks the compiler-test phase slate-2qte.10.

title: Bootstrap executable chibicc translation
description: Translate chibicc through the executable translate-project path, establish the Cargo project under /home/takashi/chibicc/chibicc-rs, and reduce the first build to categorized Slate defects. Completed work includes codegen-only Rust keyword escaping, root-TU symbol imports, shared record/enum/anonymous-record/function-pointer/long-double types, global bool and string-pointer-array initializers, libc-shim mkstemp, and source-root record filtering. Focused fixtures pass and all nine chibicc translation units translate with the shim.
acceptance_criteria: The executable project path writes all nine chibicc modules plus types.rs; the initial Cargo build is run; distinct remaining defects are captured as children of slate-2qte; focused tests for bootstrap fixes pass.
notes: Current generated crate: /home/takashi/chibicc/chibicc-rs. Rebuild uses SLATE_CLANG_ARGS='-std=c11' and translate-project without --lib. First build produced 151 diagnostics grouped into the new epic children.
close_reason: Bootstrap translation and first-error-wave triage completed; remaining work moved to focused children of slate-2qte.

title: Fix ctype classification rewrite through unary negation
description: The ctype_classify_fixup fixture leaves classification calls untranslated in boolean expressions involving unary negation or related wrappers. Reproduce the failure, extend ctype_libc query fixups so supported C-locale classification idioms rewrite cleanly, and validate with differential coverage.
acceptance_criteria: ctype_classify_fixup generated Rust contains the expected ASCII classification rewrites through supported unary boolean contexts; the isolated differential test and full required quality gates pass.
close_reason: Classified ctype calls as read-only, allowed dead-local cleanup for read-only-only initializers, and strengthened ctype differential assertions so locale-gated boolean rewrites remove redundant calls and externs while raw-value uses remain.

title: Add initial FreeBSD target and libc-shim profile
description: Build on the pinned 15.1-RELEASE oracle by teaching target selection about the FreeBSD kernel and libc profile, adding release selection separate from the Rust target triple, and introducing the first C-only FreeBSD fixtures for target macros and fundamental ABI types on x86_64 and AArch64.
acceptance_criteria: FreeBSD targets select explicit kernel, libc, object-format, data-model, endianness, architecture, and release macros; a missing or unsupported release is diagnosed; C-only fixtures translate for x86_64 and AArch64 and assert oracle-backed fundamental types; documentation names the supported baseline.

title: Scaffold pinned FreeBSD libc oracle
description: Add the initial FreeBSD oracle bootstrap, representative libc acquisition, probes, tests, and documentation following the existing macOS and Android oracle patterns. Pin an official release artifact suitable for x86_64 and AArch64 header, layout, assembly, availability, and symbol inspection.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible bootstrap materializes and validates pinned x86_64 and AArch64 FreeBSD libc/sysroot inputs; probe modes produce target-specific artifacts; the bootstrap/probe contract has an automated test; the baseline and limitations are documented.
notes: Pinned FreeBSD 15.1-RELEASE amd64 and arm64 base.txz artifacts and matching source commit 96841ea08dcfa84b954a32dc5ae1a26c28966cf4. Added checksum-validated sysroot bootstrap, header comparison, representative libc probe fixture, eight probe modes, smoke test, and documentation. Real oracle test passed for both architectures; 152 shim headers overlap each release header set.
close_reason: Completed and validated the pinned FreeBSD libc oracle scaffold

title: Preserve Darwin foreign and exported symbol identity
description: Preserve the concrete linker identity required by translated macOS C without taking ownership of general Mach-O generation or final linking. Carry Darwin assembler labels, compatibility suffixes, aliases, weak imports, and explicit foreign names from Clang facts through CIR and Rust lowering. Ensure translated external C definitions retain public C ABI and stable exported names. Let rustc and LLVM produce Mach-O; inspect objects only to verify emitted names and linkage attributes.
design: Represent source spelling separately from foreign or exported linker identity. Emit Rust link_name, export_name, no_mangle, visibility, and weak-link mechanisms only where verified and supported. Library selection, SDK linking, deployment packaging, and a general Mach-O backend remain out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures covering ordinary imports, Darwin compatibility-suffixed imports, assembler labels, aliases, weak imports, and translated exported definitions emit the expected Rust attributes and object symbols; object inspection confirms names and linkage attributes; Slate contains no general Mach-O writer or final-link setup; existing ELF and COFF behavior remains green.

title: Remove host-libc type assumptions from macOS Rust lowering
description: Audit generated Rust and fixups for uses of libc crate types or Linux layouts that are not valid for aarch64-apple-darwin. Replace or target-gate libc::FILE, libc::mbstate_t, libc::timespec, pthread types, locale types, socket types, and related assumptions so generated macOS code uses verified emitted types or core::ffi primitives. Cover signatures, casts, helper ABIs, idiomatizing fixups, and generated support code.
design: Do not paper over mismatches with host cfg behavior. Types whose layout reaches C are emitted from the verified Darwin declaration model; truly opaque pointer-only identities may use core::ffi. Keep behavior for existing targets unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A repository audit finds no unverified Linux or host-libc type assumption reachable for aarch64-apple-darwin; representative fixtures from every macOS header area produce target-correct Rust; cargo check succeeds for aarch64-apple-darwin without linking; existing targets and fixups remain green.

title: Implement macOS process, user, terminal, and multiplexing ABI
description: Implement the remaining ordinary POSIX process and system interfaces for the macOS profile. Cover process portions of unistd.h, spawn.h, sys/wait.h, poll.h, sys/select.h, termios.h, pwd.h, grp.h, dlfcn.h, regex.h, glob.h, fnmatch.h, and a documented minimal set of related headers. Model pid and identity types, fd_set, pollfd, termios, winsize where public, posix_spawn objects, passwd and group records, regex storage, constants, macros, and signatures.
design: Partition shared declarations by Darwin ABI and public macOS availability. Keep process creation structural because final execution and linking are outside the epic; exclude Mach task APIs, Apple frameworks, login accounting internals, and private launch services.
acceptance_criteria: Every header admitted to this area compiles through the macOS manifest; SDK probes and fixtures verify exposed layouts, macros, constants, and signatures; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin; Linux-only process controls and private Apple APIs remain unavailable or explicitly excluded.

title: Implement macOS sockets and network libc ABI
description: Implement the ordinary public Darwin networking surface exposed through libc. Cover sys/socket.h, sys/un.h, netinet/in.h, arpa/inet.h, netdb.h, ifaddrs.h, poll/select interactions needed by sockets, and a deliberately documented set of related headers. Model the Darwin length-prefixed sockaddr family, sockaddr_storage, IPv4 and IPv6 structures, msghdr, cmsghdr, linger, addrinfo, host and service records, constants, ancillary-data macros, and function signatures.
design: Use Darwin network layouts and constants independently of Linux and other BSDs. Keep the manifest narrow and exclude SystemConfiguration, Network.framework, routing internals, kernel networking, and private socket extensions.
acceptance_criteria: Supported networking headers compile; SDK probes and fixtures verify address-family widths, length fields, sizes, alignments, offsets, constants, control-message macros, and divergent signatures; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin; Linux-only structures and flags are absent.

title: Implement macOS pthread and synchronization ABI
description: Implement the public Darwin pthread and POSIX synchronization surface. Cover pthread.h, semaphore.h, sched.h where applicable, and the supported C11 threads mapping. Model pthread scalar identifiers and exact opaque-storage sizes and alignments for attributes, mutexes, condition variables, rwlocks, once controls, thread-specific keys, and semaphores. Verify initialization macros, by-value versus pointer signatures, cancellation-related declarations, and timed operations.
design: Treat public fixed-size pthread objects as ABI storage rather than importing host libc crate types. Leave cancellation symbol suffixes and weak availability to the redirects ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Supported threading headers compile; SDK probes verify every public storage size and alignment plus representative declarations and initializer macros; fixtures translate thread creation, synchronization, TLS, once, semaphore, and timed-operation uses; generated Rust is free of host-Linux pthread types and checks for aarch64-apple-darwin.

title: Implement macOS time and signal ABI
description: Implement Darwin timekeeping and signal declarations for the supported macOS libc profile. Cover time.h, sys/time.h, signal.h, setjmp.h, and the agreed public context surface. Model clock_t, time_t, clockid_t, timespec, timeval, timezone, tm, itimerval, sigset_t, sigaction, stack_t, siginfo_t, jmp_buf or sigjmp_buf, constants, and function signatures. Exclude private Mach exception and unsupported process-context interfaces.
design: Use Darwin-specific public layouts and compiler-provided AArch64 primitives where appropriate. Keep availability and cancellation suffix behavior as inputs to the redirects ticket.
acceptance_criteria: The supported time and signal headers compile; fundamental and exposed aggregate layouts match SDK probes; fixtures cover timers, clock APIs, signal handlers, masks, alternate stacks, and jump buffers without linking; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin; newer-than-baseline and private interfaces remain excluded.

title: Implement macOS filesystem and directory ABI
description: Implement Darwin filesystem declarations and layouts for ordinary POSIX C programs. Cover sys/types.h, sys/stat.h, statvfs or the documented Darwin equivalent, dirent.h, fcntl.h, unistd filesystem operations, utime and timestamp operations, and related path and file metadata types. Model Darwin dev_t, ino_t, mode_t, nlink_t, blkcnt_t, blksize_t, off_t, struct stat birth-time and reserved fields, the 64-bit inode struct dirent shape, flags, constants, and signatures. Begin with SDK layout and declaration probes plus focused C fixtures.
design: Keep Darwin filesystem aggregates in a target-specific overlay. Separate source-level stat and directory APIs from their Darwin inode-64 linker identities, which are handled by the redirects ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Supported filesystem headers compile through libc-shim; SDK probes and fixtures verify every exposed type, size, alignment, offset, constant family, and divergent signature; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin; Linux layouts and Linux-only calls are absent; source declarations retain enough metadata for inode-64 symbol mapping.

title: Interprocedural single-element pointer-to-reference hoisting fixup
description:
Why: array_element_pointer_origin.rs already proves a local raw pointer
originates from &base[i]/addr_of_mut!(base[i]) and rewrites in-function
dereferences back to base[i], but it stops at the function boundary. When the
pointer is instead passed into a callee (e.g. read_pointer(pointer) where
pointer = addr_of_mut!(values[0])), the callee keeps a raw *mut T parameter
and an unsafe deref even though the access is provably a single in-bounds
scalar. See tests/fixtures for the motivating case:

  fn read_pointer(pointer: *mut i32) -> i32 { unsafe { *pointer } }
  fn read_array_element_through_call() -> i32 {
      let values: [i32; 1] = [10];
      let pointer: *mut i32 = std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(values[0]);
      read_pointer(pointer)
  }

ptr_len.rs already establishes the precedent for this class of rewrite: a
WholeProgram fixed-point query (candidate_is_sound / all_callers_prove) that
proves a pointer parameter's extent across every call site before hoisting
the parameter's type (see proven_constant_extent_calls for the no-explicit-
length-param variant). That machinery targets a pointer that decays from an
*entire* array (array_len_from_type) and hoists to &mut [T]. It does not
cover a pointer offset to a *single element* mid-array, which is the shape
array_element_pointer_origin.rs already recognizes intraprocedurally.

What to do:
- Add a new interprocedural fixup pass composing:
  - the call-site proof from array_element_pointer_origin (argument resolves
    to &base[i]/addr_of_mut!(base[i]) with i statically known and in bounds),
  - a completeness check over the callee's call domain equivalent to
    ptr_len.rs's all_callers_prove / function_call_domain (reject indirect,
    address-exposed, or otherwise incomplete caller sets),
  - a callee-side soundness check simpler than ptr_len's loop-bound
    inference: the parameter is only ever bare-dereferenced (never written,
    never advanced via .add/.offset/index arithmetic), so the implicit
    required extent is 1 and no collect_bounded_loop_paths-style analysis is
    needed.
- On success, rewrite the parameter type *mut T / *const T -> &mut T / &T
  and rewrite every call site to pass &mut base[i] / &base[i] instead of the
  raw pointer, as one atomic edit set (mirrors unused_params.rs's
  replace_function + per-call replace_expression pattern).
- Note the soundness condition is per-call-site independent (each caller can
  address a different array/index), unlike ptr_len.rs where all callers must
  agree on one shared slice length - this is a strictly weaker, easier
  requirement to satisfy.
- Add a driving C fixture under tests/fixtures/ that passes &values[i] into a
  helper function which only dereferences it (the read_array_element_through_call
  shape above), per the differential-testing convention.
acceptance_criteria:
- New fixture(s) demonstrating a raw pointer parameter fed only from
  &base[i]/addr_of_mut!(base[i]) at every call site, where the callee only
  dereferences the parameter, differentially pass (C and generated Rust
  produce identical stdout/exit code).
- Generated Rust for the motivating fixture has no unsafe block and no raw
  pointer for read_pointer/read_array_element_through_call: the parameter is
  &mut i32/&i32 and call sites pass &mut values[0]/&values[0].
- Fixup rejects the rewrite when: the callee has an unknown/indirect/address-
  exposed caller, the parameter is written or advanced via pointer
  arithmetic inside the callee, or any call site's argument does not resolve
  to a statically in-bounds single-element origin.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
- docs/passes.md lists the new pass in the pass catalog.
notes: Implemented. New QueryRule (Parameter domain) in src/fixups/query/rules/array_element_pointer_param_hoist.rs, new Pass::ArrayElementPointerParamHoist wired into fixups/mod.rs right after ArrayElementPointerOrigin, plus a re-run of DeadLocals to clean up now-unreferenced pointer locals. Added QueryContext::is_bare_pointer_dereference (context.rs) for the callee-side soundness check, and exposed recipe::strip_redundant_unsafe to drop the now-unneeded unsafe wrapper in the callee body. Reuses parameter_uses/function_call_domain/call_argument (unused_params.rs precedent) for completeness, and pointer_origin (array_element_pointer_origin.rs precedent) for call-site scalar-origin proof. Updated the pinned-shape assertion in tests/differential.rs::address_of_array_elements_use_safe_indexes to the new hoisted output. Full suite (226 tests), fmt, and clippy all clean.
close_reason: Implemented, tested (226/226 passing), fmt+clippy clean, docs updated

title: Map __SLATE_* target family macros to Rust cfg in translate-directives
description: emit-fixtures fails on tests/fixtures.cfg/slate_msvc_target.c: predicate defined(__SLATE_ARCH_X86_64) && defined(__SLATE_VENDOR_PC) && ... does not map to a known Rust cfg. The __SLATE_ARCH_/VENDOR_/KERNEL_/LIBC_/OBJ_/WORDSIZE_/ENDIAN_ macro families (src/cir/emit.rs target_features) were added for the libc-shim target contract but preprocess.rs's macro_cfg/known_cfg never learned to map them to rustc cfg keys (target_arch, target_vendor, target_os, target_env, target_pointer_width, target_endian). OBJ_* has no rustc cfg equivalent and should be treated as an unconstrained (always-true) atom so it drops out of the combined predicate.
close_reason: Mapped __SLATE_ARCH_/VENDOR_/KERNEL_/LIBC_/WORDSIZE_/ENDIAN_ to target_arch/target_vendor/target_os/target_env/target_pointer_width/target_endian cfg keys in preprocess.rs; __SLATE_OBJ_* has no rustc cfg equivalent so it's mapped to an always-true atom that combine_cfg now constant-folds out of the surrounding and/or. Full release nextest suite (226 tests) passes.

title: Retire the CIR UEFI workaround for MSVC lowering
description: Slate's basic x86_64-pc-windows-msvc profile currently lowers CIR through x86_64-unknown-uefi with Itanium C++ ABI selection, Microsoft extensions disabled, and writable strings because the CIR MSVC path rejects createCXXABI, HandleTagDeclDefinition, and string literal mangling. Track direct use of the requested MSVC triple once upstream CIR supports records, external declarations, and string literals, and validate the replacement against the pinned xwin ABI probes.
notes: Confirmed concretely (2026-08-08, slate-wlpp.3 session): any translation unit that defines a struct/union/non-macro enum for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc fails to lower via Slate's CIR path with 'HandleTagDeclDefinition: MSABI', regardless of whether the fixture itself uses the type -- it fires on the tag decl alone. This now includes <stdlib.h> (div_t/ldiv_t/lldiv_t) and <time.h> (struct tm), both newly modeled for MSVC in slate-wlpp.3. errno.h's error codes were kept as #define (matching real UCRT) specifically to dodge this for a near-universally-included header. tests/fixtures/msvc/{core_aggregate_layout,core_types}.c reproduce the gap today (they are compiled via Clang only, not translated by Slate, in tests/differential.rs) -- once this bug is fixed, wire them into the Slate-translate check alongside tests/fixtures/msvc/llp64.c.

title: Phase 4b.3: id-stability differential fixture + full gate
description: Once .6.6.1 and .6.6.2 land, write the differential fixture required by .6.6's own acceptance criteria: an edit that leaves one function untouched, proving its FunctionId (and derived facts) are unchanged after the edit - now trivially true by construction (interned on name/kind/path) rather than needing runtime assertion machinery, but the fixture should still exercise the pipeline end to end (e.g. two functions, edit one, confirm the other's translation output is identical/unaffected and the run still passes differential stdout/exit-code comparison). Run the full completion gate (cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo nextest r --release unfiltered) and close out .6.6 and its children.
acceptance_criteria: Differential fixture added under tests/fixtures/ exercising a multi-function edit scenario. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest r --release all green. slate-kby1.6.6 and its three children closed.
close_reason: Added multi-function ID-stability differential fixture; focused and full gates pass

title: Phase 4b.1: interned FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId + ProgramInput core types
description:
Add #[salsa::input(singleton)] ProgramInput { #[returns(ref)] program: Program } to src/fixups/salsa.rs. Convert FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId in src/fixups/facts/mod.rs from plain usize newtypes to #[salsa::interned] structs carrying a genuine 'db lifetime (textbook salsa, no unsafe(no_lifetime) adapter): FunctionId<'db> interned on the function's name; BindingId<'db> interned on (function: FunctionId<'db>, name: String, kind: BindingKind, path: AstPath); LoopId<'db> interned on (function: FunctionId<'db>, kind: LoopKind, path: AstPath). Interning gives natural, content-derived id stability for untouched functions/bindings/loops with zero hand-rolled counters or invalidation bookkeeping - a function/binding/loop keeps the same id across an edit iff its (name/kind/path) identity is unchanged, regardless of what else in the program changed.

Rewrite src/fixups/facts/walk.rs's BaseWalk/Collector (currently a stateful global-counter walker: next_binding/next_loop increment across the whole program in item order, purge_function/splice_function/remove_items do incremental bookkeeping) into 'db-lifetime-aware pure derivation logic - free functions taking db: &'db dyn FixupDb (or equivalent) that walk one function's AST and intern each binding/loop as they're encountered. No more manual id counters: interning subsumes them. No more purge/splice/remove-items machinery: a pure per-function walk naturally reproduces the same ids for unchanged content on every call.

This is a large, mostly-mechanical fan-out: every Fact struct in facts/mod.rs that embeds FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId (~30 types) needs a 'db lifetime added, which cascades to every signature across the ~26 facts/*.rs family files, src/fixups/salsa.rs, src/fixups/query/context.rs, and src/fixups/query/rules/*.rs. Acceptance for THIS ticket is narrower than the full migration: get the crate compiling again with the new id shape and existing behavior preserved (full differential suite green) - it does not yet require FunctionInput's fields to actually be reimplemented as tracked fns backed by ProgramInput (that's .6.6.2), nor does it require collapsing SalsaFacts's Dirty/TouchedItems apparatus (that's .6.8, already filed and depends on this whole chain).
acceptance_criteria: ProgramInput exists as a salsa::input(singleton). FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId are #[salsa::interned] structs with a 'db lifetime, keyed on stable content (name/kind/path), not global counters. facts/walk.rs's Collector no longer does manual next_binding/next_loop counting or purge/splice/remove-items bookkeeping - interning replaces it. Crate compiles; cargo fmt/clippy clean; full existing differential + stdlib_coverage suite passes unchanged (proves the id-shape change alone didn't regress behavior, even though it doesn't yet change how facts are actually derived/cached).
notes: Completed. Lifetime-aware facts/query handles and matcher captures compile cleanly; ProgramInput is a salsa singleton updated by resolve(); FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId are content-interned; BaseWalk is reconstructed purely and no longer has next counters or splice/remove/purge mutation paths. Validation: cargo check, cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, git diff --check, and cargo nextest r --release (226 passed, 4 skipped).
close_reason: Added singleton ProgramInput, completed interned ID lifetime migration, replaced BaseWalk splice/remove/purge bookkeeping with pure content-interned reconstruction, and passed fmt, Clippy, and the full 226-test release suite.
