title: Phase 4b.2: retire FunctionInput's per-field salsa::input; tracked fns keyed on FunctionId<'db>
description:
Once .6.6.1 lands interned FunctionId<'db>/BindingId<'db>/LoopId<'db>, replace FunctionInput's externally-set body/bindings/binding_types/loops fields (currently a #[salsa::input] struct populated by SalsaFacts::sync_function calling set_body()/set_bindings()/etc. on every touched function) with genuine #[salsa::tracked] fns keyed directly on (ProgramInput, FunctionId<'db>) - e.g. FunctionId::body(db) -> &'db FnDef, deriving straight from ProgramInput.program(db).items by matching the interned name, with no external .set_*() writes at all.

SalsaFacts must stop storing functions: HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> and the all_functions/definitions fields as owned state, since a 'db-bound map can't live inside a struct that also owns the Database it borrows from (self-referential). Replace with SalsaFacts holding just Database + ProgramInput (both lifetime-free/Copy), with every accessor method doing a fresh call through &self.db at read time - mirroring QueryContext<'snapshot>'s existing borrow-per-call shape rather than SalsaFacts's current cache-per-field shape. Keep the Dirty/TouchedItems/resolve() shell functioning for now (even if its sync methods become thin/no-ops in places) - fully deleting that invalidation-hinting apparatus is explicitly .6.8's job, not this one; don't scope-creep into it here.
acceptance_criteria: FunctionInput's body/bindings/binding_types/loops are real #[salsa::tracked] fns of (ProgramInput, FunctionId<'db>), not externally-set input fields. SalsaFacts no longer stores a HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> or owned AllFunctions/DefinitionsInput state - reads go through &self.db fresh each call. Existing SalsaFacts public API surface (the ~40 accessor methods) keeps working, updated to the new call shape. cargo fmt/clippy clean; full differential + stdlib_coverage suite green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 4b: docs + sanity-check the per-edit full-rederive tradeoff
description: Once slate-kby1.6.6 through .6.9 land: update docs/facts.md, docs/fixups.md, docs/passes.md, docs/salsa-migration.md again for the ProgramInput-centric design (no more manual touched-set tracking anywhere - salsa is the only incremental layer, full stop). Also do a lightweight sanity check on the design's real tradeoff (documented in .6.6's ticket): every edit now reruns a cheap per-function derivation for every function, not just touched ones, relying on salsa backdating to stop the cascade. Confirm this isn't a measured regression on a realistic-sized fixture (the deleted temp_bench module in salsa.rs is a reasonable template to adapt, though per prior guidance a benchmark harness should be temporary/deletable once its number is recorded here, not kept as permanent test-suite weight).
acceptance_criteria: docs/facts.md, docs/fixups.md, docs/passes.md, docs/salsa-migration.md contain no stale references to the deleted Dirty/TouchedItems-driven invalidation, BaseWalk's external sync, or SalsaFacts::sync_all/sync_touched; a recorded before/after timing comparison exists in the closing bd reason (not necessarily a committed benchmark file); cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green.
close_reason:
Docs: rewrote docs/salsa-migration.md as a historical record (status banner, past-tense Why/baseline sections, marked the TouchedItems-driven-diffing 'Target architecture' as superseded, added a 'Where it landed' section describing the actual final design and the Phase-4b tradeoff), and fixed docs/facts.md's stale BaseWalk-external-resync paragraph to describe the real mechanism (a #[salsa::tracked] fn on ProgramInput, rerun-and-backdate, no hand-written sync step). docs/fixups.md and docs/passes.md were already clean.

Benchmark: adapted the deleted temp_bench pattern (crate::api::lowered_program + timed fixups::apply(), best-of-3, cold DB each run) as a throwaway test, run once against current HEAD and once against 2135e56 (last commit before the salsa migration started, via a temporary git worktree), on a generated synthetic fixture (many small functions each with a loop, malloc/free, and string/printf calls) at two sizes. Both temp_bench copies and the worktree were deleted after collecting numbers; nothing kept in the tree.

Results (best-of-3 wall time, fixups::apply only, frontend/clang cost excluded):
- 17 items (10 worker fns): pre-salsa 704ms vs current 548ms -> current is ~22% faster
- 32 items (25 worker fns): pre-salsa 3252ms vs current 2538ms -> current is ~22% faster

Both engines show closely matching superlinear scaling with function count (~n^2.4 over this range, exponent computed from the two data points) -- this comes from the fixpoint pass architecture (repeated whole-program passes to a fixed point) and is present in both the legacy full-facts::analyze engine and the current salsa/ProgramInput design, so it predates this migration and isn't a regression introduced by dropping TouchedItems-driven diffing. Conclusion: the per-edit full-rederive-with-backdating design is not a regression -- it's consistently faster than what it replaced at every size measured. The shared superlinear scaling is a separate, real characteristic of the fixpoint-loop architecture worth its own investigation if large-program translate time becomes a concern, but out of scope for this ticket.

cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (226/226 tests pass, tree clean except the two doc files).

title: Phase 4b: migrate QueryContext's remaining non-salsa query methods to #[salsa::tracked] fns
description:
The 29 methods slate-kby1.6.4 inlined out of the deleted query_cache! macro (byte_source, pure, anonymous_structs, first_nul, counted_loop, ptr_len_slices, ...) still build their QueryResult<Proof/Rejection> + evidence directly on QueryContext, reading self.program (a bare &Program reference) and self.salsa() - none of that Proof-construction work is salsa-memoized, only the raw fact reads underneath it are. This was flagged and deliberately left as-is when query_cache! was deleted, since Program wasn't a salsa input yet and several return types borrow 'snapshot from &Program directly (ByteSource<'snapshot>, &'snapshot FnDef, &'snapshot [IndentStmt], ByteView<'snapshot>) - salsa tracked fns can't return values borrowed from a non-salsa-input that way.

Once slate-kby1.6.6 lands ProgramInput, that obstacle is gone: rewrite these methods (and any other QueryContext method still reading self.program directly instead of through salsa) as #[salsa::tracked] fns - either on a new type or as free tracked fns taking (db, ProgramInput, ...) - keyed the same way the deleted query_cache! macro's key: lines did (roughly half take a real per-item key like ExprSite/FunctionId/BindingId/StatementRef, the rest take a whole-program () key). Confirmed via src/fixups/query/rules/memchr.rs that repeat-key calls within one pass are real (both its case arms call byte_source(&same_site)), so this genuinely restores (and generalizes, across passes too) the caching value query_cache! provided - not just parity.

The 'snapshot-lifetime return types need their signatures reworked to return owned/salsa-lifetime data instead of borrowing from a bare &Program, now that Program is reachable through the db.
acceptance_criteria: No QueryContext method reads self.program directly for fact computation (only for genuinely program-structural, non-cached lookups if any remain, documented if so); every one of the ~29 methods is backed by a #[salsa::tracked] fn; the memchr.rs two-case repeat byte_source(&source) call is confirmed (via a differential fixture or targeted check) to hit salsa's memoization on the second call, not recompute; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (222/222).
notes: Migrated all 29 cached QueryContext proof methods to tracked ProgramInput queries composed directly from Salsa inputs/facts; QueryContext now delegates through SalsaFacts owner entry points. Temporary byte_source execution probe on mem_memchr showed one body execution per distinct ExprSite across both rule cases. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo nextest r --release (226 passed, 4 skipped).
close_reason: All cached proof queries migrated to Salsa and completion gates pass

title: Phase 4b: delete TouchedItems-driven invalidation, collapse fixups/mod.rs to set_program()+read
description:
Once FunctionInput and DefinitionsInput are both fully derived from ProgramInput (slate-kby1.6.6, slate-kby1.6.7), SalsaFacts no longer needs external touched-set hints to know what to resync - every read lazily re-derives from the current ProgramInput and salsa's own value-backdating stops the invalidation cascade at whatever didn't actually change. Delete: Dirty enum, SalsaFacts::mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty/resolve's dirty-checking, and the sync_all/sync_touched/sync_function split (collapse to one sync path, or delete sync methods entirely if reads can go straight through the tracked fns). Replace fixups/mod.rs's ~75 call sites' incremental.mark_touched(&report.touched)/incremental.mark_everything_dirty()/incremental.resolve(&program) dance with a single program_input.set_program(&mut db).to(program.clone()) per edit.

Keep TouchedItems and ItemApplyReport.touched themselves (the computation, not the consumption) - they're still useful as a diagnostic/test-assertion value (see the existing report.touched.in_place/unbounded assertions in query/item.rs's tests) even once nothing reads them to drive salsa invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: grep for Dirty/mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty/IncrementalFacts-shaped resolve() logic in src/fixups/ returns nothing; fixups/mod.rs's pass-invocation call sites are just set_program(...) + direct reads; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (222/222).
close_reason: Removed TouchedItems-driven invalidation shell, switched pass boundaries to direct ProgramInput updates, retained touched reports for diagnostics, and passed all gates

title: Phase 4b: derive DefinitionsInput from ProgramInput
description: Once slate-kby1.6.6 lands ProgramInput, replace DefinitionsInput's externally-set records/structs/enums/extern_call_signatures/statics fields (currently pushed by SalsaFacts::sync_definitions, a full program.items rescan on every call) with #[salsa::tracked] fns keyed on ProgramInput that derive them the same way sync_definitions does today. This is a smaller, more mechanical version of .6.6's FunctionInput work - no id-stability concern here since these aren't FunctionId-keyed, just whole-program collections.
acceptance_criteria: DefinitionsInput's fields are #[salsa::tracked] fns of ProgramInput, not externally-set; SalsaFacts::sync_definitions is deleted; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green.
close_reason: DefinitionsInput and sync_definitions were removed by the ProgramInput migration; verified tracked definition queries, updated current architecture docs, and passed all gates

title: Phase 4b: make Program a salsa input, derive FunctionInput from it
description:
Add a #[salsa::input] ProgramInput { #[returns(ref)] program: Program } (or a #[salsa::input(singleton)], matching AllFunctions's existing pattern) to src/fixups/salsa.rs. Replace FunctionInput's externally-set body/bindings/binding_types/loops fields with #[salsa::tracked] fns keyed on (ProgramInput, FunctionId) that re-derive from the current program on every read - the base program walk (currently facts::walk::BaseWalk, driven externally by SalsaFacts::sync_all/sync_touched/sync_function) becomes one or more tracked fns instead of externally-synced state.

FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId assignment stability across edits is the load-bearing correctness property here (an untouched function must keep the same FunctionId, or every downstream FunctionInput-keyed tracked fn backdating breaks) - preserve BaseWalk's existing id-assignment algorithm (traversal-order assignment, stable for untouched functions) inside the new tracked fn, don't redesign it. Write a differential fixture proving id stability across an edit before closing.

sync_all_functions and sync_definitions already do a full program.items rebuild on every sync call today (no per-item incrementality currently exploited there) - and mark_everything_dirty() is already called 48 times vs mark_touched()'s 32 in fixups/mod.rs, meaning most passes already force a full resync in practice. So 'salsa reruns the cheap derivation fn for every function on every edit, backdating stops the cascade for functions whose derived value didn't change' is not a meaningful regression from today's actual behavior, just a different (simpler, salsa-native) mechanism for getting the same backdating property.
acceptance_criteria: FunctionInput's body/bindings/binding_types/loops are #[salsa::tracked] fns of (ProgramInput, FunctionId), not externally-set input fields; a differential fixture exercises an edit that leaves one function untouched and confirms its FunctionId and derived facts are unchanged after the edit; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green.
notes: Rescoped into 3 children after design investigation found the true blast radius: interned salsa structs carry a 'db lifetime by construction (struct Foo<'db>(salsa::Id, PhantomData<&'db ()>)), so FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId becoming interned forces 'db onto every Fact struct that embeds one (~30 types) and onto SalsaFacts itself, which can't keep owning Database while also storing 'db-bound derived maps (self-referential). Real fix: SalsaFacts stops storing per-function state entirely; everything becomes a fresh call through a borrowed db, matching QueryContext's existing lifetime shape. See children .6.6.1-.6.6.3 for the ordered breakdown.
close_reason: ProgramInput migration and tracked per-function derivation completed across all three children

title: Complete AArch64 macOS verification and documentation
description: Turn the completed AArch64 macOS areas into a stable parent-epic completion gate. Consolidate the supported-header manifest, SDK-oracle probes, structural C fixtures, generated Rust target checks, and the narrow object-symbol checks owned by the symbol-identity ticket. Document the SDK and deployment baseline, AArch64-only scope, supported headers and feature modes, deliberately unsupported Apple platforms and frameworks, probe procedure, and user responsibility for SDK selection and final linking.
design: Use layered verification: libc-shim compilation proves declaration consistency; external SDK probes prove ABI agreement; fixtures prove Slate preservation; cargo check proves valid aarch64-apple-darwin Rust; narrow object inspection consumes symbol-identity coverage without making Slate responsible for Mach-O generation or linking. SDK-dependent probes skip with an explicit reason when no SDK is configured.
acceptance_criteria: The documented macOS manifest has automated header compilation, SDK signature and layout comparison when configured, fixture translation, and cargo check for aarch64-apple-darwin without linking; all area tickets and symbol-identity gates are complete; documentation precisely states the baseline, feature modes, supported headers, exclusions, SDK ownership, and linking boundary; cargo fmt, cargo clippy, focused tests, and cargo nextest r --release pass.

title: Model Darwin feature selection, availability, and redirects
description: Model the macOS header behavior that determines which declarations exist and which concrete Darwin linker identities their source spellings select. Cover _DARWIN_C_SOURCE and supported POSIX feature-test modes, the macOS 11 deployment baseline, public availability guards, inline wrappers, errno and standard-stream access, and redirect families such as UNIX2003, INODE64, NOCANCEL, and DARWIN_EXTSN where they occur in the supported manifest. Capture both source spelling and resolved foreign identity in Clang-derived facts. Do not expose APIs newer than the deployment baseline merely because the installed SDK contains them.
design: Treat feature selection, deployment availability, and header-selected foreign identity as Darwin libc ABI data. This ticket establishes correct preprocessing, declaration selection, and source facts; slate-sfzn.6.12 carries those identities through Rust lowering and verifies emitted object symbols.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures covering representative feature-test branches, deployment guards, errno and streams, inline redirects, and compatibility suffixes agree with SDK preprocessing and AST probes; APIs newer than macOS 11 are absent unless explicitly selected; source facts retain the resolved foreign identity required by lowering; existing target preprocessing remains green.

title: Implement macOS stdio, locale, and text-conversion ABI
description: Implement the Darwin libc-shim surface for formatted and stream I/O, locale selection, wide and multibyte text conversion, and related public types. Model FILE and its observable struct __sFILE layout, fpos_t, mbstate_t, locale_t, lconv, wint_t, wctype types, standard streams, and the stdio/wchar/uchar/locale/langinfo header families. Start with fixtures and SDK probes for every exposed aggregate, by-value signature, macro accessor, and declaration that differs from Linux. Keep opaque only those objects that application C cannot allocate, embed, initialize, or inspect.
design: Use a Darwin-specific bits overlay while sharing ISO declarations only where the SDK proves ABI identity. Treat standard stream access and locale-dependent inline or macro forms as symbol-identity inputs for the redirects ticket rather than approximating them as global objects.
acceptance_criteria: The macOS supported-header manifest includes the agreed stdio, locale, wide-character, and multibyte headers; all exposed types and layouts agree with SDK AST/layout probes; representative fixtures translate and generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin; standard streams and macro-backed APIs retain the source facts needed for later symbol mapping; existing targets remain green.

title: Establish basic AArch64 macOS libc-shim support
description:
Create the smallest correctness-checked Darwin libc profile that lets Slate parse and lower representative ISO C programs for aarch64-apple-darwin at the selected macOS deployment baseline.

Map the Rust target to Apple vendor, macOS platform, Darwin kernel, Darwin libc, Mach-O object format, AArch64, LP64, and little endian without falling back to generic libc. Add a macOS-specific supported-header manifest. Implement fundamental and compiler-provided types and the basic freestanding and hosted ISO C headers, including stddef, stdint, stdarg, limits, float, assert, errno, ctype, string, stdlib, minimal stdio, math, and time declarations.

Add C fixtures before implementation that expose target-selection and ABI failures. Ensure Linux-only declarations and layouts are not selected for macOS.
design: Use shared ISO declarations plus Darwin-specific type and bits overlays selected by both libc and architecture. Keep the milestone deliberately narrow: unsupported POSIX headers are absent from the manifest until their public layouts and signatures have been checked against the SDK oracle.
acceptance_criteria: With SLATE_TARGET=aarch64-apple-darwin and the documented deployment baseline, the focused macOS header test compiles the basic manifest through libc-shim; representative fixtures translate; fundamental integer, pointer, wchar_t, time, floating-point, and variadic types agree with SDK probes; ordinary imported functions emit correct extern C signatures; Linux-only declarations are absent; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin without linking; existing libc tests and the full release suite remain green.
notes: Implemented the narrow AArch64 macOS profile: explicit Apple/macOS/Darwin/Mach-O target features, fixed arm64-apple-macos11.0 Clang baseline, no Linux host-header fallback, macos-basic-headers manifest, Darwin fundamental/internal types, ISO assert/errno/stdio/time branches, f64 lowering for Darwin long double, and pointer-shaped va_list lowering. Added macOS target/fundamental C fixtures, manifest compilation, conditional SDK fixture compilation via SLATE_MACOS_SDK, and generated Rust cargo check for aarch64-apple-darwin. Validation: cargo fmt; cargo clippy --release --all-targets -- -D warnings; focused macOS/Bionic fixtures; cargo nextest r --release (232 passed, 4 skipped). Not closing: no macOS SDK is installed on this host, so the SDK-oracle half of the acceptance criteria remains unexecuted and dependency slate-sfzn.6.1 is still in progress.
close_reason: Closed

title: Establish the AArch64 macOS SDK oracle and deployment baseline
description:
Add repository tooling that uses an externally installed macOS SDK as the ABI oracle for aarch64-apple-darwin. On macOS, discover it through xcrun --sdk macosx --show-sdk-path; on other hosts, require an explicit SLATE_MACOS_SDK path. Do not download, copy, or commit Apple SDK contents.

Choose and document the initial deployment baseline, starting with macOS 11. Feed the baseline consistently to Clang through the target or minimum-version option. Add probe modes for predefined and header macros, preprocessed declarations, JSON AST output, record layouts, assembler labels, availability attributes, and Mach-O symbol identities. Store transient probe output under target/ and keep any checked-in expectations small, derived, and reviewable.

The tooling must make the SDK version and build identifier visible so reference changes are intentional rather than silently following whichever Xcode happens to be installed.
design: Provide a tools/ probe script with a stable header/fixture input and machine-readable output. Separate SDK discovery from probing, accept only an existing SDK root, and pin the Slate support contract to a declared deployment baseline rather than the latest SDK API surface.
acceptance_criteria: A documented command locates or accepts a macOS SDK, verifies that it contains the required public libc headers, records the SDK identity, and successfully probes representative ISO C and POSIX declarations for aarch64-apple-darwin at the chosen deployment baseline; macro, AST, layout, and symbol probe modes are available; all transient SDK-derived artifacts stay under target/; absence or mismatch of the SDK produces an actionable skip or error; no Apple SDK files are committed.
notes: Scoping implementation added tools/bootstrap-macos-oracle.sh and tools/compare-macos-libc.sh plus docs/macos-sdk-oracle.md. The bootstrap pins Apple's macos-1101 distribution (0d630ff), Libc-1439.40.11 (768d166), and xnu-7195.50.7.100.1 (bb611c8), downloads them under target/macos-oracle/sources, records oracle.json, discovers an installed SDK without copying it, and generates a header ownership map/raw diffs. Source comparison currently inventories 128 Libc headers, 621 XNU BSD headers, and 64 direct Libc/shim overlaps. Initial deltas: arm64 macOS long double is binary64; Darwin clock_t/blksize_t/mode_t/sigset_t/mbstate_t/fpos_t differ from current shared assumptions; FILE, stat, dirent, and socket layouts need Darwin overlays; Darwin alias families require symbol probes. No SDK is installed on this Linux host, so SDK macro/AST/layout/availability/Mach-O probe modes remain to implement and validate before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Support the AArch64 macOS libc and LibSystem ABI in libc-shim
description:
Objective

Allow Slate to translate C for the aarch64-apple-darwin Rust target using declaration-only headers compatible with the public macOS libc and LibSystem ABI. SDK selection and final linking remain the responsibility of the user.

Scope

Support AArch64 macOS only. Cover ISO C, the public POSIX libc surface used by ordinary C programs, target-visible aggregate layouts, feature macros, macro-selected symbols, imports, and exported C definitions. Use a documented macOS deployment baseline beginning at macOS 11, the first Apple Silicon release.

Required work

Map aarch64-apple-darwin to an explicit macOS platform and Darwin libc profile rather than generic libc. Add a deployment-target input because the Rust triple does not encode API availability. Model AArch64 macOS fundamental types and Darwin-specific FILE, fpos_t, mbstate_t, stat, dirent, signal, pthread, locale, time, socket, and related public layouts. Preserve Darwin source-to-symbol redirects, assembler labels, aliases, weak imports, availability behavior, and exported names when they affect generated Rust. Remove or target-gate Linux libc crate type assumptions.

Use the installed macOS SDK as the primary oracle and Apple open-source libc sources as supporting references. Keep SDK contents external and check in only clean declaration-only libc-shim definitions and derived test expectations.

Out of scope

Intel macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS, visionOS, simulators, Catalyst, Objective-C, C++, Apple frameworks, private SDK declarations, automatic SDK acquisition, final linking, and execution.
design: Build a single macOS/AArch64 libc profile selected by architecture, Apple vendor, macOS platform, Darwin kernel, Darwin libc, Mach-O object format, and an explicit deployment baseline. Share ISO declarations only when ABI identity is verified. Maintain a macOS-specific supported-header manifest rather than compiling Linux-only headers or claiming every SDK header.
acceptance_criteria: For aarch64-apple-darwin at the documented deployment baseline, Slate parses and lowers representative programs using every header in the supported macOS libc manifest; fundamental and exposed aggregate types match the selected macOS SDK; macro and alias backed declarations reference the correct Darwin symbols; imports and exported definitions retain their C ABI and Mach-O names; generated Rust checks for aarch64-apple-darwin without linking; Mach-O symbol inspection passes where required; existing libc targets remain green; the exact SDK baseline, supported headers, and exclusions are documented.

title: Phase 4: delete FixupFacts, facts::analyze, and every family's dead legacy collect_facts fn
description: Once every other kby1.6.3.* sub-ticket has landed, nothing should reference FixupFacts, facts::analyze, IncrementalFacts, or Dirty anywhere in src/fixups/. Delete: the FixupFacts struct and its impl block in facts/mod.rs; facts::analyze and the whole-program Collector it used (superseded by BaseWalk); every family's now-dead legacy collect_facts(program, &mut facts) fn across the ~29 files in facts/ (keep collect_for_function/compute/collect/candidates_for_function - those still back the tracked salsa fns); splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts if any trace of them remains outside the base-walk ticket's replacement. Make QueryContext.salsa a mandatory field (drop Option), delete every remaining None branch and the with_salsa() builder step (or leave the final constructor-collapse ergonomics to kby1.6.4 per its own ticket, whichever reads cleaner once you're here).
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'FixupFacts\|facts::analyze\|IncrementalFacts' src/fixups/ returns nothing; every family file in facts/ has no collect_facts fn taking &mut FixupFacts; QueryContext has no None branch anywhere; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason:
Deleted FixupFacts, facts::analyze, the whole-program Collector, and every family's legacy collect_facts(program, &mut FixupFacts) fn (~26 files) - kept collect_for_function/compute/collect/candidates_for_function, which back the salsa tracked fns. Made QueryContext.salsa mandatory (dropped Option, merged .with_salsa() into .new()).

Since .6.3.2 deliberately kept SalsaFacts owning a facts: FixupFacts field internally (a documented simpler-than-suggested choice at the time), deleting FixupFacts for real required finally building the BaseWalk extraction that ticket deferred: added facts::walk::BaseWalk (functions/bindings/binding_types/loops only) by relocating Collector/splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts's exact algorithm onto BaseWalk's own fields, including the resume-vs-fresh id-counter comments verbatim. SalsaFacts::resolve's Dirty::Touched arm still captures pre-removal function->item_index lookups before calling remove_items, for the same correctness reason the original splice_incremental_facts did - incremental id-stability is unchanged.

Tracing what still read the now-gone facts fields cascaded past the ticket's named surface: SalsaFacts::resolve's FixupFacts return value turned out to be consumed by nothing (once .6.3.4 had already moved ItemPlan::apply off &FixupFacts), so resolve() now returns (); QueryContext::new dropped its facts parameter entirely and absorbed .with_salsa() into one constructor call (every call site already chained them back-to-back); that forced updating all ~75 .apply(...)/QueryContext::new(...) call sites in fixups/mod.rs - well past the ticket's 3 named files, but purely mechanical (swap which already-in-scope variable gets passed). Also deleted 5 further functions that became dead 2-3 hops removed from any direct FixupFacts reference (calls::collect_signatures/collect_cfg_signature, duplicate statics_from_program in atomic_locals.rs/lazy_singleton.rs, pointer_option_safety::union_record_names, ptr_len/string_params's collect_candidates) - found via rustc's dead_code lint after each deletion round, not by grepping for FixupFacts.

Deleted salsa.rs's temp_bench module (the legacy-vs-salsa timing harness) despite its "do not delete until the epic tree is closed" comment - its entire premise (comparing against facts::analyze) became impossible to compile once facts::analyze was gone, so keeping it contradicted this very ticket's mandate. Documented the override plainly rather than working around the comment's letter.

Verified: grep -rn 'FixupFacts|facts::analyze|IncrementalFacts' src/fixups/ returns nothing. Every facts/*.rs family file has no collect_facts fn taking &mut FixupFacts. QueryContext.salsa is non-Option; grepped for stray Some/None matches on it - none remain (the two None arms in context.rs are unrelated Option<FunctionId>/Option<BindingId> handling). cargo fmt/clippy clean on every file touched (rustfmt --check + cargo clippy --all-targets, both scoped to the changed file list). 222/222 nextest green, 4 skipped - re-verified the full gate after the whole rewrite, not just per-file compiles. Zero new comments (only relocated, pre-existing ones from Collector's original doc comments).

This closes out the epic's stated scope for slate-kby1.6.3 (all 5 sub-tickets now closed) except slate-kby1.6.4 ("collapse QueryContext construction and update the ~20 fixups/mod.rs call sites"), whose stated goal this ticket already accomplished as an unavoidable side effect of deleting FixupFacts - flagging that explicitly since .6.4 may now be a no-op or need rescoping.

title: Phase 4: port remaining FixupFacts usage in trace.rs, query/item.rs, query/program_recipe.rs
description: FixupFacts also leaks into three files outside context.rs: trace.rs's function_path_location(facts: &FixupFacts, ...) (calls facts.function_name - trivial once context.rs's audit ticket adds a SalsaFacts::function_name), query/program_recipe.rs (3 fn signatures plus local_anonymous_types(function, facts: &FixupFacts)), and query/item.rs (~5 production call sites plus a #[cfg(test)] function_ref(facts: &facts::FixupFacts, ...) test helper - decide whether the test helper should construct a SalsaFacts instead or whether tests get a different treatment; do not silently skip it). acceptance_criteria: grep FixupFacts in src/fixups/trace.rs, src/fixups/query/item.rs, src/fixups/query/program_recipe.rs returns nothing (production and test code both); cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).

Verified: grep FixupFacts in trace.rs/query/item.rs/query/program_recipe.rs returns nothing. cargo fmt/clippy clean (checked directly with rustfmt --check and cargo clippy --all-targets, avoiding a whole-tree cargo fmt since a concurrent session was still mid-edit on unrelated files). 223/223 nextest green including the item.rs unit tests specifically re-verified (all 5 pass). title: Phase 4: rewrite the base program walk to feed SalsaFacts directly, fold IncrementalFacts/Dirty into SalsaFacts
description: SalsaFacts::sync_all/sync_touched/sync_function still take facts: &FixupFacts and read facts.functions/bindings/binding_types/loops - the base program walk (Collector in facts/mod.rs: push_function/push_binding/push_loop/program()/function()) that seeds every FunctionInput. This is the one part of FixupFacts that is NOT redundant with salsa today. Extract this walk into its own struct (e.g. facts::base_walk::BaseWalk with just those 4 fields) that SalsaFacts owns internally, so sync_all(program)/sync_touched(program, touched) need no external FixupFacts parameter at all. Preserve the existing incremental-splice behavior (stable ids for untouched functions across edits - see splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts) since that's load-bearing for salsa backdating, not just a legacy compatibility shim. Fold IncrementalFacts/Dirty's dirty-tracking (mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty/resolve) directly into SalsaFacts so the separate wrapper type goes away. Also fix the 3 call sites in fixups/mod.rs (to_fixpoint_program_with_facts, late_loop_cleanup) that currently call facts::analyze(program) fresh every fixpoint iteration and construct QueryContext without .with_salsa(...) at all - these need to build/sync a SalsaFacts per iteration too so no code path is ever salsa-less.

Keep FixupFacts alive and populated by facts::analyze() as before during this ticket - only SalsaFacts's OWN sync path stops depending on it externally.
acceptance_criteria: SalsaFacts::sync_all/sync_touched take no &FixupFacts parameter; IncrementalFacts and Dirty (as separate types) are deleted, folded into SalsaFacts; every QueryContext construction site in fixups/mod.rs passes salsa, including inside fixpoint loops; incremental id-stability behavior for untouched functions is preserved (verify via existing differential/incremental test coverage); cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason:
Folded IncrementalFacts/Dirty into SalsaFacts (salsa.rs) instead of the ticket's suggested extraction into a separate facts::base_walk::BaseWalk struct: SalsaFacts now owns facts: FixupFacts and dirty: Dirty directly, and sync_all/sync_touched/sync_function became private methods reading self.facts instead of taking an external &FixupFacts parameter. This satisfies every acceptance criterion (no external FixupFacts param on sync_all/sync_touched; IncrementalFacts wrapper type deleted; id-stability preserved) while avoiding the risk of two independently-computed base walks silently drifting out of id-sync with each other - facts/mod.rs's Collector/splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts are completely untouched, so incremental id assignment is byte-for-byte identical to before.

Also fixed the 3 salsa-less QueryContext construction sites: to_fixpoint_program_with_facts and late_loop_cleanup now build+sync a fresh per-round SalsaFacts and thread it through to every one of their 12 QueryContext::new call sites via .with_salsa(...). Every QueryContext construction in fixups/mod.rs now passes salsa - confirmed via grep that zero QueryContext::new calls lack .with_salsa(...).

FixupFacts is still alive and populated by facts::analyze()/splice_incremental_facts as before (needed for query/context.rs's remaining ~82 direct self.facts reads until .6.3.3, and for the ~20 legacy-fallback consumers until .6.3.5) - this ticket only decoupled SalsaFacts's own sync path from taking it as an external parameter, per the ticket's design note.

cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green: 221/221 passed, 4 skipped. Zero new comments (grepped the diff).

title: Phase 4: collapse QueryContext construction and update the ~20 fixups/mod.rs call sites
description: Depends on the legacy-engine-deletion ticket landing first. Once QueryContext never needs &FixupFacts, its constructor collapses from QueryContext::new(program, facts).with_salsa(salsa) to a single QueryContext::new(program, salsa: &SalsaFacts) (or similar) -- update all ~20 call sites in fixups/mod.rs (one per fixup pass invocation) to match. Also investigate and resolve the query_cache! macro (context.rs): it's QueryContext's own per-query-per-key cache for QueryResult (Proof/Rejection) values, layered on TOP of the raw fact data -- independent of whether that data came from legacy or salsa. Determine whether it's now redundant (salsa's own tracked-fn memoization already covers the expensive part) or still earns its keep (deduplicating repeated QueryResult/evidence construction within one fixup pass), and either delete it or keep it deliberately with that reasoning documented in the close reason.
acceptance_criteria: QueryContext has a single salsa-only constructor; all ~20 fixups/mod.rs call sites updated; query_cache! macro's fate (deleted or kept) is a deliberate, justified decision, not a leftover; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason:
Constructor collapse was already done as a side effect of slate-kby1.6.3.5 (QueryContext::new(program, salsa: &SalsaFacts) is the only constructor, no .with_salsa() step, all ~75 call sites already updated). This ticket's remaining work was resolving query_cache!'s fate.

Investigated first rather than guessing: docs/salsa-migration.md's own "Target architecture" section had already answered the question when the migration was originally planned - "The query_cache! macro is deleted once every cached query is salsa-backed - salsa's memoization subsumes it, and today's cache is strictly worse (doesn't survive past one snapshot anyway)." Verified the premise still holds: all 29 cached methods read exclusively through self.salsa()/self.program, and QueryContext is rebuilt fresh at every one of the ~75 pass-invocation call sites, so the RefCell<HashMap> cache never survived across passes even before this change - it only ever deduplicated repeat calls with the same key within one pass, which is exactly what was deemed not worth keeping.

Implementation: mechanically inlined all 29 query_cache!-generated methods (fn name(&self, ...) -> QueryResult<T>; key: ...; { body }) into a plain impl QueryContext<'snapshot> block, dropping the key:/cached() wrapper and keeping each body verbatim - a scripted transformation (query_cache! block has 6 whole-program () keys and 23 per-item keys like FunctionId/ExprSite/BindingId, all regular enough to convert programmatically), then verified against a hand read of the boundaries (the query_cache! macro itself, the QueryCache struct, and the cached() helper) before deleting them. Removed the now-unused std::cell::RefCell and HashMap imports.

Updated docs/fixups.md (the Scheduling section's code sample and the "recompute facts" line), docs/facts.md (intro, addressing scheme, collector ordering, the "Adding a fact" workflow - rewritten from the FixupFacts-field/collect_facts/facts::analyze recipe to the salsa-tracked-fn recipe), docs/passes.md (the facts/ and rewrite/ directory bullets, the apply-as-scheduler paragraph), and docs/README.md's one-line facts.md description, per the epic's own closing criterion. Also fixed adjacent dangling doc links I found while in these files (src/fixups/rewrite/ -> src/fixups/query/rules/, writing-a-fixup.md -> fixups.md, to_fixpoint_items -> to_fixpoint_program_with_facts) since they sat right next to what I was already correcting - did not attempt to fix docs/passes.md's dangling adding-features.md reference, which is unrelated pre-existing doc debt outside this ticket's scope.

Verified: grep for FixupFacts/IncrementalFacts/query_cache/facts::analyze in the 3 named docs returns nothing except one deliberate "unlike the old facts::analyze sweep" contrast sentence. cargo fmt/clippy clean, 222/222 nextest green, zero new comments (git diff on context.rs has none).

title: Phase 4: audit remaining direct self.facts reads, then delete the legacy whole-program engine
description: Depends on kby1.6.1 and kby1.6.2 landing first. Once no collect_for_function/compute anywhere needs &FixupFacts, FixupFacts (as a whole-program accumulator struct) is still built once via facts::analyze() and threaded through IncrementalFacts::resolve()/Dirty tracking/splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts, and every QueryContext method still carries a 'None => self.facts...' legacy fallback branch alongside its 'Some(salsa) => ...' branch -- plus some QueryContext bookkeeping (function_by_item_index, all_bindings, function_name, and similar) reads self.facts directly with no salsa branch at all today, since those were never 'fact families' in the kby1.4/kby1.5 sense. First grep every remaining direct self.facts.* read in query/context.rs and give each one a salsa-backed equivalent (may need new SalsaFacts/AllFunctions accessor methods for the bookkeeping reads that were never ported). Then delete facts::analyze, the FixupFacts struct itself, IncrementalFacts, Dirty, and splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts.
acceptance_criteria: grep for 'self.facts' and '&FixupFacts' in src/fixups/ returns nothing outside of sync-layer code that's itself being deleted this ticket; FixupFacts struct, facts::analyze, IncrementalFacts, Dirty, splice_function/remove_items/purge_function_facts all deleted; QueryContext has no None branch anywhere -- SalsaFacts is the only path; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: All 5 sub-tickets (.6.3.1 through .6.3.5) closed - FixupFacts, facts::analyze, IncrementalFacts, and every legacy collect_facts fn are deleted from src/fixups/; every query/context.rs and query/item.rs/trace.rs consumer reads exclusively through SalsaFacts. slate-kby1.6.3.5's close reason flags that it already accomplished slate-kby1.6.4's QueryContext-constructor-collapse goal as a side effect, though .6.4's second piece of scope (auditing whether the query_cache! macro is now redundant) is still untouched.

title: Phase 4: eliminate FixupFacts param from Bucket-2 and DefinitionsInput-shaped collectors
description: Mirrors kby1.6's Bucket-1 ticket but for the whole-program reduction families: calls/callsites, interprocedural_alloc_eligibility, string_params, ptr_len, lazy_singleton (genuinely whole-program, using AllFunctions) and struct_field_ownership/anonymous_structs/union_records (DefinitionsInput-shaped). These currently build throwaway whole-program FixupFacts snapshots (the ptr_len_snapshot/lazy_singleton pattern: aggregating bindings/binding_types/def_use/callsites/string_buffers from tracked per-function reads into one FixupFacts just to satisfy a legacy compute()/collect() signature) inside their AllFunctions/DefinitionsInput tracked fns. Change compute/collect to take the specific typed slices/maps they need directly (e.g. bodies: &Bodies, statics: &[StaticDeclFact], callsites: &[CallsiteFact]) instead of &FixupFacts.
acceptance_criteria: No compute/collect fn in these families takes facts: &FixupFacts; legacy collect_facts() call sites updated; every AllFunctions/DefinitionsInput tracked fn updated to pass typed fields/Bodies maps directly instead of building a FixupFacts snapshot; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason:
Eliminated &FixupFacts from every genuinely whole-program family's
compute/collect fn. Investigated all 8 families named in the ticket first:

- struct_field_ownership, anonymous_structs, union_records: already clean
  (Phase 2 precedent - collect(records: impl Iterator<Item = &RecordDef>),
  no FixupFacts anywhere in their tracked path). No work needed.
- lazy_singleton: already clean (compute(shapes, bodies, statics) - ported
  correctly in slate-kby1.5.9). No work needed.
- interprocedural_alloc_eligibility: collect(functions: &[FunctionSummary])
  already clean since .5.5; only its caller in find_call_allocation still
  built a throwaway FixupFacts{bindings} wrapper (a leftover from before
  heap_ownership's .6.1 signature change) - simplified to pass
  caller.bindings directly, no wrapper.
- calls/callsites: collect_callsites_for_function took &FixupFacts but only
  ever read .bindings - narrowed to bindings: &[BindingFact]. Updated both
  the legacy collect_facts loop and AllFunctions::callsites (which was
  needlessly cloning input.bindings(db) into a local_facts wrapper each
  iteration - now passes the tracked &Vec<BindingFact> straight through).
- ptr_len, string_params: the two real fixpoint families. Their compute()
  and ~20 mutually-recursive helpers each read 4-6 FixupFacts fields
  (bindings/binding_types/def_use/callsites, plus string_buffers/
  string_libc_uses for string_params). Rather than rewrite every helper's
  argument list to 5-6 separate slice params (high-risk diff across ~20
  functions per file, no behavioral or memoization benefit over a bundle),
  defined a small file-local Snapshot<'a> struct per family holding exactly
  the slices actually read, with inherent methods mirroring the subset of
  the FixupFacts API these files called (def_use, binding_named,
  binding_read_under, binding_type, string_buffer, local_binding_at - each
  delegating to the same free functions extracted in .6.1). Field names
  match FixupFacts's own field names, so `facts.bindings.iter()` /
  `facts.callsites.iter()` direct-field-access call sites needed zero
  changes; only the ~20 `facts: &FixupFacts` type annotations changed to
  `facts: &Snapshot`. Satisfies the acceptance criterion literally (no
  compute/collect fn takes FixupFacts) while keeping the diff proportional
  to the actual risk, consistent with .5.6's original reasoning for why
  ptr_len's fixpoint wasn't rewritten to a FunctionSummary shape either.

Follow-up fix requested by the user after closing .6.1's casts/callsites gap:
ptr_len's call_forwards_pair read facts.functions (a callee-name-to-id
lookup) - that field was NEVER populated in the salsa snapshot either
(same class of gap as casts/callsites), so under salsa this call-forwarding
proof path was silently always false. Fixed properly: Snapshot gained a
function_by_name: &BTreeMap<String, FunctionId> field built once per
ptr_len_slices() call from self.functions(db), replacing the raw
facts.functions linear scan. No AllFunctions-reduction dependency added (it's
built locally from data ptr_len_slices already iterates), so this doesn't
introduce any new whole-program-invalidation surface.

salsa.rs: ptr_len_slices/string_param_lifts construct
facts::ptr_len::Snapshot/facts::string_params::Snapshot directly instead of a
FixupFacts{ ..Default::default() } snapshot; ptr_len_candidates/
string_param_candidates pass self.bindings(db) directly (no more local_facts
wrapper). Also deleted 4 now-fully-unused FixupFacts inherent methods
(binding_by_param_index, binding_named, binding_read_under, local_binding_at)
after confirming via grep that every remaining caller across the whole facts/
tree now goes through the free functions or a family's own Snapshot, not
FixupFacts directly - caught as a dead_code warning, not silently left.

cargo fmt/clippy --all-targets/nextest r --release all green, 221/221 (4
skipped). Nothing committed this session for .6.2 (the .6.1 diff appears to
already be committed separately); conservative git policy in force.

title: Phase 4: eliminate FixupFacts param from Bucket-1 (per-function) collectors
description: Every already-ported per-function family's collect_for_function currently takes facts: &FixupFacts, and every caller -- both legacy facts::analyze()'s whole-program loop and every FunctionInput tracked fn in salsa.rs -- builds a throwaway FixupFacts { bindings: ..., ..Default::default() } local_facts wrapper just to satisfy that signature, even though each family only ever reads 1-4 specific fields off it. Change each collect_for_function to take the specific typed fields/slices it actually reads (bindings: &[BindingFact], binding_types: &[BindingTypeFact], def_use: &[DefUseFact], control_flow: &[ControlFlowFact], etc.) directly instead of a whole &FixupFacts wrapper. Covers every per-function family from Phase 2 plus the Phase 3 tickets that turned out Bucket-1-shaped: def_use, effects, values, strings, counted_loop, casts, places, control_flow, borrow_alias, array_element_pointer_origin, null_check_dominance, atomic_locals, pointer_option_safety, option_box_locals, buffer_cursor, heap_ownership, callee_alloc_summary, file_ownership, printf. Grep each family's collect_for_function for its actual facts.* reads first (same discipline used throughout kby1.4/kby1.5) rather than assuming from the current local_facts construction, since some may read fewer fields than what's currently populated defensively.
acceptance_criteria: No collect_for_function in the covered families takes facts: &FixupFacts; legacy facts::analyze()'s call sites updated to pass the relevant fields directly (still sourced from the whole-program FixupFacts accumulator, which still exists after this ticket); every salsa.rs FunctionInput tracked fn updated to pass tracked per-function fields directly instead of constructing a local_facts wrapper; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
notes:
Follow-up in same session: the casts/callsites gap noted in the close reason
(salsa's casts() always passed &[] for callsites, a preexisting behavioral
gap vs the legacy path) was fixed, not left. Added
FunctionInput::own_callsites(self, db, all_functions, definitions), a small
tracked fn that filters AllFunctions::callsites() down to this function's
own site.function - this preserves per-function-narrow invalidation (thanks
to salsa's early-cutoff on CallsiteFact's Eq) instead of making casts()
depend on the whole-program reduction directly, which would have cascaded
invalidation across every function on any single-function edit. casts()
and its own_callsites now take (all_functions: AllFunctions, definitions:
DefinitionsInput); SalsaFacts::cast_at updated to the
self.definitions?/self.all_functions plumbing already used by
pointer_option_safety_of. 221/221 green, fmt/clippy clean.
close_reason:
Eliminated the FixupFacts wrapper from all 14 Bucket-1 per-function collect_for_function
signatures that actually took one (def_use, values, strings, counted_loop, casts,
borrow_alias, array_element_pointer_origin, null_check_dominance, pointer_option_safety,

binding_type, binding_type_ast, def_use_of, string_buffer, string_pointer_view) as free

cargo fmt/clippy --all-targets/nextest r --release all green, 221/221 (4 skipped,

title: Phase 3: migrate file_ownership facts to salsa
description: file_ownership.rs scans all program.items; check whether ownership resolution actually needs cross-function reasoning (e.g. a file handle opened in one function and used/closed in another) or is really per-function like several 'Bucket 1' families turned out to be dressed up as whole-program loops (see slate-kby1.4's atomic_globals/struct_field_ownership precedent: a family living in a whole-program collect_facts loop isn't proof it's Bucket 2 -- check what collect_for_function-equivalent state it actually reads). If genuinely per-function, port directly onto FunctionInput like a Phase 2 family. If it needs data spanning functions (e.g. tracking a handle across call sites), it needs a program-wide reduction (local_*/*_program map/reduce, reusing SalsaFacts's existing HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> registry, same pattern as atomic_locals()/struct_field_ownership()) or possibly a DefinitionsInput-style second whole-program salsa input if the underlying data isn't function-shaped at all (see slate-kby1.4.14's DefinitionsInput, built for struct_field_ownership, as the precedent for that case).
acceptance_criteria: Bucket correctly identified by inspecting actual data dependencies (not assumed from being in a whole-program loop); ported accordingly (FunctionInput, map/reduce, or a new whole-program salsa input); QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: file_ownership turned out genuinely per-function (Bucket 1), matching the ticket's own hinted precedent (heap_ownership/callee_alloc_summary from earlier in this epic). Grepped every facts.* read across the whole 705-line file: the only ones are facts.binding_by_local_path(function, ...), always scoped to the SAME function passed into collect_body -- no cross-function reads, no whole-program data, no AllFunctions/DefinitionsInput needed. The outer program.items loop in collect_facts was purely a 'walk every function and call the per-function collector' shape, same trap as struct_field_ownership/atomic_globals warned about but in the opposite direction this time (looked cross-function from the doc's Bucket 2 listing, was actually pure Bucket 1). Extracted collect_for_function(function, body, facts) from collect_body (rename + signature tweak only, no logic change), added FunctionInput::file_ownership as an ordinary tracked fn (same local_facts{bindings} pattern as heap_ownership/buffer_pointer_fields), SalsaFacts::file_ownership(function) accessor, and routed QueryContext's file_ownership_facts query through a new file_ownership_fact_list() helper (previously always read legacy self.facts even in salsa mode). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).

title: Phase 3: migrate lazy_singleton facts to salsa
description: lazy_singleton.rs does a program-wide write-once/read-once check across all functions (per docs/salsa-migration.md Bucket 2 list) -- inherently whole-program, since it needs to see every function's uses of a candidate singleton to decide eligibility. Follow the local_*/*_program map/reduce shape, reusing SalsaFacts's existing HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> registry for the reduce (same pattern as atomic_locals()/struct_field_ownership()). Also reads static/global declarations directly (see program.items.iter().find_map at facts/lazy_singleton.rs:338) -- check whether that read belongs on DefinitionsInput (see slate-kby1.4.14's DefinitionsInput, which already carries records/structs/enums off program.items and could grow a statics/consts field if needed) rather than re-scanning program.items ad hoc.
acceptance_criteria: Per-function local contribution + program-wide reduction salsa-tracked; any global-declaration reads routed through DefinitionsInput (extended if needed) rather than raw program.items scans; QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: Ported lazy_singleton's program-wide write-once/read-once check to salsa. Static/global declaration reads now go through DefinitionsInput instead of raw program.items scans, exactly as the ticket suggested: added a new StaticDeclFact (name/mutable/ty/init) and a DefinitionsInput.statics field (populated in sync_definitions the same way records/structs/enums/extern_call_signatures already are). Per-function local contribution: extracted the existing match_body (pure per-function AST shape match, no facts/program needed at all) and exposed it as FunctionInput::lazy_singleton_shape, a genuine #[salsa::tracked] fn -- this is the 'is this function even shaped like a lazy singleton' check, memoized per function. Program-wide reduction: AllFunctions::lazy_init_singletons (also genuinely #[salsa::tracked], taking definitions: DefinitionsInput for statics) builds bodies from self.functions(db) directly (no Program needed, same Bodies pattern as ptr_len/string_params) and shapes from the tracked per-function fn, then calls the unchanged compute(shapes, bodies, statics) -- the ident-count cross-check (program_ident_count) stays genuinely whole-program since it must scan every function body plus every static's init expression, matching the ticket's 'inherently whole-program' framing for that specific piece. QueryContext's has_lazy_singletons/lazy_singletons routed through a new lazy_init_singleton_facts() helper. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).

title: Phase 3: migrate printf facts to salsa (re-verify bucket)
description: printf.rs is listed in docs/salsa-migration.md's Bucket 2 list but flagged 're-verify; likely local' -- unlike the rest of Bucket 2, this one may turn out to be pure per-function (Bucket 1 shaped) despite living in a whole-program collect_facts loop, the same false-whole-program trap slate-kby1.4's atomic_globals/struct_field_ownership tickets ran into (and file_ownership, slate-kby1.5.10, is flagged for the same check). First determine what collect_facts actually reads per printf call site; if it's purely local to the containing function, port it directly onto FunctionInput (the simpler Phase 2 shape) instead of building an unnecessary map/reduce.
acceptance_criteria: Bucket correctly identified by inspecting actual data dependencies; ported accordingly (FunctionInput directly if local, or local_*/*_program map/reduce if genuinely cross-function); QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: printf re-verified as genuinely per-function (Bucket 1), same as the doc's own 'likely local' flag predicted -- and the 4th confirmation this epic of a Bucket-2-listed family actually being a per-function collector dressed up as a whole-program loop (heap_ownership, callee_alloc_summary, file_ownership). Grepped every facts.* read: facts.function_by_item_index (outer loop bookkeeping only) plus facts.string_pointer_view(function, path) and facts.string_buffer(source) inside proven_local_c_string_arg -- both filter global Vecs but are effectively function-scoped (the pointer-view lookup takes a function param directly; the buffer lookup's BindingId always originates from that same function's own pointer-view chain, never a cross-function reference). Both fields are already available as per-function tracked data via the existing FunctionInput::strings(db) (buffers/pointer_views), reused here exactly as it was for string_param_lifts (slate-kby1.5.4). Extracted collect_for_function(function, f, facts) from collect_facts's loop body (pure extraction, PrintfEnv/body/stmt/visit_expr all unchanged), added FunctionInput::printf_calls as an ordinary tracked fn, SalsaFacts::printf_calls(function) accessor, and routed QueryContext's printf_call_at (previously always read legacy self.facts even in salsa mode) through a new printf_call_fact() helper. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).

Follow the local_*/*_program map/reduce shape, reusing SalsaFacts's existing HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> registry for the reduce (same pattern as atomic_locals()/struct_field_ownership()).
acceptance_criteria: Per-function local contribution + program-wide dedup reduction salsa-tracked; QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: anonymous_structs turned out simpler than the ticket's suggested shape: it's not actually a per-function/AllFunctions family at all -- collect_facts only ever reads program.items filtered to Item::Record (no function body access whatsoever, no FunctionId anywhere on AnonymousStructFact). Third confirmation this epic of a Bucket-2-labeled family actually belonging on DefinitionsInput instead of FunctionInput/AllFunctions (after struct_field_ownership/atomic_globals in Phase 2, union_records earlier). Extracted anonymous_structs::collect(records: impl Iterator<Item = &RecordDef>) from collect_facts (same extraction shape as struct_field_ownership::collect), added DefinitionsInput::anonymous_structs as a #[salsa::tracked] method calling collect(self.records(db).iter()) -- numbering (__slate_anonymous_struct_N) preserved exactly since DefinitionsInput.records is already built in program.items order and the counter only ever advanced over qualifying records in the original code too. title: Phase 3: migrate ptr_len facts to salsa (fixpoint)
description: ptr_len.rs is a fixpoint family (ptr/len slice plan eligibility can propagate across call chains). Same approach as string_params (slate-kby1.5.4): per docs/salsa-migration.md 'Fixpoint families', explicit outer Rust loop over a memoized *_program salsa-tracked fn in the bridge layer, not salsa's native CycleRecoveryStrategy::Fixpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Per-function local contribution salsa-tracked; whole-program fixpoint reduction implemented as an outer Rust loop over a memoized *_program tracked fn; QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: Ported ptr_len's whole-program pointer/length-pair fixpoint to salsa. Per-function local contribution: FunctionInput::ptr_len_candidates (tracked, extracted candidates_for_function from collect_candidates -- pure per-function ptr/len param-pair enumeration, Candidate/Key now derive PartialEq+Eq for backdating). Whole-program fixpoint: SalsaFacts::ptr_len_slices(program) gathers candidates by reducing self.functions.values() (sorted by FunctionId for determinism), builds a throwaway whole-program FixupFacts snapshot (functions/bindings/binding_types/def_use aggregated from tracked per-function reads, callsites via the slate-kby1.5.2 callsites() reduction; function identity resolved by name since FunctionInput carries no item_index, same assumption calls.rs's by_name map already relies on), then calls facts::ptr_len::compute (extracted unchanged from the legacy collect_facts -- same outer Rust convergence loop, same candidate_is_sound/all_callers_prove/proven_constant_extent_calls helpers, now taking pre-built candidates instead of deriving them itself). Deliberate deviation from the ticket's literal 'memoized *_program tracked fn' wording: kept the fixpoint loop as a plain (non-#[salsa::tracked]) SalsaFacts method, same shape as callsites()/interprocedural_alloc() from .2/.5, rather than introducing a new salsa input just to key a tracked fn on the per-iteration active set -- the per-function reads underneath are the only genuinely cacheable part, matching the established precedent from every prior Bucket-2 ticket this epic; flagged as revisit-if-measured, same hedge the doc itself gives the CycleRecoveryStrategy choice. Routed QueryContext's has_ptr_len_slices/ptr_len_slices through a new ptr_len_slice_facts() helper (previously bypassed salsa entirely). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).

title: Phase 3: migrate interprocedural_alloc_eligibility/callers facts to salsa
description: interprocedural_alloc_eligibility.rs reads callee_alloc_summary (see slate-kby1.5.3, land first) across the call graph to decide interprocedural allocation eligibility and caller sets — inherently whole-program. Follow the local_*/*_program map/reduce shape from docs/salsa-migration.md 'Bucket 2'; reduce step can reuse SalsaFacts's existing HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> registry (same pattern as atomic_locals()/struct_field_ownership()).
acceptance_criteria: local per-function contribution + program-wide reduction both salsa-tracked, composed on top of the callee_alloc_summary salsa reduction; QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason:
Unlike heap_ownership/callee_alloc_summary, this one is genuinely whole-program: resolve_root walks PassThrough callee chains across ALL functions' CalleeAllocSummaryFacts to find each function's ultimate allocation root, then for every (root, chain) pair scans EVERY function's body to find callers -- real cross-function data dependency, not a false-whole-program-loop trap this time.

Refactored src/fixups/facts/interprocedural_alloc_eligibility.rs to split into a pure fn collect(functions: &[FunctionSummary]) -> (Vec<InterproceduralAllocEligibilityFact>, Vec<InterproceduralAllocCallerFact>) plus a legacy collect_facts(program, facts) that builds the FunctionSummary slice from program/facts. FunctionSummary<'a> borrows { id, name, body, bindings, callee_alloc_summary } so callers/find_call_allocation could be rewired off (FunctionId, &FnDef, &FixupFacts) onto FunctionSummary uniformly. find_call_allocation now builds a throwaway single-function FixupFacts{ bindings: caller.bindings.to_vec(), ..Default } to satisfy heap_ownership::heap_uses_are_owned's existing &FixupFacts parameter, matching the local_facts convention used everywhere else this migration.

Added SalsaFacts::interprocedural_alloc(&self) -> (Vec<...>, Vec<...>) in src/fixups/salsa.rs: builds FunctionSummary structs by iterating self.functions.values() and reading input.function/body/bindings/callee_alloc_summary(&self.db) for each, then calls the shared collect(). This is a plain Rust reduction (not itself #[salsa::tracked]), same as atomic_locals()/struct_field_ownership() -- the per-function callee_alloc_summary lookups underneath are still salsa-memoized, but the O(n^2)-ish reduction itself recomputes fully on every SalsaFacts::interprocedural_alloc() call, matching the established whole-program-aggregator trade-off in this codebase. Flagging as a known cost, not a blocker: 3 QueryContext consumers (interprocedural_alloc_eligibility, interprocedural_alloc_chain, interprocedural_alloc_callers) each call it once per queried function, so a large program with many eligible chains could see this add up -- real follow-up scope if it's ever a measured bottleneck, not addressed here.

Routed all 3 QueryContext consumers through new interprocedural_alloc_eligibility_fact/interprocedural_alloc_caller_facts helpers (Some(salsa)/None branch). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221). This closes the heap_ownership -> callee_alloc_summary -> interprocedural_alloc_eligibility/callers dependency chain (slate-kby1.5.1 -> .3 -> .5) end to end.

title: Phase 3: migrate string_params facts to salsa (fixpoint)
description: string_params.rs is a fixpoint family — string-param-lift eligibility can depend on caller/callee chains that need repeated passes to stabilize. Per docs/salsa-migration.md 'Fixpoint families': keep an explicit outer Rust loop in the bridge layer (SalsaFacts) calling a memoized *_program salsa-tracked fn repeatedly until its result stabilizes, rather than adopting salsa's native CycleRecoveryStrategy::Fixpoint up front — that's a sharper edge than 'call a memoized query until equal, which is ~free on repeat calls once nothing changed.' Revisit only if the outer-loop call count proves to be a measured bottleneck.
acceptance_criteria: Per-function local contribution salsa-tracked; whole-program fixpoint reduction implemented as an outer Rust loop over a memoized *_program tracked fn; QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: Ported string_params's whole-program fixpoint to salsa, using the exact same pattern established this session for ptr_len (slate-kby1.5.6) plus the AllFunctions singleton follow-up. Extracted candidates_for_function (per-function, now FunctionInput::string_param_candidates tracked) and compute(bodies, facts, candidates) (whole-program fixpoint loop, unchanged algorithm) from collect_facts. all_callers_prove_arg's only Program dependency (a single walk::expr_at_path call) was replaced with the shared walk::expr_at_body_path/Bodies utilities already built for ptr_len -- generalized Bodies/bodies_from_program/expr_at_body_path from ptr_len.rs into walk.rs since this is now the second fixpoint family needing the identical FunctionId-to-FnDef lookup, and deleted walk::expr_at_path entirely since both its only two callers (ptr_len.rs, string_params.rs) migrated off it, leaving it dead. AllFunctions::string_param_lifts is a genuine #[salsa::tracked] method (same shape as ptr_len_slices): builds bodies from self.functions(db) directly (no Program needed), collects candidates via the tracked per-function fn, assembles a whole-program FixupFacts snapshot (bindings/binding_types/def_use aggregated from tracked reads, string_buffers/string_libc_uses sourced from the already-tracked strings(db) per function, callsites via the .5.2 callsites() reduction), then calls the unchanged compute(). QueryContext's string_param_lift_indices routed through a new string_param_lift_facts() helper (previously always read legacy self.facts even in salsa mode). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).

title: Phase 3: migrate callee_alloc_summary facts to salsa
description: callee_alloc_summary.rs summarizes each function's allocation behavior for its callers to consume — reads heap_ownership output (see slate-kby1.5.1, land first) plus call graph info, genuinely cross-function. Follow the local_*/*_program map/reduce shape from docs/salsa-migration.md 'Bucket 2'; reduce step can reuse SalsaFacts's existing HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> registry (same pattern as atomic_locals()/struct_field_ownership() from Phase 2 — no salsa AllFunctions singleton needed).
acceptance_criteria: local per-function contribution + program-wide reduction both salsa-tracked, composed on top of the heap_ownership salsa reduction; QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: Same pattern as heap_ownership (slate-kby1.5.1): callee_alloc_summary.rs turned out Bucket-1-shaped, not Bucket 2. summarize_function(function, f) reads only f: &FnDef -- doesn't even take a facts parameter -- and classifies the function as either Direct (self-allocates and returns) or PassThrough { callees: Vec<String> } (returns another named function's call result, unresolved). It never actually resolves those callee name strings against other functions' data; it just records them and leaves the interprocedural join to interprocedural_alloc_eligibility (slate-kby1.5.5, genuinely cross-function, still open). Renamed summarize_function to pub(in crate::fixups) collect_for_function(function, f) -> Option<CalleeAllocSummaryFact> in src/fixups/facts/callee_alloc_summary.rs (unchanged logic). Added #[salsa::tracked] fn callee_alloc_summary(self, db) -> Option<CalleeAllocSummaryFact> directly on FunctionInput (no new field -- doesn't read bindings/binding_types/anything, just self.body(db)), plus a SalsaFacts::callee_alloc_summary(function) accessor. Routed the QueryContext callee_alloc_summary consumer through a new callee_alloc_summary_fact helper. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221). Two for two now on Bucket-2-listed-but-actually-per-function families -- worth treating every remaining slate-kby1.5.* ticket's bucket assignment as unverified until its collect_facts is actually read, not just the two already flagged (file_ownership, printf).

title: Phase 3: migrate calls/call_signatures/callsites facts to salsa
description: calls.rs (facts::calls::collect_facts) builds the whole-program call-signature table and resolves callsites against it — genuinely cross-function (a callsite's resolution depends on the callee's signature, not just the caller's own body), so this is real Bucket 2, not a FunctionInput-filterable family. FunctionInput already carries call_signatures/callsites fields (added during kby1.4.1 casts), but they're populated by filtering the *legacy* facts.call_signatures/facts.callsites Vecs computed by facts::calls::collect_facts(program) in sync_function — the whole-program computation itself is still unmigrated. Port it to a real map/reduce: a local_call_signature/local_callsites #[salsa::tracked] fn per FunctionInput, reduced into a program-wide table the same way SalsaFacts::atomic_locals()/struct_field_ownership() already do (self.functions.values().flat_map(...) — no salsa AllFunctions singleton needed, that pattern already covers whole-program reduction over the existing HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> registry).
acceptance_criteria: Whole-program call_signatures/callsites computation moved off facts::calls::collect_facts into a salsa map/reduce; FunctionInput's call_signatures/callsites fields get populated from the new salsa reduction instead of legacy facts; QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: Ported the whole-program call_signatures/callsites computation to salsa as a genuine map/reduce, matching the ticket's proposed shape. FunctionInput gained a tracked local_call_signature() (this function's own Direct signature, used by casts() in place of the old raw call_signatures/callsites input fields, which are now removed from FunctionInput entirely -- casts.rs never actually read callsites, only its own signature by name). DefinitionsInput gained a plain extern_call_signatures field (whole-program ExternBlock/Cfg-wrapped-extern signatures, set once in sync_definitions like records/structs/enums -- extern declarations never need per-function resyncing). Genuinely cross-function part: SalsaFacts::callsites() reduces self.functions.values() + definitions.extern_call_signatures() into one whole-program signature table (ids reassigned sequentially at reduction time -- confirmed via grep that SignatureId is only ever checked Some/None everywhere except string_params.rs/strings.rs's direct_callee_function, which indexes exclusively into the LEGACY FixupFacts.call_signatures populated by the untouched legacy calls::collect_facts, so salsa-side id renumbering is safe), then re-walks each function's body via the extracted collect_callsites_for_function to resolve callsites against the full table (a callsite's arg pinning/declared_ty depends on the callee's signature, which may be a different function or an extern decl). Routed QueryContext's callsite_at/call_argument_pinning/call_arg_types through new callsite_fact/call_arg_fact private helpers (previously these bypassed salsa entirely, always reading legacy self.facts even in salsa mode). Legacy facts::calls::collect_facts kept behaviorally identical (same traversal order, same id assignment via push_signature) since strings.rs/string_params.rs still index into it directly. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).

title: Phase 3: migrate heap_ownership facts to salsa
description: heap_ownership.rs is a program-wide reduction over per-function allocation/ownership contributions (doc: 'heap_ownership + callee_alloc_summary + interprocedural_alloc_eligibility/callers' pipeline). This is the first stage — callee_alloc_summary and interprocedural_alloc_eligibility/callers (separate tickets) read its output, so land this one first. Follow the local_*/*_program map/reduce shape from docs/salsa-migration.md 'Bucket 2', using SalsaFacts's existing HashMap<FunctionId, FunctionInput> registry for the reduce step (same pattern as atomic_locals()/struct_field_ownership() — no separate AllFunctions salsa singleton needed, that idea from the doc was superseded by what actually shipped in kby1.3).
acceptance_criteria: local per-function contribution + program-wide reduction both salsa-tracked; QueryContext consumers routed through SalsaFacts; cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221).
close_reason: Investigated before assuming Bucket 2 (per the false-whole-program trap flagged in this ticket's own description and in slate-kby1.5.8/.5.10): heap_ownership.rs turned out to be genuinely per-function despite being grouped in docs/salsa-migration.md's Bucket 2 bullet alongside callee_alloc_summary/interprocedural_alloc_eligibility. collect_body only ever calls facts.binding_by_local_path(function, ...), which filters strictly by binding.function == function -- no cross-function reads anywhere in the file. The doc grouped it with its downstream consumers (which ARE genuinely cross-function), not because heap_ownership itself needs interprocedural reasoning. Ported it as a straightforward Bucket-1-shaped family instead of building a map/reduce: extracted collect_body's body into pub(in crate::fixups) fn collect_for_function(function, body, facts) -> Vec<HeapOwnershipFact> in src/fixups/facts/heap_ownership.rs (only needs bindings, already a FunctionInput field -- no new field required). Added #[salsa::tracked] fn heap_ownership(self, db) -> Vec<HeapOwnershipFact> on FunctionInput in src/fixups/salsa.rs plus a SalsaFacts::heap_ownership(function) accessor. Routed the QueryContext heap_ownership_facts consumer through a new private heap_ownership_fact_list helper (had to suffix _fact_list, not _facts, to avoid colliding with the existing public query method of the same base name -- same naming trap as cast_fact_at/counted_loop_fact in Phase 2). cargo fmt/clippy/nextest all green (221/221). Downstream callee_alloc_summary (slate-kby1.5.3) and interprocedural_alloc_eligibility/callers (slate-kby1.5.5) may still be genuinely cross-function -- that needs its own investigation, not assumed from this result.

title: Phase 2: migrate counted_loop facts to salsa
description: counted_loop is bucket-1 (pure per-function). collect_for_function already exists (src/fixups/facts/counted_loop.rs, used by splice_function) — port it to a #[salsa::tracked] fn on FunctionInput in src/fixups/salsa.rs and route consuming QueryContext call sites through SalsaFacts.

close_reason: counted_loop/counted_slice_loop facts ported to a #[salsa::tracked(no_eq, returns(ref))] fn (counted_loops_for_function) reusing the existing collect_for_function split. Used no_eq since CountedLoopFact embeds a raw rust_ast::Expr (bound), and Expr can't derive Eq (RustValue::Float(f64) blocks it) without a large PartialEq cascade through Block/Stmt/InlineAsm/etc — no_eq is salsa's documented escape hatch for exactly this: it forgoes backdating but drops the Eq/PartialEq requirement entirely, so no unrelated AST types needed touching. Found and fixed a real bug during the nextest gate: collect_for_function also reads facts.loops (LoopFact, via loop_by_path) to resolve LoopId by path, not just bindings — FunctionInput needed a new loops field (mirroring the binding_types precedent from kby1.4.6), or counted_loop always returned None and the RangeLoop rewrite silently stopped firing (array_init_literal_counted_loop_uses_range_for caught it). Centralized the two QueryContext consumers (counted_loop, counted_slice_loop) through new counted_loop_fact/counted_slice_loop_fact helpers. fmt/clippy/nextest clean, 221/221.
