Out of scope: a generic/derived matcher mechanism (Matchable derive) - matcher-plan.md already called this "scope this down" until hand-written matcher structs are repetitive across 3+ item kinds; right now there's exactly one candidate (ExternFnMatch), so a reflection layer would be premature.
acceptance_criteria:
- dead_local and sole_use predicates are gone, replaced by no_reads/no_writes/sole_read composed directly in dead_locals.rs's and final_return_temps.rs's rule cases.
- never_returning_extern is gone, replaced by an ExternFnMatch<Cx> matcher struct (built from Field<T,Cx>) and a QueryContext method that takes it and returns a cached QueryResult; libc_exit.rs's rule case composes name/arity/returns explicitly via the matcher.
- No new generic/derive matcher mechanism introduced - hand-written matcher structs only, matching existing patterns.rs precedent.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass; full differential suite output identical to before this change (pure internal refactor, no behavior change).
close_reason: All four children complete: .10.1 (dead_local/sole_use decomposition, superseded by the later Value/Local matcher work), .10.2 (ExternFn matcher replacing never_returning_extern), .10.3 (FnCall matcher generalizing CallRule candidate selection), .10.4 (Definition matcher generalizing DefinitionRule candidate selection). The query engine's rule-selection layer is now uniformly matcher-driven: CallRule::matches(FnCall), DefinitionRule::matches(Definition), StmtWindowRule::matching_local(Local), and case-level predicates like extern_fn(ExternFn) all compose from the same Field<T,Cx> combinator, replacing the earlier one-constructor-per-shape and bundled-predicate APIs. Full differential gate clean throughout (191 passed, 2 skipped).

title: Generalize the diagnostic consistency check to cover every resolve() call
description:
Why: .8.3's diagnostic-only check (FixupFacts::diff_incremental, slate verify-incremental-facts, tests/incremental_facts_regression.rs) only verified the two hand-picked splice sites .8.4 wired up (LazySingleton, RangeLoop's no-op-changed path). Now that .9.2 makes every fact-needing point in the pipeline go through incremental.resolve(), the diagnostic should cover all of them uniformly, not just two.

What to do: update the verification hook (verify_incremental_facts/IncrementalFactsReport in fixups/mod.rs) to instrument IncrementalFacts::resolve itself (or wrap every resolve() call site) so that whenever a Touched(set) resolution happens, it's compared against a full facts::analyze of the same post-edit program - same diff_incremental-based comparison as before, just triggered generically instead of at two hand-picked call sites. Everything resolutions need no check (they already recompute via full facts::analyze, nothing to compare against).

Verify via:
- slate verify-incremental-facts <file.c> on a few manually chosen fixtures spanning several different migrated/legacy step transitions (not just LazySingleton/RangeLoop).
- cargo nextest r --release --test incremental_facts_regression --run-ignored=all across the whole fixture corpus - expect the same 238/240 baseline (the 2 failures are the pre-existing c23-args gap, unrelated).
- Full cargo nextest r --release (191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output).

Update matcher-plan.md's "Verification" section if the mechanism ends up differing from what's currently described there.
close_reason: Cancelled per explicit user direction: the full differential suite (cargo nextest r --release) is sufficient verification for this mechanism swap - no separate diagnostic-only consistency check needed beyond what .8.3 already built. .9.2's acceptance criteria (byte-identical differential output) stands as the verification bar.

title: Rewire fixups/mod.rs to thread one IncrementalFacts through apply_with_logger
description:
Why: this is where the payoff lands - replacing ad hoc facts::analyze rebindings and .8.4's hand-picked LazySingleton/RangeLoop splice special-casing with the uniform IncrementalFacts mechanism from .9.1.

What to do: apply_with_logger currently rebinds `let facts::AnalyzedProgram { facts, .. } = facts::analyze(&program);` about 20 times by hand, plus has bespoke splice-vs-analyze logic for LazySingleton and RangeLoop from .8.4 (including RangeLoop's special-case around late_loop_cleanup). Replace all of this with:

- One `let mut incremental = IncrementalFacts::from(facts::analyze(&input).facts);` (or equivalent) constructed once near the top of apply_with_logger.
- Every migrated (query-engine) step calls `incremental.mark_touched(&report.touched)` after plan.apply() - uniformly, not just for LazySingleton/RangeLoop.
- Every legacy (Fixup-trait) step, and late_loop_cleanup, calls `incremental.mark_everything_dirty()` when it reports changed - uniformly, replacing RangeLoop's late_loop_cleanup special-case with the same generic treatment every legacy mutation gets.
- Every place that currently does `let facts::AnalyzedProgram { facts, .. } = facts::analyze(&program);` to get facts for the next step instead does `let facts = incremental.resolve(&program);`.
- Delete .8.4's splice_incremental_facts helper and the LazySingleton/RangeLoop-specific Option<TouchedItems> plumbing (lazy_singleton_touched, range_loop_touched) - fully subsumed.
- verify_incremental_facts/IncrementalFactsReport (the .8.3 diagnostic hook) needs updating to call into the new resolve() path instead of its own splice_incremental_facts copy - coordinate with .9.3, or do a minimal compatible update here and let .9.3 generalize it further.

Acceptance: cargo nextest r --release produces byte-identical output to before this change (same bar .8.4 used) - this is a pure internal-mechanism swap. cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets clean.
close_reason:
Rewired apply_with_logger to thread one IncrementalFacts (from .9.1) through the whole pipeline, replacing all ~20 manual `let facts::AnalyzedProgram { facts, .. } = facts::analyze(&program);` rebindings with `let facts = incremental.resolve(&program);`, and deleting .8.4's hand-picked LazySingleton/RangeLoop splice-vs-analyze special-casing entirely (the lazy_singleton_touched/range_loop_touched Option<TouchedItems> plumbing and their match blocks are gone).

Pattern applied uniformly to every step:
- Every migrated (query-engine Plan-based) step - AnonymousStructs, LazySingleton, MemchrPreludeFixupCalls, MemchrPrelude, RangeLoop (only on its no-op-changed path), LibcExit, PruneUnusedDefinitions - captures `let report = plan.apply(...)` and calls `incremental.mark_touched(&report.touched)`. This is now uniform across all 7 migrated steps, not just the 2 .8.4 hand-picked.
- Every legacy (Fixup-trait) step calls `incremental.mark_everything_dirty()` unconditionally as the last statement in its block (naturally gated by the step! macro's `run` check, so it only fires when the step actually executes) - matching today's actual behavior exactly, since the pre-existing code already blindly reanalyzed at every fact-consuming point regardless of whether intervening steps changed anything.
- RangeLoop's late_loop_cleanup hazard (mutates arbitrary functions without reporting what) is now handled by the same generic split every migrated step could hit: if report.changed (meaning late_loop_cleanup ran), mark_everything_dirty(); else mark_touched(&report.touched). No RangeLoop-specific code path anymore - it's the same two-branch pattern any future migrated step with a similar hazard would use.
- MemchrPreludeFixupCalls/MemchrPrelude/LibcExit's previously-internal `facts::analyze` calls (self-contained within their step bodies) now go through `incremental.resolve(&program)` too, so these three also benefit from splicing if they ever end up adjacent to another migrated step with nothing legacy in between.

Removed the .8.3 diagnostic infrastructure per explicit user direction (differential tests are sufficient verification for this mechanism, no separate diagnostic-only check needed): `fixups::verify_incremental_facts`, `IncrementalFactsReport`, the `slate verify-incremental-facts` CLI command in main.rs, and tests/incremental_facts_regression.rs (plus its Cargo.toml [[test]] entry) are all deleted. `FixupFacts::diff_incremental` itself (the comparison primitive) was left alone since it's not exclusively coupled to the deleted CLI/test surface, but nothing calls it anymore after this cleanup - noting this in case it becomes genuinely dead and worth removing in a future pass.

Verified via the full differential suite: cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output to before this change, confirming the uniform IncrementalFacts mechanism produces exactly the same program transformations as the old hand-audited per-step-pair logic across every step transition in the pipeline, not just the two .8.4 covered. cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt clean throughout.

Also spot-checked cargo run -- translate on a few fixtures spanning different step transitions (add.c, lazy_singleton.c, range_loop_local_array.c) - all translate cleanly with no panics.

The epic's main promised payoff now holds: any future pass migration under slate-04q.75 that ends up adjacent to another migrated step (nothing legacy between them) gets the splice-instead-of-analyze treatment automatically via mark_touched/resolve, with zero additional wiring in fixups/mod.rs - no more per-pair auditing needed.

title: Add IncrementalFacts type: Dirty marker, mark_touched, mark_everything_dirty, resolve
description:
Why: this is the core mechanism slate-04q.75.56.9 needs - a single place that owns the splice-vs-analyze decision instead of it being hand-audited per call site.

What to do: add a new type (proposed name IncrementalFacts, likely in src/fixups/facts/mod.rs alongside FixupFacts) wrapping a FixupFacts plus a Dirty marker enum with three states: Clean, Touched(TouchedItems), Everything.

- mark_touched(&mut self, touched: &TouchedItems): unions touched.in_place/removed into the existing Touched set (or escalates to Everything if touched.unbounded, or if the current state is already Everything - Everything is absorbing). Cheap, no recompute.
- mark_everything_dirty(&mut self): sets the marker to Everything unconditionally.
- resolve(&mut self, program: &Program) -> &FixupFacts: the only place recompute happens. Clean is a no-op. Touched(set) splices via the existing FixupFacts::remove_items (for the removed set) then FixupFacts::splice_function per in-place item (reusing the exact logic already proven as fixups/mod.rs's splice_incremental_facts helper from .8.4 - move/adapt that helper's logic in here rather than duplicating it). Everything falls back to a full facts::analyze(program) and replaces self.facts entirely. Either way, clears the marker to Clean before returning.

This ticket only adds the type and its logic - do not wire it into fixups/mod.rs yet (that's a separate ticket, .9.2), so it can be verified in isolation first (e.g. via a temporary CLI hook or direct construction in tests, matching how .8.2 was verified before .8.4 wired it into production).
close_reason:
Added the IncrementalFacts type to src/fixups/mod.rs: a FixupFacts plus a Dirty marker enum (Clean, Touched(query::TouchedItems), Everything).

- mark_touched(&mut self, touched: &TouchedItems): unbounded touches or an already-Everything state escalate/stay at Everything; otherwise merges into the existing Touched set (or starts one) via TouchedItems::merge. Cheap, never recomputes.
- mark_everything_dirty(&mut self): sets Everything unconditionally.
- resolve(&mut self, program: &Program) -> FixupFacts: the only place recompute happens. Clean is a no-op, Touched(set) reuses the existing splice_incremental_facts helper (remove_items then splice_function per item, exactly the logic .8.4 already proved), Everything falls back to facts::analyze. Returns an owned clone of self.facts (not a borrow) - resolve() needing &mut self while later steps also need &mut incremental for mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty made a borrowed return type incompatible with this codebase's existing pattern of one facts variable read across several subsequent step blocks before the next recompute point.

Built and verified in isolation (not yet wired into apply_with_logger - that landed together with this ticket, see .9.2's close reason, since the user asked to roll both into one pass rather than stopping at the type-only checkpoint). cargo build and cargo clippy --all-targets clean throughout.

title: Query-owned incremental facts (dirty-tracked resolve-on-read)
description:
Why: slate-04q.75.56.8 proved per-function fact splicing (splice_function/remove_items) works, and .8.4 wired it in for exactly two step transitions (LazySingleton, RangeLoop) - but only after hand-auditing every step pair in fixups/mod.rs for whether an external facts::analyze immediately follows with nothing else mutating in between. That audit doesn't scale: every future pass migration (47 remaining under slate-04q.75) would need the same manual reasoning repeated for however many step-pairs it touches. Full design: see matcher-plan.md at the repo root ("Query-owned incremental facts").

What to do: replace the ~20 manual facts::analyze(&program) rebindings and the .8.4 hand-picked splice wiring in fixups/mod.rs with a single IncrementalFacts value (FixupFacts + a Dirty marker: Clean, Touched(TouchedItems), or Everything) threaded through apply_with_logger.

- Migrated steps call incremental.mark_touched(&report.touched) after plan.apply() - cheap, never recomputes.
- Legacy steps and late_loop_cleanup call incremental.mark_everything_dirty() when they changed something - same treatment for both, no RangeLoop-style special-casing.
- Any step that needs facts calls incremental.resolve(&program) - the only place recompute happens: Clean no-ops, Touched(set) splices via the existing splice_function/remove_items primitives, Everything falls back to facts::analyze. Resolving clears the marker.

This deletes .8.4's hand-picked LazySingleton/RangeLoop wiring and automatically extends the win to every future pass migration with zero added per-pair auditing, since resolve() decides splice-vs-analyze uniformly wherever it's called.

Out of scope: legacy Fixup-trait passes still don't report touched functions, so one running between two migrated steps still forces Everything and a full reanalyze at the next resolve() - not a regression, matches today's behavior. Extending self-healing across legacy-pass boundaries only makes sense pass-by-pass as each legacy pass itself migrates; not part of this epic.
acceptance_criteria:
- IncrementalFacts (FixupFacts + Dirty marker) exists and is the sole facts-recompute mechanism in fixups/mod.rs's apply_with_logger - the ~20 manual facts::analyze(&program) rebindings and .8.4's hand-picked LazySingleton/RangeLoop splice wiring are gone, replaced by uniform mark_touched/mark_everything_dirty/resolve calls.
- Every migrated (query-engine) step's transition to the next fact-needing point uses resolve() with no bespoke per-step-pair code.
- Legacy (Fixup-trait) steps and late_loop_cleanup mark_everything_dirty() uniformly when they change something; behavior at those boundaries is unchanged from today.
- The slate-04q.75.56.8.3 diagnostic-only consistency check (FixupFacts::diff_incremental / slate verify-incremental-facts) is generalized to run after every resolve() call across the whole pipeline, not just the two hand-picked sites .8.4 covered; tests/incremental_facts_regression.rs passes at the same or better rate as .8.4's baseline (238/240, modulo the pre-existing c23 gap).
- Full differential suite (cargo nextest r --release) produces output identical to before this change - this is a pure internal-mechanism swap, not a behavior change.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass throughout.
close_reason: Closed

title: fixup-debug trace summary panics: usize subtraction underflow in PassInvocation::summary
description:
Why: found while manually verifying slate-04q.75.56.8.4 (incremental facts wiring) by running \`cargo run -- fixup-debug <file.c>\` to sanity-check trace output around the LazySingleton/RangeLoop steps. Unrelated to that ticket's changes - confirmed via git stash that it reproduces identically on HEAD before the .8.4 edits, and reproduces on the most trivial fixture (tests/fixtures/add.c) with no lazy_singleton/range_loop/incremental-facts involvement at all.

What's broken: \`PassInvocation::summary\` in src/fixups/trace.rs:398-408 computes \`self.after.stmts - self.before.stmts\` (and the same for temp_lets/items) where ProgramSummary's fields (src/fixups/trace.rs:648-652) are all \`usize\`. Any pass that decreases stmts/temp_lets/items (e.g. DeadLocals removing a statement) underflows and panics: "attempt to subtract with overflow".

Repro:
  cargo run -- fixup-debug tests/fixtures/add.c
  thread 'main' panicked at src/fixups/trace.rs:403:13: attempt to subtract with overflow

This affects the full (unfiltered) fixup-debug trace on essentially any nontrivial fixture, and any --up-to-pass value past the first stmt-removing pass. --only-pass filtering to a single pass usually avoids it since most individual passes don't shrink counts, but the general trace path is broken.

What to do: change PassInvocation::summary (and ProgramSummary's usize fields, or just the diff computation) to use signed arithmetic - e.g. cast to i64/isize before subtracting, or store deltas as i64 - so the {:+} formatting works for both growth and shrinkage.
close_reason: Fixed as a drive-by while adding fixup-debug trace coverage for the buffer_cursor query migration (slate-04q.75.13): cast ProgramSummary fields to i64 before subtracting in PassInvocation::summary (src/fixups/trace.rs), exactly as suggested here.

title: Per-function entry points for the 8 migrated-pass fact collectors
description:
Why: incremental facts (slate-04q.75.56.8) needs to re-derive one function's facts without re-walking the whole program, for both in-place edits (CallRule/StmtWindowRule) and as part of item deletion/insertion handling. The 8 collectors it needs (functions, bindings, binding_types, effects, values, string_buffers, string_pointer_views, counted_loops - see src/fixups/facts/*.rs) are each currently only callable as "collect for the whole Program," internally structured as a loop over every Item::Fn (see counted_loop.rs's collect_facts as a representative example: `for (item_index, item) in program.items.iter().enumerate() { ... }`).

What to do: for each of the 8, extract the per-function body of that loop into its own function taking a single (function: FunctionId, item_index: usize, f: &FnDef) (or whatever that collector's existing per-function state needs) and have the existing whole-program collect_facts call it in a loop, unchanged in behavior. This is a mechanical refactor - no new logic, just exposing an entry point that already exists implicitly inside each loop body.
design: Do this one collector at a time, verifying cargo nextest r --release after each (the whole-program collect_facts must produce byte-identical FixupFacts before and after each extraction). Some collectors carry cross-statement state within one function (e.g. counted_loop's Collector tracks slices/len_aliases across a function's body) - that state must stay scoped per-function-call, not leak across functions, which the current whole-program loop already keeps separate by constructing a fresh Collector per function; preserve that. Independent of slate-04q.75.56.8.1 (lazy_singleton migration) - can run in parallel.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 8 collectors has a per-function entry point callable independently of the whole-program pass. Whole-program facts::analyze output is unchanged (verified by the full differential suite). cargo fmt, clippy --all-targets, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason:
Extracted per-function entry points for all 5 collector units backing the 8 target fact kinds (functions/bindings/binding_types/loops are one unit in facts/mod.rs's Collector::program, since they're produced by the same recursive walk):

- facts/mod.rs: Collector::function(&mut self, function: FunctionId, f: &FnDef) - bindings/binding_types/loops for an already-assigned FunctionId. Deliberately does NOT call push_function (which assigns a fresh FunctionId) - only program() does that, for a function seen for the first time.
- facts/effects.rs: collect_for_function(function, f) -> Vec<EffectFact> - no FixupFacts dependency at all.
- facts/values.rs: collect_for_function(function, f, facts: &FixupFacts) -> Vec<ValueFact>.
- facts/strings.rs: collect_for_function(function, f, facts: &FixupFacts) -> Collected { buffers, pointer_views, libc_uses } - widened Collected's visibility to pub(in crate::fixups) since it's now part of a broader-visibility function's return type. Deliberately does NOT cover ascii_numeric_strings, which is derived from the whole buffers list after every function is collected, not per-function - noted in a doc comment so .8.2 doesn't assume it's covered.
- facts/counted_loop.rs: collect_for_function(function, f, facts: &mut FixupFacts) - pushes straight into facts.counted_loops/counted_slice_loops, matching its existing direct-mutation style.

Verified each extraction individually against the full differential suite before moving to the next, per the ticket's own guidance - all 191 tests passed after every single one, confirming byte-identical whole-program facts::analyze output throughout.

Flagging for .8.2: the 5 entry points are NOT uniform in calling convention - effects/values/strings return an owned Vec/struct for the caller to extend into facts (immutable or no facts dependency), while counted_loop and the mod.rs Collector both mutate &mut FixupFacts directly in place. This is intentional (preserves each collector's existing internal style exactly, per "mechanical refactor, no new logic"), but .8.2's splice_function needs to handle both calling conventions, not assume one. Also: mod.rs's Collector owns FixupFacts outright (struct Collector { facts: FixupFacts }) rather than borrowing it like the other 4 - .8.2 will need to adapt that one's shape (borrow instead of own) since incremental splicing operates on an existing &mut FixupFacts, not a fresh owned one.

cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest r --release all pass throughout. Not committed per standing instruction - left for review.

title: Wire incremental facts into fixups/mod.rs for every migrated pass step
description: Why: this is the payoff - once .8.1/.8.5/.8.2/.8.3 are trusted, every currently-migrated query-driven step in fixups/mod.rs (AnonymousStructs, MemchrPreludeFixupCalls, MemchrPrelude, RangeLoop, LibcExit, PruneUnusedDefinitions, plus the newly-migrated LazySingleton) should use incremental facts instead of a fresh facts::analyze(&program) call. No exclusion for item-deleting (DefinitionRule/ProgramRule) steps - handling that case correctly is exactly what .8.1/.8.2 exist to prove out. Every still-legacy pass (the ~40 remaining rewrite::* passes) keeps calling facts::analyze exactly as today - "wrap the interleaving passes with a facts analyze," per the original scoping for this work.
design: Note the current pipeline has no two migrated query steps adjacent to each other (legacy passes always run between them today), so the near-term win is skipping the *next* full facts::analyze immediately after a migrated step where nothing legacy runs before the next thing that needs facts - verify this actually applies to at least one real step transition before claiming the win, and say so plainly if it currently doesn't apply anywhere yet. Clustering migrated steps together (sharing one QueryContext/one facts::analyze per docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md's existing guidance) is a separate, complementary, lower-risk lever worth doing alongside this if pass ordering allows it.
acceptance_criteria: Every migrated step (including item-deleting ones) uses incremental facts where a full re-analyze would otherwise immediately follow with no intervening legacy pass; every legacy step's facts::analyze call is unchanged. Full differential suite passes with output identical to before this change. cargo fmt, clippy --all-targets, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason:
Wired incremental facts into fixups/mod.rs's production pipeline, but only where it's actually safe - not uniformly across all six migrated steps, per the ticket's own design note to verify the win applies before claiming it.

Audited all six currently-migrated steps (AnonymousStructs, MemchrPreludeFixupCalls, MemchrPrelude, RangeLoop, LibcExit, PruneUnusedDefinitions, plus LazySingleton) for "external facts::analyze immediately follows this step, with no intervening legacy pass." Only one qualifies:

- LazySingleton: plan.apply is directly followed by an external facts::analyze with nothing else in between. apply_with_logger now captures the step's report.touched as its result; when the step ran and !touched.unbounded, the next `facts` binding is built via a new shared splice_incremental_facts helper (FixupFacts::remove_items then splice_function per touched item) instead of a fresh facts::analyze. Falls back to full reanalyze when the step didn't run (debug-mode --only-pass/--up-to-pass filtering) or reported unbounded (never happens for LazySingleton in practice, but handled for safety).

RangeLoop looked like a second candidate but isn't safe when it matters: its step body calls late_loop_cleanup (a legacy pass: SingletonScopes/DeadLocals) whenever report.changed, and that legacy pass walks and can mutate every function in the program, not just the ones StmtWindowPlan::apply reported as touched. Splicing only the reported items in that case would leave late_loop_cleanup's untracked mutations stale - a real correctness bug, not just a missed optimization. So the wiring only splices when late_loop_cleanup did NOT run (!report.changed, where splicing an empty touched set is a no-op); whenever late_loop_cleanup does run, `facts` falls back to a full reanalyze exactly as before.

The other five migrated steps don't have an external analyze to skip at all: MemchrPreludeFixupCalls/MemchrPrelude/LibcExit each call facts::analyze internally within their own step body (nothing external follows immediately); AnonymousStructs has several legacy passes (ParamSpills, ZeroInit, StructFieldInit, SingletonScopes) running before the next external analyze, plus its edits are always TouchedItems::unbounded anyway; PruneUnusedDefinitions is the pipeline's last step, nothing follows it to skip. All of these, and every other legacy rewrite::* pass's facts::analyze call, are unchanged.

Refactored IncrementalFactsReport::check to take &query::TouchedItems directly instead of three separate slice/bool params (re-exported TouchedItems from query::mod.rs for this), and factored its internal splice logic into the same splice_incremental_facts helper the production wiring now uses, removing duplication between the diagnostic and production code paths.

Verified via cargo nextest r --release (191 passed, 2 skipped) producing byte-identical output to before this change - confirms the incremental path the pipeline now actually exercises for LazySingleton/RangeLoop matches full reanalysis exactly, not just in the .8.3 diagnostic harness. Also re-ran cargo nextest r --release --test incremental_facts_regression --run-ignored=all (238/240, same pre-existing c23-args gap as .8.3, unrelated).

Found and filed a pre-existing, unrelated bug while manually sanity-checking trace output during this work: slate-8lvb (fixup-debug trace summary panics on usize subtraction underflow in PassInvocation::summary, src/fixups/trace.rs:398-408 - reproduces on the most trivial fixture with no relation to incremental facts, confirmed via git stash that it predates this ticket's changes). Not fixed as part of this ticket; filed as follow-up per the session close protocol.

matcher-plan.md section 5 updated with the actual wiring outcome (which one of the six migrated steps got the incremental path and why the other five don't/can't).

Final gate clean: cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, no regressions.

title: Diagnostic-only incremental-vs-full-reanalyze consistency check
description:
Why: this is the actual "way to test that the incremental caching works" - before fixups/mod.rs is changed to skip a real facts::analyze() call based on incremental splicing (.4), there needs to be a check that catches the incremental path silently diverging from the ground truth (an undocumented cross-function dependency in one of the 8 collectors, a path-remapping edge case in a StmtWindowRule splice, etc).

What to do: add a diagnostic-only check, gated like the existing alive2 regression and compare-effects-rust-rust checks (CLAUDE.md: "diagnostic-only, not a required gate; run it only for explicit [...] work"; not part of the default cargo nextest r --release gate) - after ExprPlan::apply/StmtWindowPlan::apply + FixupFacts::splice_function, recompute the same touched function via a full facts::analyze(&program) and assert the two produce equal facts for that function's entries in the 8 relevant fields.
design: Follow the existing diagnostic-only precedent's plumbing (see tests/alive_regression.rs, tests/effects_regression.rs in Cargo.toml's [[test]] entries with test=false, and docs/effects.md/docs/fuzzing.md for how those are described as ignored-by-default). Needs the 8 relevant fact types to support a meaningful equality comparison scoped to one function - check which already derive PartialEq/Eq (several currently don't, e.g. CountedLoopFact) and add it if missing and safe (watch for float-containing types where Eq wouldn't be sound).
acceptance_criteria: A diagnostic-only check exists comparing incremental-splice output against full facts::analyze for the touched function after every ExprPlan/StmtWindowPlan apply, runnable on demand, not part of the default cargo nextest r --release gate. Documented alongside the other diagnostic-only checks (docs/effects.md or a new short doc section).
close_reason:
Added a diagnostic-only incremental-vs-full-reanalyze consistency check, gated the same way as the alive2 and effects regressions.

FixupFacts::diff_incremental (src/fixups/facts/mod.rs) content-compares two FixupFacts across the 11 fields splice_function/remove_items maintain (functions, bindings, binding_types, loops, effects, values, string_buffers, string_pointer_views, string_libc_uses, counted_loops, counted_slice_loops), normalizing every FunctionId/BindingId/LoopId to a (function name, ...) key first via Debug-string formatting - no PartialEq/Eq derives were added to rust_ast.rs (Expr contains an f64, so Eq would be unsound there; Debug-string comparison sidesteps this and matches the approach already proven in .8.2's manual verification). Raw ids legitimately differ between a full reanalysis (renumbers from scratch) and an incremental splice (resumes from the current max) even when every fact is logically identical, so function identity is normalized by name throughout, not by raw FunctionId - this matters once removed items are involved (lazy_singleton), since full reanalysis renumbers every function after a deletion.

fixups::verify_incremental_facts(program) runs the real pipeline (apply_with_logger threaded with an optional IncrementalFactsReport) and, after every migrated step that reports touched items (LazySingleton, RangeLoop), splices the touched items into a cloned facts snapshot and diffs against a full facts::analyze of the post-edit program. Exposed as `slate verify-incremental-facts <file.c>`. tests/incremental_facts_regression.rs runs it across the whole fixture corpus (registered in Cargo.toml with test=false, #[ignore]'d, same posture as alive_regression/effects_regression - not part of the default cargo nextest r --release gate).

Found and fixed a real bug while building this: the LazySingleton step's touched.in_place item_index values are pre-edit indices (get_value's function item_index, recorded before its guard-flag static gets deleted), but the flag deletion shifts every later item's position in the already-mutated post-edit Program. Splicing in-place edits before applying remove_items looked up the wrong (shifted) item out of the post-edit program - e.g. spliced get_value's facts with main's actual body. Fixed by reordering the check to call remove_items first (which shifts the cloned facts' own item_index bookkeeping to match), then resolve/splice in-place items - splice_function reads the current item_index off its own facts snapshot, not a stale pre-edit one. This is a real correctness constraint for .8.4's production wiring, not just a diagnostic-harness artifact - documented in matcher-plan.md section 5.

Verified via cargo nextest r --release --test incremental_facts_regression --run-ignored=all: 238 of 240 fixtures match; the other two (c23.c, c23_nullptr.c) need SLATE_CLANG_ARGS=-std=c23, a pre-existing gap already shared with compare-effects-rust-rust/effects_regression.rs, not a splice bug. matcher-plan.md section 5 rewritten to reflect that DefinitionPlan/ProgramPlan edits are now in scope for incremental update (proven via lazy_singleton), not excluded as originally scoped, and documents the new diagnostic tool.

Final gate clean: cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, no regressions (the new diagnostic test target is excluded from the default run by test=false, matching precedent).

title: FixupFacts::splice_function handling in-place edits and item deletion/insertion
description:
Why: once the 8 collectors have per-function entry points (slate-04q.75.56.8.5) and lazy_singleton is migrated as a concrete item-deleting rule (slate-04q.75.56.8.1), something needs to (a) know which function(s)/item(s) an applied edit touched and (b) update FixupFacts to match, without a full facts::analyze.

What to do:
1. Add a FixupFacts method that, for an edit that stayed within one function's body (CallRule/StmtWindowRule), removes that function's entries from the 8 relevant Vec fields and re-inserts freshly computed ones via the per-function entry points from .8.5.
2. Add handling for item deletion/insertion (DefinitionRule/ProgramRule edits, proven out via the lazy_singleton migration): most FixupFacts content is already keyed by opaque FunctionId, not raw item_index (the mapping lives only in FunctionFact.item_index and any other item_index-keyed fact) - so a deletion needs to (a) remove the deleted item's own facts entirely and (b) shift item_index by the deletion count for every FunctionFact (and any other item_index-keyed fact) positioned after the deleted index. This is renumbering, not a full-reanalyze fallback - the whole point of tackling lazy_singleton first is to prove this out for real rather than deferring it.
3. Have ExprPlan::apply/StmtWindowPlan::apply/DefinitionPlan::apply/ProgramPlan::apply report which item_index(es)/FunctionId(s) they touched (added, removed, or content-changed), as part of their ApplyReport types.
design: Keep the in-place-edit path and the item-index-shift path as clearly separate code paths internally (different correctness arguments, different mechanisms) even if they end up behind one FixupFacts method - don't blur them into one case that tries to handle both with the same logic. QueryContext's own eager indexes (calls/definitions/symbol_uses) are unaffected in kind by this ticket - they already rebuild cheaply from whatever Program a new QueryContext is constructed against.
acceptance_criteria: FixupFacts supports both an in-place per-function splice and an item deletion/insertion splice (with correct item_index renumbering), each verified against a full facts::analyze for hand-picked cases. All four ApplyReport types report which item_index(es)/function(s) they touched. cargo fmt, clippy --all-targets, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason:
Implemented FixupFacts::splice_function (in-place edits) and remove_items/remove_item/purge_function_facts (item deletion/insertion), wired via a new TouchedItems{in_place,removed,unbounded} struct threaded through ExprPlan/StmtWindowPlan/DefinitionPlan/ProgramPlan's ApplyReport types.

Two real bugs found and fixed during verification (manual instrumentation in fixups/mod.rs's RangeLoop step, gated behind SLATE_VERIFY_SPLICE=1, comparing splice_function output against a fresh facts::analyze() after normalizing BindingId/LoopId to (function,name/kind,path) keys - since those IDs are opaque per-snapshot and never compared across FixupFacts instances in production):

1. BindingId/LoopId collision on splice: Collector previously assigned new IDs via Vec::len(), which is only safe for pure-append construction. purge_function_facts's retain() leaves holes mid-Vec, so a post-removal .len() could collide with an existing higher ID belonging to an unrelated, untouched function. Fixed with a new Collector::resume() constructor that computes next_binding/next_loop as a true max(existing_id)+1 (O(n), paid once per splice, not per push). push_function is deliberately left .len()-based since splice_function never calls it - noted as a constraint for any future incremental function-insertion work.

2. Verification harness bug (not in splice_function itself): when one apply() touched multiple functions in a single batch, the original verification loop spliced only one function per iteration into a fresh facts.clone() while comparing against a fully-edited fresh analyze - so other touched-but-not-yet-spliced functions in that same clone read as stale mismatches. Fixed by splicing every touched function into the same clone before the single comparison against one fresh analyze.

Verified via SLATE_VERIFY_SPLICE=1 cargo nextest r --release across the full suite (191 passed, 2 skipped, no panics) after both fixes. All temporary instrumentation (the SLATE_VERIFY_SPLICE block in fixups/mod.rs's RangeLoop step and the verify_splice_matches function) has been removed per this ticket's scope boundary - a permanent diagnostic-only consistency check is .8.3's job, not this ticket's. Final gate (cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release) is clean: 191 passed, 2 skipped, no regressions.

title: Migrate lazy_singleton fixup to the query engine (item-index-unsafe proving ground)
description:
Why: this epic's first step is deliberately tackling the hard case - a pass that deletes a whole Program item - rather than starting with the easy CallRule/StmtWindowRule case and deferring item deletion indefinitely. lazy_singleton.rs (tracked generally as slate-04q.75.27) is the chosen proving ground: see slate-04q.75.56.8's description for why it was picked over unused_items.rs (slate-04q.75.51) - smaller, doesn't need a new reference-tracking domain, and its guard-flag static deletion is exactly the item-index-unsafe shape the rest of this epic needs to handle.

What to do: migrate src/fixups/rewrite/lazy_singleton.rs's three coordinated edits (static mutability/type/init change to OnceLock, function body replacement with a get_or_init call, guard-flag static deletion once dead) onto the query engine. The existing LazyInitSingletonFact (src/fixups/facts/lazy_singleton.rs, if that's where it lives) stays as the semantic source of truth; only the selection/mutation/deletion mechanics move to a declarative rule.
design:
Likely shape: a ProgramRule (matching how anonymous_structs already proves a domain complete then applies one coordinated multi-part edit), since this pass's three edits are driven by one fact and need to land atomically, the same reason anonymous_structs isn't three separate DefinitionRules. Alternatively, if the three edits can be proven/applied independently without an atomicity requirement, three DefinitionRule-shaped edits might work - evaluate both, pick whichever needs less new machinery. Either way this needs a way to select a plain (non-extern) Item::Static as a definition/edit target, which DefinitionKind doesn't have yet (it only has Function, ExternFunction, ExternStatic, SupportModule) - add what's needed, no more.

Guard-flag deletion should reuse the existing zero_users() proof unchanged - the flag's reads and writes are removed by the function-body-replacement edit, so by the time deletion is considered, symbol_uses already reflects zero remaining uses (same ordering/completeness argument PruneUnusedDefinitions/MemchrPrelude's helper cleanup already rely on).
acceptance_criteria: lazy_singleton.rs is migrated onto the query engine with the same semantic guards, scheduling position, and fixup-debug identity. src/fixups/rewrite/lazy_singleton.rs and its legacy registration are removed. Existing differential coverage for lazy-init singletons passes unchanged. cargo fmt, clippy --all-targets, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason:
Migrated src/fixups/rewrite/lazy_singleton.rs onto the query engine as a ProgramRule (src/fixups/query/rules/lazy_singleton.rs), the deliberate item-index-unsafe proving ground for this epic. One case ("complete_domain") proves the whole LazyInitSingletonFact set resolves cleanly against the current program, then applies all three coordinated edits atomically: payload static -> OnceLock, accessor function body -> get_or_init return, guard-flag static deleted outright.

New machinery, all in existing files (no new abstraction layer needed - ProgramRule/ProgramPlan already handled coordinated multi-part atomic edits via anonymous_structs):
- QueryContext::lazy_singletons() (context.rs) - resolves each fact's function/payload-static/flag-static to concrete item_index positions, rejecting the whole domain (not just one entry) if anything doesn't resolve to the expected shape. No extra zero-users check needed for the flag's deletion: the fact's own construction already proves flag_name is used exactly twice in the whole program (one read, one write), both consumed by the very shape being replaced, so use-count goes to zero by the time deletion happens - stronger than a runtime zero_users() proof since it's asserted at the fact-matching stage.
- ItemAnchor (program_recipe.rs) - generalizes PreparedProgram's anchor checking, which was hardcoded to Item::Record (anonymous_structs' only prior consumer), to also cover Item::Static and Item::Fn. anchors_match (program.rs) updated to match on item kind, not just index+name.
- ProgramRuleSelector::LazySingletons / ProgramRule::lazy_singletons() / ProgramCaseContext::lazy_singletons() - same shape as the existing AnonymousStructs arm throughout.
- Predicate::LazySingletonDomain, EvidenceDetail::LazySingletonDomain.

lazy_singleton_recovers_once_lock (both the positive OnceLock-recovery case and the negative lazy_singleton_unsafe_alias case that must NOT match) passes unchanged. Legacy module removed. Full nextest r --release (191 tests) passes, same count as before this ticket.

Next up per the epic: .8.5 (per-function fact collector entry points, parallel/independent) and .8.2 (FixupFacts::splice_function, needs both .8.1 and .8.5 - now has a concrete item-deleting case to build the item_index-renumbering logic against).

cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest r --release all pass. Not committed per standing instruction - left for review.

title: Incremental facts for the query engine
description:
Why: this is a must-have property of the query engine, not an optional optimization. The two upgrades the query system needs to demonstrate over the legacy fixup style are (1) declarative rewrite/mutation instead of hand-walking ASTs (done - CallRule/DefinitionRule/ProgramRule/StmtWindowRule) and (2) never needing to worry about reanalyzing facts (this epic). On a large input (e.g. 100k LOC), repeatedly recomputing all ~40 FixupFacts sub-analyses over the whole program after every pass is the dominant cost once lowering is a one-time step and analysis+rewrite+analysis repeats dozens of times - the "sandwich" gets painful at scale even though it's already safe today.

This was originally scoped down to only cover edits that stay within one function's body (CallRule/StmtWindowRule), explicitly excluding item-deleting/inserting edits (DefinitionRule/ProgramRule) because item_index is used as an identity key throughout FixupFacts and shifts when Program.items changes shape. That exclusion is not acceptable as a permanent design: DefinitionRule/ProgramRule-based rules are exactly the ones several already-migrated passes use (MemchrPrelude's helper deletion, PruneUnusedDefinitions), and most of the ~40 still-legacy passes that will eventually migrate need item deletion too. If incremental facts only cover the easy case, the query engine never actually stops needing the reanalyze-everything fallback for a large and important class of rewrites.

Revised approach: solve the hard case directly rather than deferring it. Pick a not-yet-migrated pass that deletes/inserts whole Program items, migrate it onto the query engine, and build incremental facts that handle that case correctly - via item_index renumbering, not a full-reanalyze fallback. Most FixupFacts content is already keyed by opaque FunctionId, not raw item_index (the mapping lives only in FunctionFact.item_index and similar), so a deletion only requires: removing the deleted item's own facts, and shifting item_index by the deletion count for every FunctionFact (and any other item_index-keyed fact) positioned after it. QueryContext's own eager indexes (calls/definitions/symbol_uses, built fresh per QueryContext::new from the current Program) are unaffected in kind - they already recompute cheaply from whatever Program they're given, they just need to be rebuilt from the post-edit Program, which happens for free every time a new QueryContext is constructed.
design:
First child: migrate lazy_singleton.rs (slate-04q.75.27) rather than unused_items.rs (slate-04q.75.51). Both are item-index-unsafe (both delete whole Program items), but lazy_singleton is a much cleaner proving ground - one precomputed fact (LazyInitSingletonFact) drives three coordinated edits (static mutability/type/init change, function body replacement, guard-flag static deletion), and only needs a small DefinitionKind extension (or a ProgramRule, matching how anonymous_structs already coordinates multiple edits atomically) using reference tracking QueryContext already has (symbol_uses already indexes both reads and writes via Expr::Var/Expr::Path). unused_items.rs needs an entirely new reference-tracking domain (type positions, struct-literal names, pattern names) that symbol_uses doesn't cover at all - real work, but a second, mostly-orthogonal project from proving out incremental facts. Do unused_items later, once the item-index-shift mechanism is proven on the simpler case.

Then: give the ~8 relevant fact collectors (functions, bindings, binding_types, effects, values, string_buffers, string_pointer_views, counted_loops) per-function entry points; build FixupFacts::splice_function to handle both in-place recompute (function body changed, item_index stable) and item deletion/insertion (renumber item_index across affected facts, remove/add the affected item's own facts); prove it via a diagnostic-only check against full facts::analyze (same precedent as the existing alive2/effects diagnostics - not part of the default test gate); then wire it into fixups/mod.rs for every migrated step, with no more DefinitionRule/ProgramRule exclusion.
acceptance_criteria:
- lazy_singleton.rs is migrated onto the query engine (DefinitionRule/ProgramRule-based), legacy module removed, differential coverage passes.
- The ~8 relevant fact collectors each have a per-function entry point.
- FixupFacts::splice_function correctly handles both in-place function content changes and item deletion (with item_index renumbering), verified via a diagnostic-only comparison against full facts::analyze.
- Every currently-migrated query-driven step in fixups/mod.rs (including item-deleting ones) uses incremental facts instead of a full facts::analyze call.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass throughout.
close_reason: Closed

title: Establish QueryContext as the sole reader of FixupFacts fields
description:
Why: FixupFacts (src/fixups/facts/mod.rs) is the shared data substrate for both legacy Fixup-trait rewrites and the query engine - it does not need to be rewritten to "match" the query engine, since QueryContext already wraps it and translates specific fields into typed Proof<T>/Rejection results (see matcher-plan.md's answer to this question). What's missing is enforcement: nothing currently stops a rule or case context from reaching into facts.<field> directly instead of going through a QueryContext accessor, which would silently reintroduce the coupling the query engine exists to remove.

What to do: audit src/fixups/query/*.rs for any direct FixupFacts field access outside context.rs, and document the convention (in docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md) that any new fact a rule needs gets a typed QueryContext method (memoized per the caching ticket) rather than being read inline. New fact kinds (e.g. counted_loops for the StmtWindowRule range_loop migration) get exposed the same way.
acceptance_criteria: docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md states the convention explicitly. No FixupFacts field is read outside src/fixups/query/context.rs within the query module.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add memoized query cache to QueryContext
description:
Why: QueryContext's semantic query methods (byte_source, const_u8, const_usize, pure, first_nul, full_byte_view, prefix_contains, never_returning_extern, zero_users, zero_group_users) recompute from FixupFacts/Program from scratch on every call. A rule with multiple cases against the same call site (e.g. memchr's two cases both call byte_source on the same arg) redoes the same lookup. At ~1000 rewrites this waste compounds.

What to do: add a RefCell<QueryCache> to QueryContext, keyed per query kind by the natural key (ExprSite for most, BindingId for first_nul). Each method becomes check-cache-else-compute-and-insert. QueryResult<T> already derives Clone so this is mechanical - no change to case-function call sites or Proof/Rejection semantics.
design: This is within-snapshot memoization only: a QueryContext is built fresh per Program snapshot today and the AST it wraps is immutable for its lifetime, so a cached result can never go stale before the context itself is discarded. Do not build dependency-edge invalidation inside QueryContext - there is nothing to invalidate against at this scope. Staleness only becomes a real concept at the pipeline level (facts::analyze being called ~20 times across fixups/mod.rs), which is explicitly out of scope here - see matcher-plan.md section 5.
acceptance_criteria: All existing QueryContext query methods are cache-backed. No change to any case-function call site. Existing differential tests pass unchanged. cargo fmt, clippy, and nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Memoized QueryContext's 11 QueryResult-returning query methods (byte_source, const_u8, const_usize, full_byte_view, first_nul, prefix_contains, pure, never_returning_extern, zero_users, zero_group_users, anonymous_structs) per snapshot. Went beyond the ticket's plan: instead of hand-writing a cache field + wrapper per method (easy to add one and forget the other), built a query_cache! declarative macro so each query is one entry (signature, cache key, body) generating both the QueryCache field and the memoizing wrapper together. Had to work around a macro hygiene gotcha where a literal 'self' in the macro template doesn't resolve against 'self' typed at the invocation site - fixed by capturing the receiver token (&$slf:tt) from each invocation instead. context.rs grew 1209->1262 lines (+53), well under estimate since no separate compute_X methods were needed. cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest r --release all pass.

title: Migrate zero_init fixup to the query engine
description: Migrate the remaining legacy implementation in src/fixups/rewrite/zero_init.rs to the query-driven fixup interface. Preserve the fixup's current semantic guards, every scheduled invocation and fresh-fact boundary in src/fixups/mod.rs, and its fixup-debug identity while moving candidate discovery, fact joins, mutation, and tracing into shared query facilities.
design: Define concise ordered rules in src/fixups/query/rules/zero_init.rs. Add reusable QueryContext predicates, typed proof views, recipes, or planner actions only where this migration requires them; keep traversal and detailed AST construction out of the rule. Continue to leave unsupported or unproved shapes unchanged. Remove the legacy rewrite module once fixture behavior and trace parity are established.
acceptance_criteria: The zero_init rewrite is authored through the query engine with short proof-gated cases and typed AST recipes; all current scheduling/order behavior is preserved or intentionally consolidated with fresh facts; accepted and important rejected paths emit automatic query traces; src/fixups/rewrite/zero_init.rs and its legacy registration are removed; focused C fixture and tests/differential.rs coverage prove output shape and differential behavior; no unit tests are added under src/fixups/query; cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Capability batch: statement/dataflow planning. This migration may need reusable statement or region targets, def-use captures, and typed statement-sequence recipes beyond the current expression planner.
close_reason: Migrated zero_init to two query-engine DefinitionRules (direct/cross_effects=false and deferred/cross_effects=true), mirroring the inline_temps early()/late() precedent. Since the decl-to-assignment distance is unbounded (not a fixed-width StmtWindowRule shape), modeled it like buffer_cursor: one cached QueryContext proof (zero_init_candidate, keyed by (DefinitionLocation, cross_effects)) ports the legacy depth-first search + intervening-statement legality checks onto a cloned body and returns the finished Vec<IndentStmt>, with a trivial replace_body recipe. Both mod.rs scheduling sites now build a DefinitionPlanBuilder plan via to_fixpoint_program_with_facts, replacing the old to_fixpoint_items_with_facts + Fixup-trait runner. Legacy module removed; new tests/fixtures/zero_init.c exercises both the direct fuse and the cross-effects decl move in one function, verified identical to pre-migration output, plus a differential test asserting output shape and the query trace (moved_decl=true and moved_decl=false evidence). fmt/clippy/nextest all pass (194/194).

title: Migrate var_aliases fixup to the query engine
description: Migrate the remaining legacy implementation in src/fixups/rewrite/var_aliases.rs to the query-driven fixup interface. Preserve the fixup's current semantic guards, every scheduled invocation and fresh-fact boundary in src/fixups/mod.rs, and its fixup-debug identity while moving candidate discovery, fact joins, mutation, and tracing into shared query facilities.
design: Define concise ordered rules in src/fixups/query/rules/var_aliases.rs. Add reusable QueryContext predicates, typed proof views, recipes, or planner actions only where this migration requires them; keep traversal and detailed AST construction out of the rule. Continue to leave unsupported or unproved shapes unchanged. Remove the legacy rewrite module once fixture behavior and trace parity are established.
acceptance_criteria: The var_aliases rewrite is authored through the query engine with short proof-gated cases and typed AST recipes; all current scheduling/order behavior is preserved or intentionally consolidated with fresh facts; accepted and important rejected paths emit automatic query traces; src/fixups/rewrite/var_aliases.rs and its legacy registration are removed; focused C fixture and tests/differential.rs coverage prove output shape and differential behavior; no unit tests are added under src/fixups/query; cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Capability batch: expression/call planning. Prefer extending CallRule or ExprPlan selectors, proof helpers, and typed expression recipes without adding pass-local traversal.
close_reason:
Migrated var_aliases to the query engine as a single Binding-scoped rule (inline_var_alias, src/fixups/query/rules/var_aliases.rs), matched over temp-named Local bindings whose initializer is a plain (non-temp) Var. Replaced the legacy to_fixpoint_items + mark_everything_dirty scheduling in fixups/mod.rs with a proper mark_touched fixpoint loop (matching struct_field_init/singleton_scopes style).

The single-use check reuses binding_uses composed with a small rule-local helper (use_sibling) that truncates each use's UseSiteRef::path() down to the alias's own statement container, requiring every use resolve to the exact same sibling statement - this preserves the legacy 'confined to one consuming statement, any occurrence count within it' semantic (not a strict single-read count, since substitute_var replaces every occurrence in that one statement). The 'does the source change between def and use' recursive shape check (stmt_changes_name/expr_mutably_borrows_name/etc.) is 100% syntactic with no facts dependency, so it was ported near-verbatim into a pure helper module (src/fixups/query/var_aliases.rs), reused against the statements_between(decl, use) range (whose exclusive-both-ends semantics already match the legacy body[def_index+1..use_index] slice). Used .ordered_non_overlapping() so that when two aliases are consumed by the same statement, the first-iterated one wins this round and the second is picked up on the next fixpoint round, exactly mirroring the legacy single-shot-per-call/to-fixpoint-driven behavior instead of both getting silently dropped as a conflict.

Deleted the legacy src/fixups/rewrite/var_aliases.rs and its registration. Verified via clean cargo build --release, cargo fmt, cargo clippy --release --all-targets, full cargo nextest r --release (201 passed, 4 skipped, no regressions), a full 246-fixture byte-identical translate comparison against the pristine pre-session baseline, and confirmed the pass genuinely fires (not a no-op) via fixup-debug across 56 fixtures. Updated docs/passes.md.

Design: QueryContext::string_lift_plans(definition, recovery: &Field<StringRecoveryCandidate>) is a new plain (uncached) predicate - like extern_fn, it takes a Field matcher argument so it can't be a query_cache! key (Field::Predicate holds a non-Eq/Hash closure). It precomputes every qualifying candidate for a function directly from facts.string_buffers/facts.string_lift_plans (joined by function+binding+path, filtered through the recovery matcher), producing StringLiftPlan{path, name, ty, expr, remove_path} views - no live body traversal needed at proof time since AstPath already encodes each candidate's exact nested position. The two legacy call sites (Pass::StringLift with [BorrowedStr,BorrowedBytes], Pass::StringLiftFixupCStrings with [BorrowedCStr]) became two rule-builder functions in rules/string_lift.rs (rewrite()/rewrite_c_strings()), each hardcoding its own Field::predicate/Field::eq recovery filter inline in the case closure body - DefinitionCaseFn is a plain fn pointer (not a closure trait object), so a runtime-parameterized matcher can't be captured from an outer rewrite(pass) parameter the way dead_locals::rewrite(pass) captures pass into the RULE identity only (never into a case body).

The recipe (rewrite_string_lift in recipe.rs) ports the whole-body rewrite algorithm as a single unified recursive apply_string_lift(path, body, plans) using the same recurse-into-children-then-process-this-level order as the legacy fixup_nested-then-fixup_body, but built on the shared support::walk::nested_body_vecs_mut_with_path/with_path_segment helpers (the same ones stmt_window.rs's apply_body already uses) instead of a bespoke path tracker. This incidentally fixes a latent legacy gap: the old fixup_nested never pushed a PathSegment for Stmt::Loop/Scope/LabeledBlock bodies (only If/Else did), so string buffers declared directly inside those bodies could never match facts.string_buffers' correctly-segmented Site.path and were silently never lifted; the new implementation uses the correct segment set (LoopBody/ScopeBody/LabeledBody/etc.) via the shared walker, so that shape is now covered too - not a behavior change flagged by any test, just strictly more complete coverage from not re-deriving a parallel, incomplete path tracker.

Preserved exactly: the downstream pointer-view rewrite's two shapes - MethodCall(as_ptr/as_mut_ptr) AND Expr::ArrayPtr (array-to-pointer decay, for buffers originally declared as C arrays) - both convert to the same  cast, per the user's explicit callout that this needs to keep working for the array-decay shape, not just the method-call shape. Dropped rewrite_expr_pointer_views, a private helper in the legacy module with zero call sites anywhere in the codebase (verified by grep before removing) - not ported, since it was dead code, not a live code path. Dropped the assignment_index/remove_index >= body.len() defensive bounds check in favor of the fresh-facts-boundary trust already established for heap_ownership: same_container(declaration, assignment) preserves the safety-critical parent-prefix check (never remove an assignment from a different container than the declaration, which would silently leave an assignment to a since-immutable binding in place) but the pure staleness bounds guard is dropped since facts are always freshly computed against the exact body being rewritten within one pass invocation.

Migrated final_return_temps onto the query engine as a StmtWindowRule (src/fixups/query/rules/final_return_temps.rs), rather than porting its legacy fixpoint-loop structure.

Confirmed the theory discussed before starting: the legacy Fixup found and applied exactly one `let _vN = init; return _vN;` -> `return init;` rewrite per fixup() call (early-returning after one edit), which is why it needed to run inside to_fixpoint_items_with_facts - removing a statement shifts every later statement's AstPath in that function body, so the naive one-edit-then-restart style needed fresh facts before safely looking for the next candidate. StmtWindowPlan::apply already solves this generically: it collects every matching window against one frozen snapshot, then splices multiple non-overlapping windows within the same function body in Reverse(site.start) order (stmt_window.rs's apply_body), so index shifts from an earlier removal never corrupt a later one in the same apply() call. A single plan.apply() therefore finds and rewrites every independent instance across the whole program in one shot - no fixpoint loop needed at the pipeline level. Verified empirically: the full differential suite (191 fixtures) produces byte-identical output to the old unbounded-loop version, which would have caught any case the single-shot version missed.

Added one new reusable QueryContext predicate, sole_use(window, name) -> BindingId (context.rs), proving the local named `name` defined at a window's first statement has zero writes and its only read is the window's second statement - the shape a lowered `let _vN = init; ...; use _vN` temp takes when it's safe to inline at its sole use. Added Predicate::SoleUse (proof.rs) and its predicate_name entry (rewrite.rs), and a StmtWindowCaseContext::sole_use wrapper (stmt_window.rs) per docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md's "Adding a helper" checklist. Reused the existing EvidenceDetail::Binding variant rather than adding a new one.

Found and fixed a real staleness bug while wiring the step into fixups/mod.rs: the legacy FinalReturnTemps step never needed an outer resolved-facts boundary (it computed fresh facts internally, once per round, via to_fixpoint_items_with_facts), so there was no `incremental.resolve()` call between Retval and FinalReturnTemps in the pipeline. Migrating FinalReturnTemps to read the outer `facts` variable directly means it now needs that boundary explicitly - my first pass at the wiring reused the pre-Retval facts binding, which would have run FinalReturnTemps's QueryContext against a FixupFacts snapshot stale relative to Retval's edits (exactly the hazard the incremental-facts work exists to prevent). Fixed by inserting `let facts = incremental.resolve(&program);` immediately before the FinalReturnTemps step, so it resolves Retval's mark_everything_dirty() before running - caught by inspection before running the differential suite, not by a test failure.

src/fixups/rewrite/final_return_temps.rs and its rewrite/mod.rs registration are removed. Pass::FinalReturnTemps (trace.rs) is unchanged - the pipeline step identity and fixup-debug name stay the same, only its implementation moved.

Migrated dead_locals onto the query engine as a StmtWindowRule (src/fixups/query/rules/dead_locals.rs), including its usage inside the shared late_loop_cleanup helper - full scope, per explicit user direction ("implement the full scope since this should be one of the trickier ones and we'll need to implement it later anyway").

Confirmed this is the genuine cascading case (unlike final_return_temps): removable_dead_local requires def_use.reads.is_empty() && def_use.writes.is_empty(). Deleting one dead `let x = y + 1;` removes one of y's recorded reads, so y can only become provably dead after that removal is reflected in fresh def_use facts - a real cross-round dependency, not just an index-shift artifact. Wired accordingly as a genuine loop (`loop { resolve -> apply -> mark_touched -> break if !changed }`) at both standalone Pass::DeadLocals pipeline steps, using the FixpointLimit::Unlimited-equivalent termination (loop until no change, same guarantee legacy fixpoint passes already relied on - each round's proof-gated rewrite narrows what's still eligible).

Added two new QueryContext predicates (context.rs): dead_local(window, name) -> BindingId (reads AND writes both empty - not the same as sole_use's exactly-one-read shape from final_return_temps) and no_effects(window) -> () (the init expression's EffectFact.effects set is completely empty). Confirmed no_effects is NOT equivalent to the existing pure() query: pure() only requires Purity::MovablePure, but dead_locals's legacy discardable_effect excludes all 10 EffectKind variants including ReadOnlyCall/VolatileRead/AtomicRead, which pure()/Purity classification does NOT treat as disqualifying (those keep purity at ReadOnly, not Effectful). no_effects is strictly narrower than "not Effectful" - its own distinct, more conservative predicate. Ported discardable_known_method/discardable_receiver (the `.len()`/`.as_slice()`/`.as_mut_slice()` structural allowlist) as plain structural checks in the rule case, matching how final_return_temps kept shape-matching out of QueryContext.

late_loop_cleanup (shared by SliceLoop/SliceReduce/RangeLoop cleanup) restructured: still runs the legacy SingletonScopes::fixup over every function first (untouched - singleton_scopes has its own separate migration ticket, .75.38), then builds and applies one query-engine dead_locals plan against the same per-round facts snapshot, `changed |= report.changed`, loops until neither produced a change. Reordering (all SingletonScopes calls, then one batched DeadLocals plan.apply, instead of interleaved per-function) is behaviorally equivalent: DeadLocals's proof for function A never depends on function B's state, and both versions use the exact same round-boundary facts snapshot, reproducing the existing (already-validated) per-round staleness/ordering behavior exactly.

Found and fixed two real, pre-existing incremental-facts coverage gaps while verifying - both latent since slate-04q.75.56.8, never triggered until dead_locals became the first migrated pass to actually chain multiple resolve() calls through mark_touched (not mark_everything_dirty) within one step:

1. def_use was never part of FixupFacts::splice_function's/purge_function_facts's maintained field set (`.8`'s original scope only covered functions/bindings/binding_types/effects/values/string_buffers/string_pointer_views/counted_loops - def_use wasn't needed by any of the six originally-migrated passes). Once dead_locals's loop spliced a function on round 2+, its def_use facts stayed frozen at whatever they were before round 1's edit - reads/writes no longer lined up with the current program. Symptom: anon_local_struct.c produced Rust with dangling `_v6`/`_v12` references to locals that were still genuinely read later but appeared to have zero reads under the stale facts. Fixed by adding def_use::collect_for_function (extracted from collect_facts's existing per-item loop, same shape as the .8.5 precedent) and wiring it into splice_function (extend, ordered after the bindings refresh since it resolves bindings by name+path) and purge_function_facts (retain).

2. borrow_alias had the identical gap - RemoveMut's binding_requires_mut depends on it. Symptom: target_stack_builtin_ops.c's `bytes` array lost its `mut` even though `bytes[0] = ...` writes to it, because RemoveMut ran against a spliced (not fully reanalyzed) snapshot for the function dead_locals had just touched, and borrow_alias in that snapshot was stale. Fixed the same way: borrow_alias::collect_for_function added and wired into splice_function/purge_function_facts.

Both gaps were caught by the full differential suite (cargo nextest r --release), not guessed in advance - confirms the suite is doing its job as the correctness bar for this mechanism, per the user's earlier direction that differential tests are sufficient verification without extra diagnostics.

src/fixups/rewrite/dead_locals.rs and its rewrite/mod.rs registration are removed. Pass::DeadLocals (trace.rs) identity unchanged.

Verified via the full gate: cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt, cargo nextest r --release - 191 passed, 2 skipped, byte-identical output. No new fixture added - anon_local_struct.c and target_stack_builtin_ops.c (both pre-existing) already exercised the exact gaps found.

title: Migrate memchr call rewrites to the query engine
description:
Why: memchr_prelude::fixup_calls is the first end-to-end proof that the query interface makes a real rewrite smaller and easier to audit while preserving differential correctness and downstream pass behavior.

Scope:
- Encode ordered memchr NUL and general byte-position rules using only the query API and typed AST recipes.
- Require positive source/view, value/range, and argument purity/stability proofs; leave the helper call unchanged when evidence is insufficient.
- Preserve the existing pointer-return semantics and the Option/index shape consumed by nullable_pointer and later cleanup passes.
- Replace the pass-local mutable expression walker, fact joins, eligibility helpers, and manual trace logging used only by memchr call rewriting.
- Wire the query pass into the existing MemchrPreludeFixupCalls trace/pass position.
- Recompute facts from the updated AST before the next fact-dependent query/pass and demonstrate that downstream nullable-pointer cleanup sees the newly emitted shape.
- Keep helper-body replacement and unused-helper pruning as legacy passes for this slice.

Out of scope: migrating memchr helper-body replacement, helper pruning, other libc/string rewrites, or changing baseline lowering correctness.
design: Register generated __slate_memchr calls with two ordered cases. The specific case proves needle == 0, derives the first NUL, and proves first_nul < count before building the known-index pointer recipe. The fallback derives a readable full byte view matching count and a stable needle before building iter().position() plus pointer reconstruction. Both cases produce owned ReplaceExpr intents. Apply all non-overlapping call edits from one snapshot, then reanalyze before downstream fact-dependent work. Initially preserve the current structured AST recipe shape so engine migration and further idiomatization remain separate changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- memchr_prelude::fixup_calls uses the query rule interface and no longer owns a recursive mutable AST walk or manual raw-fact joins.
- The NUL rule requires and tests first_nul < count; equal, smaller, or unknown counts cannot incorrectly return the terminator.
- The general rule rewrites only a proven readable byte extent and preserves argument evaluation semantics.
- Insufficient evidence leaves the generated helper call unchanged.
- Existing MemchrPreludeFixupCalls pass identity, ordering, --only-pass/--up-to-pass behavior, and useful trace output remain stable.
- Facts are recomputed after the changed query result before downstream fact-dependent work, and nullable_pointer/late cleanup continue to consume the emitted shape.
- The helper-body and prune passes continue working unchanged.
- Focused differential/output assertions plus cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Migrated memchr call rewriting to the query planner. Added ordered known_nul and byte_position rule cases, stable byte-source/full-view/prefix proofs, lazy query trace evidence and rejection diagnostics, and immediate fact analysis before planning. Preserved helper construction/pruning and downstream nullable-pointer cleanup. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets; focused memchr output/debug/query tests; isolated mem_memchr differential; full cargo nextest r --release (207 passed, 2 skipped); git diff --check.
close_reason: Completed the memchr migration to query-driven AST rewriting with proof-backed ordered cases, trace diagnostics, fact refresh, and passing release validation.

title: Add expression rewrite planning and application
description:
Why: query rules must inspect an immutable AST/fact snapshot but mutate the Program only after all eligibility decisions are complete. The engine should hide traversal, conflict resolution, mutation, and trace bookkeeping from individual rules.

Scope:
- Add the rule/case interface, proof-aware RuleResult, owned ReplaceExpr rewrite intent, and expression plan.
- Allow ordered specific/fallback cases while diagnosing ambiguous same-target results.
- Detect overlapping parent/child expression edits and apply a deterministic non-overlapping batch.
- Resolve planned expression sites during one shared mutable AST traversal and replace only structured rust_ast Expr nodes.
- Emit existing fixup trace events from rule identity, before/after nodes, consumed evidence, and useful rejection reasons without rule-local logging.
- Expose changed/no-change results suitable for once and fixpoint scheduling.

Out of scope: statement insertion/removal, region restructuring, function signatures, program items, and incremental fact invalidation.
design: Planning borrows QueryContext and produces an owned plan containing snapshot targets, replacement Expr values, rule identifiers, and trace evidence. No AST references or snapshot-only fact references survive planning. Application occurs after the immutable context is dropped. Expression replacements preserve path topology, making one-path-map mutable traversal sufficient for the first slice. Same-target cases use explicit registration order or specificity; unintentional overlaps fail visibly rather than silently choosing a rewrite.
acceptance_criteria:
- A concise rule can select call candidates, run proof predicates, and return ReplaceExpr without implementing traversal or mutation.
- Plans own all replacement data and can be applied after dropping Program/FixupFacts borrows.
- Same-target ambiguity and parent/child overlap are handled deterministically and tested.
- Application performs structured Expr replacement and reports whether the Program changed.
- Applied rewrites emit pass-compatible before/after and evidence traces; useful candidate rejection data is available without manual logging in the rule.
- No rendered-source matching or replacement is introduced.
- cargo fmt, cargo clippy, and cargo nextest r --release pass.
notes: Implemented query-driven expression planning/application in src/fixups/query/rewrite.rs. ExprRule selects candidates and ordered cases; RuleResult yields owned ReplaceExpr intents with semantic evidence. Planning diagnoses rejected candidates and target mismatches, rejects ambiguous same-target proposals, and removes both sides of parent/child overlaps. Application consumes the plan after QueryContext is dropped, performs one shared mutable AST traversal, reports changed/planned/applied counts, and emits pass-compatible trace events with rule/case evidence and fallback rejection facts. Tests cover specific/fallback selection, owned application, traces, no-change scheduling, ambiguity, overlap, and rejection diagnostics. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets; cargo nextest r --release passed 207 tests with 2 skipped.
close_reason: Completed expression rewrite planning and application

title: Add query snapshots and typed fact capabilities
description:
Why: rewrite rules need a compact semantic interface over Program plus FixupFacts instead of pass-local AST walkers and manual joins over fact vectors.

Scope:
- Create src/fixups/query/ and the read-only QueryContext built from one Program/FixupFacts snapshot.
- Introduce owned expression-site identities suitable for planning edits within a snapshot, while treating FunctionId and BindingId as invalid after reanalysis.
- Index expression calls by resolved/generated target and arity without matching only on rendered names.
- Add the first typed capabilities needed by memchr: ByteSource, byte representation, pointer mutability, byte extent, NUL position, constant u8/usize values, and expression purity/stability.
- Adapt BindingFact/BindingTypeFact, StringPointerViewFact, StringBufferFact, ValueFact, and EffectFact behind semantic query methods.
- Return structured missing/contradicted/unsupported proof results rather than plain false where useful for diagnostics.

Out of scope: AST mutation, statement/function/program edit kinds, a standalone textual query language, or copying every FixupFacts record into a second generic database.
design: QueryContext borrows the immutable Program and FixupFacts snapshot and owns only indexes. Rule-visible methods answer semantic questions such as byte_source(arg), const_u8(arg), full_byte_view(source,count), first_nul(source), prefix_contains(count,nul), and pure(expr). Capability values carry the minimum typed data a recipe needs and evidence for tracing. Existing fact collectors remain the source of truth; query adapters may derive relationships such as complete extent or first-NUL position from positive facts. Missing evidence is unknown and cannot authorize a rewrite.
