title: CirOpKind: define the enum and parse Op.name into it
description:
Foundational ticket for slate-m6e. Add a CirOpKind enum to src/cir/ir.rs covering the 141 known "cir.*" op names (see the epic description for the full list, gathered via grep -rhoE '"cir\.[a-zA-Z_.]+"' src | sort -u). Keep Op.name: String as the source of truth (round-tripping/error messages depend on the raw text, and CIR gains new ops across Clang versions this crate doesn't control), and add a way to classify it as a CirOpKind, with a CirOpKind::Other(String) fallback (or equivalent) for anything not in the closed set.

Acceptance criteria:
- CirOpKind enum defined with one variant per known op name, plus a catch-all for unrecognized names.
- Op has a way to get its CirOpKind (e.g. a `kind()` method or a field populated at parse time in src/cir/parse.rs).
- Existing cargo test / cargo nextest suite still passes unchanged (this ticket adds the type, it does not migrate any call site yet).
- No call site in src/lower.rs, src/effects/cir.rs, or src/fixups/** is changed to use it yet — that's the subsystem-specific child tickets below.
close_reason: Added CirOpKind enum (141 variants + Other(String) catch-all) in src/cir/ir.rs with parse()/as_str(), plus Op::kind() accessor. Op.name remains the string source of truth; no call sites migrated (reserved for slate-jdn/7fr/gnc/ja3). Verified via cargo check --bin slate and cargo test --bin slate effects:: / cir::ir::.

title: Replace stringly-typed CIR op dispatch with a typed CirOpKind enum
description:
Every CIR op is dispatched by matching op.name.as_str() against string literals like "cir.add", "cir.if", "cir.ptr_stride". This pattern is used at ~318 call sites in src/lower.rs, ~97 in src/effects/cir.rs (the effect-trace walker added in slate-b8y.1/.3/.13), and scattered across most of src/fixups/facts/* and src/fixups/rewrite/*. A grep across the tree for `"cir\.[a-zA-Z_.]+"` string literals finds 141 distinct op names currently matched on.

Problems with the current approach:
- Typos in a match arm's string literal silently fall through to a default/panic arm instead of failing to compile.
- No exhaustiveness checking: adding a new CIR op (or handling for an existing-but-unhandled one) can't be verified by the compiler across all the places that should handle it.
- IDE navigation (go-to-definition, find-references) doesn't work across a string literal the way it does across an enum variant.

Fix: give `Op` (src/cir/ir.rs) a typed `CirOpKind` enum covering the 141 known op names, keep `name: String` as-is for round-tripping/diagnostics, and add a `kind()` accessor (or similar) that classifies it, with an `Other(String)`-style fallback for op names the enum doesn't yet enumerate (CIR is Clang's IR and gains ops over Clang versions — the enum can't be a closed world). Migrate call sites subsystem-by-subsystem so this can land incrementally without one giant PR.

This is a large, cross-cutting mechanical refactor, not a small ticket, hence the epic with per-subsystem child tickets below.
close_reason: All child tickets complete: CirOpKind enum defined (slate-421), migrated in src/effects/cir.rs (slate-7fr) and src/lower.rs (slate-jdn) — the only two subsystems that actually dispatch on CIR op.name. src/fixups/facts/** and src/fixups/rewrite/** (slate-gnc, slate-ja3) turned out not to touch CIR at all — closed as invalid premise.

title: Effects: scalar variable reassignment (Stmt::Assign to a plain local)
description:
src/effects/rust_ast.rs's Stmt::Assign arm only accepts Expr::Index as the
target and panics on anything else (assign_index() is the only case
wired up) - there is no path for reassigning a plain scalar local (`i = i
+ 1;`, `acc += x;` post-desugar). This blocks control-flow (slate-b8y.1)
before it even starts: a raw lowered loop's counter increment and
slice_reduce's accumulator (`acc OP= *item`, see
src/fixups/rewrite/slice_reduce.rs) both need it, and compound_assign
(src/fixups/rewrite/compound_assign.rs) only changes the syntax of an
assignment that already has to be walkable underneath.

Small and foundational enough to land before slate-b8y.1's loop bodies can
be interpreted at all.

Acceptance: `Stmt::Assign { target: Expr::Var(_), value }` updates
self.scalars in Interp and does not push a new effect (a local reassign is
silent - only heap/global reads and writes are effects); unit test
covering a fixture with a mutated loop-counter-shaped local.
close_reason: Implemented cir.if/cir.for + scalar ops in cir.rs, and Stmt::If/Stmt::For/Stmt::Assign(Var)/Stmt::CompoundAssign in rust_ast.rs, with hand-built if/else and for-loop-fill-and-sum fixtures on both walkers. All effects-scoped tests pass (cargo test --bin slate effects::).

title: Effects: function parameters as trace inputs
description:
Every existing and planned fixture traces a zero-argument `main`; the
walkers have no notion of a parameter entering the function with a
pre-existing value or location. Interp::run in both src/effects/cir.rs and
src/effects/rust_ast.rs starts from an empty env/scalars/vecs map and never
looks at FnDef::params / the CIR function's block arguments. This blocks
tracing any function that isn't `main` with no args, which includes most
of the fixup surface once it's ready to test standalone: ptr_len
(src/fixups/rewrite/ptr_len.rs, pointer+length param -> slice param),
slice_index/slice_loop on a sliced parameter, string_params (pointer param
-> &str).

Needs: a convention for seeding a parameter as a fresh AllocId (for
pointer/slice params, analogous to what malloc produces) or a plain scalar
value (for int params) at trace start, on both walkers, with the same
seeding order on both sides so the resulting AllocIds line up.

Acceptance: a fixture function taking a `*mut i32`/length pair (CIR) and
its `&mut [i32]` idiomatized form (rust_ast) - not `main` - produce
matching effect traces when driven with the same input values.
close_reason: Added ParamSeed (Scalar/Buffer) to src/effects/mod.rs and interpret_with_params on both walkers, seeding a fresh AllocId+heap for buffer params and env/scalars for scalar params, same seeding order on both sides so AllocIds line up. Added hand-built bump(items, len) fixtures on both walkers (cir.rs::bump_len_fixture, rust_ast.rs::bump_fixture) proving matching traces when driven with the same input values, per acceptance criteria. Filed slate-1gl as a follow-up for cir.scope/cir.inc support, needed to run a real (non-hand-built) loop-containing ptr_len fixture through the full pipeline -- out of scope for this ticket.

title: Effects: control-flow support (if/loop) in CIR and rust_ast walkers
description:
Both effect walkers (src/effects/cir.rs, src/effects/rust_ast.rs) only walk
a flat op/stmt list. Neither handles a conditional or a loop, so no fixture
with a branch or a loop can be traced. Add:

- CIR side: cir.if / cir.scope / cir.brcond (whatever the CIR-opt generic
  form actually emits for `if`), plus a loop construct (structured
  `cir.for`/`cir.while` if CIR preserves it post-goto-structuring, else the
  conditional-branch loop shape).
- rust_ast side: Stmt::If and a loop Stmt (for/while, whatever
  src/rust_ast.rs already models) so the interpreter can execute them,
  branching/looping on evaluated conditions the same way the CIR side does.

Needs comparison/scalar ops (see sibling issue) to evaluate loop bounds and
if-conditions, so implement together or land that one first.

Acceptance: a fixture with an `if` and a fixture with a bounded loop (e.g.
array fill via a for-loop) each produce identical effect traces from the
CIR walker and the rust_ast walker, wired into the regression test the same
way the malloc/array fixture is (src/effects/regression.rs).
close_reason: Implemented cir.if/cir.for + scalar ops in cir.rs, and Stmt::If/Stmt::For/Stmt::Assign(Var)/Stmt::CompoundAssign in rust_ast.rs, with hand-built if/else and for-loop-fill-and-sum fixtures on both walkers. All effects-scoped tests pass (cargo test --bin slate effects::).

title: Effects: stdout effects for printf/println!/print!
description:
Effect::Call { name, args } already exists in src/effects/mod.rs but neither
walker emits it - the CIR walker's call() only handles malloc/free and
panics on any other callee; the rust_ast walker has no printf/println!/
print! handling at all. Differential testing's correctness oracle is
stdout+exit-code equality, so an effect-equivalence checker that is silent
on stdout is checking the wrong thing for any fixture that prints.

Add:
- CIR side: recognize `printf`-family calls in call(), push a stdout effect
  (reuse Effect::Call, or add a dedicated Effect::Print(String) if Call's
  shape - name + Vec<Value> - can't represent formatted output cleanly;
  decide during implementation which fits mod.rs's vocabulary better).
- rust_ast side: recognize println!/print!/write! (whatever printf_format's
  fixup - src/fixups/rewrite/printf_format.rs - actually emits) and push the
  equivalent effect.

Acceptance: a fixture that calls printf/println! produces matching stdout
effects from both walkers, wired into the regression test.
close_reason: Both walkers now emit Effect::Call{name:"printf", args} for stdout calls (args = only the substituted values, not the format template). Also fixed a latent cir.get_global bug where its result was never registered in env, which crashed the cast chain used to build printf's format-string pointer. Fixture tests/fixtures/effects_printf.c wired into effects::regression. cargo fmt && cargo nextest r --release: 625/625.

title: Effects: scalar ops beyond add/mul (sub/div/mod/cmp/bitwise/unary)
description:
src/effects/cir.rs's Interp::binop only wires up cir.add and cir.mul (see
step()'s match arms). src/effects/rust_ast.rs's eval() only handles
BinOp::Add. Neither models subtraction, division, remainder, comparisons
(lt/gt/le/ge/eq/ne), bitwise ops, logical and/or, or unary neg/not. These
are needed as plain expression coverage and are also a hard prerequisite
for the control-flow issue (loop bounds and if-conditions are almost always
a comparison).

Acceptance: extend the existing binop()-style dispatch on both walkers to
cover the remaining BinOp/cir.* arithmetic and comparison ops, with a unit
test per op group (arithmetic, comparison, bitwise, logical) on each
walker.
close_reason: Implemented cir.if/cir.for + scalar ops in cir.rs, and Stmt::If/Stmt::For/Stmt::Assign(Var)/Stmt::CompoundAssign in rust_ast.rs, with hand-built if/else and for-loop-fill-and-sum fixtures on both walkers. All effects-scoped tests pass (cargo test --bin slate effects::).

title: Extend effects module: control flow, stdout, scalar ops
description:
The effect-trace equivalence checker (slate-0hf) only covers straight-line
programs today: the CIR walker (src/effects/cir.rs) handles alloca/const/
add/mul/cast/call(malloc,free)/ptr_stride/store/load/return, and the
rust_ast walker (src/effects/rust_ast.rs) handles Vec alloc + push/index +
std::process::exit. Neither walker executes a branch or a loop, and no
fixture exercises one.

Cross-referencing this against the 39-pass fixup ladder (docs/passes.md)
shows almost none of the real fixups (slice_loop, range_loop, slice_reduce,
sort_search, goto, ...) are straight-line, so the checker currently can't
validate the fixups it exists to validate. This epic extends the shared
Effect vocabulary and both walkers to close the gaps, ordered P2 (core,
do first) -> P3 (large well-defined surfaces) -> P4 (niche/harder, revisit
last):

  P2 - core, unblocks everything else:
    .13 scalar variable reassignment (Stmt::Assign to a plain local) -
        blocks .1, loop counters/accumulators need it
    .1  control flow (if/loop) in both interpreters - depends on .3, .13
    .2  stdout effects (printf/println!/print!) - Effect::Call exists but
        unemitted; stdout equality is the actual differential-testing oracle
    .3  scalar ops beyond add/mul (sub/div/mod/cmp/bitwise/logical/unary) -
        also a prerequisite for .1's conditions/bounds
    .11 function parameters as trace inputs - every fixture so far traces
        zero-arg main; most of the fixup surface takes a real parameter

  P3 - large, well-defined fixup surfaces once the core lands:
    .7  struct field read/write (struct_field_init, anonymous_structs,
        buffer_cursor)
    .10 string buffer effects (string_lift/string_copy/string_libc/
        string_params/c_strings)
    .8  iterator-idiom recognition (slice_loop/slice_reduce/range_loop,
        memchr_prelude) - depends on .1
    .5  Dealloc effect for free/Box-drop (heap_ownership) - catches UAF/
        double-free divergence
    .12 global/static variable read/write (lazy_singleton,
        atomic_locals' promoted globals) - cir.get_global is a no-op today
    .14 Option<T> value representation (nullable_pointer, memchr/
        string_libc search results)

  P4 - niche, harder to make deterministic, revisit last:
    .6 atomic op effects (atomic_compare_exchange/atomic_locals)
    .4 file I/O effects (stdio fixup)
    .9 sort/search comparator-callback effects - depends on .3, first case
       needing cross-function interpretation

Deliberately NOT ticketed - purely syntactic fixups that rearrange code
without changing observable effects, so they get validated for free once
the categories above land, with no new Effect variant needed: call_args,
compound_assign, constant_index_casts, dead_locals, drop_call_results,
early/late_inline_temps, final_return_temps, for_continue, goto (CIR is
already structured; rust_ast walker runs post-fixup), main_zero_exit,
param_spills, prune_unused_externs, remove_mut, retval, singleton_scopes,
unnecessary_casts, unused_items, unused_params, va_list, zero_init,
array_element_pointer_origin (already covered by existing pointer/index
support).
close_reason: Closed

title: Effect trace comparator (stuttering equivalence)
description: Program that takes two Effect traces (one from CIR, one from rust_ast) and decides equivalence: only observable effects need to match, in order: differences in tick count, allocation identity, or intermediate silent steps are not divergences. Must reconcile representational differences the two producers introduce (e.g. pointer-offset locations vs Vec-index locations referring to the same logical cell) rather than requiring literal trace equality.
design: This is where the reconciliation logic from the design discussion lives: canonicalize locations to offset-from-allocation before comparing, collapse non-observable steps, and diff the remaining event sequences. On mismatch, report the first diverging effect with enough context (which allocation, which index, which value) to debug it.
acceptance_criteria: Comparator returns equal for the CIR and rust_ast traces of the same malloc/array fixture from the two sibling issues, and returns a clear diff for a deliberately mutated (incorrect) trace.
close_reason: Implemented compare(cir, rust_ast) -> Result<(), Box<Divergence>> in src/effects/interpreter.rs. Walks both traces in lockstep (no silent-step collapsing needed since only observable effects are ever pushed) and reports the first EffectMismatch (exact index + both sides' effects) or LengthMismatch. Verified with cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo test --bin slate effects::, cargo fmt.

title: CIR -> Effects: malloc + array write + read
description: Interpreter that walks a CIR op-tree for a narrow fixture (malloc an int array on the heap, assign into it by index, read it back, e.g. via a pointer) and emits the shared Effect trace: Alloc on the malloc call, Write per indexed store, Read per indexed load. Scope to exactly this slice — no general C stdlib coverage yet, no control flow beyond what the fixture needs.
acceptance_criteria: A CIR tree for a malloc/assign/read fixture produces an Effect trace with the right Alloc/Write/Read sequence and values; covered by a unit test in the new interpreter module.
close_reason: Implemented CIR -> Effects walker for malloc + indexed array write/read + return, following the shared Effect vocabulary from slate-0hf.1. Verified with cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo fmt.

title: RustAst -> Effects: matching idiom (Vec or Box)
description: Interpreter that walks the emitted rust_ast for the idiomatized counterpart of the CIR malloc/array fixture (e.g. Vec::with_capacity + indexing, or Box<[i32]>) and emits the same shared Effect vocabulary: Alloc on the allocation, Write per index assignment, Read per index access. The whole point of this issue is proving the shared Effect type can represent both a raw-pointer walk and its idiomatized Vec/Box equivalent without a special case.
acceptance_criteria: A rust_ast tree for the idiomatized fixture produces an Effect trace comparable in shape to the CIR trace from the sibling issue, using only the shared Effect enum.
close_reason: Implemented RustAst -> Effects walker for Vec::with_capacity + push + indexed read/return, using the shared Effect vocabulary from slate-0hf.1. Its trace for the idiomatized fixture is byte-for-byte identical to the CIR walker's trace for the equivalent malloc/array fixture. Verified with cargo build, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, cargo test --bin slate effects::, cargo fmt.

title: Design shared Effect type for CIR/RustAst execution traces
description: Define the shared Effect vocabulary that both the CIR interpreter and the Rust-AST interpreter will emit, and that the comparator consumes. Needs: an Alloc effect (id, size) for heap allocation; Write/Read effects keyed by an abstract location (offset-from-allocation, never a raw address, so a *const i32 walk and a Vec<i32> index compare equal despite different concrete addresses); a Call effect for stdlib/std boundary crossings (malloc now, printf/print! later); Return/Exit. Keep the enum minimal — extend only when the CIR-side malloc slice actually needs more.
design: This is the one piece every other issue in the epic depends on — CIR effects, rust_ast effects, and the comparator all need to agree on this shape before any of them can be written against real fixtures.
close_reason: Closed

title: Effect-trace equivalence checker for CIR/Rust-AST fixups
description: Fixups idiomatize baseline Rust (ptr->Vec, ptr->Box, etc.), so C-to-Rust translation validation (alive2) can't cover Rust-to-Rust fixup correctness, and libc calls are opaque to alive2 anyway. Build an effect-trace equivalence checker: two small interpreters (CIR->Effects, RustAst->Effects) emit a shared Effect type from a program's execution, and a separate comparator decides if two effect traces are equivalent (stuttering/event equivalence: only observable effects must match in order, not tick-for-tick state). This is a fast, tree-level pre-check that complements (does not replace) the existing compile-and-run differential tests, which remain the correctness oracle.
design: Shared Effect enum lives in one module so both CIR and rust_ast lowering-to-effects and the comparator agree on vocabulary. Memory locations must be abstracted (offset-from-base, not raw address) so a raw pointer effect and a Vec/Box effect over the same logical buffer can compare equal. Start narrow: CIR side only, one C stdlib effect (malloc) plus array write/read through the resulting pointer. Rust AST side and the comparator follow once the shared vocabulary proves out on that slice.
close_reason: All children complete. Effect-trace equivalence checker landed: shared Effect/EffectTrace vocabulary (mod.rs), CIR walker (cir.rs), rust_ast walker (rust_ast.rs, covering both idiomatization Vec shapes), comparator (interpreter.rs), and an end-to-end regression test (regression.rs) running the real emit-cir/lower/fixups pipeline on the malloc/array fixture.

title: Emit before/after LLVM IR for a skippable fixup pass
description: Harness code that, for a given fixture and a given skippable pass (starting with range_loop from slate-4us.1), runs the full slate pipeline twice — once with the pass skipped, once normal — and emits LLVM IR for each via 'rustc --emit=llvm-ir -C opt-level=0 --crate-type=lib' against the generated Rust source. Both compiles must share crate name/module path/fn names so mangled symbols line up across the two .ll files (needed for alive-tv's two-file name-matching in slate-4us.4). Also needs a cheap way to tell whether the pass actually fired on a given fixture (reuse the bool already returned by rewrite::range_loop::fixup) so callers can skip fixtures where before/after are identical.
acceptance_criteria:
Given a fixture path and Pass::RangeLoop, the helper returns paths to (or contents of) before.ll and after.ll.
For a fixture where range_loop does not fire, the helper reports 'unchanged' without needing to diff the .ll text.
For a fixture where it does fire, the two .ll files differ only in the rewritten function's body, and matching function symbols have identical mangled names across both files.
notes: Superseded: emit_pass_effect and the before/after-fixup-pass comparison approach described above were removed and replaced by tests/support::alive::emit_lowering_ir, which compares C's LLVM IR against src/lower.rs's baseline (SLATE_RAW_LOWER=1) lowering instead — see slate-4us's design notes. Left closed/unedited above as historical record of what was built at the time.
close_reason: Wired SLATE_SKIP_PASS through the translate CLI into fixups::apply_with, and added tests/support::alive::emit_pass_effect: runs slate translate twice (pass skipped vs default), and when they differ, compiles both to LLVM IR via rustc with pinned --crate-name/-C metadata so touched-function symbols match across before.ll/after.ll. Handles libc-dependent fixtures and non-identifier file stems. Verified end-to-end against ptr_len_slice.c (fires), add.c (unchanged), mt-atomics.c (libc + hyphenated stem).

title: Pilot: tests/alive_regression.rs runs alive-tv against range_loop fixtures
description: Opt-in nextest target (tests/alive_regression.rs) that alive-tv-verifies src/lower.rs's baseline C -> Rust lowering directly, instead of comparing a fixup's before/after Rust IR (see the epic's updated design note: representation-changing fixups aren't comparable via alive-tv). For each fixture in FIXTURES, compiles the C source (clang) and the SLATE_RAW_LOWER=1 baseline Rust (rustc, --emit=llvm-ir, panic=abort, overflow-checks=off, matched target triple, non-main fns forced to #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C") and runs alive-tv two-file mode, asserting refinement.
acceptance_criteria:
cargo nextest r --release --test alive_regression passes when alive-tv is installed and available fixtures verify.
The target is excluded from the default 'cargo nextest r --release' invocation.
Without SLATE_ALIVE_TV / a resolvable binary, the target reports a clear skip rather than a failure.
A deliberately broken lowering (verified live via a temporary local edit to src/lower.rs's cir.add handler, reverted after) produces a failing test with alive-tv's counterexample, confirming the harness actually detects regressions.
close_reason: Delivered under the pivoted design (see epic notes): tests/alive_regression.rs + tests/support/alive.rs verify src/lower.rs's baseline (SLATE_RAW_LOWER=1) lowering against clang's C IR via alive-tv, rather than a fixup's before/after IR. Full cargo nextest r --release (601 tests) passes with alive_regression excluded by default; cargo nextest r --release --test alive_regression passes explicitly; verified it catches a regression by temporarily flipping cir.add's BinOp::Add to BinOp::Sub in src/lower.rs (reverted, git diff clean).

title: Add per-pass skip toggle to fixups::apply
description: fixups::apply (src/fixups/mod.rs) is a flat, order-dependent sequence of ~40 pass calls with no way to disable a single one. Add a SkipSet (or Pass enum + HashSet) threaded through an apply_with(program, skip) entry point, with apply() calling apply_with(program, SkipSet::none()). Wrap each pass call site in 'if !skip.contains(Pass::X) { ... }'. Start by making only range_loop skippable — the pilot for slate-4us — rather than wiring all ~40 passes up front.
acceptance_criteria:
apply_with(program, skip) exists and apply() delegates to it with an empty skip set.
Pass::RangeLoop can be added to a SkipSet and, when present, rewrite::range_loop::fixup is not called (and late_loop_cleanup is not triggered by it).
Existing fixup unit tests and differential tests still pass unmodified.
Behavior with an empty SkipSet is byte-identical to current apply() output on every fixture.
notes: touches: src/fixups/mod.rs
close_reason: Closed

title: Wire up local alive-tv toolchain via SLATE_ALIVE_TV
description: User is building alive2 locally in ~/alive2. Once built, add SLATE_ALIVE_TV following the existing SLATE_CLANG/SLATE_CIR_OPT pattern (default path under ~/alive2, overridable via env var), and document it in CLAUDE.md's toolchain table. This issue tracks the wiring/documentation side; the actual alive2 build is being done manually outside the agent workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
SLATE_ALIVE_TV documented in CLAUDE.md toolchain table with the same shape as SLATE_CLANG/SLATE_CIR_OPT/SLATE_CC.
A small helper (e.g. in test support code) resolves the alive-tv binary path from SLATE_ALIVE_TV with a sensible default, for use by the regression harness in slate-4us.4.
Running without SLATE_ALIVE_TV set and without a binary at the default path does not break any existing test run.
close_reason: Added SLATE_ALIVE_TV to CLAUDE.md toolchain table and tests/support::alive_tv() helper resolving ~/alive2/build/alive-tv by default; verified against confirmed binary path, full nextest suite (600/600) still passes.

title: Alive2 translation-validation harness for fixup-pass regressions
description:
Build a translation-validation regression check for Rust-AST fixup passes: compile a fixture's generated Rust to LLVM IR with a given fixup enabled and with it disabled, then run Alive2's alive-tv in two-file refinement mode on the pair. This complements differential testing (concrete C vs Rust execution on one input) with symbolic-input equivalence checking over the fixup's actual before/after Rust IR — it can catch regressions that a single concrete fixture input would miss, without needing to formalize C or Rust semantics (fixups are Rust-AST to Rust-AST, so rustc's own LLVM backend supplies the semantics on both sides).

Pilot on range_loop (the counted-loop -> 'for i in 0..n' fixup, src/fixups/rewrite/range_loop.rs) since it is the motivating case; generalize the skip mechanism and harness to more passes once the pilot proves out. Caveat carried into the design: alive-tv is bounded translation validation, so this proves equivalence for the concrete functions fixtures exercise (exhaustively over their symbolic inputs), not an unbounded proof of the rewrite schema in general.
design: Pivoted from before/after-fixup-pass comparison to comparing C against src/lower.rs's baseline (pre-fixup) lowering directly. Fixups that change representation (raw pointers -> Box/Vec/slice/String, char* -> &str, malloc'd buffers -> String, ...) change a function's memory layout and ABI, not just its LLVM instructions, so alive-tv cannot meaningfully compare a fixup's before/after Rust IR across that boundary (different allocators, different calling convention, sometimes a different declared signature). Comparing C's LLVM IR (clang) against SLATE_RAW_LOWER=1's baseline Rust LLVM IR (rustc) sidesteps this: baseline lowering is a close transliteration of the C (repr(C), raw pointers, libc, unsafe) with no representation changes, so its IR is directly comparable to clang's for the same function. Implemented in tests/support/alive.rs (emit_lowering_ir + verify) and tests/alive_regression.rs; SLATE_RAW_LOWER=1 added to src/main.rs's translate command to emit lower::lower's output with zero fixups applied. The SkipSet/Pass/SLATE_SKIP_PASS machinery from slate-4us.1/.3 is no longer used by this harness (nothing else consumes it) but was left in place since it's still self-tested and may have other uses.
acceptance_criteria:
fixups::apply can skip an individual named pass (starting with range_loop) so the same program can be lowered with and without that one fixup, everything else held constant.
A new opt-in test target compiles both variants of an affected fixture to LLVM IR via rustc and runs alive-tv in two-file mode (alive-tv before.ll after.ll), asserting refinement for the touched function.
The harness only invokes alive-tv on fixtures where the pass actually fired, skipping fixtures with identical before/after IR.
The test target skips with a clear message (not a hard failure) when SLATE_ALIVE_TV / the alive-tv binary is unavailable, matching the existing toolchain-prerequisite pattern (SLATE_CLANG etc. in CLAUDE.md).
New SLATE_ALIVE_TV env var and how to run the check are documented alongside the existing toolchain table.
close_reason: Closed

title: Recover tagged unions as Rust enums with data
description:
Why: the tag-plus-union idiom (a struct with an enum/int discriminant field plus a union field, where each union arm is only ever accessed under a matching discriminant check) is extremely common in C and has no idiomatic Rust equivalent today — it can only render as #[repr(C)] union + manual tag bookkeeping, never a safe enum. This is likely the single highest-value uncovered idiom.

What to do:
- New fact: a struct has a discriminant field and a union field where every union-arm access is provably guarded by a matching switch(tag)/if(tag==X) check on the discriminant.
- Rewrite: collapse the struct into a genuine Rust enum Variant { A(T1), B(T2), ... }, and rewrite tag-guarded union field accesses into match arms.
- Whole-program in scope (need to see every access site of the struct type to prove guard-safety), so likely needs new fact-collector scope similar to the Result recovery ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Fact collector proves discriminant-guarded union access for a candidate struct type across the whole program. Rewrite emits a real Rust enum and match-based accessors. Differential tests pass on fixtures with 2+ variants, nested access, and at least one case where the guard can't be proven (must stay on baseline union path).

title: Recover out-params as tuple/struct return values
description:
Why: C functions commonly pass a second (or third) return value through a pointer out-parameter (e.g. int parse(const char *s, int *out)). Baseline lowering keeps this as a raw pointer write, which is unidiomatic and forces callers to pre-declare and pass &mut locals.

What to do:
- New fact: a pointer parameter is write-only (never read before written, not aliased/escaped, written on every return path) — a disguised second return value.
- Rewrite: fold provably write-only out-params into the function's return type as a tuple (2 values) or generated named struct (3+), and rewrite call sites to destructure the result instead of pre-declaring an out local.
- Composes with the existing string_params/slice_index/ptr_len fact families and pointer-provenance neighborhood in the pass sequence.
acceptance_criteria: New fact collector proves out-param write-only-ness per function. New rewrite pass folds it into return type + rewrites call sites. Differential tests pass; fixture covers single and multi out-param cases.

title: Recover status-code returns as Result<T, E>
description:
Why: many C functions follow an errno-style convention: return 0/negative for success/failure, with callers only ever comparing the return value against 0 (never using it arithmetically). This is Rust's Result<T, E> idiom in disguise, but baseline lowering leaves it as a raw int with libc-style checks.

What to do:
- New fact: a function's return value is only ever compared against 0/negative at every call site (whole-program, not per-function — this needs new fact-collector scope beyond current per-function FixupFacts).
- Rewrite: convert the function to return Result<T, i32> (or a generated error enum), and propagate ? at call sites that immediately check-and-bail in the same status-code style.
- Higher risk than most fixups since it changes call-site control-flow shape everywhere the function is called, not just the callee body. Scope carefully; may need to start with a conservative subset (e.g. static functions with a closed set of call sites) before considering exported/API functions.
acceptance_criteria: Fact collector proves status-code convention across all call sites of a candidate function. Rewrite changes signature + call sites together, preserving control flow via ?. Differential tests pass on new fixtures; explicitly scoped to avoid rewriting functions whose return value is used non-boolean-ly anywhere.

title: Emit #[unsafe(no_mangle)] for externally-linked C symbols
description:
Why: emit_pub mode currently grants pub visibility to externally-linked items (src/lower.rs, the linkage_is_external(op) gate feeding the emit_pub Visibility::Pub branch) but attaches no symbol-name-preserving attribute. Rust's default mangling means the emitted pub fn/static does not actually keep the C symbol name, so any C caller expecting to link against e.g. void foo(void) cannot find it -- pub alone does not give C ABI linkage. This is the foundational gap all other jep.4 sub-tickets build on: weak, used/retain, and alias all attach to an already-externally-visible, correctly-named symbol.

What to do:
- In src/lower.rs, wherever linkage_is_external(op) currently gates Visibility::Pub, also attach a no-mangle marker to the emitted Item (function or static).
- Add an Item-level attribute variant in src/rust_ast.rs (e.g. Attr::NoMangle) rather than string-formatting; extend the existing Attr enum used for Allow/Repr/Derive.
- In src/codegen.rs, render it edition-2024-correctly: #[unsafe(no_mangle)] not bare #[no_mangle] (confirmed empirically: rustc --edition 2024 hard-errors E0658 'unsafe attribute used without unsafe' on bare #[no_mangle]).
- Only apply to items with CIR linkage == 0 (ExternalLinkage) that are actual definitions with a fixed C name.
- Internal linkage (CIR linkage == 7, InternalLinkage/static) must NOT get no_mangle -- keep current private-visibility behavior.
design: CIR linkage attr (attr_int(op, "linkage")) is the sole source of truth; no AST JSON needed. Confirmed encoding matches LLVM GlobalValue::LinkageTypes: External=0, Internal=7. Reuses the existing linkage_is_external() helper already in src/lower.rs -- this ticket extends its consumer, not the detection logic itself.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture: a C function and a C global with external linkage translated with emit_pub produce #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn/static in the generated Rust; nm/readelf on the compiled cdylib shows the undecorated C symbol name present. A static (internal-linkage) counterpart fixture confirms no no_mangle is emitted and the symbol does not appear in the dynamic symbol table. cargo fmt/cargo nextest r --release green.
notes: Empirically verified on local nightly (rustc 1.99.0-nightly): #[unsafe(no_mangle)] compiles cleanly under --edition 2024; bare #[no_mangle] is a hard E0658 error under that edition.
close_reason: Implemented typed no_mangle attributes and ABI-qualified external-linkage definitions. External emit_pub functions now render #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub extern "C" fn, external globals render #[unsafe(no_mangle)] pub static mut, and internal-linkage items remain private/unmangled. Verified with cargo test --test cross_tu and cargo nextest r --release on work/slate-jep.8 before merge.

title: Lower noreturn attributes into Rust never-returning signatures and call flow
description:
Why: noreturn affects function type, reachability, and dead code after calls. Preserving it can improve correctness around functions that exit, abort, or longjmp-style escape.

What to do:
- Add fixtures for __attribute__((noreturn)) and any _Noreturn spelling already visible to Clang.
- Extract noreturn facts from AST/CIR.
- Lower definitions/prototypes to Rust return type ! where the body/callee shape supports it, or keep conservative return type with explicit diagnostics otherwise.
- Ensure call sites after noreturn calls do not require fake fallthrough values.

Acceptance: noreturn fixtures compile and match C behavior; generated signatures use ! where supported; unsupported non-returning mechanisms are diagnosed explicitly.
close_reason: Merged: noreturn attributes lowered to Rust never-returning signatures in 622b28f (main 40490d8)

title: Lower __attribute__((constructor)) and __attribute__((destructor)) lifecycle hooks
description:
Why: constructor/destructor attributes change program lifecycle behavior and are common in C libraries for registration, counters, and process setup/teardown. Rust has no direct portable source-level equivalent, so Slate needs deliberate lowering or a clear unsupported diagnostic.

What to do:
- Add fixtures with constructor-only, destructor-only, and multiple priority-ordered hooks if Clang exposes priorities.
- Inspect Clang AST JSON and CIR/linkage output to identify where the attribute facts are available.
- Choose a Rust representation, likely platform/linker-section based init/fini arrays or generated runtime registration where supported.
- Preserve order where C requires it, and explicitly diagnose unsupported crate/target shapes.

Acceptance: fixtures prove hooks run before/after main when supported; generated Rust compiles and links on the default target; unsupported priority/target combinations produce intentional diagnostics rather than silently dropping hooks.
close_reason: Merged: constructor/destructor attributes lowered in 2103fb7

title: Lower packed and aligned record attributes into Rust repr attributes
description:
Why: packed/aligned attributes affect ABI layout, field offsets, and pointer safety. Dropping them can produce wrong generated Rust even if field access appears to compile.

What to do:
- Extract GNU/Clang packed and aligned attributes for structs/unions from AST facts.
- Lower to #[repr(C, packed)] / #[repr(C, packed(N))] / #[repr(C, align(N))] where Rust can express the layout.
- Audit field access for packed records so generated Rust avoids creating unaligned references.
- Add layout-sensitive fixtures using sizeof, alignof, offsetof, and field reads/writes.

Acceptance: packed/aligned fixture outputs match C; generated Rust uses the correct repr attributes; unaligned field access is handled safely or rejected.
notes: touches: src/lower.rs, tests/fixtures/
close_reason: Merged: packed/aligned record attributes lowered in eec7985

title: Lower C attributes with semantic Rust equivalents
description:
Why: Slate currently focuses on CIR operations and core type/layout facts, but C attributes can carry real semantics: lifecycle hooks, ABI/linkage, layout, allocation contracts, nullability, and control-flow facts. These are not optional fixups; when an attribute affects behavior, layout, or linkage, baseline lowering must preserve it or explicitly reject it.

What to do:
- Extract relevant GNU/Clang attributes from Clang AST JSON or CIR attrs where available.
- Lower behavior-affecting attributes into Rust items, ABI/linker attributes, runtime support, or explicit diagnostics.
- Keep optimization-only attributes as facts only when they can safely improve later analysis.
- Add one focused fixture per attribute family and verify with differential tests or compile/link shape tests as appropriate.

Out of scope: cosmetic-only source preservation unless it helps a semantic attribute.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level attribute families are tracked as children; implemented children add focused fixtures, preserve behavior/layout/linkage or diagnose unsupported semantics, and document the source of truth for attribute facts.
close_reason: All 13 children complete. Attribute families lowered across the epic: constructor/destructor lifecycle (jep.1), packed/aligned records (jep.2), noreturn (jep.3), linkage/visibility/weak/alias/used/retain/section (jep.4, jep.9, jep.10, jep.11, jep.13), nonnull/returns_nonnull pointer facts (jep.5), malloc/alloc_size/alloc_align/assume_aligned allocation facts (jep.6), no_mangle for externally-linked symbols (jep.8), alias forwarding wrappers (jep.12), and diagnostic/optimization attributes with direct Rust equivalents plus diagnosed-not-lowered fallback for the rest (jep.7).

title: Emit __builtin_assume as core::hint::assert_unchecked under UB-preserving mode
description:
Why: cir.assume is currently dropped, which is correct as a conservative optimizer-hint erasure but loses the source-level UB assumption. Rust has core::hint::assert_unchecked for exactly this kind of unchecked assumption, but emitting it is unsafe and makes false assumptions immediate undefined behavior.

What to do:
- Add a fixture for __builtin_assume and inspect the emitted cir.assume shape.
- Decide whether this is a default lowering change, an opt-in translation mode, or a fixup gated by an explicit UB-preserving policy.
- If implemented, emit unsafe { core::hint::assert_unchecked(cond) } with the condition preserved exactly and no extra runtime check.
- Keep a conservative path that can still erase the hint when Slate is not preserving optimizer assumptions.

Assumption: this is only valid when Slate intentionally preserves C's UB contract for violated assumptions.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures cover true and guarded assumption shapes; generated Rust uses core::hint::assert_unchecked only in the chosen UB-preserving path; default behavior and docs make the UB tradeoff explicit; cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Implemented cir.assume lowering to unsafe core::hint::assert_unchecked, added true and guarded __builtin_assume fixture coverage, documented the UB-preserving contract, and verified with cargo fmt plus cargo nextest r --release.

title: Promote atomic globals to native AtomicN storage
description: Why: fixtures such as tests/fixtures/mt-atomics.c already translate correctly, but file-scope _Atomic objects still lower as static mut primitive storage accessed through unsafe AtomicN::from_ptr(addr_of_mut!(...)). That keeps unnecessary unsafe in threaded code and obscures the intended std::sync::atomic storage shape.\n\nWhat to do: add a conservative fact/fixup path for file-scope integer/bool atomic globals that are only accessed through matching atomic operations, rewrite their static initializer to AtomicN::new(...), rewrite matching atomic places to AtomicPlace::Local, and leave ambiguous globals on the baseline path. Add output-shape coverage for mt-atomics and keep differential tests green.
acceptance_criteria: mt-atomics generated Rust emits static counter: std::sync::atomic::AtomicI32 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicI32::new(0); atomic counter uses call counter.fetch_add/load directly without unsafe AtomicI32::from_ptr(addr_of_mut!(counter)); ambiguous or mismatched global uses remain on the baseline path; cargo fmt and focused differential tests pass.
notes: touches: src/fixups/facts/atomic_locals.rs, src/fixups/rewrite/atomic_locals.rs, src/fixups/mod.rs, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Implemented conservative atomic global promotion in the atomic storage fixup. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Clean up non-volatile integer bit builtin temps
description: integer_bit_builtin_ops.c currently uses volatile inputs, forcing separate volatile reads. Make the fixture non-volatile and improve builtin temp generation so generated integer_bit_builtin_ops.rs does not keep pure result/copy temps around clz/ctz/popcount/parity/ffs/clrsb. Preserve volatile behavior for genuinely volatile fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: tests/fixtures/integer_bit_builtin_ops.c no longer declares the builtin input locals volatile; generated integer_bit_builtin_ops.rs has direct builtin expressions without _v temps for clz/ctz/popcount/parity/ffs/clrsb; differential coverage asserts these shapes; cargo test --test differential generated_differential passes; cargo test and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Made integer_bit_builtin_ops non-volatile and cleaned pure builtin temps by classifying primitive bit methods as movable pure and allowing same-statement alias inlining. Verified with cargo test --test differential generated_differential, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Use effect facts for dead-local discardability
description: Dead-local cleanup hand-rolls a narrow discardable initializer whitelist, so unread pure temps such as heap_vec_malloc index literals survive after ownership/index rewrites. Replace the discardability check with the existing effect analysis where safe, keeping volatile/atomic/call/memory side effects preserved, and run dead-local cleanup late enough to delete temps orphaned by heap/vector rewrites.
acceptance_criteria: heap_vec_malloc generated output has no let _v temps; dead_locals tests cover pure literal/value expressions being deleted and volatile/effectful initializers being kept; cargo test heap_malloc_buffer_uses_vec_drop and cargo test dead_locals pass; final cargo test and cargo nextest r --release pass.
close_reason: Implemented dead-local discardability using EffectKind-backed effect facts in src/fixups/rewrite/dead_locals.rs, added a late dead-local fixpoint after heap ownership cleanup, and covered heap_vec_malloc no-temp output. Verified with cargo test --test differential generated_differential, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Lower for-loop continue as direct structured control flow
description: Why: tests/fixtures.generated/continue_for.rs and tests/fixtures.generated/loop_break_continue.rs still lower C for-loop continue into synthetic labels and labeled blocks like '__continue0: { ... break '__continue0; }' plus labeled loop breaks. The original C fixtures are straightforward for loops with break/continue and should emit direct structured Rust, not workaround blocks or state-machine-like labels. Evidence: continue_while.rs and break_for.rs are already simple loop/break/continue forms, but continue_for.rs wraps the body so the step expression runs after a C continue. Root area: src/lower.rs lower_for/lower_for_loop_body/lower_continue, especially the LoopFrame continue_label path around lines 347-354 and 4771-4833. What to do: teach for-loop lowering or a narrow post-lowering fixup to represent the step explicitly so C continue lowers to a real continue target without '__continue blocks. Likely shape: split the loop body into condition, body, explicit step, and make continue jump to the step before looping, while preserving break and nested-loop behavior. Verify against continue_for.c and loop_break_continue.c.
acceptance_criteria: tests/fixtures.generated/continue_for.rs has no '__continue labels and uses direct structured loop control; tests/fixtures.generated/loop_break_continue.rs has no '__continue labels while preserving the inner break behavior; break_for.rs and continue_while.rs remain semantically unchanged; cargo test --test differential generated_differential passes; cargo nextest r --release passes.
notes: touches: src/lower.rs or src/fixups/rewrite/* for for-loop continue cleanup, src/fixups/mod.rs if adding pass, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Implemented a for-loop continue cleanup pass that rewrites synthetic __continue blocks into direct guarded bodies and removes unused __loop labels. Verified with cargo test --test differential generated_differential, cargo test, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Densify the compare_exchange result/expected chain
description:
Why: each atomic_compare_exchange_strong currently expands to a 4-temp chain: 'let _v34: Result<i32,i32> = ...compare_exchange(...); let _v35 = match _v34 { Ok(v)|Err(v) => v }; let _v36 = _v34.is_ok(); let _v37 = !_v36; if _v37 { expected = _v35; } cmpxchg_bool = _v36;'. The C pattern (write expected on failure, yield success bool) maps to one dense match.

What to do: add a fixup recognizing the lowered cmpxchg chain shape and rewriting it to 'ok = match a.compare_exchange(expected, desired, succ, fail) { Ok(_) => true, Err(v) => { expected = v; false } };' (or '.is_ok()' when the expected out-param is provably unused afterward). At minimum the '!is_ok' double negation must go. Keep baseline lowering (src/lower.rs lower_atomic_cmpxchg) as the correct verbose form; the strong-only policy (never compare_exchange_weak, to avoid spurious-failure divergence in differential runs) must be preserved.

Verify: differential atomics test passes; both success and failure cmpxchg paths in the fixture stay correct (ok=1/expected untouched, bad=0/expected2 updated to 42).
acceptance_criteria:
- cmpxchg lowers to a single match (or is_ok) expression per call after fixups.
- Failure path still writes back the observed value to the expected local.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Implemented a late atomic compare_exchange fixup that rewrites the result/value/is_ok/negation/failure-write chain into a single match expression preserving expected writeback. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Inline single-use atomic result temps into their bindings
description:
Why: even after lowerer-side alloca forwarding, atomic results that survive as temps ('atomic_temp = a.fetch_add(...); fa = atomic_temp;') should collapse to 'fa = a.fetch_add(...)' and then fuse with the zero-init declaration into 'let fa = a.fetch_add(5, Ordering::SeqCst);'. Existing pure-temp inlining refuses side-effecting expressions, so atomic calls need an order-preserving single-use inline: safe only when the temp's sole use is the immediately following statement with no intervening effects.

What to do: extend the effects facts (src/fixups/facts/effects.rs) and the inline-temps family (src/fixups/rewrite/inline_temps.rs or a sibling) to permit adjacent single-use inlining of Atomic* expressions. Cover match arms / dispatch bodies via the shared walkers so goto-fallback functions benefit too.

Verify: differential tests pass; atomics.rs shows 'let fa = ...fetch_add(...)' shape with no atomic_temp intermediary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Atomic fetch/swap/load results bind directly to their named local.
- Inlining only fires for adjacent single-use with no intervening effectful statement.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Implemented adjacent atomic result temp chaining and late zero-init declaration sinking so atomics.c emits direct let bindings for load/fetch/swap results. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features, and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Promote non-escaping _Atomic locals to native AtomicN storage
description:
Why: an atomic_int local currently keeps plain integer storage ('let mut a: i32 = 0') and every access re-derives 'unsafe { AtomicI32::from_ptr(std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(a)) }'. When the local's address never escapes non-atomically, this is pure noise: the local can own AtomicN storage and every access becomes a safe direct method call.

What to do:
- Add a fact (src/fixups/facts/) proving a local is only accessed through AtomicN::from_ptr(addr_of_mut!(local)) atomic ops (plus its initializer and plain reads expressible as atomic loads, e.g. the final '(int)a' cast in the fixture).
- Add a rewrite fixup (src/fixups/rewrite/) that changes the declaration to 'let a = AtomicI32::new(init);' and rewrites each access to a direct call on 'a', dropping the unsafe blocks and from_ptr wrappers.
- AST-to-AST only per docs/writing-a-fixup.md; use the shared walkers (facts/walk.rs, support/walk.rs). Baseline lowering stays as-is — disabling this fixup must still leave correct Rust.

Verify: differential atomics test passes; output-shape assertion that atomics.rs contains no from_ptr and no unsafe for the promoted local.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fact collector proves non-escape; conservative on any address escape or non-atomic write.
- Fixture local 'a' becomes AtomicI32 storage with safe method calls.
- Disabling the fixup still yields correct (verbose) Rust.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Atomic ops now carry AtomicPlace (Ptr unsafe from_ptr view vs Local safe direct call); baseline unsafe moved from codegen into an explicit Expr::Unsafe in the lowerer. New fact facts/atomic_locals.rs proves a local int slot is only named as the pointer operand of matching-width atomic ops; rewrite/atomic_locals.rs re-declares it as AtomicN::new(init) and unwraps ops to safe direct calls. atomics.rs now has zero unsafe/from_ptr; escaping/global atomics stay on baseline. Verified with cargo nextest r --release (513 passed incl. 4 new unit tests + new shape test).

title: Forward per-call CIR atomic temp allocas in the lowerer
description:
Why: clang emits a fresh .atomictmp alloca for each atomic op's value operand and an atomic-temp alloca for each result. Slate's lowerer hoists every one as a named local, so tests/fixtures.generated/atomics.rs opens with ~15 shadowed 'let mut _atomictmp'/'let mut atomic_temp' declarations, and zero_init fuses the first store's value into the last shadow's initializer — correct only by accident of shadowing order, and unreadable.

What to do: in src/lower.rs, recognize these single-store-then-single-load compiler temps and forward the stored value directly instead of materializing a named local: 'a.store(100, SeqCst)' rather than '_atomictmp = 100; ...store(_atomictmp, ...)', and bind results straight to their consumer slot instead of routing through atomic_temp. This is baseline-lowering work (correctness must not depend on any fixup); keep the named-local path for allocas that genuinely have multiple stores or escape.

Verify: differential test for atomics.c passes; generated output has zero shadowed _atomictmp/atomic_temp declarations; full nextest suite green.
acceptance_criteria:
- No shadowed compiler-temp declarations in atomics.rs.
- Atomic operand values appear inline in the atomic call expression.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
close_reason: Lowerer now forwards single-store/single-load compiler-temp allocas (.atomictmp, atomic-temp, cmpxchg.bool) as SSA values instead of hoisting shadowed named locals; non-literal values snapshot into immutable temps at the store site. Verified with cargo nextest r --release (508 passed) and a new output-shape test asserting no _atomictmp/atomic_temp/cmpxchg_bool locals and inline atomic operands.

title: Lower atomics densely to idiomatic std::sync::atomic
acceptance_criteria:
- atomics.rs contains no shadowed _atomictmp/atomic_temp declarations; atomic operands inline into the call site.
- A non-escaping local atomic_int lowers (via facts+fixup) to AtomicI32 storage with safe direct method calls; no unsafe/from_ptr for it.
- The compare_exchange chain collapses to a single dense expression per call.
- memory_order/atomic_flag items are not emitted when unused.
- Differential tests pass throughout; correctness never depends on a fixup.
- Fuzzer (tests/support/cgen.rs) and c.bnf cover the atomic subset.
close_reason: Closed

title: Drop redundant casts around narrow integer array arithmetic
description: array_types.rs emits casts like ((values[0] as i32) + (values[1] as i32)) as i8 for C narrow integer array arithmetic. Add a safe rewrite so equivalent same-width narrow additions assigned back to that type render closer to the C source.

title: Inline aggregate member access temps in generated fixtures
description: aggregate_value_member_ops.rs currently spills function return/member accesses into temporaries instead of keeping the expressions close to the C source. Fix the relevant lowering/fixup path and cover the generated fixture output.
notes: touches: tests/fixtures/generated/aggregate_value_member_ops.rs and likely temp/member access fixups
close_reason: Classified pure field and tuple-field reads as movable pure so inline_temps can collapse aggregate member/index temp chains; added unit and aggregate fixture shape coverage. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo nextest r --release.

title: Fuse zero-init array locals with first literal assignment
description: Why: array_init still emits local arrays as zero-initialized mutable declarations followed by immediate full-array assignments, e.g. let mut a = [0; 5]; a = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]; This keeps unnecessary mutability and separates the original C initializer from the declaration.\n\nWhat to do: extend the fixup layer so safe zero-init locals with an immediate full replacement assignment are emitted as declaration initializers, including fixed-size arrays and padded char arrays, allowing remove_mut to drop mut where no later writes remain. Use tests/fixtures/array_init.c as the regression.
design: Keep this in the existing zero_init/fixup pipeline. Reuse binding/fact checks and only fuse when the assignment is the first overwrite for the exact local binding and does not rely on the placeholder value.
acceptance_criteria: array_init generated Rust combines a, partial, and padded declarations with their literal initializers; no immediate follow-up assignment remains for those locals; remove_mut drops mut for locals that are not otherwise mutated; differential tests remain green.
notes: touches: src/fixups/rewrite/zero_init.rs, tests/differential.rs
close_reason: Implemented repeated zero array placeholder facts so zero_init fuses array declarations with first literal assignments, allowing remove_mut to drop array mutability in array_init. Verified with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features and cargo nextest r --release.

title: M4: Flip lowerer to always-dispatch; delete structured lowering
description: In lower.rs replace try_lower_structured_goto/lower_dispatch branch with always lower_dispatch. Delete try_lower_structured_goto, try_lower_acyclic_static_goto, try_lower_localized_cycle, simple_self_loop and their helpers; re-point any remaining CFG use at facts/goto.rs. All goto* fixtures now route dispatch->fixup. Update differential.rs shape assertions naming __state0/__dispatch0 where the fixup now emits __blockN/structured forms.
acceptance_criteria: Lowerer has one goto path (naive dispatch); cargo nextest r --release green; every goto* output at least as good as before; computed_goto_ops stays dispatch.

Structuring now lives entirely in fixups/rewrite/goto.rs (self-loop + localized-cycle added). 497 tests green; goto fixtures at least as good as before; computed_goto_ops stays dispatch.

title: I1: Structure acyclic reducible branch-with-join (if/else)
description: Extend rewrite::goto to handle a state whose terminator is Branch(cond,a,b) reconverging at a post-dominator: emit if cond {..} else {..} then continue at the join. Turns goto_if_scope into if/else + println!, and goto_return_value into two guard ifs with early returns (no join -> no loop, no state var).
acceptance_criteria: goto_if_scope output is if/else + println with no __state/__dispatch; goto_return_value is two guard ifs + return 1 with no loop; differential green.

title: M2: Recognize dispatch loop from Rust AST in facts/goto.rs
description: Facts collector matching Stmt::Loop{[Match{Var(__stateN), arms}]}. Extract entry state and per-state (body, terminator) where terminator is Goto(k)/Branch(cond,a,b)/Terminal. Guard flags forcing fallback: non-constant state assignment (computed goto __state=[..][idx]) and irreducible multi-entry SCC. Unit-tested on hand-built AST; no rewrite yet.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover Goto/Branch/Terminal extraction and both guard flags; computed_goto + irreducible flagged unstructurable.

title: M3: goto_structure rewrite fixup at parity (src/fixups/rewrite/goto.rs)
description: New rewrite::goto fixup run to fixpoint at top of apply() (before early inline_temps). Reproduce today's three structured shapes from the dispatch loop: linear chain -> straight-line (goto_forward); single-block back-edge -> loop{...; if !cond break} (goto_backward_loop); one non-entry cycle -> peel entry/exit, residual loop{match __blockN} (goto_irreducible). Behavior parity (differential), not byte parity.
acceptance_criteria: With lowerer still structuring, fixup fires only on dispatch loops; differential green; goto_forward/backward_loop/irreducible behavior unchanged.
close_reason: goto-structuring fixup landed; goto_if_scope->if/else, goto_return_value->guard ifs, others unchanged. 501 tests pass.

title: M1: Move goto CFG analysis into src/fixups/facts/goto.rs
description: Relocate the dispatch CFG graph algorithms (DispatchCfg, dominators, natural_loop, cyclic_sccs, cycle_entry_targets, CfgNode/CfgEdge types) out of lower.rs into src/fixups/facts/goto.rs. Front-end-agnostic graph code so both the (soon-deleted) CIR path and the new Rust-AST recognizer can use it. Do NOT create src/cfg.rs (collides conceptually with src/cfg_translate config translation). Pure refactor: no output change.
