title: Fix string non-libc-shim blocker
description: memset is lowered to slice fill and then used as an expression.
notes: Root cause: clang-ir crate's #cir.const_array trailing_zeros parser only ever emitted trailing_zeros_num=0/1 (bool cast) instead of the actual byte gap (outer array size - literal length), so any C string constant with more than one trailing zero byte (e.g. "abc\0\0\0\0" as an 8-byte memcmp buffer) got truncated when re-encoded as a Rust byte string. Fixed in /home/takashi/Projects/clang-ir/clang-ir/src/parser/attrs.rs parse_cir_const_array to compute trailing_zeros_num from the outer array type's size minus the literal's element count. Not a memset/slice-fill issue as originally described -- memset lowers to a direct extern call here. libc and lowering/rewrites profiles all pass; promoted tests/fixtures.libc-test/functional/(un)supported/string.c and tests/fixtures.gcc-torture(.unsupported)/string-opt-5.c.
close_reason: Fixed clang-ir const_array trailing_zeros parsing bug; string.c and string-opt-5.c promoted to supported, libc/lowering/rewrites all green

title: Fix setjmp non-libc-shim blocker
description: CIR codegen does not implement volatile aggregate lvalue-to-rvalue casts.
notes: Confirmed root cause: ClangIR's CIRGenExprAggregate.cpp (AggExprEmitter::VisitCastExpr, CK_LValueToRValue case, ~line 289) explicitly calls errorNYI for a volatile-qualified aggregate lvalue-to-rvalue cast (e.g. 'set = oldset;' where oldset is 'volatile sigset_t'). This is upstream ClangIR codegen (~/llvm-project/clang/lib/CIR/CodeGen/), not a Slate lowering/fixup gap -- Slate never sees the construct because clang -emit-cir fails outright. Classic (non-CIR) CodeGen handles this in CGExprAgg.cpp's CK_LValueToRValue case by forcing the destination into existence and visiting the subexpr; ClangIR needs the equivalent implemented before this fixture can even reach Slate. Blocked on upstream ClangIR, not actionable from the slate repo.

title: Fix pthread_cancel-points non-libc-shim blocker
description: Anonymous struct field accesses are not lowered correctly.
notes: Root cause: src/frontend/lowerer/types.rs cir_type_to_ctype() unwrapped every pointer type generically via cir_ptr_pointee before checking what it pointed to, so a function-pointer field's pointee (CirType::Func) fell through every match arm to the int32 default, producing CType::Ptr(CType::Int{32}) i.e. Rust *mut i32 for function-pointer struct fields (anonymous or named). lower_record_def then only trusted the separately-derived CIR field type when field.ty was ALREADY CType::FuncPtr, so the wrong CType silently won. Fixed by special-casing CirType::Func in cir_type_to_ctype to build CType::FuncPtr{ret,params} directly. Also silently fixed the same latent bug in tests/fixtures/gnu_libc_allocation.c's obstack bitfield storage fields (previously *mut i32/*mut c_void, now correctly Option<fn ptr>) -- updated its snapshot. libc, lowering, and rewrites profiles all green; promoted pthread_cancel-points.c to supported.
close_reason: Fixed cir_type_to_ctype function-pointer field mis-derivation; pthread_cancel-points.c promoted, libc/lowering/rewrites all green

title: Fix pthread_cancel non-libc-shim blocker
description: CIR codegen does not implement CleanupAttr for pthread cleanup handlers.
notes: Confirmed root cause: pthread_cancel.c uses pthread_cleanup_push/pop, which libc-shim/include/pthread.h implements via a struct with __attribute__((__cleanup__(...))) (GNU cleanup attribute). ClangIR's codegen has no support for this: clang -emit-cir fails outright with 'ClangIR code gen Not Yet Implemented: emitAutoVarCleanups: CleanupAttr' at each pthread_cleanup_push call site. This is upstream ClangIR (~/llvm-project/clang/lib/CIR/CodeGen/), matching the bead's original 'CIR cleanup attr' description -- not reachable/fixable from the slate repo. Blocked on upstream ClangIR, same class of issue as slate-os0h.19.3.6.5 (setjmp's volatile aggregate cast NYI).

title: Audit long double pointer parameter typing (out-params, scanf-style)
description: long double* parameters (e.g. scanf("%Lf", &ld)) don't need new ABI shimming -- a pointer argument is just an address, not subject to SysV eightbyte classification, and .2's F80 struct already matches C's real long-double memory representation byte-for-byte (align 16, size 16, payload in bytes 0-9), so a *mut F80 / long double* pun should already be sound. This is an audit, not new machinery: confirm codegen actually emits *mut F80 (not e.g. *mut f64) for long double* parameter and return-pointer types, on all three ABI variants.
acceptance_criteria: Extern declarations and generated code use *mut F80 / *const F80 for long double* on x87 targets (and the corresponding f64/f128 pointer on f64-abi/quad-abi targets); a pointer out-param fixture (scanf-style) round-trips bit-exact.
notes: Verified pointer ABI coverage without new lowering machinery. Added bit-exact x87 sscanf %La out-parameter differential coverage; retained ext_store/ext_load mutable/const pointer runtime coverage in the long-double link fixture; added macOS/MSVC f64 and Bionic f128 target fixtures plus generated-signature assertions. Full lowering profile, link suite, Clippy, and formatting pass.
close_reason: Pointer parameter audit complete with x87 runtime and f64/f128 target regressions

title: scsi/scsi.h and arpa/telnet.h define conflicting ABORT/NOP enumerators
description: scsi/scsi.h's SCSI command enum defines ABORT=0x06 and NOP=0x08; arpa/telnet.h's option enum defines ABORT=238 and NOP=241. Both are real, independently-correct glibc headers -- no real C program includes both together, so this is arguably not a shim bug but a property of the two upstream header surfaces. It only surfaces because tests/libc_shim_suite.rs compiles every public header into a single translation unit per arch/os target (mirroring the user's ask to prove 'all the headers it can' compile). Needs a decision: either exclude one member of specific known-incompatible header pairs from the combined all-headers compile (documented, not silent), or determine there's a real fix (unlikely, since both enumerator sets are what real glibc/POSIX ships).
acceptance_criteria: Either the combined-header test has a documented, explicit exception for this pair, or the collision is resolved; tests/libc_shim_suite.rs no longer fails on ABORT/NOP redefinition.
close_reason: Changed the public-header gate to compile every header independently, preserving self-containment coverage without requiring two legitimately incompatible glibc headers in one translation unit; all six architecture gates pass and are enabled.

title: Delete slate's hand-rolled goto/switch-fallthrough machinery once flatten-cfg+dispatch path is proven
description:
Tracked separately from slate-5udb (which builds the general
--cir-flatten-cfg --cir-goto-solver + dispatch-mode lowering path) so
removal is a distinct, deliberately-sequenced step: land and prove the new
path first (full corpus + nextest clean), THEN come back and delete what it
makes redundant, rather than coupling "add" and "remove" into one risky
change.

Two things to delete/simplify once slate-5udb is verified in production
(real corpus regenerated, differential suite green, no regressions):

1. DEFINITELY delete: the hand-rolled goto closure-extraction machinery
   slate-sy7c/slate-fex8 added to handle specific goto shapes one at a time
   (find_goto_label_tail, free_cir_operands, the goto_closures field on
   FunctionLowerer, the "extractable" tail-shape filtering in lower_func,
   the CirOpKind::Goto special-case in region_ends_control_flow). slate-5udb
   already lists this in its own acceptance criteria -- this ticket exists
   so it doesn't get forgotten/skipped once the new path lands, and so
   slate-fex8 gets closed as superseded instead of separately implemented.

2. OPEN QUESTION, needs a decision when this is picked up: does
   lower_switch's OWN fallthrough-loop synthesis (the `'__switchN: loop {
   match __switch_caseN { ... __switch_caseN = next; continue '__switchN;
   } }` construct it builds by hand for C-style case fallthrough) also
   become redundant now that a general flatten+dispatch path exists for
   goto-bearing functions? Two ways this could go, and this ticket doesn't
   presuppose which is right:

     (a) Keep lower_switch as-is for switches that don't contain a goto --
         it produces more idiomatic output (a real loop+match rather than a
         numbered state machine) for the common case, and only goto-bearing
         functions pay the "ugly but correct" dispatch-mode cost. This is
         the status quo shape slate-5udb's design already assumes.

     (b) Route EVERY switch with fallthrough (goto or not) through
         flatten+dispatch uniformly, and delete lower_switch's own
         loop-synthesis, region_ends_control_flow's switch-specific
         reasoning, and the SwitchCase/switch_case helper entirely, on the
         theory that clang/cir-opt already solves "arbitrary C control flow
         -> canonical lowerable form" and slate re-deriving a chunk of that
         itself (case fallthrough loop synthesis, case-index remapping,
         etc.) is duplicated effort now that the general path exists for
         the harder (goto) case anyway. Cost: measurably uglier generated
         Rust for the (much more common) plain-fallthrough-switch case,
         since every such switch would become a numbered state machine
         instead of a `'label: loop { match {...} }`. Needs an actual A/B
         look at generated output for a representative switch before
         deciding this is worth it -- "shouldn't have to hand-roll this
         since clang already can" is a real argument for less code to
         maintain, but idiomatic-output quality is also a stated project
         goal (CLAUDE.md: "idiomatize later" implies later passes exist to
         recover idiom -- deleting a working idiom-preserving path for
         everything is the opposite direction unless a later fixup pass
         can cheaply re-collapse a simple dispatch loop back into a plain
         match, in which case (b) plus that fixup might net out equivalent
         in both correctness and quality).
design: Do not start until slate-5udb has landed and been verified against the full corpus (real libexpat rebuild + differential suite green). Then: (1) delete the slate-sy7c/slate-fex8 goto-extraction code listed above and confirm nextest still passes; (2) spend a short investigation comparing generated output for a handful of representative switch fixtures under option (a) vs (b) before committing to deleting lower_switch's own synthesis -- this is a quality/maintenance tradeoff, not a correctness one, so it deserves a deliberate look rather than defaulting to 'delete more code'.
acceptance_criteria: find_goto_label_tail/free_cir_operands/goto_closures/the extractable-filter in lower_func are deleted and nextest is still 254/254 (or current count) green. A decision (with rationale, either keep or delete) is recorded for lower_switch's fallthrough-loop synthesis before this closes.
notes: Done. Removed find_goto_label_tail, free_cir_operands, goto_closures field, and the extractable-filter branch in lower_func. lower_goto reverted to its original pre-slate-sy7c form (dispatch-mode only, no-op otherwise -- correct now since any structured function containing a goto is unconditionally routed through cir::emit_module's flatten path before lower_func ever sees it, so the structured-mode goto branch was provably unreachable). Verified: full nextest 254/254, real libexpat corpus rebuilt+run at 100% (4836/4836) both before and after the deletion, confirming the old code was truly dead and nothing regressed.
close_reason: Dead code removed and verified (254/254 nextest, 4836/4836 real libexpat corpus unchanged).

title: Indirect call arguments not cast to void* through a function-pointer parameter/value
description: eep4.16 fixed void* argument casting for DIRECT calls (via self.parent.externs / function_param_types, both keyed by callee name) and for local-array-decay in lower_cast. Indirect calls (callee_name is empty string in lower_call) never get this treatment: cast_void_ptr_call_args is only consulted via a name-keyed lookup, and eep4.17's new loaded_field_types map only populates for struct-field loads whose function-pointer return type is a named enum, not for plain function-pointer PARAMETERS (which have no associated struct field load at all) or void-returning function pointers. Real libexpat: xmlwf/readfilemap.c's 'void (*processor)(const void*, size_t, const tchar*, void*)' parameter, called as 'processor(p, nbytes, name, arg)' where 'p'/'filemap_c' is a differently-typed pointer -- generated Rust: 'processor.unwrap()(std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(filemap_c), 0, name, arg);' errors 'expected *mut c_void, found *mut i8'.
acceptance_criteria: New C fixture: a function taking a function-pointer parameter whose own signature has a void* parameter, called indirectly through that parameter with an argument of a distinct pointer type. Generated Rust casts the argument to void* and compiles. Differential tests clean. translate-project against real libexpat's xmlwf/readfilemap.c produces zero such errors. cargo fmt/clippy/nextest pass.
close_reason: Root cause was NOT lower_call's argument-cast logic at all (though widened function_param_types/loaded_field_types lookups there for indirect calls, via new per-parameter loaded_field_types registration at function entry, to generalize eep4.17's enum-only tracking to any fn-ptr-typed value) -- the actual bug was in lower_cast's fallback for casting the address of a KNOWN Rust global (e.g. XML_SetUserData-style static-local char) that isn't an array: it fell through global_array_decay_expr (array-only) straight to an unmodified Val::Global passthrough, silently dropping the cir.cast's pointer-type reinterpretation entirely. Fixed by materializing an explicit Cast{AddrOf{Var(sanitized_name)}, target_ty} in that fallback. First attempt routed through pointer_operand_expr/store_address_expr, which incorrectly derefs over-aligned globals (breaking the chibicc alignof test, since deref-through-a-mutable-static requires unsafe); switched to a direct AddrOf matching the codebase's existing pattern for the same shape. Verified against real libexpat: cargo check now reports ZERO errors (down from 15 originally across all 5 child bugs).

title: Invasive allocation/AST refactor: arena/bump allocation + reduce Expr/Stmt/Type clone pressure
description:
Backburner - deferred after slate-nufb.1/slate-nufb.2's fishing rounds hit
a wall that isn't fixable with targeted per-function fixes.

Context: after slate-nufb.1 (per-function salsa split) and slate-nufb.2's
several rounds of cargo-flamegraph-driven fixes (expression_parents
algorithm, all_binding_refs consolidation, redundant clone removal),
real xmltok.c translation time went from 32.2s/32.5s to ~14.8-15.4s
(>52% reduction, epic total). The remaining profile is now dominated by
two things that DON'T have a narrow fix:

1. mimalloc allocator overhead (~12% of runtime: _mi_page_malloc_zero,
   mi_free, mi_theap_malloc_aligned, etc.) - this is call-VOLUME driven
   (millions of small allocations across the pipeline, confirmed via
   heaptrack earlier in slate-te22.4), not allocator inefficiency -
   mimalloc is already the fast allocator. Reducing this requires cutting
   allocation COUNT, which likely means arena/bump allocation for
   short-lived per-round/per-pass data (fixup rule evaluation scratch
   state, EditSet construction, etc.) rather than swapping allocators
   again.

2. The core AST walk (exprs_with_path, called from QueryContext::new()
   and elsewhere) plus Expr/Stmt/Type::clone/drop_glue - together ~11-13%
   of runtime, close to irreducible without restructuring either the
   walker itself or how pervasively the AST gets cloned (many query/rule
   code paths clone whole Expr/Stmt/Type subtrees where a reference or
   Rc/Arc-based sharing might suffice).

Both are real, measured (via cargo flamegraph on real xmltok.c, not
guessed), but both require an invasive, cross-cutting refactor rather
than a targeted fix in one function - the "easy wins" methodology that
worked for slate-nufb.1/.2 (measure -> find one narrow fix -> verify ->
measure again) has run its course; what's left needs its own design pass
before implementation starts.

NOT scheduled - no acceptance criteria yet. When picked up: start with a
cargo flamegraph baseline (current numbers: ~14.8-15.4s on real
xmltok.c/expat), decide arena-allocation scope (which structures/lifetimes
are actually short-lived enough to arena-allocate safely without fighting
the existing owned-Program-in-place-mutation model), and decide whether
AST clone reduction is feasible without a larger Rc/Arc-based ownership
change to rust_ast::{Expr,Stmt,Type}.

title: Investigate residual superlinear scaling on serial-dependency-chain functions
description:
After all five fixes in slate-xzn6.4/slate-xzn6.6, a synthetic adversarial
fixture (one function, one variable serially read-modify-written thousands of
times, e.g. `total = total + (x+i)*3-2;` repeated N times) still scales
worse than linear: at the time slate-xzn6.6 closed, going from 1500 to 4500
statements (3x) took wall-clock time from ~4.5s to ~26s (~5.8x, expected ~3x
if linear). The last `perf report` taken (see slate-xzn6.6 notes) no longer
had a single dominant contributor - it was spread across many <10% sites
including SalsaFacts::place, binding_type_ast, binding_by_local_path (now
tracked as slate-te22.1/te22.2) plus generic allocation overhead (cfree,
malloc, Vec<PathSegment> cloning).

This ticket is specifically about *re-measuring* the scaling curve after
slate-te22.1 and slate-te22.2 land, since they may already resolve most or
all of the residual superlinearity (they were found on exactly this
fixture's profile). If a real gap remains after those land, profile again
and either find the next contributor or conclude it's architectural (the
fixpoint round loop in src/fixups/mod.rs's to_fixpoint_program_with_facts
re-collects and re-scans on every round; a serial dependency chain forces the
overlap-avoidance windowing in PlanBuilder::finish/add_rule to spread
resolution across many rounds when adjacent temps' edit sites conflict) and
document the tradeoff rather than chasing it further, since real C code
(including the original xmltok.c motivator) doesn't produce this shape.

Note: don't add a fixture for the fully-fixed-linear case unless the curve
actually becomes linear - the point of this ticket is honest re-measurement,
not proving a predetermined conclusion.
acceptance_criteria:
Notes on this ticket record: the N=1500/3000/4500 (or similar) wall-clock
scaling curve measured after slate-te22.1/te22.2 land, whether it's now
linear-ish, and if not, either a further fix + updated curve, or a documented
explanation of the architectural cause with no fix attempted.

Repro (same generator used in slate-xzn6.6, not currently checked in - regenerate
with a small script):
  for each N in 1500 3000 4500:
    write a C file: `static long chain(long x) { long total = 0;
    total = total + (x+i)*3-2; /* repeated N times, i = 1..N */ return total; }
    int main(void) { printf("%ld\n", chain(1)); return 0; }`
    time slate translate <file>  (after SLATE_CLANG/SLATE_CIR_OPT env are set)
Compare ratio of times to ratio of N to judge linearity.
notes:
Re-measured after te22.1/te22.2/te22.5/te22.6/te22.7 landed, then did substantial additional work this session. Summary of what was tried, in order:

1. Sanity baseline: clang -O3 compiles the 4500-statement serial-chain fixture in ~0.1s. Slate was at 18.1s at the start of this session - confirmed there was real room, not just noise.

2. mimalloc (kept): swapped the global allocator (#[global_allocator] in src/main.rs, mimalloc crate). Zero logic changes. Gave a clean, consistent ~20-24% wall-clock win across all sizes with the SAME scaling shape (ratios for 2x/1.5x size inputs were unchanged before/after) - confirms allocator overhead was a real but constant-factor cost, not the source of superlinearity.

3. heaptrack allocation-site analysis (glibc malloc build, since heaptrack can't see mimalloc's internal allocations - had to temporarily disable/re-enable mimalloc for this). Top site at N=300: 1.56M calls to facts::def_use_query_path (called from bindings_read_under/bindings_written_under), which allocates a fresh filtered Vec<PathSegment> every call just to run one paths_overlap comparison, then discards it.

4. Tried caching QueryContext::binding_uses results with a RefCell inside QueryContext - DEAD END. RefCell<T> is always invariant in T, and T here would need to carry the 'snapshot lifetime, which made QueryContext<'snapshot> invariant and broke lifetime-subtyping assumptions relied on in 10+ fixup rule files. Reverted immediately; this is why proper caching needs real salsa memoization instead (see slate-nufb).

5. Tried making AstPath's inner storage SmallVec<[PathSegment; 8 or 4]> instead of Vec<PathSegment>, to make the def_use_query_path allocation free (inline/stack-only for typical short paths). This backfired: PathSegment is 16 bytes, so SmallVec<[PathSegment;8]> made AstPath 144 bytes (vs Vec's 24) - and AstPath is embedded in Rejection (clippy flagged it directly, 328 bytes), DefUseFact (Vec<AstPath> for both reads and writes), BTreeMap keys in several of this epic's own indexes, etc. Every QueryResult<T> = Result<Proof<T>, Rejection> returned by case.fact(...) - which is most of the engine's hot path - got wider to move on every call, most of which are rejections. Benchmarked SmallVec<4>: consistently SLOWER than plain Vec+mimalloc (e.g. 4500: 14.8s vs 13.8s). Reverted fully via git checkout back to the pre-session commit for all facts::/query:: files, keeping only the genuinely-unrelated te22.7 salsa.rs work and the mimalloc change. smallvec dependency removed.

6. Instead, wrote facts::def_use_query_path_overlaps(query_path: &AstPath, other: &[PathSegment]) -> bool, an allocation-free equivalent of paths_overlap(&def_use_query_path(path).0, other) - compares the filtered-on-the-fly segments of query_path against other element-by-element via iterators, without ever materializing an intermediate AstPath/Vec. Used only in the two confirmed-hot call sites (SalsaFacts::bindings_read_under/bindings_written_under); the older facts::binding_read_under free function (collector-internal, not per-candidate) was left alone. Small but real and risk-free win: ~3-5% additional improvement, zero struct-size or variance tradeoff.

Final scaling curve (mimalloc + def_use_query_path_overlaps), vs this session's starting point:
  N=1500: 3.07s -> 2.37s (23% faster)
  N=3000: 8.78s -> 6.84s (22% faster)
  N=4500: 18.1s -> 13.24s (27% faster)
Cumulative vs the pre-te22-epic baseline (slate-xzn6.6's endpoint): roughly 2x faster across the board (e.g. N=4500: 25.8s -> 13.24s).

Scaling shape is still mildly superlinear (2x input size costs ~2.9x time, 1.5x input size costs ~1.9x time - both down from worse ratios at session start, but not linear). Full nextest 250/250, fmt/clippy clean, byte-identical output on every fixture including real xmltok.c (~33s, down from the te22.7 endpoint's ~43.5s mostly via mimalloc).

Conclusion: the remaining superlinearity is architectural, not a remaining low-hanging fruit. QueryContext gets fully rebuilt (a fresh O(program-size) walk) on every (pass x round) combination, and proper fixes (real memoization of derived per-candidate queries like binding_uses, avoiding full QueryContext reconstruction) require QueryContext's own state to become salsa-tracked - which is exactly slate-nufb's scope, filed as a backburner epic this session. Not chasing further here.
close_reason: Landed mimalloc (~20-24% win, kept) and an allocation-free def_use_query_path_overlaps (~3-5% additional, kept). Tried and reverted a SmallVec<PathSegment> experiment - it made AstPath 6x wider, which bloated Rejection/DefUseFact/BTreeMap-key sizes throughout the hot path and was a net loss despite eliminating allocations (PathSegment being Copy didn't save it - the cost was struct-size amplification through Result<T,Rejection> plumbing, not copy cost). Also confirmed a QueryContext-level cache for binding_uses isn't viable without breaking lifetime variance - real caching needs salsa itself. Net: ~2x faster than the pre-epic baseline on the adversarial fixture (N=4500: 25.8s -> 13.24s), real xmltok.c ~43.5s -> ~33s. Remaining superlinearity is architectural (full QueryContext rebuild every pass x round) - filed as slate-nufb, backburner.

title: Audit fixups/salsa.rs for remaining linear-scan fact accessors
description:
slate-xzn6.4 and slate-xzn6.6 fixed five instances of the same anti-pattern
(a memoized `Vec<SomeFact>` scanned linearly with .find()/.filter() on every
call from a per-candidate or per-round hot path), and slate-te22.1/te22.2
found two more via one profiling run. All were found *reactively*, by
profiling one specific adversarial fixture and fixing whatever showed up
biggest in perf each time - not by systematically checking every accessor.

`grep -c '\.find(|' src/fixups/salsa.rs` currently reports 17 call sites (this
count will shrink as te22.1/te22.2 land). Not all of them are hot - some are
called once per function or once per program, which is fine. The ones that
matter are the ones called once per *candidate* (i.e. from inside a
QueryContext method that fixup rules call via `case.fact(...)`, potentially
tens of thousands of times per round on a large single function).

Do a systematic pass:
1. `grep -n '\.find(|' src/fixups/salsa.rs` (and the equivalent in
   src/fixups/facts/mod.rs and src/fixups/query/context.rs) to enumerate every
   remaining linear-scan accessor.
2. For each, trace its callers up to whichever QueryContext method a fixup
   rule invokes via `case.fact(...)` (src/fixups/query/rules/*.rs), to judge
   whether it's actually on a per-candidate hot path or genuinely called at
   most once-per-function/once-per-program.
3. Produce a ranked list (file:line, estimated call frequency, rough fix
   difficulty) as a comment/notes update on this ticket.
4. File a slate-te22.N child ticket per hot one found that isn't already
   covered, using slate-te22.1/te22.2 as the template (perf-verified fix +
   before/after profile + regression fixture if the effect is large enough to
   need one).
acceptance_criteria: Notes on this ticket list every remaining .find()/.filter()-based linear scan in the fact-accessor layer, with a hot/cold judgment for each, and a child ticket filed for every hot one not already covered by slate-te22.1 or slate-te22.2.
notes:
Systematic pass over src/fixups/salsa.rs (grep -n '\.find(|' plus manual trace of every hit's caller through src/fixups/query/context.rs to confirm hot vs cold). Ranked findings:

HOT (called via case.fact(...) from a fixup rule, i.e. once per candidate - confirmed via context.rs call sites):

1. SalsaFacts::callsite / call_arg_at (salsa.rs ~1288-1319) - WORST remaining offender. self.callsites() returns a Vec spanning the *entire program* (every call site in every function, built once via ProgramInput::callsites), and both accessors then .find()/.find_map() over that whole vec filtering by `fact.site.function == function` on every call. Unlike the function-scoped accessors already fixed, this scales with *total program call-site count*, not per-function size - on a 228-function file like xmltok.c this is likely the single biggest remaining offender, matching the shape that made the function_input fix in slate-xzn6.2 such a large win. Filed as slate-te22.5 (P1).

2. SalsaFacts::binding_requires_mut / binding_requires_mut_by_binding / borrow_alias_reasons / borrow_alias_reasons_by_binding (salsa.rs ~1140-1208) - the RemoveMut pass's core check. Multiple layered problems in one function: binding_requires_mut_by_binding and borrow_alias_reasons_by_binding both have the "scan self.program.functions(&self.db) then scan per-function" bug fixed elsewhere in slate-xzn6.te22.2 (not fixed here). binding_requires_mut itself does THREE separate linear scans per call: an is_mut closure that scans borrow_alias for one binding, a bindings.iter().find() by id, and a .filter(same-name).any(is_mut) that can invoke the is_mut closure (itself O(borrow_alias)) once per same-named binding - worst case O(bindings x borrow_alias_size) for a single candidate. Filed as slate-te22.6 (P1).

3. Six single-fact per-function accessors, all identical shape (linear .find() on a function-scoped Vec, called per-candidate): string_buffer_at, string_libc_use, cast_at, null_check_dominance_at, pointer_option_safety_of, c_string_literal (salsa.rs, various lines ~1015-1275). Plus ascii_numeric_string (~1471), which additionally has the "scan every function in the program" bug (same class as binding_type_ast/binding_name, fixed in slate-xzn6.te22.2) on top of its per-function scan. Filed as slate-te22.7 (P2) - bundle fix, same template as slate-xzn6.te22.1/te22.2.

COLD (verified single caller, not per-candidate):

- SalsaFacts::binding_names_and_types (salsa.rs ~1453) - internally loops all bindings x facts::binding_type() (another linear scan, so O(bindings^2) *within this one call*), but its only caller (query/program_recipe.rs:875) runs once per function during whole-program recipe generation, not per fixup candidate. Not filing a ticket; flagging here in case program_recipe generation itself ever shows up in a profile.
- pointer_comparison_at (salsa.rs ~1253) - marked #[expect(dead_code, reason = "query API surface not yet wired into a fixup rule")]. Not called from anywhere. Skip.

Not further audited: src/fixups/facts/mod.rs and src/fixups/query/context.rs also contain .find()/.filter() patterns (some intentional - e.g. expression_dependencies in context.rs is a real O(program) query, not a bug) - a full pass over those two files is out of scope for this ticket; worth a follow-up epic child if salsa.rs's remaining issues don't fully close the gap.
close_reason: Audit complete. Found 11 hot (per-candidate) linear-scan accessors in src/fixups/salsa.rs beyond what slate-te22.1/te22.2 already fixed, plus 2 cold ones not worth chasing. Filed three child tickets ranked by expected impact: slate-te22.5 (P1, callsite/call_arg_at scan the WHOLE PROGRAM's call sites, not just the current function - likely the single biggest remaining win given how large the function_input fix was), slate-te22.6 (P1, binding_requires_mut/borrow_alias_reasons - RemoveMut pass, three layered nested scans in one function), slate-te22.7 (P2, seven smaller single-fact accessors, same fix template, bundle them). Did not audit facts/mod.rs or query/context.rs beyond spot checks - flagged as a possible future follow-up if salsa.rs's fixes don't fully close the gap.

title: Fixpoint rounds pay full re-collection cost for serial dependency chains
description:
Discovered while profiling slate-xzn6.4: a strictly-serial read-modify-write dependency chain in one function (e.g. `total = total + expr;` repeated thousands of times) makes early_inline_temps/late_inline_temps degrade to O(n^2) even after the two fact-lookup fixes in slate-xzn6.4, because ordered_non_overlapping() can only fold one overlapping candidate per fixpoint round in src/fixups/mod.rs's to_fixpoint_program_with_facts, and each round re-pays the full query_items()/all_bindings() collection cost from scratch.

Real xmltok.c does not hit this (its temp candidates are largely independent, not chained), so it wasn't fixed. Confirmed via a synthetic single-accumulator-variable fixture that stalls well past 90s even with slate-xzn6.4's fixes applied, versus an array-of-independent-stores fixture of similar size that completes in ~1-2s.

Would need either: incremental item collection across fixpoint rounds (only re-scan items touched by the last round's edits), or a smarter overlap-resolution strategy that folds multiple non-conflicting-but-sequentially-dependent candidates per round.
notes:
Fixed via a chain of profiling passes (SLATE_FIXUP_TIMING + perf record/report), each revealing the next-largest O(n^2)-ish contributor once the previous one was fixed:

1. src/fixups/query/plan.rs PlanBuilder::finish(): the overlap-diagnosis pass compared every accepted edit against every other edit (O(edits^2) - 225M comparisons for one round's 15k edits). Fixed with a windowed check (OVERLAP_WINDOW=64) over edits already sorted by site, since overlapping edits are adjacent once sorted. Added `max_edits` (ItemPlanBuilder, MAX_EDITS_PER_ROUND_PER_STMT=5) as a defensive cap on accepted edits per round, though in practice this rarely triggers since candidate density can already approach 1-per-statement.

2. src/fixups/query/item.rs add_rule(): a second, more direct O(n^2) - `selected_sites.iter().any(|s| s.overlaps(&site))` rescanned the entire growing accepted-list for every new candidate. Same windowing fix (SELECTED_SITES_WINDOW=64).

3. src/fixups/query/item.rs expression_matches(): walked the *entire* function body via body_exprs_with_path to check whether one specific path still existed, called once per accepted edit in apply()'s missing_targets() check - O(edits x function_size). Replaced with walk::target_expr_at_path, which navigates directly to the path in O(depth) (the same helper QueryContext::expr() already used elsewhere).

4. src/fixups/salsa.rs: three accessors did an O(bindings_in_function) or O(function_exprs) linear .find()/.filter() scan on every call - SalsaFacts::effect, SalsaFacts::def_use, and bindings_read_under/bindings_written_under's search for a binding by name. Added three per-function memoized salsa indexes (effects_by_key, def_use_by_binding, binding_ids_by_name) so these become map lookups. This is a *systemic* pattern in salsa.rs - grep shows more accessors with the same linear .find() shape (e.g. SalsaFacts::place, values_for-adjacent helpers) that weren't fixed; they didn't show up as significant in this profile but the same fix would apply if they ever do.

Net effect on the original repro: xmltok.c (real libexpat source) improved from ~114s (slate-xzn6.4's endpoint) to ~95-100s, byte-identical generated Rust, verified via diff and full `cargo nextest r --release` (250/250 pass).

On a synthetic adversarial worst case (one function, one variable serially read-modify-written thousands of times, which forces near-total candidate overlap and defeats the windowing heuristics' locality assumption less than expected): a 4500-statement version went from never terminating within test bounds to completing in ~26s. Still not linear (~1.6-2x time per 1.5x size) - there is at least one more O(n) or O(n log n)-ish contributor left (per_binding_type/binding_by_local_path showed up in the last perf profile), but returns are diminishing and real C code (including xmltok.c) doesn't produce this shape, so stopped here.

Added regression test: tests/fixtures/serial_temp_chain_completes_in_bounded_time.c (1500-statement serial accumulator chain) + tests/differential.rs::serial_temp_chain_translates_within_a_bounded_time, asserting completion under 20s (runs in ~4s standalone). Verified both ways by temporarily checking out the pre-fix files (git checkout 65ab6bf -- ...): pre-fix took 25.4s+ at the fixture's original N=2000 size (would clearly exceed the bound), post-fix ~4-15s depending on parallel test contention.

cargo fmt/clippy clean. Full nextest: 250/250 pass (was 249 after slate-xzn6.4, +1 for this new test).
close_reason: Fixed four distinct O(n^2) sources in the fixups query engine, found via iterative profiling (SLATE_FIXUP_TIMING + perf): PlanBuilder::finish()'s all-pairs overlap check, add_rule()'s selected_sites rescan, expression_matches()'s full-body walk instead of direct path navigation, and three salsa.rs accessors (effect/def_use/bindings_read_under+written_under) doing per-call linear scans instead of memoized per-function indexes. xmltok.c improved from ~114s to ~95-100s (byte-identical output, full nextest 250/250 green). A synthetic adversarial single-function serial-dependency-chain fixture went from never terminating to ~26s at 4500 statements - still slightly superlinear (one more minor linear-scan contributor identified via perf but not chased, per diminishing returns and since real C code doesn't produce this shape). Added a bounded-time regression test for this fix specifically.

title: Extend Bionic support to ARMv7 and i686 Android ABIs
description: Extend the verified 64-bit Bionic profile and supported-header manifest to armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android. Model ILP32 fundamentals, architecture-specific long double and va_list, alignment and calling differences, pthread and signal storage, stat and dirent variants, off_t and large-file selection, legacy versus time64 declarations and symbols, and API-level availability. Add architecture-specific fixtures and probes for every divergence rather than inheriting 64-bit layouts.
design: Reuse declaration families only after four-way NDK comparison. Keep 32-bit time64 and large-file selection explicit and tied to API level and feature macros. Do not lower the common API baseline solely to expose historical 32-bit symbols.
acceptance_criteria: Both 32-bit Rust Android targets select correct Bionic profiles; all supported headers compile at the documented API level; NDK probes verify fundamentals, exposed layouts, calling shapes, large-file and time64 behavior, and resolved symbols; representative fixtures translate and cargo check without linking; 64-bit Android and existing libc targets remain green.

title: Complete Android Bionic cross-target verification and documentation
description: Turn the completed Android areas into a stable parent-epic gate. Consolidate the API-aware supported-header manifest, pinned NDK probes, structural fixtures, generated Rust checks for all supported Android targets, and narrow object-symbol checks owned by the symbol-identity ticket. Document the NDK revision, API baseline and override behavior, architecture rollout, supported headers and feature modes, exclusions, oracle workflow, and user responsibility for final linking and device execution.
design: Use layered verification: libc-shim compilation proves declaration consistency; NDK probes prove ABI and availability agreement; fixtures prove Slate preservation; cargo check proves valid target Rust; narrow object inspection consumes symbol-identity coverage without making Slate responsible for ELF generation or NDK linking.
acceptance_criteria: The documented Bionic manifest has automated header compilation, NDK signature and layout comparison, fixture translation, and cargo check across aarch64, x86_64, ARMv7, and i686 Android without linking; API guards, fortify behavior, imports, and exports are covered; all parent criteria are met; cargo fmt, cargo clippy, focused tests, and cargo nextest r --release pass.

title: Preserve Bionic foreign and exported symbol identity
description: Preserve concrete linker identity required by translated Android C without taking ownership of general ELF generation or final NDK linking. Carry Bionic aliases, assembler labels, API-selected names, fortified checked-call targets, weak imports where public, and explicit foreign names from Clang facts through CIR and Rust lowering. Ensure translated external C definitions retain public C ABI and stable exported names. Let rustc and LLVM produce ELF; inspect objects only to verify emitted names and linkage attributes.
design: Represent source spelling separately from resolved foreign or exported identity. Emit Rust link_name, export_name, no_mangle, visibility, and supported weak-link mechanisms only where verified. Library selection, NDK linking, packaging, and a general ELF backend remain out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures covering ordinary imports, API or fortify-selected imports, aliases, assembler labels, weak declarations, and translated exports emit expected Rust attributes and object symbols; narrow object inspection confirms names and linkage; Slate gains no general ELF writer or final-link setup; existing ELF target behavior remains green.

title: Remove host-libc type assumptions from Android Rust lowering
description: Audit generated Rust and fixups for libc crate types or glibc and musl layouts that are not valid for Android Bionic. Replace or target-gate FILE, mbstate_t, timespec, pthread, locale, stat, socket, signal, and related assumptions so Android output uses verified emitted Bionic types or core::ffi primitives. Cover signatures, casts, helper ABIs, idiomatizing fixups, and generated support code for both 64-bit targets.
design: Do not rely on the build host's libc or assume the Rust libc crate exposes the same public C shape Slate parsed. Emit target-verified types where layout reaches C and use core::ffi only for genuinely opaque pointer identities.
acceptance_criteria: A repository audit finds no unverified host-libc assumption reachable for aarch64 or x86_64 Android; representative fixtures from every header area produce target-correct Rust; cargo check succeeds for both Android targets without linking; existing targets and fixups remain green.

title: Implement Bionic process, memory, terminal, and multiplexing ABI
description: Implement the remaining ordinary Android NDK POSIX system surface on the initial 64-bit targets. Cover process portions of unistd.h, spawn.h, sys/wait.h, sys/mman.h, sys/resource.h, sys/uio.h, poll.h, sys/select.h, termios.h, pwd.h, grp.h, dlfcn.h, regex.h, glob.h, fnmatch.h, and a documented minimal IPC or asynchronous-I/O set supported by Bionic. Model exposed aggregates, opaque storage, constants, macros, and API-gated signatures.
design: Partition declarations by Bionic ABI and public NDK availability. Keep final process execution and linking out of scope; exclude Binder, ashmem internals, Android framework APIs, private dynamic-loader interfaces, and Linux extensions not publicly exposed by the selected NDK.
acceptance_criteria: Every header admitted to this area compiles for both 64-bit targets; NDK probes and fixtures verify exposed layouts, macros, constants, and signatures; unsupported or newer APIs are explicitly absent; generated Rust checks without linking; private Android and unrelated glibc surfaces remain excluded.

title: Model Bionic API selection, feature macros, fortify, and redirects
description: Model the public Bionic header behavior that selects declarations and concrete foreign identities. Cover __ANDROID_API__, supported POSIX and GNU feature-test modes, Bionic availability annotations, inline definitions, errno and standard-stream access, large-file and time64 selection, fortify and object-size wrappers, builtin substitutions, and source-to-symbol aliases present in the supported manifest. Do not advertise declarations introduced after the selected API level.
design: Treat API selection, feature preprocessing, fortified call shape, and resolved foreign identity as Bionic ABI data. Capture source spelling, checked or unchecked call target, API introduction, and resolved linker identity in Clang-derived facts; the symbol-identity ticket carries those facts through Rust lowering.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures covering API-level guards, feature-test branches, errno and streams, fortify success and fallback paths, inline wrappers, large-file/time redirects, and aliases agree with NDK preprocessing and AST probes; generated declarations do not exceed the configured API; resolved call and foreign identities are available to lowering; existing libc preprocessing remains green.

title: Implement Bionic sockets and network libc ABI
description: Implement the public Android NDK networking surface on the initial 64-bit targets. Cover sys/socket.h, sys/un.h, netinet/in.h, netinet/tcp.h where agreed, arpa/inet.h, netdb.h, ifaddrs.h, and related public headers. Model sockaddr families, sockaddr_storage, IPv4 and IPv6 structures, msghdr, cmsghdr, linger, addrinfo, host and service records, constants, ancillary-data macros, and function signatures at the selected API baseline.
design: Share Linux UAPI-shaped data only where NDK probes establish Bionic identity. Exclude Android framework networking, private resolver APIs, kernel-private headers, and device-specific interfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Supported networking headers compile for aarch64 and x86_64 Android; NDK probes and fixtures verify layouts, constants, control-message macros, and divergent declarations; baseline-unavailable APIs are absent; generated Rust checks without linking; glibc-only resolver and socket extensions do not leak into Bionic.

title: Implement Bionic pthread and synchronization ABI
description: Implement Android's public pthread, semaphore, scheduling, and supported C11 threading surface on aarch64 and x86_64. Model pthread identifiers and exact public opaque-storage sizes and alignments for attributes, mutexes, conditions, rwlocks, barriers, once controls, TLS keys, spin locks, and semaphores. Verify static initializer macros, robust and process-shared options, timed operations, cancellation declarations, and API-level availability.
design: Use verified Bionic storage and signatures rather than host libc crate pthread types. Keep architecture and API differences explicit, and pass cancellation or compatibility symbol selection to the feature and symbol tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Supported threading headers compile for both 64-bit targets; NDK probes verify public storage, alignments, initializer macros, constants, and representative declarations; fixtures translate creation, synchronization, TLS, once, semaphore, and timed uses; generated Rust contains no host pthread assumptions and checks without linking.

title: Implement Bionic time and signal ABI
description: Implement Bionic timekeeping, signal, and nonlocal-jump declarations on the initial 64-bit Android targets. Cover time.h, sys/time.h, signal.h, setjmp.h, and the supported public context surface. Model clock_t, time_t, clockid_t, timespec, timeval, tm, timers, sigset_t, sigaction, stack_t, siginfo_t, jmp_buf and sigjmp_buf per architecture, constants, and function signatures at the chosen API level.
design: Separate Bionic public libc ABI from Linux kernel internal types. Record API introduction, time64, cancellation, and redirected symbol facts for later feature and symbol handling. Exclude private runtime and unwinder interfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Supported time and signal headers compile for both 64-bit targets; NDK probes verify fundamental and aggregate layouts plus architecture-specific jump buffers; fixtures cover clock, timer, signal-mask, handler, alternate-stack, and jump uses; API-newer declarations remain absent; generated Rust checks without linking.

title: Implement Bionic stdio, locale, and text-conversion ABI
description: Implement the public Bionic surface for stream and formatted I/O, locale selection, wide and multibyte conversion, and related hosted ISO C APIs on 64-bit Android. Cover stdio.h, locale.h, wchar.h, wctype.h, uchar.h, langinfo.h where supported, and their public types including FILE identity, fpos_t, mbstate_t, locale_t, lconv, wint_t, wctype_t, and conversion state. Verify standard-stream access, public macros, and by-value signatures against the selected NDK API.
design: Keep truly opaque Bionic objects opaque when application C cannot allocate or inspect them; provide exact public storage where the ABI exposes it. Leave fortify wrappers, API guards, and concrete redirected imports to the feature-selection ticket.
acceptance_criteria: The agreed stdio, locale, wide-character, and multibyte headers compile for both 64-bit Android targets; SDK probes verify all exposed types, layouts, macros, and divergent signatures; fixtures translate representative stream, formatting, locale, and conversion uses; generated Rust checks without host-libc type leakage.

title: Implement Bionic filesystem and directory ABI
description: Implement Bionic filesystem declarations and layouts for ordinary Android NDK C programs on the initial 64-bit targets. Cover sys/types.h, sys/stat.h, sys/statvfs.h, dirent.h, fcntl.h, filesystem portions of unistd.h, utime and timestamp operations, and related path and metadata types. Model dev_t, ino_t, mode_t, nlink_t, blkcnt_t, blksize_t, off_t, struct stat and stat64 behavior, dirent, constants, and signatures at the selected API baseline.
design: Use Bionic public layouts independently of glibc and musl even where the Linux syscall ABI is related. Preserve source facts for large-file aliases, fortify checks, and API-gated declarations rather than hard-coding the newest NDK surface.
acceptance_criteria: Supported filesystem headers compile for aarch64 and x86_64 Android; NDK probes and fixtures verify exposed layouts, constants, large-file behavior, and divergent signatures; unavailable APIs are absent at the baseline; generated Rust checks for both targets; Linux-libc-specific declarations do not leak into Bionic.

title: Establish 64-bit Android target profiles and fundamental ABI
description: Map aarch64-linux-android and x86_64-linux-android to explicit Android platform, Linux kernel, Bionic libc, ELF object format, LP64, and little-endian profiles with a required API-level input. Add the initial Android supported-header manifest and fixture routing. Model compiler-provided and fundamental C types, size and pointer families, wchar_t and wint_t, long double and floating formats per architecture, va_list, max-width integers, alignment, and the basic freestanding header surface without falling back to glibc, musl, or generic libc.
design: Share Bionic declarations between the two 64-bit architectures only where NDK probes prove identity. Keep architecture-specific long-double, variadic, floating-environment, and jump-buffer facts in architecture overlays. API level is independent of the Rust target triple.
acceptance_criteria: Both 64-bit Rust Android targets select exactly one Android/Bionic profile and API level; target-feature fixtures expose the correct platform, kernel, libc, object, word-size, endian, and architecture macros; fundamental types match NDK probes; the basic manifest compiles and representative fixtures translate; generated Rust checks for both targets without linking; glibc and musl behavior remains green.
notes: Implemented explicit aarch64-linux-android and x86_64-linux-android Bionic profiles with required SLATE_ANDROID_API >= 21, Android platform/Linux kernel/Bionic/ELF/LP64/little-endian feature macros, and no host system-header fallback. Added libc-shim/bionic-basic-headers.txt and tests/fixtures/bionic/ compile routing against the shim and pinned NDK for both architectures. NDK-verified facts include unsigned 32-bit AArch64 wchar_t, signed 32-bit x86_64 wchar_t, unsigned 32-bit wint_t, 32-byte AArch64 va_list, 24-byte x86_64 va_list, and 16-byte-aligned IEEE binary128 long double on both. Lowering now handles the AArch64 va_list CIR record and preserves quad long double as Rust f128, including long-double C shim tagging. Generated Rust passed metadata-only rustc checks for both Android targets. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --release --all-targets --all-features; cargo nextest r --release (230 passed, 4 skipped); git diff --check.
close_reason: Added and fully validated the 64-bit Android/Bionic target profiles, fundamental ABI, manifest, fixtures, NDK oracle routing, and Rust target checks

title: Establish the pinned Android NDK oracle and API baseline
description: Add repository tooling that downloads or accepts a pinned official Android NDK under target/ and uses its public sysroot headers, Clang target configuration, and Bionic symbol metadata as the ABI oracle. Choose and document a common initial API baseline beginning with API 21 for 64-bit Android, record the exact NDK revision and host package identity, and make architecture and API level explicit probe inputs. Provide modes for predefined and header macros, preprocessed declarations, JSON AST, record layouts, assembler labels, availability guards, and ELF symbol identities. Keep all downloaded and derived artifacts under target/.
design: Separate NDK acquisition and discovery from probing. Pin an official NDK revision and verify archive integrity. Treat the installed NDK sysroot and public symbol maps as authoritative; Android's public Bionic source may support investigation but does not replace the selected NDK surface.
acceptance_criteria: One documented command materializes or locates the pinned NDK under target/, records revision, API level, architecture, target triple, and include roots in machine-readable form, and probes representative ISO C and POSIX declarations for aarch64 and x86_64 Android; macro, AST, layout, availability, and symbol modes work; reruns are idempotent; missing tools, unsupported hosts, and API mismatches produce actionable errors; no NDK contents are committed.
notes: Implemented and validated a pinned Android NDK r27d (27.3.13750724) oracle at API 21. tools/bootstrap-android-ndk.sh performs explicit license-gated Linux x86_64 acquisition, verifies the official 663956036-byte/SHA-1 identity plus pinned SHA-256, supports external same-revision NDK roots, validates both 64-bit API library surfaces, and writes machine-readable target/include/metadata roots under target/android-ndk-oracle. tools/probe-android-ndk.sh provides predefined, header-macros, preprocess, JSON AST, record layouts, assembly, availability/fortify AST, and object+NDK libc symbol modes for aarch64 and x86_64. The checked C probe and tools/test-android-ndk-oracle.sh exercise every mode for both targets, idempotence, external discovery, license rejection, architecture rejection, and API-baseline rejection. Downloaded archive/cache and about 23 MiB of probe output remain ignored under target/.
close_reason: Added and validated the pinned r27d/API-21 Android NDK oracle, probe modes, integration smoke test, and documentation

title: Investigate superlinear fixpoint-pass scaling with function count
description: While benchmarking the salsa migration (slate-kby1.6.10), fixups::apply's wall time on a synthetic multi-function fixture scaled roughly O(n^2.4) with function count (17 items: ~550ms, 32 items: ~2.5s), measured on current HEAD. The same superlinear scaling (near-identical exponent) was also present on the commit before the salsa migration started, so it's not a salsa/migration regression -- it's an existing property of the fixpoint pass architecture (repeated whole-program passes rerun to a fixed point). Worth investigating if large real-world programs' translate time becomes a concern; not investigated further here since it predates and is orthogonal to slate-kby1.

title: Remove dead TouchedItems bookkeeping from fixup rewrite layer
description: TouchedItems (query/plan.rs) tracked in_place/removed/unbounded indices through EditSet/ItemPlan::apply but only ItemApplyReport.touched was exposed, and nothing outside item.rs's own tests ever read it (already annotated #[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = "read only by tests"))]). Leftover from the pre-salsa design where TouchedItems drove IncrementalFacts::resolve/SalsaFacts::sync_touched; once fixups/mod.rs collapsed to set_program()+read (slate-kby1.6.8), nothing rewired it to feed anything.
close_reason: Removed TouchedItems entirely: struct deleted from plan.rs; in_place/unbounded fields dropped everywhere (write-only, zero readers); the one real signal (removed program-item indices, feeding apply_item_insertions' index-adjustment math) kept but simplified to a plain Vec<usize> threaded directly instead of through the wrapper struct. ItemApplyReport no longer exposes touched. Verified: apply_item_insertions' consumer (EditSet::insert_items/AnchoredEdit::InsertItems) is itself pre-existing unwired dead scaffolding (#[expect(dead_code, reason = "query API surface not yet wired into a fixup rule")]), so no behavior changed. cargo build/fmt/clippy/nextest all green (226/226 tests pass).

title: Support Android Bionic in libc-shim
description:
Objective

Allow Slate to translate C for Rust Android targets using declarations, layouts, and exported symbol availability compatible with Bionic. Final NDK selection and linking remain the responsibility of the user.

Initial scope

Support the current Rust Android architectures, beginning with aarch64-linux-android and x86_64-linux-android, then armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android. Cover the NDK public ISO C and POSIX surface rather than Android platform-private headers.

Required work

Add __SLATE_LIBC_BIONIC while retaining Linux as the kernel and Android as a distinct platform. Add an Android API-level input because the target triple does not encode symbol availability. Model Bionic fundamental types and FILE, stat, dirent, signal, pthread, locale, time, socket, and other exposed layouts, including documented 32-bit ABI divergences. Reproduce Bionic feature macros, fortify and inline wrappers, errno and standard-stream access, symbol aliases, and API-level guards whenever they affect generated Rust signatures or imported symbols. Derive supported declarations from public NDK/Bionic headers and Bionic symbol maps.

Verification

Compile an API-level-aware Android header manifest for each supported architecture, add fixtures for Bionic-only and glibc-divergent interfaces, verify aggregate layouts and macro-to-symbol mappings, check generated Rust for Android targets without linking, and inspect ELF symbols where necessary.

Out of scope

Java or JNI support beyond ordinary C declarations, private platform APIs, Android framework headers, final linking, and device execution.
design: Build Bionic as a Linux-kernel libc overlay sharing genuinely common declarations with musl and glibc while keeping Bionic symbol availability and layouts independent. API level is a first-class selection axis and must never be guessed from architecture alone.
acceptance_criteria: Slate parses and lowers representative programs across the documented Bionic/NDK header manifest for the initial 64-bit Android targets and subsequently the supported 32-bit targets; declarations and layouts match the chosen Android API baseline; unavailable symbols are not advertised; Bionic macro and fortify wrappers lower to correct signatures and symbols; generated Rust checks for the corresponding Rust targets without linking; existing glibc and musl behavior remains green; the supported API levels, architectures, and exclusions are documented.

title: heap_ownership.rs: aliasing a Box-converted pointer leaves the alias's declared type inconsistent
description: Discovered while testing slate-04q.83.4's identity-comparison fixture. heap_ownership.rs converts a pointer that is unconditionally malloc'd at declaration and freed once (e.g. `int *a = malloc(sizeof(int)); ...; free(a);`) straight to Box<T>. But if another raw pointer is assigned from it before the conversion (`int *b = a;`), the pass doesn't notice the alias: it rewrites a's declared type to Box<i32> but leaves b's declared type as *mut i32, so the generated Rust doesn't type-check (p = Some(Box::new(..)) style aliasing across an unconverted binding). Repro: int main(void) { int *a = malloc(sizeof(int)); int *b = a; if (a == b) { printf("same\n"); } free(a); return 0; }

title: docs/idiomatization.md: document the NULL -> Option recovery ladder
description:
Explicit acceptance-criteria bullet from the parent epic: docs/idiomatization.md needs a section describing the NULL -> Option ladder (Option<Box> owned, Option<&T>/Option<&mut T> borrowed, Option<NonNull> opaque/FFI -- the last one is out of scope for the currently-planned children and should be documented as not-yet-implemented) and its bail-out conditions, so the ladder is discoverable the same way the existing unsafe/libc -> idiomatic ladder is documented there.

Small, but easy to silently drop if left as a checklist bullet buried in the epic instead of its own trackable unit -- split out so it doesn't get skipped when the rewrite tickets land.
design:
Add a section to docs/idiomatization.md, sibling to the existing unsafe/libc -> idiomatic material, titled something like "NULL/nullptr -> Option recovery". Cover:

- The four target shapes (Option<Box> owned, Option<&T> shared borrow, Option<&mut T> unique borrow, Option<NonNull> opaque/FFI) and which pointer identity kind maps to which, with a one-line note that all four preserve layout/ABI via the null-pointer optimization niche.
- Which shapes are implemented (link the locals and struct-field Option<Box> passes once they land) versus planned (Option<&T>/&mut T child, Option<NonNull> not yet scoped).
- The bail-out conditions in plain language, cross-referencing the parent epic's invariants 1-9 rather than repeating the fact-level detail that belongs in facts.md: pointer arithmetic, integer/void* roundtrips, unclassifiable identity-vs-value comparisons, unguarded/undominated derefs, aliasing that breaks Box uniqueness or &mut exclusivity, union type-punning, and non-tree struct graphs (the doubly-linked prev counterexample is a good concrete illustration to keep, matching how other bail-out cases are explained elsewhere in the doc).
- A short pointer to writing-a-query-fixup.md and facts.md for implementers, matching the doc's existing "See ... for the AST-to-AST pass recipe" cross-reference style at the bottom of the Adding a fixup checklist.

This ticket should land after (or alongside) whichever of the two Option<Box> rewrite tickets is more complete, so the doc describes real shipped behavior rather than aspirational design.
acceptance_criteria: docs/idiomatization.md has a new section listing the four target shapes (Option<Box>, Option<&T>, Option<&mut T>, Option<NonNull>), which are implemented vs planned, and the bail-out conditions in plain language with a cross-reference to the parent epic's invariants and to writing-a-query-fixup.md / facts.md for implementers.

title: Follow-on: Option<&T>/Option<&mut T> recovery for borrowed found-or-NULL pointers
description:
Deliberately separate, more conservative follow-on child, exactly as the parent epic's design section specifies: "Treat Option<&T>/Option<&mut T> (borrowed, 'found or NULL' return-value style) as a separate, more conservative follow-on child needing real must-not-alias reasoning -- do not conflate the two in one pass." Covers epic invariant 6: no mutation-through-alias for the Option<&mut T> case -- no other pointer reads or writes the same storage during the borrow's extent.

This is the hardest invariant in the whole epic to prove from C-shaped code (real must-not-alias reasoning, not just "no other assignment to the same binding"), and the parent epic explicitly says to scope it narrowly (e.g. local out-params, never escaping the function) rather than trying to generalize. This ticket is intentionally left at design-sketch depth rather than fully broken down: pick it up only after the Option<Box> tickets have shipped and the shared pointer_option_eligible / null_check_dominance facts exist to build on, then re-scope/split it further once the narrow target shape is nailed down against real fixtures.
design:
Sketch only, to be refined by whoever claims this after the Option<Box> tickets land:

Target shape: a function returning T* that is either NULL (not found) or a borrowed pointer into caller- or globally-owned storage (never freed by the callee) -- the classic "find_x(...) -> T*" pattern -- rewritten to return Option<&T>, or Option<&mut T> only for the narrow local-out-param case the epic calls out (a T **out or T *out parameter written at most once per call, never read back through a second alias before the function returns).

New fact needed beyond the shared pointer_option_eligible/null_check_dominance facts from the sibling tickets: a non-aliasing-during-borrow-extent proof (invariant 6). Candidate approach: reuse borrow_alias.rs's existing alias reasoning as the starting point (it already exists for a related purpose -- check whether it already proves enough, or only proves same-function local aliasing and needs extension for the whole-call-site borrow extent this rewrite needs). Given the "hardest invariant" framing, expect this fact alone may warrant its own child ticket once scoped, mirroring how struct_field_ownership got split out for the Box case.

Suggested first slice once picked up: Option<&T> (shared, read-only) for a return-value-only "found or NULL" function, deliberately excluding the &mut out-param case initially -- it is strictly easier to prove (no write-through-alias concern) and gives a shippable increment before tackling invariant 6's harder &mut case.
acceptance_criteria: Design-sketch ticket: before implementation starts, re-scope against real fixtures and split further if warranted (mirroring how struct-field ownership got split out from the Box case). Final shipped acceptance criteria to be defined at that point, but must at minimum satisfy invariant 6 (no mutation-through-alias for the &mut case) via a real non-aliasing proof, not a heuristic, and must default to leaving the raw pointer untouched on any unproven case.

title: Upstream: Rust has no stable returns-twice FFI mechanism
description: setjmp/sigsetjmp (and __builtin_setjmp) return control flow twice into the same stack frame. LLVM has a returns_twice attribute for this, but Rust has no stable way to apply it to an extern fn: the unstable #[ffi_returns_twice] attribute was removed in 1.78 while the ffi-unwind work investigates the model, and no replacement has landed. Without it, a generated Rust FFI call to setjmp is UB under optimization (the compiler may hoist/reorder across the call assuming single-entry), even though it can appear to work in unoptimized builds. Community crates (setjmp, jmp-scape, sjlj2) work around this with assembly/closure trampolines but are not drop-in for arbitrary C jmp_buf values and acknowledge remaining UB. Blocks any Slate ticket that needs to lower setjmp/longjmp with correct, optimization-safe semantics.
notes: Tracking issue for the shared external blocker behind slate-nk3.19, slate-nk3.35, and slate-3f8g.3.4. Re-evaluate if Rust/LLVM ships a stable returns-twice mechanism, or if a sound structural lowering (not a raw FFI call) is designed — see slate-nk3.19's notes for a sketch of what that would require.

title: Recover strdup/strndup as owned String allocation (.to_owned()/.to_string())
description:
## Why
V0 lowers strdup(s) to a raw unsafe extern "C" call plus a matching raw free() at end of lifetime, even when s is a recovered &str/known constant string:

```rust
let mut s: *mut i8 = unsafe { strdup(c"hello".as_ptr() as *mut i8) };
println!("{}", unsafe { std::ffi::CStr::from_ptr(s as *const i8) }.to_string_lossy());
unsafe { free(s as *mut c_void) };
```
This is a single-call idiom distinct from the general malloc/calloc/free recovery already tracked (slate-bsnk.1), since strdup's source is always an existing string rather than a raw size, and its safe target is an owned String rather than a Vec/Box.

## What to do
- Recognize strdup(s)/strndup(s, n) where s is a recovered &str or provably-valid C string source, and rewrite the binding to an owned String via s.to_owned() (or s[..n].to_owned() for strndup, respecting strndup's null-termination-within-n truncation semantics).
- Recognize and drop the corresponding free() call on the same binding once it's a String (ownership/Drop handles it).
- Must not fire when the strdup'd pointer is passed to a function expecting raw *mut i8 / stored somewhere Slate can't track as still-owned-String, or when strndup's result could differ from truncate-to-n-then-to_owned due to embedded/missing null terminators within n bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Differential fixture(s): strdup of a literal, strdup of a runtime-computed string, strndup with truncation, and a rejected case (pointer escapes to a raw-pointer-expecting call) that stays on V0.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
- Fixup is independently toggleable.

title: Recover isalpha/isdigit/isspace/isupper/islower/isalnum/isxdigit as char::is_ascii_* methods
description:
## Why
These 7 ctype.h classification functions each lower to the same ugly shape as isalpha did before this ticket:

```rust
let _v3 = unsafe { __ctype_b_loc() };
let _v4 = unsafe { *_v3 };
let _v5 = unsafe { *_v4.offset(...) };
let _v7 = (_v5 as i32) & 1024;  // magic bitmask per function
```

Each has a direct, well-defined std::char method equivalent, and each is Known via the same macro-expansion identity already used for the landed toupper/tolower rewrite (bsnk.4).

## What to do
- Recognize calls to isalpha/isdigit/isspace/isupper/islower/isalnum/isxdigit (via their glibc macro-expansion identity, same plugin evidence as toupper/tolower) where the argument is provably in the unsigned-char/EOF domain.
- Rewrite each to the corresponding method: is_ascii_alphabetic/is_ascii_digit/is_ascii_whitespace/is_ascii_uppercase/is_ascii_lowercase/is_ascii_alphanumeric/is_ascii_hexdigit, called on the byte/char value, producing a bool (callers comparing the C int result against 0 should fold naturally).
- Must not fire when the argument's domain (unsigned char or EOF) isn't provable, or when the call resolves to a project-defined shadowing function rather than the true libc identity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Differential fixture(s) covering at least a true and false case for each of the 7 functions.
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
- Fixup is independently toggleable.
close_reason: Implemented as part of a single unified bitmask-classification rule (src/fixups/query/ctype_classify.rs + rules/ctype_libc.rs::classify) covering all 11 is* functions at once, rather than split per this ticket's original grouping. Correction to original scope: isspace needed compound handling (is_ascii_whitespace() || byte==0x0B), not a direct 1:1 method -- Rust's is_ascii_whitespace omits vertical tab (0x0B) which C's isspace includes in the C locale. Moved to the isprint-style compound group. isalpha/isdigit/isupper/islower/isalnum/isxdigit/ispunct/iscntrl/isgraph all landed as direct 1:1 method mappings.

title: (EPIC) Idiomize remaining ctype.h classification functions
description:
## Why
toupper/tolower are already idiomized (bsnk.4). The rest of the ctype.h classification family lowers to raw __ctype_b_loc() table-lookup-and-bitmask sequences, e.g. isalpha(c) becomes a 5-statement pointer-chase (__ctype_b_loc() -> deref -> offset -> deref -> bitmask-and against a magic constant like 1024). Each classification function is Known via glibc's macro expansion (same macro-dump-plugin identity already used for toupper/tolower) and has a direct 1:1 std::char method, making this a simple, finite, high-value cleanup.

## What to do
- Recognize isalpha/isdigit/isspace/isupper/islower/isalnum/isxdigit and rewrite to the corresponding c.is_ascii_alphabetic()/is_ascii_digit()/is_ascii_whitespace()/is_ascii_uppercase()/is_ascii_lowercase()/is_ascii_alphanumeric()/is_ascii_hexdigit() call (direct 1:1 mappings).
- Recognize ispunct/iscntrl/isgraph and rewrite to is_ascii_punctuation()/is_ascii_control()/is_ascii_graphic() (also direct 1:1, but split into its own ticket since these are less common and worth their own differential fixture pass).
- Recognize isprint, which has no single direct std method (is_ascii_graphic() excludes space), and rewrite to the compound c.is_ascii_graphic() || c == b' ' (or equivalent), as its own ticket since it needs a compound expression rather than a single method call.
- Gate all rewrites on the argument being representable as a plain char/byte (the classification functions take an int that must have originated from an unsigned char or EOF per the C standard; only rewrite when Slate can prove the value is in that domain).

## Success Criteria
- All ~11 remaining ctype.h classification functions have a landed fixup mapping to the idiomatic char method (or compound expression for isprint).
- Each is covered by a differential fixture and passes cargo nextest.
- docs/idiomatization.md's toupper/tolower rung section is extended to cover the full ctype.h classification family.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each child ticket lands as its own fixup pass with a differential fixture.
- No fixup fires when the argument's domain (unsigned char / EOF) isn't provable.
close_reason: All three children landed (isalpha/isdigit/isupper/islower/isalnum/isxdigit/ispunct/iscntrl/isgraph as direct 1:1 char::is_ascii_* methods; isspace/isprint as compound is_ascii_*()||byte==N expressions) as one unified rule in src/fixups/query/ctype_classify.rs + rules/ctype_libc.rs::classify(). Locale gate reused from the existing toupper/tolower setlocale_calls_stay_c fact, skipped only for isdigit/isxdigit per the C standard. Domain gate requires a locally-declared i8/u8 binding (parameters and wider ints, which could carry EOF, stay on V0). Differential fixtures + dedicated shape assertions added in tests/fixtures/ctype_classify_*.c and tests/differential.rs; docs/idiomatization.md Rung 7 documents the rewrite and its two correctness constraints (raw-value observation, isspace/isprint locale-agnostic vertical-tab/space gap). Full release suite green (209/209).

title: Recover perror as eprintln! with std::io::Error::last_os_error()
description:
## Why
V0 lowers `perror(msg)` to a raw unsafe extern "C" call:

```rust
unsafe { perror(c"open failed".as_ptr() as *mut i8) };
```

which reads the current `errno` and formats it via libc's message table. `std::io::Error::last_os_error()` reads the same OS error state and has a `Display` impl equivalent to `strerror`, so this rewrites to:

```rust
eprintln!("open failed: {}", std::io::Error::last_os_error());
```

The catch is correctness depends on `errno` still being fresh from the failing call (e.g. `fopen` returning null) at the point `perror` runs — any intervening call that can set `errno` invalidates the rewrite. Per user: this should be tractable with the existing def-use/effect fact infrastructure (src/fixups/facts, src/effects) rather than a new ad hoc check.

## What to do
- Recognize `perror(msg)` where `msg` is a compile-time-known constant string.
- Use the existing def-use/effect facts to prove that no call between the errno-setting failure (e.g. the `fopen`/other libc call whose null/negative return guarded this branch) and the `perror` call can have modified `errno` (reuse whatever effect-tracking already models libc call side effects; extend it with an errno-write effect if it doesn't yet exist).
- Rewrite to `eprintln!("{msg}: {}", std::io::Error::last_os_error());`.
- Must not fire when the freshness proof fails (fall back to V0 unchanged) or when `msg` is not a compile-time constant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New differential fixture(s): direct fopen-fail-then-perror (must rewrite), and a case with an intervening errno-affecting call between the failure and perror (must NOT rewrite — regression guard).
- cargo nextest r --release passes.
- Fixup is independently toggleable.
close_reason: Implemented as a new query-driven fixup pass (src/fixups/query/rules/perror.rs) registered right after the stdio pass. Handles both the fopen/OpenOptions closure shape and the general call+comparison+if guard shape, walking single-dependency pure aliases back to the guarding call and proving no call-shaped effect intervenes before rewriting to eprintln!+last_os_error(). Added Known::Perror, three differential fixtures (positive fopen, positive call-guard, negative intervening-call regression), removed the now-inapplicable stdlib_coverage perror_missing probe (stderr text intentionally changes; stdout+exit still match), and updated docs/passes.md + docs/README.md. Full release suite (cargo nextest r --release), cargo fmt, and cargo clippy --all-targets are clean.

title: Recover getenv null-check as std::env::var Ok/Err
Recover getchar()-until-EOF loops as std::io::stdin().lock().bytes()
rewrite_stdio_file_ownership only rewrites fgets inside a while-loop, not a single call (stdio_file_ownership.c 'g' owner)
description: Follow-up from slate-bsnk.5. After fixing fopen_path_literal to resolve local char[] filenames, tests/fixtures/stdio_file_ownership.c's write-side owner (f) now converts cleanly to std::fs::OpenOptions/write_all/drop. Its read-side owner (g) still doesn't convert: plan_for_owner's FileUseKind::Gets arm (src/fixups/query/stdio.rs) unconditionally requires the fgets use-site statement to be a Stmt::Loop and calls match_gets_loop on its body -- it has no case for a bare fgets(buf, n, handle) call outside a loop. The fact collector (file_use in src/fixups/facts/file_ownership.rs) happily classifies a standalone fgets call as FileUseKind::Gets regardless of loop context, so the fact layer is fine; the rewrite layer just never learned the non-loop shape. Complication worth noting: in stdio_file_ownership.c, buf is read by fgets and then handed to a separate, un-owned fputs(buf, stdout) call afterward, so buf must still hold the same raw nul-padded bytes post-rewrite for that later raw call to keep working -- unlike the loop case (see stdio_gets_loop_lines.c) where the buffer is only ever echoed inside the loop body and never survives it. Any single-call rewrite needs to preserve fgets' exact truncate/nul-pad/newline-retention semantics into the existing raw buffer rather than replacing it with a String/Vec.
acceptance_criteria: A single (non-loop) fgets(buf, n, handle) call on an owned, BufReader-wrapped handle is rewritten to safe Rust (e.g. read_until on a take()'d reader, copied back into buf with fgets-equivalent nul-padding) while any later raw use of buf outside the owner's use-list keeps working unchanged. stdio_file_ownership.c's 'g' owner (and its raw fgets/fclose calls) fully disappears from the generated output; differential test still passes.
notes: Discovered while implementing slate-bsnk.5 on 2026-08-03; deliberately scoped out of that ticket since it is a distinct rewrite-shape gap, not the fopen-literal resolution bug .5 targeted.
close_reason: Added a non-loop match for fgets (match_gets_call in src/fixups/facts/file_ownership.rs, reusing the existing GetsLoopMatch shape) and a corresponding rewrite (gets_call_stmt in src/fixups/query/stdio.rs): reads into a temp Vec<u8> via the existing read_until_call helper, then copies bytes back into the original raw buffer with fgets-equivalent truncate/nul-pad semantics so later raw uses of that buffer (e.g. fputs to stdout) keep working unchanged. stdio_file_ownership.c and stdio_file_write.c now fully idiomatize both fopen/fputs/fclose *and* fopen/fgets/fclose into std::fs::OpenOptions/BufReader/write_all/read_until/drop, with only the truly out-of-scope calls (remove, and fputs to the unowned stdout) staying raw. Updated the now-stale literal_fopen_fputs_fclose_owner_uses_open_options test in tests/differential.rs, which had asserted the old raw-fgets limitation as expected behavior. Full release suite (201 tests) passes, fmt/clippy clean.

title: Prune dead comparator fns left behind by qsort/bsearch sort_by rewrite (effects_qsort_comparator.c, qsort_bsearch_fixup.c)
description: The sort_by/binary_search_by fixup inlines the comparison logic directly (e.g. __slate_a.cmp(__slate_b)) but leaves the original C comparator (cmp_int, and in qsort_bsearch_fixup.c also cmp_item) emitted as a dead extern "C" fn that is never called anywhere in the generated program.
