Confirmed via grep -n 'cmp_int|cmp_item' on both generated .rs files -- only the definitions appear, no call sites. Separately, qsort_bsearch_fixup.c also round-trips bsearch's result through a raw pointer + null check (hit != std::ptr::null_mut()) even though binary_search_by already produced an Option internally; staying in Option/if-let form would be more idiomatic than reconstructing and re-checking a raw pointer.
acceptance_criteria: After the sort_by/binary_search_by rewrite fires and a comparator function has no remaining call sites, the now-unreferenced extern "C" fn is removed from the generated item list (matches the project's orphan-cleanup convention). Stretch: bsearch call sites keep the Option from binary_search_by instead of converting to a raw pointer + null check when the result is only used for a null check + single deref.
notes: This is likely the same class of fix as the existing dead_locals/unused_items/prune_unused_definitions passes (see fixup-debug pass list) -- may just need those passes to also consider now-orphaned top-level fn items reachable only from the pre-rewrite call.

title: Idiomatize fixed-size malloc/calloc/free to Vec/Box (allocation_attribute_metadata.c)
description: tests/fixtures/allocation_attribute_metadata.c allocates two fixed-size, non-escaping buffers (3*sizeof(int), 2*sizeof(int)) via malloc/calloc, uses them purely locally, and frees them before returning. The generated Rust (tests/fixtures.generated/allocation_attribute_metadata.rs) keeps malloc/calloc/free as a raw extern "C" block with ~12 unsafe sites and raw pointer arithmetic for the assume_aligned offset helper.
acceptance_criteria: A fixup (or baseline change) recognizes single-owner, non-escaping, compile-time-constant-sized malloc/calloc allocations that are freed exactly once with no aliasing, and rewrites them to Vec<T> (or a stack array where size permits), removing the extern "C" block and associated unsafe derefs. Differential test for allocation_attribute_metadata still passes.
notes:
See conversation with claude on 2026-08-03 for the audit that surfaced this; ticket text has the concrete C invariants.

2026-08-03 scoping update: heap_ownership (src/fixups/facts/heap_ownership.rs) is single-function scoped today -- it walks one function's body linearly, tracks a local alias set for one pointer, and requires every statement touching that pointer/alias to be classified as {alloc, alias-copy, realloc, free, read, write} or the whole match aborts (heap_uses_are_owned). This fixture's malloc/calloc calls are indirected through wrapper functions (allocate/allocate_array), which that walk never sees since allocation_temp only recognizes a direct Known::Malloc/Known::Calloc call as the RHS.

Confirmed via user discussion this needs a real interprocedural function-summary pass (not a guard tweak like slate-bsnk.5/.6): tag functions whose return value is a fresh, uniquely-owned allocation ("allocation sources") and functions that consume-and-free a pointer parameter ("free sinks"), then let call sites to summarized functions feed the existing local walk the same way a direct malloc/free call does today.

First implementation attempt assumed a summarized callee's body would already be in its simplified final form (e.g. `return malloc(size);`). That assumption is wrong: dumped allocate()'s body at the exact point heap_ownership runs (via a temporary eprintln, not fixup-debug -- fixup-debug's rejected_case trace doesn't show the live body) and found 11 statements, not 1. retval/final_return_temps/param_spills all run before heap_ownership in the pass list but don't collapse this shape, so heap_ownership sees raw scaffolding: params spilled to locals (arg3 -> size, arg4 -> alignment) and the malloc temp threaded through three more copies (_v1 -> _v2 -> __retval -> _v3) before the final Return.

Implication: the summary prover can't pattern-match a fixed small shape. It needs the same alias-tracking/escape-or-reject discipline heap_uses_are_owned already applies to a local pointer's free, generalized to prove two things per candidate function, walking once: (1) the malloc/calloc result's alias chain terminates in a Return with nothing else touching it (mirrors the existing free-terminal case, just with Return as the new success terminal instead of Free), and (2) each malloc/calloc argument's own alias chain traces back to a formal parameter (or a literal), through the param-spill copies, to know what to substitute at the call site. This is a bounded, mechanical generalization of the existing per-function walk (two tracked alias sets and a new terminal case, not a new dataflow framework) -- but it is real new work, not a small tweak, and the first attempt (a narrow 1-2 statement body matcher) was reverted since it can never match what heap_ownership actually sees pre-simplification.

title: printf %c falls back to raw libc instead of println! (chars.c and friends)
description: The printf -> println! fixup handles %d/%s correctly but %c falls through to raw printf/fflush/stdout even for plain i32/i8 values with no formatting subtlety. Seen in tests/fixtures/chars.c (2 of 4 printf calls), and the same gap recurs in string_lift.c and typedef_ptr_signedness.c, so it looks systemic rather than a one-off.
acceptance_criteria: printf("...%c...", expr) lowers to println!/print! with expr cast back to char, same as the %d/%s cases already handled. chars.rs, string_lift.rs, and typedef_ptr_signedness.rs generated output no longer contains raw printf/fflush/stdout calls purely for %c formatting.
notes: Likely lives in the same fixup pass that already handles %d/%s printf->println! (printf_format pass per fixup-debug pass list).
close_reason:
Fixed the traced printf %c gap and, per user direction, generalized it into a broader mutation-tracking fix for printf's %s/%c constant-folding:

1. printf_macro_arg (src/fixups/query/printf.rs): %c now falls back to a runtime `(expr as u8) as char` cast when the value isn't a compile-time constant, instead of unconditionally rejecting the whole printf call. %s gets the analogous fallback: `CStr::from_ptr(ptr as *const i8).to_string_lossy()`.

2. Discovered mid-implementation that this exposed a real, pre-existing correctness bug: proven_local_c_string_arg's "is this buffer still a compile-time constant" check only recognized strcpy/strncpy/strcat/strncat as mutators (mutated_by_string_libc), so a buffer written through by memcpy/memmove kept its stale initializer value baked into the generated Rust as a literal -- confirmed on unmodified main with a minimal repro (memcpy(d, "abcd", 5) then printf("%s", d) printed "xxxx"). Verified this independently caused stdlib_coverage's memcpy/memmove probes to fail once the %c fix stopped masking it by forcing the whole call to raw libc printf.

3. Per user direction, flipped this conservative: any call other than printf taking a tracked buffer's address now marks it unprovable (strings.rs Collector, new StringBufferRejection::EscapedToCall variant), rather than maintaining a hand-written allowlist of "known" mutators. Two follow-up corrections during review: (a) initially reused this signal to block string_copy/string_lift's own rewrites of the exact strcpy/strcat calls they exist to handle -- fixed by keeping EscapedToCall out of candidates()'s blocking check, since that gates a different consumer's needs; (b) the runtime CStr::from_ptr fallback call was itself being re-discovered as "escaping" on the next fact pass, self-poisoning affected buffers -- fixed by exempting the generated CStr::from_ptr callee by name, same as printf itself; (c) the check was initially blanket "any rejection reason" instead of specifically EscapedToCall, which incorrectly picked up the pre-existing, unrelated Indexed rejection (set whenever a buffer is indexed elsewhere, e.g. `padded[4]`) and broke unrelated printf/string_lift cases -- fixed by checking specifically for EscapedToCall.

Verified: chars.c/string_lift.c/typedef_ptr_signedness.c (the originally reported %c gap) all fully idiomatize; the memcpy/memmove bug is fixed and falls back to the new runtime CStr rendering rather than either raw printf or (worse) a stale literal; string_copy_fixup.c's unrelated rewrite still fires correctly; array_init.c's s/padded lifting and const-folding are both intact. Full release suite (201 tests) passes, fmt/clippy clean.

title: Idiomatization gaps found in fixture audit (alphabetical scan)
description: Manual audit of tests/fixtures/*.c vs tests/fixtures.generated/*.rs, scanning alphabetically for translations that still lean on extern "C" libc calls or excessive unsafe where the C source's invariants would support a more idiomatic Rust translation. Each child ticket names one fixture, the specific gap, and (where traced) the exact code location responsible.

title: use_site cannot resolve expression sites ending in BlockTail
description: QueryContext::use_site (src/fixups/query/context.rs) falls into its expression-site branch for any raw def_use AstPath not ending in a Stmt segment, then calls self.expr(&expression_site(...)) to confirm the site resolves. For a read inside an unsafe { .. } tail expression (path ending in PathSegment::BlockTail, e.g. 'unsafe { ap.next_arg::<i32>() }'), self.expr(..) returns None, so use_site returns None and the whole path.map(...).collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>() in binding_def_use fails, rejecting the binding's def-use entirely (both reads and writes) even when only the unresolvable read is at fault. Discovered while migrating va_list (slate-04q.75.53): the fix used the raw facts.def_use(id) fact directly instead of binding_def_use to sidestep the gap, since va_list only needed AstPath equality, not resolved UseSiteRefs. Worth fixing generically (likely: teach the expression-site map / self.expr to resolve BlockTail paths, mirroring how BlockBody is already walked) so future binding_def_use callers on VaList-like locals used only inside unsafe-block tail positions don't hit the same silent rejection.
close_reason: Fixed generically in QueryContext::use_site (src/fixups/query/context.rs). Root cause was broader than the BlockTail symptom: facts/def_use.rs records read/write AstPaths anchored coarsely at the nearest enclosing statement/container (it never pushes an Expr(N) discriminator when descending through Assign/CompoundAssign targets/values, or through nested sub-expressions generally), while use_site's non-Stmt-ending branch routed those paths through target_expr_at_path, which expects the fully-qualified Expr(N)-marked convention used by expression_sites. That mismatch made use_site return None for any read/write whose path happened to end past a container segment (BlockTail being the case that surfaced it, but the same class of path fails for any nested sub-expression). Fix: use_site now tries exact expression resolution first (unchanged, no regression risk), and falls back to resolving the nearest enclosing statement (same technique as enclosing_statement, truncating at the last Stmt(_) segment) whenever the exact resolution fails - matching the actual precision def_use's paths support. Verified with a before/after byte-identical translate comparison across all 246 fixtures with the fix isolated (reverted just the use_site fallback, rebuilt, retranslated everything, restored, retranslated again): only c89.c and varargs.c differ, and only in the expected direction (the va_list alias now collapses, matching slate-04q.75.53's fix). va_list's context.rs now uses the standard binding_def_use wrapper again instead of the raw facts.def_use bypass, restoring proper evidence tracing; docs/passes.md entry #25 updated to drop the now-stale workaround description. cargo fmt, cargo clippy --release --all-targets, and full cargo nextest r --release (201/201, 4 skipped) all pass.

title: Recover 3-statement temp-swaps as std::mem::swap
description:
Why: the classic 'tmp = a; a = b; b = tmp;' swap idiom also appears over plain local bindings (not slice elements), e.g. in sort/search helpers operating on scalars or struct fields by value. This is a direct, zero-risk mapping to std::mem::swap(&mut a, &mut b).

What to do:
- New fact/matcher: a StatementSequence(3) over plain identifier bindings matching the temp-swap shape — tmp is written once (its own let) and read exactly once (the third statement), and has no other touches anywhere in its enclosing block (binding_touches_in_body gives the complete lifetime since Rust block scoping means tmp can't escape it).
- Restrict a/b to plain expr_ident targets only for this pass — indexed/dereferenced places (e.g. a[i]/a[j]) belong to the separate slice.swap() ticket (slate-04q.55), since std::mem::swap(&mut a[i], &mut a[j]) does not borrowcheck for runtime indices.
- Reject when a and b are the same binding: swapping a value with itself needs two simultaneous &mut borrows of the same place, which does not borrowcheck.
- Rewrite: replace the 3 statements with a single std::mem::swap(&mut a, &mut b); statement.
- Self-contained, single-function, low blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: Fact/rewrite recognizes the swap shape only over plain identifier bindings with tmp fully dead outside the window. Differential tests pass; fixture includes a basic scalar swap, a near-miss where tmp is reused elsewhere, and a same-binding (a == b) case that must not be rewritten.
close_reason: Implemented Pass::Swap: recognizes tmp=a;a=b;b=tmp over plain identifier bindings (tmp fully dead outside window via matcher-level Usage{reads:1,writes:0}, a!=b required) and rewrites to std::mem::swap(&mut a, &mut b). Fixture covers basic swap, tmp-reused near-miss, and same-binding reject. Differential + full suite (205/205) pass, clippy clean.

title: Hand-write Field<T,Cx> combinator and Stmt/Expr pattern structs
description:
Why: structural matching (as opposed to semantic proof queries) is currently hand-written per rule - CallRule::candidates hardcodes lookup by (CallTarget, arity), DefinitionRule hardcodes four selector kinds. Fine at 5 rules, won't scale to ~1000. The original matcher-plan.md draft's Field<T,Cx>/Any/Eq/Predicate/range combinator is the right shape for this, and is entirely reusable as-is (no macros needed, ~120 loc, codebase-agnostic).

What to do: add src/fixups/query/field.rs with Field<T,Cx>. Hand-write pattern structs only for node shapes that actually recur across multiple StmtWindowRule/CallRule cases once they exist (Stmt for window-rule structural checks, and the small set of Expr variants call/cast rewrites repeatedly gate on: Cast, MethodCall, ArrayPtr). Do not hand-write a pattern struct for Item or Type speculatively - nothing needs one yet.
design: See matcher-plan.md section 4. Do not attempt to fold semantic proof queries (byte_source, pure, etc.) into Field::predicate - cross-argument relationships like prefix_contains(count, nul) aren't independent per-field checks, this is explicitly the wrong layer for them per the layer-boundaries section.
acceptance_criteria: Field<T,Cx> exists with any/eq/predicate/range constructors and unit tests. At least 2 real StmtWindowRule or CallRule cases use hand-written pattern structs built on it, replacing equivalent hand-rolled let-else chains.
close_reason:
Added src/fixups/query/field.rs (Field<T,Cx> with any/eq/predicate/range, plus Default via #[default] on the Any variant) and src/fixups/query/patterns.rs with 3 concrete hand-written pattern structs built on it: NullaryMethodCall (zero-arg method-call-by-name, e.g. as_ptr/as_mut_ptr/as_bytes/len), LetStmtPattern, LoopStmtPattern.

Applied to 2 real sites, replacing hand-rolled let-else/match-guard chains:
1. rules/range_loop.rs's case body: the Stmt::Let/Stmt::Loop shape checks now go through LetStmtPattern::any()/LoopStmtPattern::unlabeled() instead of raw let-else matches.
2. context.rs's byte_source/full_byte_view support code: stable_pointer_source, count_matches_source_len, and matches_source_expr each had their own hand-rolled "MethodCall with empty args and a specific name" guard (3 separate copies) - now all three go through NullaryMethodCall, a genuine, non-synthetic duplication removal.

Found and fixed a real (if narrow) latent bug while building LoopStmtPattern: the original range_loop fixup never checked whether the matched Stmt::Loop was labeled. Stmt::For has no label field, so converting a labeled counted loop to range-for would have silently dropped the label - breaking any break/continue elsewhere that targeted it. LoopStmtPattern::unlabeled() now rejects that case instead. Confirmed safe and behavior-preserving for the existing corpus via the full differential suite (191 tests incl. chibicc_suite/stdlib_coverage/generated_differential all pass); the two exact-string range-for tests are unaffected since neither fixture uses labeled loops.

Deviated from my own written acceptance criteria on one point: did not add unit tests for Field<T,Cx>. docs/writing-a-query-fixup.md and existing ticket precedent (slate-04q.75.35) are explicit that src/fixups/query/ is tested through C-fixture differential tests, not unit tests - no #[cfg(test)] exists anywhere under src/fixups/ today. Validated Field/patterns instead through their real use in the 2 sites above, exercised by the existing differential suite.

Field::range exists (required by acceptance criteria's "any/eq/predicate/range constructors") but has no consumer yet - marked #[allow(dead_code)] with a comment rather than silently omitted or forced into a contrived use site.

cargo build/clippy/fmt/nextest r --release all pass. Not committed per standing instruction - left for review.

title: Delete src/fixups/query/matcher.rs scratch file
description:
Why: matcher.rs is an uncommitted, non-functional first attempt at struct-pattern matching. matches!(fn_def, match_fn) treats match_fn as an irrefutable binding pattern rather than a value comparison, so it matches every Item::Fn unconditionally - it doesn't do what it looks like it does, and every branch besides Item::Fn is unimplemented (todo!()). It's declared as a module in mod.rs but never used. This is exactly the trap matcher-plan.md's own opening section warns about: Rust patterns can't be constructed dynamically and compared against a value at runtime.

What to do: remove the file and its mod declaration once the hand-written Field<T,Cx> work (separate ticket) supersedes what it was reaching for, so the intent isn't lost without a replacement path.
acceptance_criteria: matcher.rs and its mod declaration are removed (or replaced by the Field<T,Cx> module). cargo build has no dead-code warnings from the removal.
close_reason: matcher.rs was already removed from disk before this session; fixed the resulting dangling 'mod matcher;' compile error in mod.rs as part of slate-04q.75.56.1.

title: Adopt an exact target-native long double representation
description: Slate currently stores long double as an aligned f64 and uses generated C ABI trampolines for supported libc crossings. This preserves the calling convention but loses x87 f80 precision and range. Evaluate a native Rust c_longdouble/f80 once rustc supports its ABI, or an exact byte representation with C adapters in the interim.
acceptance_criteria: Values distinguishable in the target C long double format round-trip without f64 truncation; arithmetic and casts preserve the target format; fixed calls, returns, variadics, callbacks, and aggregate crossings use the target C ABI; behavior is target-aware rather than assuming x86 f80.
close_reason: Exact byte-representation approach already implemented: Type::LongDouble (backed by __slate_f80, a 10-byte/16-byte-aligned struct in src/frontend/shims/long_double.c) round-trips the real x86 extended-precision bit pattern via memcpy load/store instead of truncating through f64, with C-ABI adapter functions covering arithmetic, comparisons, casts, libm calls, and _Complex long double (__slate_cf80). Behavior is target-aware, not x86-only: CType::Float{bits:80} only maps to the f80 shim path when crate::cir::emit::uses_f64_long_double_abi() is false; on aarch64-apple-darwin/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (long double == double) it maps to Prim::F64, and CType::Float{bits:128} (aarch64/riscv binary128 long double) reuses the existing Prim::F128 support -- see src/frontend/lowerer.rs:4030-4037,4101,4234. Extensive fixture coverage exists across tests/fixtures/long_double_*.c (f80 arithmetic, literals, unions, memcpy, complex, variadics) plus target-specific variants under tests/fixtures/{msvc,macos,bionic}/.

title: Handle GNU message and warning pragmas
description: The pragma completion target uses #pragma message and #pragma GCC warning. Clang accepts both, but translate rejects the first as an unsupported semantic directive. This is the GNU-specific completion work corresponding to the general diagnostic-directive work in slate-9msj.7.
acceptance_criteria: Both pragmas produce an appropriate Rust compile-time diagnostic without changing runtime behavior, and translation continues.

title: Support GNU inline assembly and target extensions
description: Track configured-target GNU inline assembly, named address spaces, register bindings, CPU queries, x86 instruction and SIMD intrinsics, target attributes, and function multiversioning separately from portable GNU C syntax. Completion targets are tests/fixtures.unsupported/gnu_inline_asm.c, gnu_x86_target.c, gnu_x86_intrinsics.c, and gnu_x86_multiversion.c.
acceptance_criteria: On matching x86_64 targets, every completion fixture compiles with configured Clang, Slate emits target-correct compilable Rust, and stdout/exit status match C. Architecture predicates prevent these results from being claimed on other targets; unsafe or privileged probes remain explicit exclusions.
notes: Clang 24 x86_64 audits completed in slate-3f8g.4.1 and slate-3f8g.4.2. Direct child work slate-3f8g.4.3 through slate-3f8g.4.12 tracks every observed frontend, asm, intrinsic, vector, multiversion, target-feature, and fixture-scoping gap.

title: Support C23 floating formatting and extended binary math
description: The C23 library completion target covers strfromf, strfromd, and strfroml. The standard's extended binary floating-point math inventory remains incomplete on cppreference and the configured libc does not expose strfromf16 in strict C23 mode, so wider _FloatN coverage needs a focused capability audit.
acceptance_criteria: All extended binary floating types and C23 math/formatting entry points exposed by the configured toolchain have deterministic differential fixtures; unavailable facilities are explicitly classified.

title: Enable frontend-blocked C23 language facilities
description: The configured Clang/CIR toolchain does not currently expose decimal floating-point support, rejects C23 storage-class specifiers on compound literals, and reports reproducible/unsequenced attributes unavailable. The completion target records these capability results but cannot execute the facilities yet.
acceptance_criteria: When the configured frontend exposes each facility, the C23 language target directly exercises decimal floating types and rounding, storage-duration compound literals, and reproducible/unsequenced attributes; Slate translates all available cases with matching behavior.

title: Recover #pragma pack record layout
description: Why: #pragma pack changes record ABI and silently ignoring it can produce incorrect Rust layouts. What to do: recover Clang MaxFieldAlignmentAttr plus push/pop stack effects, lower representable layouts to typed Rust attributes, and reject unrepresentable layouts.
acceptance_criteria: #pragma pack cannot silently change generated layout; supported push/pop and alignment forms have ABI coverage and unsupported forms fail explicitly.
close_reason: Verified no gap exists: #pragma pack layout recovery reads Clang's own resolved MaxFieldAlignmentAttr per-record (tools/macro-dump-plugin/MacroDump.cpp VisitRecordDecl) rather than reimplementing pack-stack semantics, so Slate only ever sees values Clang itself already validated -- invalid forms (#pragma pack(3), unbalanced pop) are rejected/ignored by Clang before Slate's plugin runs, confirmed via clang -Wall producing -Wignored-pragmas warnings and natural (unpacked) layout for both. Rust's repr(packed(N))/repr(align(N)) share C's power-of-two-only constraint, so no representable-in-C-but-not-in-Rust gap exists either. Added tests/fixtures/pragma_pack_named_and_aligned.c covering named push/pop labels, pop-stack-underflow, and pack+__attribute__((aligned)) interaction (the wrapper-struct path in lower_packed_aligned_wrapper); manually verified byte-identical sizeof/_Alignof/offsetof vs clang (differential harness still disabled repo-wide). cargo nextest --profile lowering (7/7), fmt, clippy clean.

title: Document translate-directives support and fallback contract
description:
Why: users need to know which preprocessing behavior is reconstructed, which behavior is already consumed by Clang, and which directives intentionally stop translation.

What to do:
- Replace translate-cfg documentation with translate-directives terminology.
- Document the directive disposition table, single-configuration versus portable behavior, macro-plugin boundary, #error mapping, and fallback rules.
- Document how conditional unsupported directives behave when their predicate is or is not representable.
- Update CLI examples and supported-subset documentation.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation names translate-directives consistently, lists supported and rejected directive families, explains the separate macro-expansion plugin, and states that unsupported semantic directives never silently compile.
close_reason: Added pragma disposition table to docs/src/translate-directives.md: coarse DirectiveDisposition classes, per-family fine-grained clang-resolved-vs-unsupported table (once/diagnostic/pack/visibility/weak/redefine_extname/push_macro/poison/STDC CX_LIMITED_RANGE/FP_CONTRACT/FENV_ACCESS/FENV_ROUND vs vendor/unknown), and the unconditional-vs-inside-#if distinction that drives translate vs translate-directives error behavior. Verified against src/frontend/preprocess.rs classification fns and tests/directive_translate.rs fixture behavior.

title: Handle #warning and diagnostic directives without changing semantics
description:
Why: #warning reports a build diagnostic but does not reject compilation. Treating it as compile_error or silently dropping it would be wrong.

What to do:
- Record #warning messages and effective conditions.
- Surface active warnings as structured Slate diagnostics and preserve their unexpanded messages.
- For generated Cargo projects, invoke a separate slate-support proc-macro crate that emits an unspanned nightly proc_macro::Diagnostic at Level::Warning.
- For standalone generated Rust that cannot link slate-support, emit a uniquely named deprecated constant and a compile-time reference as a no-runtime-code fallback; accept that rustc anchors this fallback warning to the reference span.
- Apply the recovered effective Item::Cfg condition to either warning representation.
- Classify common diagnostic pragmas separately from semantic pragmas.
- Add E2E tests proving active warnings are visible, inactive warnings are absent, cfg-gated warnings follow the selected configuration, and warnings never turn successful builds into failures.
design: Use one typed warning directive representation and choose its lowering backend according to output mode. Project mode emits slate_support::warning!("message"); the proc macro calls Diagnostic::new(Level::Warning, message).emit() and expands to no tokens, producing a warning without a source span. This requires nightly and a separate proc-macro crate, which is acceptable for generated multi-file Cargo projects. Standalone source mode uses a uniquely named #[deprecated(note = "message")] const of type () plus an anonymous const that references it. This has no runtime effect but necessarily reports the generated reference span; ordinary Rust cannot delete that lint span. Never use compile_error for #warning. Preserve the raw unexpanded payload and wrap the selected typed items in the effective recovered cfg. If Slate drives rustc for a single file and can inject a prebuilt slate-support artifact with --extern, it may use the project backend; stdout-only source must remain self-contained and use the deprecated-const fallback.
acceptance_criteria: #warning retains its unexpanded message and effective configuration. Project output uses an unspanned slate-support proc-macro warning; self-contained standalone output uses the deprecated-const fallback with no runtime effect. Active warnings are visible, inactive warnings are absent, cfg-selected warnings appear only for selected configurations, and otherwise valid generated Rust still compiles successfully. Diagnostic pragmas have an explicit tested disposition.
close_reason: Closed

title: Audit and progressively lower semantic pragmas
description:
Why: pragmas such as #pragma pack, STDC floating-point controls, visibility, and section controls can change program semantics. Unknown semantic pragmas cannot be treated as harmless comments.

What to do:
- Inventory pragmas used by Slate fixtures and representative C projects.
- Start with #pragma once as no-output and #pragma pack as a layout feature.
- Recover Clang MaxFieldAlignmentAttr and any required pack-stack state for Rust record layout.
- Classify floating-point, visibility, section, diagnostic, and unknown pragmas by whether their effect is already present in AST/CIR.
- Add one focused child ticket per semantic pragma family discovered to need implementation; retain explicit compile-time failure until each is supported.
acceptance_criteria: The pragma inventory and disposition table are documented; #pragma pack cannot silently produce incorrect Rust layout; supported pragma effects have differential coverage; unsupported semantic pragmas fail explicitly under the applicable configuration.
notes: tests/fixtures.unsupported/c99.c is the C99 completion target for STDC FENV_ACCESS, FP_CONTRACT, CX_LIMITED_RANGE, and _Pragma-driven FP_CONTRACT handling.
close_reason: Engineering scope (inventory via fixtures, #pragma once/pack handling with real Clang MaxFieldAlignmentAttr recovery, clang-resolved-vs-unsupported classification, explicit-failure for unknown/FP-environment pragmas, one child ticket per remaining family) was already implemented and tested pre-existing (preprocess.rs, directive_translate.rs, tests/directive_translate.rs). Closed alongside .9 now that the last acceptance-criteria gap -- documented pragma inventory/disposition table -- is filled in docs/src/translate-directives.md. Remaining real work lives in still-open .10 (STDC FP pragmas, P4 intentionally deferred), .11 (#pragma pack unrepresentable-form audit), .12 (vendor visibility/section/optimization pragma audit).

title: Classify and test common non-conditional directives
description:
Why: many common directives should not be reproduced as Rust syntax because Clang already incorporates their effect or they have no runtime output, but Slate needs explicit recorded behavior rather than accidental omission.

What to do:
- Classify #define, #undef, #include, #include_next, #import, #line, #ident, #sccs, #embed, and the null directive.
- Keep macro definition and expansion recovery on the existing Clang macro-plugin path; do not invent externs for macros.
- Verify includes and supported #embed forms are reflected through Clang AST/CIR.
- Preserve #line effects in source-location joins.
- Add tests for each supported or explicitly rejected family.
acceptance_criteria: Each listed directive has a documented and tested disposition; directives consumed by Clang retain correct generated behavior and location joins; unsupported forms fail explicitly; recognized macro-constant recovery remains unchanged.
close_reason: Documented and E2E-tested dispositions for define/undef, include/include_next/import, line, ident/sccs, embed, and null directives; enabled Clang-consumed embed forms and verified explicit missing-input failure, AST/CIR header behavior, physical-line cfg joins, generated fixtures, and the full suite.

title: chibicc float: decide handling for undefined out-of-range float-to-int cast
description: Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/float has one remaining mismatch at (double)(unsigned long)(long)-1. The intermediate unsigned long is UINT64_MAX; converting its double approximation to int is outside int range and undefined by C, while Rust float-to-int casts saturate to INT_MAX. The host C result is target/compiler-dependent, so matching it in baseline lowering would encode undefined behavior. What: decide whether the chibicc harness should exclude or normalize this assertion, classify UB fixtures separately, or support an explicitly target-specific compatibility mode. Acceptance: the float fixture has a documented deterministic policy and either promotes without relying on UB or remains in a separately tracked compatibility bucket.

title: chibicc: anonymous bitfield-backed globals lose real member names
description: Why: bitfield.c (tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/bitfield) declares an anonymous, bitfield-packed global struct type shared by two var decls: 'struct { char a; int b:5; int c:10; } g45 = {1,2,3}, g46={};'. slate-pcek.8 fixed the literal 'cannot find type anon_0' by teaching collect_anon_record_info (src/lower.rs) to also pull in anon record types referenced only by a cir.global's sym_type, and taught the anonymous_structs fixup to rewrite field-type/field-access references to a renamed sibling record. That gets anon_0 defined and compiling as a tuple struct (i8, u16, u8 -- raw packed storage), but the record has NO real member names anywhere in the pipeline for this anonymous-global case, unlike a NAMED local bitfield struct (e.g. 'struct bit1' in the same fixture), which goes through a separate, correctly bitfield-aware lowering path that knows the real a/b/c/d/e names and packs/shifts around them. The fact-collector backing the anonymous_structs fixup ends up with a plan.fields list for anon_0 that only covers 2 of the struct's 3 storage slots (a and c get converted to tuple indices .0/.1; b is left as a bare .b access on a tuple struct with no named fields, producing E0609 'no field b'), so it's not just a naming gap -- the packed-bitfield storage shape and the source-level a/b/c access names are never reconciled for globals. What: figure out where the NAMED local-struct bitfield path (that correctly handles 'bit1') diverges from the anonymous-global path, and make anon_local_records (or wherever the global's record gets its shape) carry real bitfield member names/shift-mask semantics instead of positional f0/f1/f2. Acceptance: bitfield.c promotes to supported/.
close_reason: Recovered anonymous bitfield storage slots and promoted the chibicc bitfield fixture to supported

title: chibicc: alignof.c _Alignas struct-padding/order mismatch vs C
description: Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/alignof/alignof.c now translates and builds cleanly (the alloca-name-collision bug tracked in slate-04q.62/slate-pcek.4 is fixed), but differential testing shows a genuine runtime divergence unrelated to that fix: ({ _Alignas(char) char x, y; &y-&x; }) evaluates to -1 in C but 1 in Rust, and ({ _Alignas(long) char x, y; &y-&x; }) evaluates to 8 in C but 1 in Rust. This looks like the lowerer isn't honoring _Alignas-driven field/local ordering or padding the way C does. What: investigate how _Alignas locals are laid out in lower.rs/rust_ast and fix to match C's alignment-driven storage order. Acceptance: alignof.c passes chibicc_supported_tests_match_c end-to-end; promote it to supported/.
close_reason: Implemented aligned alloca frames and promoted alignof to the supported chibicc suite

title: Lower cir.fma (fma() builtin) - unhandled CIR op after clang toolchain refresh
description:
Why: tests/stdlib/math/fma.c started failing after refreshing the build-cir toolchain (ninja rebuild from a stale clang-23.0.0git tree to current clang-24.0.0git source, done to build the new macro-dump plugin -- see tools/macro-dump-plugin/). The refreshed CIR-enabled clang now emits a cir.fma op for the fma() builtin call that this fixture uses; Slate's lowerer has handlers for cir.fmaximum and cir.fmaxnum (both map to f64::max) but no case at all for cir.fma, so it falls through to the generic unsupported-op path and emits todo!("cir.fma").

What: add a CirOpKind::Fma variant (parse/render, mirroring the existing Fmaximum/Fmaxnum in src/cir/ir.rs) and a lower.rs handler that lowers it to Rust's f64::mul_add / f32::mul_add (the exact fused multiply-add equivalent -- not a plain a*b+c, which would round differently and fail the differential stdout comparison).

Immediate gate fix: added math/fma to tests/stdlib_coverage.rs's KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED list (this bead) so the suite is green again; remove that entry once cir.fma lowers correctly.
acceptance_criteria: cir.fma lowers to f64::mul_add/f32::mul_add. tests/stdlib/math/fma.c passes end-to-end (matching C stdout/exit). Removed from KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED in tests/stdlib_coverage.rs.
close_reason:
Added CirOpKind::Fma (src/cir/ir.rs, parse/render mirroring Fmaximum/Fmaxnum) and a new lower_ternary_method() handler (src/lower.rs) lowering cir.fma -> a.mul_add(b, c), the exact fused-multiply-add equivalent -- including the long-double branch (extracts .0 from each LongDouble operand, calls f64::mul_add, rewraps in LongDouble(...)), matching the existing pattern in lower_binary_method. No fixup pass needed since mul_add is already the ideal target shape.

Removed math/fma from tests/stdlib_coverage.rs's KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED. Verified: tests/stdlib/math/fma.c now lowers directly to '_v4.mul_add(_v5, _v6)' and passes end-to-end (C/Rust stdout+exit match). Full suite green: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo nextest r --release -- 684/684 passing.

title: Recover exact macro-invocation names via a Clang PPCallbacks plugin, joined by source location
description:
Why: slate-04q.60's limits.h recovery can only match by coincidental literal value (INT_MAX -> 2147483647) since macro names are gone by the time Slate sees Clang AST JSON / CIR -- preprocessing is a textual substitution pass that runs before parsing. That forced excluding whole buckets of otherwise-legitimate constants (i8/u8 boundaries, all unsigned MIN==0) purely because their values collide with common unrelated literals.

Prototyped and empirically verified (scratch spike, not yet in-repo): a small (~50 line) out-of-tree Clang plugin hooking the standard, decade-stable PPCallbacks::MacroExpands API captures every macro invocation -- both system-header constants (INT_MAX, INT_MIN, CHAR_BIT, LONG_MAX) and user #defines -- as a (macro name, file, line, col) event. Verified output:

  MACRO_EXPANSION name=INT_MAX  file=t.c line=4 col=11
  MACRO_EXPANSION name=CHAR_BIT file=t.c line=6 col=11

The (file, line, col) of each event lines up exactly with the expansionLoc already present on the corresponding AST IntegerLiteral node in Clang's -ast-dump=json output (confirmed by direct comparison). This means macro names can be joined onto Slate's existing AST facts by source location -- the same join mechanism already used to connect CIR ops to Clang AST facts (see docs/architecture.md) -- with no new correlation mechanism needed.

What to do:
  1. Land the plugin (MacroExpands hook -> structured, ideally JSON, event stream) as a small standalone Clang plugin source file in the repo (e.g. tools/ or a new clang-plugins/ dir), built against SLATE_CLANG's own toolchain.
  2. Wire it into the C-side extraction step (alongside the existing -ast-dump=json invocation in src/c_ast.rs) so every translation unit also emits its macro-expansion event stream.
  3. Parse that stream into a new fact source (macro name keyed by source location), joined the same way c_ast.rs's other source facts are joined to CIR ops.
  4. Expose it to fixups as a value bag/lookup: "was this constant expression written as an invocation of macro X", usable by any future macro-based idiomatization, not just limits.h.
  5. Once available, slate-04q.60's limits.h pass should prefer this exact-name fact over the value-only heuristic -- this removes the need for the i8/u8 and unsigned-MIN exclusions entirely, since a real macro-name match has no ambiguity to guard against.

Blocking prerequisite (being resolved now): the plugin could not be compiled against SLATE_CLANG's own build tree (~/llvm-project/build-cir) because a generated header it needs (clang/Basic/Traits.inc) is missing and that tree's clang-tblgen predates the backend that generates it -- the tree is stale relative to the current clang source checkout. Validated instead against a separate, complete build tree, since PPCallbacks is untouched by the CIR patches. A ninja refresh of build-cir is needed before the plugin can be built against the actual toolchain Slate shells out to.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin builds cleanly against SLATE_CLANG's own build-cir toolchain. Macro-expansion events are captured for a real translation unit and correlate 1:1 by source location with the corresponding AST/CIR literal. New fact source is queryable by fixups. slate-04q.60's limits.h pass can consume it to safely recover the currently-excluded i8/u8 and unsigned-MIN constants.
close_reason: Landed: tools/macro-dump-plugin/{MacroDump.cpp,build.sh} in-repo, hooking PPCallbacks::MacroExpands and emitting MACRO_EXPANSION {name,file,offset} JSON lines on stderr per invocation. Wired into src/c_ast.rs: run_clang_ast_dump() always passes -fplugin=$SLATE_MACRO_DUMP_PLUGIN alongside the existing -ast-dump=json call, parse_macro_events() maps byte offset -> macro name, and collect_macro_consts() walks the AST confirming a node is a whole single-macro invocation when its entire range (begin==end after expansionLoc resolution) collapses to one offset matching a captured event -- verified this holds even for multi-op macros like glibc's INT_MIN (-INT_MAX - 1) and UINT_MAX ((INT_MAX * 2U) + 1U), which still fully collapse to one point despite expanding to multiple CIR ops. Result threaded onto Function.macro_consts (Vec<String>, source order) and consumed positionally in lower.rs the same way layout_queries already handles sizeof/alignof. This unblocked slate-04q.60's full limits.h scope, including the small/ambiguous values (SCHAR_MIN, UCHAR_MAX, CHAR_BIT) originally excluded there.

title: Recover limits.h constants (INT_MAX, LONG_MIN, SIZE_MAX, ...) as named Rust consts
description:
Why: #define constants from limits.h (INT_MAX, INT_MIN, LONG_MAX, UINT_MAX, SIZE_MAX, etc.) vanish during preprocessing before Slate ever sees CIR -- confirmed directly: dumping Clang's AST JSON for 'int x = INT_MAX;' gives a plain IntegerLiteral node with value "2147483647" and no field anywhere naming the macro (only spellingLoc/expansionLoc breadcrumbs). So baseline lowering only ever sees the raw literal value, and generated Rust never recovers Rust's own named equivalents (i32::MAX, u64::MAX, usize::MAX, ...) even though they exist 1:1. This is a pure idiomatization win, like the printf/string recovery rungs already have, with zero behavior change.

What to do: a static lookup table keyed by (Rust integer type, exact literal value) -> path expr (e.g. (i32, 2147483647) -> "i32::MAX", (i64, -9223372036854775808) -> "i64::MIN", (usize, usize::MAX's value) -> "usize::MAX"). Scope is short/int/long/long long: signed MIN and unsigned MAX (SHRT_MIN, INT_MIN, LONG_MIN, LLONG_MIN, USHRT_MAX, UINT_MAX, ULONG_MAX, ULLONG_MAX) plus SIZE_MAX. Deliberately exclude two buckets:
  - i8/u8 (char-sized) boundaries -- SCHAR_MIN/MAX, UCHAR_MAX, CHAR_MIN/MAX. -128/127/255 show up constantly in code for reasons unrelated to signed/unsigned char range (audio/pixel data, bitmasks, small counters), so matching on value alone has a much higher false-positive rate than it does for the wider types.
  - all unsigned MIN values (0). u8::MIN/u16::MIN/u32::MIN/usize::MIN are all exactly 0, and 0 is the single most common literal in any program for reasons having nothing to do with a type's range (initializers, loop starts, sentinels). Rewriting bare 0 into u32::MIN would be technically true but strictly less idiomatic than leaving it alone -- nobody writes u32::MIN to mean zero.
For the included set (16/32/64-bit signed MIN and unsigned MAX, plus SIZE_MAX), the literal values are large and distinctive enough that they essentially never appear by coincidence, so value-only matching is safe.

A single small fixup pass walks integer-literal exprs with a known static type and swaps in the named const on an exact match.

Placement: register this as the very first fixup pass in src/fixups/mod.rs's apply_with_logger step list, running before Pass::Goto. It's a pure value/syntax substitution with no dependency on control-flow or binding facts, so it behaves more like a lowering step than a fact-driven fixup -- running it first also means every downstream pass observes the idiomatic named form rather than the raw literal.

Existing coverage: tests/stdlib/limits/ranges.c and tests/stdlib/misc/limits.c already exercise these values numerically (see slate-nk3.11) -- this ticket is purely about the idiomatized *form* of the output, not about making the values correct (they already are).

Out of scope / future follow-up: recovering the *actual macro name* used at a call site (rather than matching by coincidental value) would require Clang's PreprocessingRecord (PPCallbacks::MacroExpands) captured as a side-channel and joined into the pipeline by source location, the same way CIR ops are already joined to Clang AST facts. That's a heavier, separate piece of work (likely needs a small Clang tool/plugin, not just a CLI flag) and should get its own ticket if ever prioritized -- not in scope here.
acceptance_criteria: Lookup table covers signed short/int/long/long long MIN, unsigned short/int/long/long long MAX, and SIZE_MAX -- explicitly excludes i8/u8 boundaries and all unsigned MIN (0) values. New pass runs first in the fixup pipeline (before Pass::Goto). Differential tests (including tests/stdlib/limits/*) still pass with no change in runtime behavior -- only the emitted Rust syntax changes from a bare literal to a named associated const.
close_reason:
Implemented using the confirmed-macro-name approach from slate-04q.61 instead of the value-only fallback originally scoped here -- so the exclusions this ticket originally called for (i8/u8 boundaries, unsigned MIN) were dropped entirely; a macro-confirmed match has no value-collision ambiguity to guard against.

New src/limits_macros.rs: static table of 19 limits.h names -> (i128 value, Rust path), covering SCHAR/UCHAR/CHAR/SHRT/USHRT/INT/UINT/LONG/ULONG/LLONG/ULLONG MIN/MAX, SIZE_MAX, and CHAR_BIT (-> u8::BITS).

In lower.rs: FunctionLowerer.macro_consts (VecDeque<String>, source order, from c_ast.rs's Function.macro_consts) is consumed positionally at two points -- next_macro_const_expr() at cir.const (handles single-literal macros like INT_MAX), and a fold-and-check added to lower_int_arith() (handles multi-op macros like INT_MIN's cir.sub or UINT_MAX's cir.mul+cir.add, via a small macro_arith_values side-table chained onto const_int_values). Both only substitute when the *folded numeric value* also matches the confirmed macro's known value, so a coincidental value match without the plugin's confirmation is never enough on its own.

Verified: tests/stdlib/limits/ranges.c (pre-existing fixture exercising exactly this scope) now emits i8::MIN/i8::MAX/u8::MAX/i16::MIN/i16::MAX/i32::MIN/i32::MAX/i64::MIN/i64::MAX/u8::BITS instead of bare literals, and still passes stdlib_coverage end-to-end (C/Rust stdout+exit match). Full suite green: cargo nextest r --release, 684/684 (after filing slate-nk3.23 for an unrelated cir.fma regression surfaced by the build-cir toolchain refresh this work required, and ratcheting it into KNOWN_UNSUPPORTED).

title: chibicc: runtime output mismatches across several compiling fixtures
description:
Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/{float,bitfield_op_assign,macro} all translate AND compile successfully on both sides, but produce different stdout or exit code than C -- meaning these are real behavioral divergences, not missing features. Each likely has its own distinct root cause; they're grouped here only because they weren't individually root-caused during the initial triage pass (run 'cargo nextest r --release --test chibicc_suite -- --ignored chibicc_unsupported_triage_report --nocapture' to see each one's specific stdout/exit diff).

(9 fixtures originally listed here -- alloc, complex, crlf_line_continuation, defined, line_continuation, macro_constexpr_ident, macro_whitespace, offsetof, va_args, vla_param, plus string.c from slate-pcek.7 -- turned out to share one root cause: a printf/println! stdio-buffering race, fixed and promoted to supported/. See notes.)

What: for each file, read the diff, find the specific expression/construct producing the wrong output, and either fix it or split it into its own ticket once the root cause is known to be distinct from the others in this group.

Acceptance: each file either promotes to supported/ or gets split out into a more specific follow-up ticket with its actual root cause identified.
notes: 9 of 12 originally-listed fixtures (alloc, complex, crlf_line_continuation, defined, line_continuation, macro_constexpr_ident, macro_whitespace, offsetof, va_args, vla_param) were actually all the SAME bug: printf-format idiomatization converts a printf(...) call to println!/print!() in one file, while common.c's assert() keeps a raw extern printf() call in another file linked into the same binary. Rust's stdout buffer and libc's stdio FILE* buffer flush independently -- Rust's println! flushes immediately on newline, but libc's buffered printf output only flushes at process exit -- so the println! output lands on the fd before the still-buffered printf output, reordering stdout relative to C. Fixed in src/fixups/rewrite/printf_format.rs by always wrapping remaining raw printf calls with a flush/fflush barrier (previously only done when the SAME file/Program also converted a call, missing the cross-file case). Remaining unresolved in this bucket: float, bitfield_op_assign, macro -- distinct root causes, still need triage.
close_reason: Promoted macro after the prior macro-name dedup fix; fixed bitfield_op_assign by lowering all-bitfield records through CIR physical backing storage and promoted it; split float's undefined out-of-range float-to-int cast into slate-pcek.17. Added bitfield init/increment differential coverage. cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, and all 684 release nextest tests pass; known aggregate Alive regressions excluded per project direction.

title: chibicc: LongDouble newtype missing PartialEq
description:
Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/long_double fails Rust compilation with E0369: binary operation == cannot be applied to type LongDouble. long double is lowered to an ABI-exact #[repr(C, align(16))] newtype (per docs/README.md) but that type doesn't derive/impl PartialEq, so C code comparing two long doubles with == doesn't translate.

What: add PartialEq (and likely PartialOrd, if long double comparisons beyond == show up elsewhere) to the LongDouble newtype, comparing the underlying f64 representation.

Acceptance: long_double.c promotes to supported/.
close_reason: LongDouble now derives PartialEq; also generalized the printf-family long-double variadic shim (any extern format-string function, any arg count/position/mix, keyed by concrete signature shape) and fixed the strtold/f64-payload representation mismatch. long_double.c chibicc fixture promoted to supported/.

title: chibicc: anonymous struct/union type naming collisions
description:
Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/union fails Rust compilation with 21 errors, mostly E0425 'cannot find type anon_11/anon_13/anon_15 in this scope' -- anonymous struct/union member types aren't being consistently named/declared when a file declares many of them. bitfield.c shows a related symptom ('cannot find type anon_0', 'cannot find value g45').

What: reproduce with a fixture declaring several anonymous struct/union members in the same file and trace where the anon_N naming is assigned vs where it's referenced, to find the indexing/ordering mismatch.

Acceptance: union.c promotes to supported/ (or gets substantially closer); note whether bitfield.c shares the same root cause.
close_reason: Root cause: collect_anon_record_info (src/lower.rs) only added an anon struct/union type to the 'needed' set when it appeared directly as an alloca's pointee type or a cir.get_member's container type. Two shapes fell through and were referenced-but-never-defined: (1) a record whose only use is as a NESTED FIELD inside another already-needed anon record (e.g. union{struct{...} c;}'s inner struct), fixed with a fixpoint closure over each needed record's expanded field types; (2) a record used only as a top-level GLOBAL's type (cir.global's sym_type, no alloca/get_member at all), fixed by adding a CirOpKind::Global case to the walker. Also fixed a second, unrelated cause hitting the same fixture: cir_type_to_ctype had no !cir.array<...> branch, so an anon record field of array type silently defaulted to scalar i32. Once nested anon types got pulled in, a sibling gap surfaced in the anonymous_structs fixup (same shape of bug, one layer up): renaming a record to a tuple struct only rewrote its own declaration, never sibling records' field types or chained/global field-access expressions referencing it -- fixed by making rewrite_item always walk field types and giving the fixup a record-field-type + global-variable-type table so it can resolve chained access (x._tmp.a, g45.a) through a renamed sibling type. union.c promotes to supported/ and passes end-to-end. bitfield.c's literal 'cannot find type anon_0' is gone, but it hits a separate, deeper issue -- its anonymous bitfield-backed global never gets real a/b/c member names anywhere in the pipeline (unlike a named local bitfield struct, which has dedicated bitfield-aware lowering) -- filed as slate-pcek.16, not the same root cause as this ticket.

title: chibicc: cross-module pointer-typed global import broken
description:
Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/extern fails Rust compilation with E0432 unresolved import crate::common::ext2. common.c defines 'int ext1 = 5; int *ext2 = \&ext1;' and extern.c cross-module-references both; ext1 (a plain int global) imports fine per the existing globals/static_linkage fixtures, but ext2 (a pointer global initialized to another global's address) does not -- suggests translate-project's cross-module global detection or pub-export logic has a gap specifically for pointer-typed globals with an address-of initializer.

What: reproduce with a minimal two-file fixture (a pointer global initialized to \&sibling_global, referenced from another translation unit) and trace defined_globals/cross_module_globals in src/lower.rs for why it isn't picked up or exported correctly.

Acceptance: extern.c promotes to supported/; consider adding a small tests/fixtures.multi/ regression fixture for this specific shape alongside the existing globals fixture.
close_reason: Same root cause as slate-pcek.5, fixed by the same commit: collect_global's #cir.global_view<@target> handling silently dropped pointer globals whose target was another data global rather than a string literal, so int *ext2 = &ext1; (common.c) was never inserted into self.globals and thus never registered in defined_globals -- translate-project's cross-module import logic had nothing to point crate::common::ext2 at, hence E0432. Now goes through global_view_init_expr (addr_of_mut!(ext1) as *mut i32), so ext2 is a real global and the cross-module import resolves. Verified end-to-end: extern.c now promotes to supported/ alongside complit.c. No separate tests/fixtures.multi/ regression fixture added -- extern.c exercises this exact shape and stays in the differential suite.

title: chibicc: compound literal lowering produces invalid Rust
description:
Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/complit fails Rust compilation with E0425 (cannot find value 'tree'), E0530 (let bindings cannot shadow statics), and E0599 (no method named as_mut_ptr found for type i32) -- compound literals ((Type){...}) used in expression position appear to lower incorrectly, referencing names that were never bound and treating a scalar as if it were array/pointer-typed.

What: reproduce with a minimal compound-literal fixture, read the generated Rust, and trace which lowering path handles (T){...} in expression (not initializer) position.

Acceptance: complit.c promotes to supported/.
close_reason: Root cause: cir.global's #cir.global_view<@target> initializer was only handled when target was a string literal (self.strings); a pointer global initialized to another data global's address (Tree *tree = &(Tree){...}) was silently dropped, and the same gap inside render_const_value_expr defaulted struct pointer fields with a global_view initializer (nested compound literals' lhs/rhs) to null. Fixed via a shared global_view_init_expr helper in src/lower.rs, restricted to Type::Ptr targets so it doesn't misfire on non-pointer global_view uses (e.g. a function address stored in an Option<fn> static). Also extended slate-pcek.4's per-function local-name dedup to check against already-collected global names, fixing the E0530 'let binding shadows a static' where a block-scope compound-literal temp reused a file-scope compound-literal static's generated name. Promoted complit to supported/.

title: chibicc: widespread i32/i64/u64 width mismatches in generated expressions
description:
Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/{arith,bitfield,cast,commonsym,decl,enum,typeof,usualconv} all fail Rust compilation with E0308 mismatched-types errors, almost always an i32 vs i64/u64 mismatch (e.g. enum.c: sizeof(x) used where assert()'s i32 parameter is expected, producing 'expected i32, found u64'). This is the same shape of bug across many files -- likely one or two root causes in how sizeof/pointer-arithmetic/enum-constant results get typed relative to their usage context (chibicc's ASSERT macro always expects int-width operands). (extern.c looked similar at a glance but its actual failure is a cross-module import bug, tracked separately as slate-pcek.6 -- not part of this cluster.)

What: pick the smallest failing case (enum.c is dense with this) and trace where a u64/i64-typed expression ends up passed somewhere expecting i32 without a cast. Likely a gap in the fixup or lowering step that should narrow sizeof/pointer-diff results to match C's int-promotion rules at the call site.

Acceptance: at least enum.c promotes to supported/; note in the ticket which of the other 7 files share the exact same root cause vs need separate fixes.
close_reason: Root cause: Clang CIR hoists all local allocas to a function's entry block, reusing generic compiler names (e.g. 'tmp') across distinct temps such as per-GNU-statement-expression result slots. lower_alloca took the CIR name verbatim, so colliding allocas produced repeated 'let mut tmp = ...' bindings that Rust resolved to the last (differently-typed) shadow, causing widespread i32/u64 call-site mismatches. Fixed by deduping local names per function in src/lower.rs (declared_local_names + unique_local_name). Promoted arith, decl, enum, macro to supported/. bitfield/cast/commonsym/usualconv/typeof still fail but from unrelated causes (anonymous-type naming collisions -- tracked in slate-pcek.8; unsafe/safe fn-pointer coercion in threads.c; a preprocessor-stage C-compile error in typeof.c) -- not part of this cluster.

title: chibicc: unresolved temp variable references in generated Rust (offset_from lowering)
description:
Why: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/{alignof,pointer_neg} translate but produce Rust that fails to compile with e.g. 'cannot find value _19 in this scope' where the let-binding is actually named _v19 -- a real name-mismatch bug in temp-variable lowering, not a missing feature. Also alignof hits 'no method named offset_from found for type i8' / 'expected u64, found i64' -- offset_from's signedness/receiver-type handling looks wrong for pointer difference expressions like ((char*)&y - (char*)&x).

What: reproduce with a minimal C fixture (a statement-expression computing a temp used inside a nested offset_from-shaped pointer subtraction), find where the _N vs _vN naming diverges, and fix the offset_from argument typing.

Acceptance: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/alignof and pointer_neg promote to supported/ (or get substantially closer -- alignof also touches unrelated width-mismatch bugs tracked separately).
close_reason:
pointer_neg promoted to supported/. alignof substantially closer but not fully promoted -- split remaining blocker to slate-04q.62 (see below), matching this ticket's acceptance criteria allowance for unrelated width-mismatch bugs.

Root cause of the originally-cited '_N vs _vN unresolved reference' and 'offset_from receiver/signedness' bugs: three CIR ops -- lower_ptr_stride, lower_ptr_diff, and the array-decay-to-integer arm of lower_cast -- called operand_expr() (which only resolves self.values/self.slots) on a pointer-typed base that was actually an ElementPtr/MemberPtr fact (never materialized into self.values), or applied no cast at all when a pointer decayed to a plain integer result type. Fixed by:
  - lower_ptr_stride/lower_ptr_diff: use pointer_operand_expr() instead of operand_expr() for pointer-typed operands, so element/member place facts resolve to a real std::ptr::addr_of_mut!(...) expression instead of falling through to a bare, unresolved SSA-name identifier.
  - lower_cast: two related ptrtoint bugs found and fixed in the same investigation -- (1) a Global operand cast to a non-pointer result type was passed through unresolved as Val::Global, which a later to_expr() rendered as a bare read of the global's VALUE (e.g. '(long)&g1 % 512' became 'g1 % 512', silently reading g1's stored contents instead of its address); (2) a local array slot decaying to a non-pointer (integer) result type produced '.as_mut_ptr()' with no enclosing cast, which doesn't type-check against an integer-typed destination. Both now correctly emit 'std::ptr::addr_of!(name) as T' / '(x.as_mut_ptr() as T)'.

Remaining, distinct blocker for alignof (NOT related to the above): repeated GNU statement-expression result temps that Clang's CIR names identically ('tmp') but allocates as separate, differently-typed SSA slots collide in Slate's lower_alloca (no name-collision detection), so Rust's own let-shadowing silently misdirects an earlier binding's reads/writes onto a later, wrong-typed one -- a genuine E0308 in the generated Rust. Filed as slate-04q.62 with a minimal repro and precise root cause; requires its own careful fix (mint a disambiguated name on collision) without disturbing legitimate nested-scope name reuse elsewhere, so intentionally out of scope here.

Verified: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo nextest r --release -- 684/684 passing, including chibicc_supported_tests_match_c (pointer_neg's C/Rust stdout+exit match).

title: Bulk-migrate remaining cc3 tests into unsupported/ and triage
description:
Why: with the harness proven (slate-pcek.1), copy the rest of cc3/test's 61 files (minus include-next.c/pragma-once.c, which need nonstandard build flags) into tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/, then run the suite once to see which already pass end-to-end.

What: one-off migration script (verbatim copies of each <name>.c, common.c/test.h symlinks, plus the handful of extra per-test headers macro.c/include_macro.c/file_line.c need). Run chibicc_unsupported_tests_still_fail, git mv every case it flags as 'now passes' into supported/.

Acceptance: tests/fixtures.chibicc/unsupported/ contains the remaining cc3 tests; tests/fixtures.chibicc/supported/ contains everything that already passes end-to-end; both harness tests are green.
close_reason: Migrated all 58 remaining cc3/test files (61 total minus include-next.c/pragma-once.c, which need nonstandard build flags). Strict-xfail run promoted attribute, file_line, stdhdr to supported/ (plus param_ptr from .1) -- 4 supported, 57 unsupported. Fixed a migration oversight along the way (macro.c was missing include2.h). Full triage done: read every unsupported case's actual failure and clustered them into 12 follow-up tickets (slate-pcek.3 through .14) by root cause -- real Rust codegen bugs (unresolved temp names, width mismatches, compound literals, cross-module pointer globals, string.c's syntactically-invalid output, anon struct/union naming, LongDouble PartialEq), a runtime-mismatch grab-bag needing further bisection, threads.h/TLS scope, a likely-cheap clang -Wno-error flag fix that could unlock 13 files at once, misc C23/builtin gaps (some permanently excludable -- nonstandard float literals, a chibicc-internal ABI test, a possible clang crash), and include-path edge cases. Full test suite green (684 tests).

title: Build chibicc test harness and validate against one fixture
description:
Why: need the translate-project -> batched-crate -> diff pipeline proven end-to-end on one simple case before bulk-migrating 60+ cc3 test files.

What: add build_multi_bin_batch to tests/support/mod.rs (mirrors build_batch/compare_batch but for two-file src/bin/<name>/{main.rs,common.rs} binaries), add tests/chibicc_suite.rs with chibicc_supported_tests_match_c and chibicc_unsupported_tests_still_fail, and land tests/fixtures.chibicc/{common.c,test.h,supported/alignof/} as the first real fixture.

Acceptance: cargo nextest r --release --test chibicc_suite passes; alignof.c translates via translate-project, builds in the batched crate, and matches C output exactly.
close_reason: Harness built: tests/chibicc_suite.rs + build_multi_bin_batch in tests/support/mod.rs (batched shared crate, Cargo's src/bin/<name>/{main.rs,common.rs} convention). Validated end-to-end with real cc3 fixtures rather than a single hand-picked one: param_ptr already passes and is promoted to supported/; alignof and enum are real discovered gaps and stay in unsupported/, correctly caught by the strict-xfail chibicc_unsupported_tests_still_fail check. Both harness tests green, full suite green.

title: Migrate cc3/chibicc C compiler test suite into differential harness
description:
Why: ~/Projects/cc3/test has 63 chibicc-style self-checking C test files (each linked with a shared common.c) covering a broad C/GNU surface (VLA, atomics, threads, GNU extensions, bitfields, varargs, inline asm, C23 #embed, etc). Migrating this into slate's differential harness gives a large, free source of ground-truth C-vs-Rust behavioral coverage well beyond slate's own hand-authored fixtures.

What: build a tests/fixtures.chibicc/{supported,unsupported}/<name>/ layout (reusing slate's existing translate-project + tests/fixtures.multi conventions), a new tests/chibicc_suite.rs harness with a batched shared-crate Rust build (Cargo's src/bin/<name>/main.rs + common.rs multi-file-binary convention, one cargo build for all cases), and a strict-xfail mechanism for the unsupported bucket so a since-fixed test can't silently rot (the harness hard-fails and tells you to promote it). See the approved plan for full design.

Acceptance: tests/chibicc_suite.rs passes with both supported and unsupported buckets wired up; all 61 auto-migratable cc3 tests land in one bucket or the other; currently-passing cases are promoted to supported/; remaining failures are clustered by root cause into follow-up tickets rather than one-per-file.

title: Instrument heap, atomic, varargs, and specialized structural facts
description:
Why: specialized passes depend on narrow fact collectors whose failures are hard to diagnose from rewrite logs alone.

Scope:
- heap ownership facts
- atomic local/global facts
- atomic compare-exchange chain facts if present or derived
- va_list alias facts
- lazy singleton facts
- anonymous struct facts and item/type dependency facts used by pruning

Acceptance:
- Fact debug explains accepted/rejected candidates for these specialized rewrites.
- Logs include relevant bindings, paths, helper/static names, and rejection reasons.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add focused fact-debug CLI smoke coverage
description:
Why: the CLI needs enough coverage to prevent regressions in filtering, group naming, and no-facts output.

Scope:
- Add minimal CLI-level tests or existing-test extensions for --debug-facts / --debug-only-facts behavior.
- Cover unknown fact group diagnostics.
- Cover at least one accepted and one rejected/empty fact group output.

Acceptance:
- Fact debug CLI behavior is exercised without adding broad rewrite fixture coverage.
- Tests remain focused on debug plumbing and filtering, not semantic expansion.
close_reason: Closed

title: Structured fact debug logging for rewrite gating
description:
Why: rewrite debug logs explain changes after a pass fires, but they do not explain why a pass did not fire. Many high-value rewrites are gated by fact collectors, so debugging needs structured visibility into which facts were accepted, which candidates were rejected, and which facts are available to a selected rewrite pass.

Scope:
- Add fact-debug CLI controls similar to fixup debug pass controls, including debug facts and debug-only-facts style filtering.
- Add structured fact events for major rewrite-gating fact collectors.
- Keep fact logs concise: accepted/rejected candidate events with reasons and relevant paths/bindings, not raw AST walk dumps.
- Wire fact logs so debug-only-pass can optionally show facts consumed by that rewrite pass, or provide an equivalent focused workflow.

Acceptance:
- Users can inspect fact discovery for selected fact groups without reading full program diffs.
- Users can tell whether a rewrite did not fire because facts were missing, rejected, or later not consumed.
- The output remains structured and filterable by fact group.
- No broad test expansion unless needed for CLI behavior.
close_reason: Closed

title: Instrument type, item, and specialized cleanup passes with explicit debug events
description:
Why: the remaining specialized and structural cleanup passes still need pass-local rewrite explanations instead of fallback whole-program diffs.

Scope:
- anonymous_structs
- param_spills
- struct_field_init
- compound_assign
- constant_index_casts
- unnecessary_casts
- lazy_singleton
- va_list
- sort_search
- heap_ownership
- atomic_locals
- atomic_compare_exchange
- prune_unused_externs
- unused_items

What to do:
- Emit pass-local events for each concrete rewrite/removal/addition with before/after snippets and relevant facts.
- Document any pass in this group that genuinely has no meaningful per-change detail.
- Do not add new tests for this migration slice.
acceptance_criteria: Each scoped pass emits explicit structured events for AST changes or has a documented no-detail rationale; generic pass_changed is not the primary debugging output for any changed scoped pass; no new tests are added.
notes: touches: src/fixups/mod.rs, src/fixups/rewrite/{anonymous_structs,param_spills,struct_field_init,compound_assign,constant_index_casts,unnecessary_casts,lazy_singleton,va_list,sort_search,heap_ownership,atomic_locals,atomic_compare_exchange,prune_unused_externs,unused_items}.rs; no new tests per request
close_reason: Implemented explicit structured debug events for anonymous_structs, param_spills, struct_field_init, compound_assign, constant_index_casts, unnecessary_casts, lazy_singleton, va_list, sort_search, heap_ownership, atomic_locals, atomic_compare_exchange, prune_unused_externs, and unused_items; routed scheduler calls through logger-aware pass structs/helpers. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo check --tests, git diff --check, targeted cargo test filters, debug-only CLI smokes for every scoped pass, differential filters for existing coverage, and release nextest filters.

title: Document structured fixup logging conventions
description: Update docs/passes.md and docs/writing-a-fixup.md with the structured debug logging conventions: pass enum usage, logger threading, rewrite event expectations, facts guidance, before/after snippet rules, and CLI examples for --up-to-pass and --only-pass.
design: Keep detailed implementation guidance in docs/writing-a-fixup.md and pass-sequence/user-facing CLI behavior in docs/passes.md.
acceptance_criteria: Docs explain how a new or existing pass should emit structured rewrite events; docs include examples like zero_init folding and late_inline_temps inlining into a method argument closure; docs warn that rendered snippets are for logs only, not matching; docs list debug CLI flags.
close_reason: Documented structured fixup logging conventions in docs/passes.md and docs/writing-a-fixup.md, including pass enum usage, logger threading, event payloads, snippet/fact rules, and fixup-debug pass controls. Verified with git diff --check.

title: Instrument remaining fixup passes with structured logs
description: After the logger API and initial temp-cleanup instrumentation land, extend structured logging across the rest of the fixup pass catalog. Each pass should emit domain-specific events that explain its rewrite decisions and relevant facts.
design: Do this after the API is stable. Instrument passes incrementally by concern area to avoid a large risky sweep.
acceptance_criteria: Every rewrite pass in docs/passes.md that can change the AST emits pass-local structured rewrite events for each change, with before/after snippets and relevant facts. Generic pass_changed fallback is allowed to remain as a safety net but no changed pass should rely on it as its primary debugging output. Passes that genuinely have no meaningful per-change detail are explicitly documented. No new tests are added for this migration unless existing tests require maintenance.
notes: Reopened: generic pass_changed fallback is only a migration bridge and does not satisfy all-pass explicit logging. Completion requires migrating passes to pass-local events like inline_temps/zero_init/dead_locals/var_aliases, with no new tests per request unless a pass-specific regression already exists and must be updated.
close_reason: Completed the all-pass trace audit. Logged singleton-scope and dead-local changes performed by slice_loop, slice_reduce, and range_loop under their active parent pass; enforced active-pass event tagging; documented ptr_copy, constant_conditions, libc_exit, and final_returns in scheduler order; removed stale WORKFLOW.md references. Verified all 197 fixtures produce no generic pass_changed fallback, cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, and cargo nextest r --release (684 passed, 1 skipped).

title: Keep fixup debug tracing off the normal translate fast path
description: The initial fixup-debug implementation snapshots pass boundaries by running a traced pipeline that clones analyses around move-based pass boundaries. Normal translate should keep the original move-based path, with tracing isolated to fixup-debug or a shared helper that only snapshots when tracing is enabled.
close_reason: Superseded by slate-wp4.5, which verifies normal apply/apply_with use the disabled no-op logger path without pass snapshots/events while fixup-debug uses the collecting logger.

title: Clean up memchr Option result temps across pure method barriers
description: After memchr_prelude, mem_memchr still keeps search-result temps like _v3/_v6 plus derived println temps because temp-chain facts treat intervening Option/iterator method calls as side-effect barriers. Add precise purity/effect facts for these known methods or a narrow fixup so those temps can be safely inlined without broad reordering.
notes: Preserved source local names for nullable pointer Option producers when the pointer alias declaration/assignment is already proven removable. mem_memchr now emits hit/miss/nul instead of _v3/_v6/_v9 for the search results. Remaining work on this bead: derived println temps like _v11/_v14 still remain and need separate temp-chain/purity handling.
close_reason: Closed

title: Effects: varargs and formatted output summaries
description: Add Rust-to-Rust effect handling for generated c_variadic functions and formatted output. Raw libc printf-family calls and fixed print!/println!/format! shapes should normalize to equivalent stdout/stderr byte effects where the supported format is known; unsupported formats should remain explicit extraction failures.
close_reason: Closed

title: Effects: Rust-side runtime/environment and external call policy
description: Define the Rust-to-Rust effect validation policy for runtime/environment interactions and unsupported external calls. Known libc/std/POSIX calls that fixups rewrite should get explicit summaries; unknown calls should either remain opaque when both sides match or report precise unsupported extraction failures.
close_reason: Closed

title: Effects: scalar, overflow, float, and complex Rust AST evaluation
description: Broaden Rust AST effect evaluation for scalar operations that appear in raw lowered Rust and fixuped Rust: overflow methods, floats, complex/long-double helper shapes, casts, comparisons, and arithmetic. This is Rust-to-Rust fixup validation only; unsupported shapes should report precise extraction failures.
close_reason: Closed

title: Effects: vector Rust AST evaluation
description: Broaden Rust AST effect evaluation for vector-extension values and native Rust vector-equivalent shapes that appear in raw lowered Rust and fixuped Rust. The goal is raw-vs-fixuped trace equivalence for vector fixtures without relying on source/CIR-side interpretation.
close_reason: Closed

title: Effects CIR walker: support cir.scope and cir.inc
description: src/effects/cir.rs's Interp::step() panics on any real clang-emitted for-loop body because clang wraps the loop-local variable in cir.scope and lowers i++ to cir.inc rather than cir.add(i, 1). All current effects tests avoid this by hand-building fixtures with plain cir.add instead of cir.inc and no cir.scope wrapper (see cir.rs's for_loop_fill_and_sum_fixture). Confirmed while investigating slate-b8y.11: tests/fixtures/ptr_len_slice.c's bump() function, a real ptr_len-fixup-recovered *mut i32/length -> &mut [i32] case, cannot be run through the real end-to-end pipeline (emit-cir -> parse -> interpret) because of this gap; ptr_len's own fact-collector requires a bounded for-loop to prove the pointer/length pair sound, so any real slice-recovered fixture will hit this.
acceptance_criteria: src/effects/cir.rs's Interp::step() handles cir.scope (run the nested region's ops inline, propagating Flow like cir.if's branches do) and cir.inc (unary +1, same shape as cir.dec would be -1) without panicking. A real C fixture with a for-loop (e.g. tests/fixtures/ptr_len_slice.c) can be run through the full emit-cir -> parse -> interpret pipeline via effects::regression's assert_cir_and_rust_effects_match without a manual/hand-built Op workaround.
close_reason: Added Inc/Dec/Scope/Yield support to effects::cir's Interp::step(), plus a real (non-hand-built) for-loop fixture run end-to-end via effects::regression.

title: Effects: Option<T> value representation (nullable pointers, search results)
description:
Value::Ref/Value::Null already exist in src/effects/mod.rs but there is no
